Authors: Muthia A.; Utari D.; Soesilo T.E.B.
Title: Environmental health conditions associated with childhood stunting during the first 1000 days of life
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Child stunting is increasingly recognized not only as a nutritional disorder but also as a complex environmental health issue. Household environmental determinants, particularly safe potable water and advanced sanitation infrastructure, exert a fundamental influence on minimizing children's susceptibility to environmental health hazards that compromise linear growth trajectories. Using the transtheoretical model as a behavioral framework, the study objectives were to examine how household environmental conditions, including access to improved drinking water and sanitation, together with maternal environmental health-related behaviors, are associated with child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life in Indonesia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey. Maternal behaviors related to nutrition, healthcare utilization, and environmental conditions were operationalized as proxies for advanced stages of behavioral change. Child stunting was defined using height-for-age z-scores based on the World Health Organization Child Growth Standards. A binary logistic regression model was utilized to evaluate the multivariate associations linking maternal behavioral patterns, socio-environmental covariates, and socio-demographic indicators to the latent risk of linear growth retardation in children. FINDINGS: The prevalence of stunting among children aged 0 to 23 months was 30.32 percent. Low birth weight and higher birth order significantly increased the odds of stunting. Maternal behaviors reflecting progression to the action and maintenance stages were protective, including routine antenatal care attendance, with an odds ratio of 0.642, and delivery assisted by a skilled birth attendant, with an odds ratio of 0.707. Findings indicate that higher maternal educational attainment, improved sanitation facilities, and safe drinking water sources significantly decreased the likelihood of stunting. In contrast, maternal under nutrition elevated the associated risk by 26.5 percent. CONCLUSION: Household environmental conditions constitute fundamental determinants of child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Maternal progression toward advanced stages of stunting prevention behavior, reinforced by adequate health services and enabling environments, plays a critical role in reducing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. The findings underscore the efficacy of the transtheoretical model as a robust conceptual paradigm for mitigating childhood stunting. By integrating maternal behavioral stages of change with healthcare access and environmental determinants, the research delineates a nuanced, stage-sensitive and contextually grounded architecture for analyzing early childhood growth dynamics. © 2027 The author(s). Authors: Pan G.; Wang J.; Liu H.
Title: Crowding and green choice: Understanding a U-shaped relationship in China's organic food market
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Organic food represents a product category in which safety-and-health attributes and environmental attributes are both salient, making it an appropriate context for examining how retail situations shape sustainable consumption. This study investigates the nonlinear effect of shopping crowding on organic food purchase behavior and purchase intention, and further examines whether different crowding levels activate different organic food attribute cues. First, transaction records from a large supermarket chain in China provide associational evidence of a statistically supported U-shaped relationship between shopping crowding and organic food purchase behavior, with the turning point located in the upper portion of the observed crowding distribution and modest changes in predicted purchase probability. Second, a randomized scenario experiment provides causal evidence for the low–moderate–high nonmonotonic pattern in organic food purchase intention and identifies distinct indirect-effect structures involving positive emotion and perceived loss of control. Third, a 2×2 experiment compares the two crowding endpoints and shows that environmental-responsibility cues are relatively more effective under low crowding, whereas safety-and-health cues are relatively more effective under high crowding. Taken together, the findings extend crowding research and sustainable consumption research by identifying a nonlinear crowding effect, integrating compensatory control theory with consumer emotion theory, and showing how the match between retail situations and product attribute cues shapes organic food choice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Framing hotel strategies for demand uncertainty: The asymmetric effects of cancellation policies and F&B incentives
Abstract: This study examines how hotels manage demand uncertainty through two contrasting strategies: cancellation policies as loss-framed uncertainty reduction tools and food and beverage incentives as gain-framed coping mechanisms. Drawing on prospect theory, we argue that these approaches generate asymmetric behavioral responses with distinct temporal and revenue implications. The findings show that loss-framed uncertainty reduction initially suppresses demand by discouraging price-sensitive and uncertain customers; however, this negative effect is largely confined to the rooms department and diminishes over time. In contrast, gain-framed coping strategies stimulate in-stay consumption, encouraging guests to engage with additional hotel services and generating positive spillover effects that enhance revenue and profitability across other departments, including in subsequent periods. Overall, uncertainty reduction filters out volatile demand, whereas uncertainty coping enhances perceived value and stimulates consumption. These results underscore the importance of considering both temporal dynamics and cross-departmental effects when designing strategies to manage demand uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From Screening to Site Control: Phytic-Acid Mediated P-Tuning of M–N Coordination to Balance Iodine Adsorption and Stability in Zn–I2 Batteries
Abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (AZIBs) show promise for grid-scale energy storage, but they are hampered by polyiodide shuttling, sluggish iodine redox kinetics, and irreversible active-site poisoning caused by uncontrolled adsorption. Title: Thermo-reversible bigels stabilized by soluble dietary fiber extracted from microwave-treated okara: Molecular interactions, network rearrangement, and application in mayonnaise
Abstract: This study investigates the preparation and structural regulation of thermo-reversible bigels composed of soluble dietary fiber from microwave-treated okara (M-SDF) hydrogels and carnauba wax/sunflower seed oil oleogels, evaluating their application in low-fat mayonnaise. Carnauba wax was introduced as the oleogelator to structure the oil phase, with its crystalline matrix largely determining the mechanical properties and thermal reversibility of the bigels, while M-SDF served as a macromolecular stabilizer to structure the hydrogel phase and enhance interfacial stability. Microwave pre-treatment altered the molecular characteristics of okara SDF, leading to altered monosaccharide composition, enhanced thermal stability and increased crystallinity, driven by strengthened hydrogen bonding and a more ordered network arrangement. Using variable-temperature FTIR and rheological temperature sweeps, the microstructure and phase transition of the bigels were systematically characterized. The spectral and structural responses were highly dependent on the oleogel-to-hydrogel ratio, with the 7:3 bigel exhibiting pronounced thermal reversibility. Temperature elevation intensified bands at 3677 and 1041 cm−1, indicating the progressive weakening of intermolecular interactions and interfacial rearrangement. Rheological measurements confirmed that the optimized bigels possessed elevated storage modulus (G′ up to 4.65 × 103 Pa) and high phase transition temperature (Tgel of 85.87 °C), supporting a mechanically robust matrix. Incorporating these bigels into mayonnaise significantly improved textural properties and viscoelastic behaviors, demonstrating their effectiveness as a clean-label structuring and stabilizing agent. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Solar Photovoltaic Adoption in East Java Non-Profit Organizations
Abstract: Non-profit organizations in East Java need dependable electricity for service continuity, daily operations, and cost control, yet face capital, regulatory, behavioral, and tropical-climate barriers to rooftop solar photovoltaic adoption. This study combines a focused literature review, bibliometric mapping of 25 verified domain studies selected from 79 unique Scopus records, a random-effects synthesis of five Global Solar Atlas locations, and a 50,000-iteration Monte Carlo model for a common 12 kWp system. The 25 studies met predefined adoption, finance/policy, governance/behavior, and tropical-performance criteria and passed metadata verification. Modeled annual output ranges from 17.231 to 18.227 MWh; pooled yield is 4.03 kWh/kWp/day (95% CI: 3.92–4.14). Median NPV is IDR 40.7–54.9 million, with a conditional positive-NPV probability of 86.4–92.5%. Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate, tariff escalation, capital cost, avoided electricity value, and self-consumption as the dominant drivers of NPV. The five-city results are screening evidence, not a representation of all tropical climates or roofs. Title: Reframing artificial intelligence as an observable market signal: Extending Signaling Theory in luxury fashion retail
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming luxury fashion retail; however, existing research primarily views AI as an operational technology that enhances efficiency and personalization. Less attention has been given to how consumers interpret AI-enabled marketing applications as signals of luxury brand meaning. Drawing on Signaling Theory, this study conceptualizes AI-enabled marketing applications as market signals through which consumers infer luxury brand attributes. Using a multi-method design comprising survey-based structural equation modeling (n = 362), exploratory consumer segmentation (n = 101), and sentiment analysis of 193 online reviews, the study examines how AI shapes perceptions of exclusivity, authenticity, innovation, and responsiveness and how these perceptions influence luxury brand performance. The findings reveal that AI-enabled marketing applications do not show a statistically significant direct effect on brand performance; instead, their effects operate through these four signaling dimensions. The exploratory segmentation identifies three consumer profiles with different signaling perceptions, while sentiment analysis reveals generally positive evaluations alongside concerns about excessive automation and diminished human interaction. The study extends Signaling Theory by positioning AI-enabled marketing applications as market signals through which technological capabilities acquire symbolic brand value. Managerially, the findings suggest that luxury brands should deploy AI strategically to reinforce symbolic value while preserving exclusivity and authenticity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Inclusive education as organizational inclusion: Creating inclusive business schools through co-curricular learning
Abstract: Knowing how to create inclusive business schools is crucial for the development of leaders navigating the workforce. This research examines co-curricular First-Year Experience (FYE) programming as an approach to supporting student integration, learning, and experiences. Using a quasi-experimental design, two studies examined academic performance and perceived transition success, belonging, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and time management behaviours across in-person and online learning contexts. In Study 1, in-person students demonstrated higher academic performance and perceived transition success than online students. At the end of the semester, online and in-person students were comparable in outcome expectations, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management. General belonging was lower among online students across the two measurement occasions however, this difference was already present at baseline and did not change significantly over time. General belonging, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management were positively associated with perceived transition success, whereas outcome expectations were not a significant unique correlate. Study 2 identified exploratory within-format patterns across co-curricular in-person, bespoke in-person, and bespoke online course formats, with university belonging emerging as a significant correlate of perceived transition success across all three. Title: Navigating the successful digital transformation of correctional services: Challenges, good governance, and a hybrid framework
Abstract: Digital transformation initiatives are essential for advancing correctional services toward digital maturity in Macao. However, the absence of a well-defined overarching strategy presents a significant impediment to the effective implementation of reforms. Due to the fact that the intelligent construction of the penal system has not yet been integrated with the extant eGovernment, the governance of the correctional system and its capabilities necessitate rigorous enhancement. Good governance encompasses legitimacy, accountability, transparency, capacity, fairness, responsiveness, participation, and consensus, which are widely considered core principles of public administration and are well-suited to linking the vision of digital transformation and smart correction initiatives. Based on the practice of eGovernment in Macao, which aspects can facilitate the digital transformation of correctional services to enhance the modernization of governance systems and capabilities, and achieve good governance? This study employs qualitative research methods, including a comprehensive literature review, secondary data collection, and analysis of legal documents, regulations, and sentencing policies within the Macao penal system. A SWOT-Plus analysis is conducted to assess potential internal and external trends and identify extant challenges. A hybrid framework is proposed that incorporates the incentives for eGovernment and the fundamental principles of good governance, including key governance beliefs and values such as organization, process, regulation, and culture. The findings also outline a series of expected impacts on correctional services that navigate the transformation ideology and foster successful implementation, thereby coordinating the vision of smart government. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Nie J.; Gao F.; Liu Y.; Umair M.; Abdalla Adam N.
Title: Reputation and value signals as moderators of advertising spend efficiency in E commerce search advertising
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: China hosts the world's largest e‑commerce search advertising market, yet merchants persistently misallocate advertising budgets by treating ad spend as a monotonic driver of sales efficiency. Drawing on the Resource‑Based View (RBV) and Information Overload Theory, this study investigates how advertising spend intensity (ASI) affects two core efficiency metrics—the Ad‑to‑Sales Ratio (ASR) and Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), as well as the moderating roles of two structural market factors. Keyword Specificity (KS) reflects the semantic breadth of keywords ranging from generic terms to long‑tail queries, whereas Category Competition Intensity (CCI) captures the density of competing products within each keyword market. Based on keyword‑level panel advertising data from a home appliances and household goods retailer operating on China's leading business‑to‑consumer platform, alongside supplementary observational data on competing products, this study identifies an inverted‑U‑shaped relationship between ASI and both ASR and ROAS: advertising efficiency improves with greater spending initially but declines after crossing a category‑specific threshold. KS shifts the efficiency peak toward higher spend levels, meaning long‑tail keywords can maintain efficiency under greater advertising investment. By contrast, CCI compresses this optimal spending range and triggers earlier efficiency deterioration in highly competitive categories. These findings extend the RBV and Information Overload Theory to sponsored‑search research and provide keyword‑type and competition‑dependent spending benchmarks for practitioners in Chinese e‑commerce. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Analysis of environmental and social impacts of quarry mining for bridging stakeholder perception gaps–a case study from Padukka, Sri Lanka
Abstract: This study investigates stakeholder perceptions of the environmental and social impacts associated with the China Harbour Aggregate Quarry in the Padukka Division of the Colombo District, Sri Lanka. Despite growing concerns about the impacts of quarrying on host communities, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how different stakeholder groups perceive and experience these impacts in the Sri Lankan context. The study involved 31 community members near the quarry, 3 quarry site professionals, and 4 officers from a technical services company, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with all stakeholder groups and structured questionnaires comprising open- and closed-ended questions administered to community members. Thematic analysis was used to analyze interview and open-ended questionnaire data, while descriptive analysis was applied to closed-ended questionnaire responses. Findings indicate that vibration was the dominant impact, reported by all community participants (100%), with concerns about noise, water dry out, dust, and occasional flyrock events. Community responses revealed high perceived annoyance (93.5%) and opposition to the mining site (87.1%), although all respondents were unwilling to relocate, highlighting sociopsychological constraints. Comparative analysis revealed convergence and divergence between community perceptions and quarry personnel perspectives, with mitigation measures implemented but challenges persisting due to spatial constraints, communication gaps, and disputed compensation claims. The study contributes context-specific evidence on stakeholder perceptions of quarrying impacts and provides practical insights for strengthening community engagement, impact mitigation, and socially responsible quarry management in Sri Lanka. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: pH-dependent foam stability of egg white protein-sodium alginate-eggshell powder systems: Roles of soluble calcium availability, bulk structuring, and interfacial behaviour
Abstract: Egg white protein (EWP)-based foams are widely used in aerated foods, and their stability depends on bulk-phase structure and air-water interfacial behaviour. This study investigated how initial pH conditions regulate soluble calcium availability, structural assembly, interfacial behaviour, and foam stability in EWP-sodium alginate (SA)-eggshell powder (EP) systems. EWP-SA dispersions were initially adjusted to pH 5.0, 7.0, or 9.0 before EP incorporation. Wet ball milling reduced EP to a submicron particle size of 0.41 μm while preserving the calcite CaCO3 crystalline structure. The pH 5.0 group showed the greatest pH increase after EP addition and the highest SWeibull plateau values for soluble calcium measured colorimetrically (21.52-24.22 mM), consistent with enhanced CaCO3 dissolution under the initially acidic condition. This group also exhibited enhanced EWP-SA association, possible Ca2+-mediated alginate crosslinking, broader particle-size distributions, higher β-Sheet contents, stronger bulk viscoelasticity, greater aggregation, and improved long-term foam retention during standing. Although the pH 7.0 and 9.0 groups generally exhibited higher dilatational moduli under the applied oscillatory conditions, the pH 5.0 group showed a faster initial adsorption response, with a maximum Kdiff of 2.359 mN m−1·s−1/2. Moreover, the 1.5% SA-1% EP and 1.5% SA-2% EP systems in the pH 5.0 group retained 100% and 95.63% of their foam volumes after 12 h, respectively. Foam stability was associated with changes in soluble calcium availability, bulk viscoelasticity, and interfacial behaviour. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for constructing stable EWP-SA-EP foams by regulating initial pH to coordinate bulk-interfacial coupling processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: From natural-extract variability to reproducible nanomaterials: AI-QbD strategies for green synthesis from agro-food waste
Abstract: Green synthesis of metal nanoparticles from agro-food waste extracts offers environmental and economic advantages over conventional chemical methods, using natural phytochemicals as reducing and stabilizing agents. However, inherent variability in botanical feedstocks, arising from seasonal fluctuation, geographic origin, and extraction protocols, poses significant challenges to reproducibility and standardization. Current literature documents fewer than 300 systematically characterized synthesis studies using non-harmonized protocols, and botanical extract composition inherently varies 15–30 % seasonally and geographically, limiting the generalization of process parameters across waste sources. This review critically examines the materials science foundations of phytochemical-mediated nanoparticle formation, including the mechanistic roles of phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and terpenoids in metal-ion reduction, nucleation kinetics, and surface capping. We analyze how feedstock composition and extraction conditions influence particle size distribution, morphology, crystallinity, and surface chemistry properties, which ultimately determine biological identity and functional performance. We then evaluate the potential of Quality-by-Design (QbD) frameworks and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches to address these reproducibility challenges. However, we emphasize that significant prerequisites remain before AI deployment is viable: AI model performance reported in the literature ranges from 65 to 85 % accuracy across heterogeneous botanical waste sources, substantially lower than idealized estimates, and current models suffer from dataset-size limitations and the risk of overfitting. We propose a phased implementation roadmap: Phase 1 (18–24 months) requires establishing harmonized botanical characterization protocols and controlled extraction procedures; Phase 2 requires 300–500 documented synthesis experiments across multiple waste sources; Phase 3 can then build predictive AI models on this standardized foundation. Throughout, we distinguish between demonstrated evidence, emerging proof-of-concept results, and areas requiring substantial further validation before clinical or industrial translation becomes feasible. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Spectrally Partitioned All-Optical Memristors for Highly Linear Neuromorphic Vision Systems
Abstract: All-optical control of synaptic weights offers a promising route toward low-power and massively parallel neuromorphic hardware. However, existing optoelectronic memristors often require electrical assistance or exhibit nonlinear and asymmetric conductance updates, limiting their energy efficiency and scalability. By contrast, visible illumination activates VOx and promotes interfacial hole-assisted recombination, leading to reversible depletion of defect-state electrons and conductance depression. This wavelength-selective carrier-transfer process enables highly linear and symmetric all-optical weight updates, achieving a linearity of 0.9994 and an effective 8-bit conductance resolution. The electrical energy consumption per optically induced synaptic event is calculated to be as low as 0.63 fJ under an ultralow probing bias. By integrating the devices into a 32 × 32 all-optically programmed array, we further demonstrate hardware-based BloodMNIST microscopic blood-cell image classification with an accuracy of 96.5% and strong noise robustness. Title: Selective partitioning of plant proteins during emulsification impairs foam stability: conformational changes of aqueous-phase residues relative to animal proteins

Title: A Manganese-Chlorella Hydrogel for an Integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” Strategy in Pancreatic Cancer Therapy
Abstract: Pancreatic cancer faces the challenges of tumor progression and postoperative pancreatic fistula during the perioperative period, which severely affect patient prognosis. In this study, an injectable self-healing multifunctional hydrogel (CMCGel) was developed based on dynamic cross‑linking between manganese ions (Mn2+) and carboxymethyl chitosan loaded with chlorella extract (CE). This platform implements an integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” (3R) strategy for comprehensive perioperative management. CMCGel exhibits distinctive pH/laser dual-responsive behavior: In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the accelerated release of CE and Mn2+ enhances photodynamic therapy and chemodynamic therapy (CDT). This combination, activated by laser and gated by endogenous pH, achieves remarkable tumor suppression rates of 85.81% in vitro and 96.01% in vivo. As pH normalizes, Mn2+ shifts from CDT to activate the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, remodeling the immune microenvironment. Crucially, CMCGel’s adhesion strength in artificial pancreatic fluid at 48 h was 4703.80 ± 50.36 Pa, only 8.17% lower than that at 10 min. This enzyme-resistant property enables durable mechanical sealing at the fistula site, reducing amylase leakage by 55.71% and creating favorable conditions for tissue repair. By integrating pH/laser-triggered combination therapy, immunomodulation, and enzyme-resistant barrier functionality into a single platform, CMCGel presents a clinically promising strategy for perioperative management of pancreatic cancer. Authors: Khan H.; Knight G.; Khan Z.
Title: Mechanisms for digital business model innovation in international new ventures from developing economies
Abstract: Digital international new ventures (DINVs) increasingly leverage ecosystem partnerships to drive digital business model innovation (DBMI) and navigate global markets. However, research to examine how such partnerships contribute to DBMI is limited, particularly in resource-constrained firms from developing economies. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities view, organizational learning theory and an ecosystem-based digital learning perspective, we investigate the role of ecosystem partnerships in enabling DBMI through the development of digital learning capabilities. Based on survey data from 147 DINVs in a developing economy, findings suggest that ecosystem partnerships enhance digital learning, which in turn facilitates DBMI. Moreover, foreign market turbulence tends to positively moderate the relationship between ecosystem partnerships and digital learning capability. In addition to demonstrating how DINVs build innovation capacity under volatile conditions, findings help to extend perspectives on capabilities, learning, and ecosystems. Leveraging ecosystem partnerships, digital learning, and digital business model innovation appears to enhance the performance of DINVs. Ecosystem partnerships appear to be especially valuable to DINVs when market turbulence is high. The study offers theoretical and practical insights into the mechanism through which DINVs from developing economies can achieve digital innovation, and provides policy implications for supporting their international growth. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Current Status of Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy in Japan: A Web-Based Survey of Endoscopists (PRESS Survey)
Abstract: Objectives: The increasing number of patients with colorectal cancer underscores the importance of colonoscopy. Adequate bowel preparation is essential to ensure the quality and safety of colonoscopic examinations; however, data on the current practices in Japan remain limited. This study aimed to clarify the current status of bowel preparation, use of bowel-cleansing agents, and associated challenges among physicians performing colonoscopies. Methods: In March 2026, we conducted a nationwide web-based cross-sectional survey of physicians performing colonoscopies in Japan. The survey assessed bowel preparation practices, use of bowel-cleansing agents, constipation, and renal function before colonoscopy. Responses were obtained from 300 physicians who performed at least 10 colonoscopies per month. Results: Low-volume polyethylene glycol (PEG) plus ascorbate preparations were the most commonly used bowel-cleansing agents, followed by high-volume PEG preparations and magnesium-based agents. Cleansing efficacy and safety were the most highly valued characteristics of bowel-cleansing agents. 64.7% of physicians reported that the perceived frequency of inadequate bowel preparation was >10% among their patients. Although 64.3% of the physicians reported always assessing constipation, only 32.7% reported always evaluating renal function before colonoscopy. Compared with hospital-based physicians, those working in clinics reported a significantly lower proportion of inadequate bowel preparation, but a significantly lower rate of renal function assessment. Conclusion: Although cleansing efficacy and safety are prioritized in bowel preparation for colonoscopy in Japan, physicians perceived inadequate bowel preparation to occur in a substantial proportion of patients. Thus, further optimization of bowel preparation strategies and more consistent assessment of renal function before colonoscopy are needed. Title: A data-informed scaling parameterization for non-Fickian retention in atmospheric boundary-layer dispersion
Abstract: Pollutant dispersion in the planetary boundary layer is usually simulated with the advection–diffusion equation closed by the gradient-diffusion hypothesis, in which the turbulent flux follows the local concentration gradient. In the convective boundary layer it cannot represent transport driven by thermals spanning the full depth of the layer. The Bevilacqua–Galeão bi-flux model separates the material into a fraction that diffuses classically and a retained fraction that does not follow the local gradient, introducing a fourth-order term governed by a retention coefficient Kz2. In previous applications Kz2 was treated as a constant, with no means of relating it to the state of the boundary layer. Here the equation is solved by a high-order implicit finite-difference scheme, and a constrained Bayesian optimization identifies the parameters best reproducing the Copenhagen and Prairie Grass tracer experiments. Dimensional analysis of these optima yields Kz2(x) in terms of the friction velocity, boundary-layer depth, source height and downwind distance, so that the coefficient is specified in advance from routine meteorological data and grows as the plume travels downwind. The same expression covers the 115 m elevated release at Copenhagen and the near-surface release at Prairie Grass with no constant adjusted to either. When it is prescribed, the absolute fractional bias falls by 57% and 27% respectively, and the normalized mean square error by 12.7% and 17.3%, while other performance measures are preserved. The scaling was determined based on the optimization results, and the validated range is limited to the source heights considered in the tests. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Constitutive metabolic signatures associated with partial resistance to fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) in tropical maize inbred lines
Abstract: Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) poses a major threat to maize production in sub-Saharan Africa, underscoring the importance of identifying durable sources and biochemical markers of host-plant resistance. This study investigated the constitutive metabolic basis of partial FAW resistance in tropical maize by integrating insect bioassays with complementary GC–MS and LC–Q-TOF–MS profiling. Whole-leaf tissues collected before infestation from three resistant (Mp716, CML71, and CKSBL10008) and three susceptible (CML370, CKSBL10025, and CML444) inbred lines were analyzed, and the same tissues were incorporated into artificial diets to evaluate larval growth and feeding preference. Diets derived from resistant genotypes consistently reduced larval relative growth rates and were less preferred by neonates than diets derived from susceptible lines, providing evidence that pre-existing leaf chemistry contributes to both antibiosis- and antixenosis-associated resistance. GC–MS detected approximately 800 analytical features and highlighted resistance-associated trends in amino-acid, nitrogen, and central-carbon metabolism. LC–Q-TOF–MS detected approximately 1,700 features, with 384 differing significantly between resistance classes after false-discovery-rate correction, revealing extensive remodeling of specialized metabolism. Resistant lines were characterized by higher relative abundances of several putative amino acids, purine-related metabolites, phytosterols, and putative defense-associated compounds, including a DIMBOA-hexoside-related feature. In contrast, susceptible lines generally contained higher levels of putative soluble sugars, central-carbon metabolites, and several flavonoid- and phenylpropanoid-related features. Pathway analysis identified 28 differentially abundant consolidated metabolites and significant enrichment of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, indicating selective metabolic reconfiguration rather than generalized accumulation of secondary metabolites. Together, these findings demonstrate that partial FAW resistance is associated with a coordinated constitutive metabolic signature integrating nutritional composition and specialized defense chemistry. Although targeted and spatially resolved validation is required to establish the functions of individual metabolites, the identified signatures provide promising biochemical candidates for resistance screening and metabolomics-assisted breeding of FAW-resistant maize. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature B.V. 2026.

Title: The value of lost load in electricity intensive industry – combining and comparing stated and production value approaches
Abstract: The value of lost load (VoLL) is a monetary metric quantifying the cost of unsupplied energy (€/kWh) during outages, providing valuable insights for policymakers, utility providers, and industrial stakeholders. Leveraging a mixed-method approach that integrates and compares survey data with publicly available microeconomic data insights, results show how value-added based measures significantly underestimate the financial impact of power outages. Shorter outages are found to be disproportionately costly, primarily due to high fixed costs associated with initial disruptions. Businesses report that the effects of a 1-h outage could linger for months, with some unable to fully recover even 12 months after the event. These extended disruptions underscore the enduring consequences of power outages, particularly for electricity-intensive industries. In a regression type of approach, the cost of power interruptions is not significantly influenced by the type of industry. Instead, the economic impact of an outage is more closely tied to the volume of electricity consumed, duration and production hours. Highlighting sectoral aspects and methodological sensitivities, the paper offers relevant insights for setting reliability standards, designing compensation schemes, and for guiding infrastructure investment. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Wei L.; Ding Z.; Zhao Z.
Title: How does responsible governance affect firms’ Innovation resilience? A matching perspective on responsible leadership and responsible AI
Abstract: Innovation resilience has become a critical capability for firms to withstand risks and achieve sustainable growth. However, how responsible governance shapes firms’ innovation resilience remains underexplored. Drawing on signaling theory and conservation of resources theory, this study examines the effects of responsible leadership, responsible AI, and their congruence on firms’ innovation resilience. Using survey data from 480 firms in China’s manufacturing and strategic emerging industries, we conduct empirical analyses with nonlinear regression and response surface analysis. The results show that: (1) responsible leadership has an inverted U-shaped relationship with firms’ innovation resilience; (2) responsible AI has a negative effect on firms’ innovation resilience; (3) congruence between responsible leadership and responsible AI is conducive to firms’ innovation resilience; (4) firms exhibit higher innovation resilience under the high responsible leadership-high responsible AI configuration than under the low responsible leadership-low responsible AI configuration; (5) compared with the low responsible leadership-high responsible AI configuration, firms achieve higher levels of innovation resilience under the high responsible leadership-low responsible AI configuration; and (6) organizational unlearning and organizational innovation climate positively moderate the effect of responsible leadership-responsible AI congruence on firms’ innovation resilience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Optimizing equity and efficiency in the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem
Abstract: This study addresses the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem, formulated as the strategic prepositioning of a heterogeneous aerial firefighting fleet across capacity-constrained airbases. A novel bi-objective model is proposed that simultaneously optimizes efficiency (aggregate risk-weighted accessibility) and equity (minimized regional service disparities). The model employs an enhanced spatial accessibility method with a distance-decay function to evaluate coverage effectiveness and distribution fairness. A multi-objective genetic algorithm is implemented to generate Pareto-approximate solutions, revealing quantifiable trade-offs. Applied to a national-scale case study in Greece using 25 years of wildfire data, results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides significantly wider coverage than current practices, thereby extending protection to underserved regions while reducing redundant overlap. Sensitivity analyses confirm robustness across various real-world conditions, such as different budget levels and aircraft availability. This transferable tool enables policymakers to make data-driven decisions by quantifying the balance between response effectiveness and social fairness in wildfire-prone regions. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Sour grapes or strategic choice? Socially disadvantaged tourism entrepreneurs' pursuit of ‘break out’
Abstract: While structural conditions impacting immigrant entrepreneurs' ‘break out’ are well-documented in tourism research, the underlying psychological processes remain underexplored. Informed by self-determination theory and adaptive preferences, this ethnographic study conducted between December 2024 and May 2025 explores how socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs negotiate structural constraints and individual agency while pursuing ‘break out’. Drawing on 345 h of ethnographic observation, digital data from two focal Nepali tourism entrepreneurs in Hong Kong SAR, and longitudinal object-oriented interviews with nineteen stakeholders, it reveals a psychological mechanism where frustration of basic psychological needs triggers adaptive preferences, hindering ‘break out’ efforts. It also shows how tourism's experiential nature enables entrepreneurs to counter stigma and negotiate autonomy. Practically, the findings highlight the need for psychologically informed support that goes beyond traditional skill-based training. While focused on Hong Kong's Nepali diaspora, the study offers broader insights into entrepreneurial ‘break out’ among socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Probabilistic wind power forecasting with tree-based machine learning and weather ensembles
Abstract: Accurate production forecasts are essential for the integration of renewable energy sources into the power grid. This paper illustrates how to obtain probabilistic forecasts of wind power generation using gradient boosting trees and an ensemble of weather forecasts. To this end, we perform a comparative analysis across three state-of-the-art probabilistic prediction methods-conformalized quantile regression, natural gradient boosting and conditional diffusion models-all of which can be combined with tree-based machine learning. The methods are validated using four years of data for all Belgian offshore wind farms. We benchmark the models against the power curve and a calibrated wake model as well as a probabilistic method using stochastic variational Gaussian process regression. The tree-based models significantly reduce the mean absolute error in comparison to the deterministic baselines. Additionally, all three methods outperform the Gaussian process baseline in probabilistic skill, while two out of the three also improve point forecast accuracy. The conditional diffusion model attains the best performance, with improvements of 5% in mean absolute error and 12% in continuous rank probability score compared to the probabilistic baseline. Last, the results indicate an average improvement in point forecast accuracy of 17% by using an ensemble of weather forecasts instead of a single provider. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Lu F.; Sun D.; He W.; Li M.; Shi Z.; Wu Y.; Sun S.-F.; Shao C.; Sun R.
Title: Hydrophobic Eutectogels Reinforced by Zn2+-Coordinated Lignin Nanoparticles for Underwater Wearable Electronics
Abstract: Wearable flexible sensors for underwater communication and biomotion monitoring are gaining attention. However, developing gel-based strain sensors with high toughness, anti-swelling performance, robust underwater adhesion, and long-term stability remains challenging. Herein, we present a hydrophobic eutectogel (DPF-Zn@LNP-HEG) fabricated via the assembly of a polymerizable hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent (PHDES), 2-phenoxyethyl acrylate (PEA), and Zn2+-coordinated lignin nanoparticles (Zn@LNP). The resulting structure, composed of hydrophobic polymer networks and metal-phenolic complexes, forms hydrophobic microdomains that disrupt the hydration layer and prevent water penetration. Meanwhile, Zn@LNP serve as dynamic sacrificial cross-linkers, enhancing the material’s mechanical strength, energy dissipation, and anti-swelling properties. The resulting eutectogel exhibits remarkable tensile strength (1.14 MPa), superior toughness (3.15 MJ m−3), excellent anti-swelling properties (< 1% after 30 days), and robust underwater adhesion (1.07 MPa on glass). Based on these properties, we demonstrate an underwater strain sensor with high sensitivity (gauge factor = 8.12) and long-term stability, enabling underwater Morse code transmission, biomotion monitoring, and Bluetooth-based tracking of swimming movements. This work not only provides a versatile design paradigm for multifunctional underwater sensing platforms but also advances the high-value utilization of bio-based materials in next-generation flexible electronics. Authors: Wang Y.; Dan B.; Lei T.; Chen Z.; Ding Y.
Title: Online direct-to-consumer channel introducing and ordering strategies of fresh supply chain considering disruption risks and yield constraints
Abstract: The rise of online direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels expands fresh producers’ distribution networks while intensifying competition with traditional retail channels. Meteorological disasters threaten the DTC channel's reliability, dynamically reshaping the coopetition between fresh producers and retailers. This study develops a theoretical framework to examine strategic interactions within a fresh supply chain, comparing a traditional monopoly model with an integrated distribution system that incorporates both DTC and traditional retail channels. Disruption risks and yield constraints faced by producers are considered. The findings suggest producers should introduce DTC channels during yield contraction but exercise caution in surplus periods. Despite disruption risks, DTC channels pressure retailers to accept higher wholesale prices and increase orders, enhancing the sales revenue of fresh produce with limited yield. However, rising disruption probabilities incentivize retailers to reduce order quantities strategically, leading to a higher risk of stagnation for fresh produce. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Artificial intelligence is not enough to enhance organizational performance
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), supply chain visibility, supplier integration, and organizational performance through the lens of Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT). Drawing on empirical data from UK-based organizations that have adopted AI technologies, we employ structural equation modeling along with mediation and moderation analyses to test our hypotheses. The findings indicate that AI does not have a significant direct effect on performance; instead, its impact is fully mediated through supply chain visibility and supplier integration. This supports the view that AI-driven supply chain visibility acts as an information-processing mechanism that enhances firms' ability to coordinate, collaborate, and integrate with supply chain partners, thereby improving organizational performance. Furthermore, supply uncertainty positively moderates the relationship between supplier integration and performance, amplifying the benefits under conditions of higher uncertainty. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying AI's indirect role in driving performance and highlighting the importance of embedding AI within broader organizational capabilities. It also offers practical insights for managers seeking to leverage AI to enhance supply chain integration and organizational effectiveness. © 2026

Authors: Cui Y.; Wu Y.; Tong Y.; Hou D.
Title: Artificial intelligence disclosure and the value relevance of earnings
Abstract: This study investigates the effect of AI disclosure on the value relevance of earnings using Chinese listed companies from 2013 to 2022. We find that AI disclosure significantly enhances earnings’ value relevance. Mechanism tests show that AI disclosure increases firms’ earnings quality and boosts investor attention, thus elevating the value relevance of earnings. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that this effect is more pronounced in firms in advanced manufacturing industries, firms in highly competitive industries and non-SOEs. Overall, this study highlights the important role of AI disclosure in the price discovery of both fundamental and unexpected earnings, and contributes to a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms through which AI affects the value relevance of earnings. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Liu Q.; Ma N.; Zhang X.
Title: Your recommendation and my choice: The impact of algorithmic recommendation convergence on consumers’ algorithmic recommendation aversion
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Personalized recommendation features launched by integrated online shopping platforms with multi-brand competition trap consumers in the dilemma of product choice constrained by algorithmic recommendation convergence, and induce consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. Against this backdrop, this article systematically examines the existence, antecedents, and boundaries of consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. The results show that algorithmic recommendation convergence significantly triggers consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion and suppresses their purchase intentions. Specifically, in addition to perceived lack of self-control affecting algorithmic recommendation aversion, consumers' state of choice overload caused by homogeneous recommendation convergence is the key reason for perceived lack of self-control and the emergence of algorithmic recommendation aversion. Meanwhile, the results further demonstrate that in multi-brand markets with multi-oligopolistic brand coexistence, brand agglomeration further narrows consumers' brand and product choice scope, making it more likely to induce consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. In contrast, in a single-brand-dominated market structure, the core brand effect can leverage its dominant market position and market recognition to mitigate the impact of algorithmic recommendation convergence on consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. These findings expand the research perspective on consumer algorithmic bias, emphasize the importance of brand strategies, and provide timely and critical insights for understanding and alleviating consumers’ algorithmic recommendation aversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Sundar, Nataraj Agaram (60729083100); Morabia, Tejas (60729101200)
Title: From conventional multi-vendor failover to adaptive API routing: An industrial experience report on resilient third-party service integration
Abstract: High-scale online services often rely on third-party APIs in user-facing flows such as authentication, messaging, payments, fraud detection, and identity verification. Integrating alternate providers and operating conventional failover controls is a common resilience baseline, but redundancy alone does not make provider selection adaptive, explainable, or policy-aware. This paper reports an anonymized industrial experience evolving a conventional multi-vendor SMS-provider failover arrangement in a large marketplace setting into configuration-driven adaptive API routing. The approach uses operation-specific pluggable factor lists to separate routing policy from application code, combines hard eligibility gates with normalized weighted provider scoring, and closes the loop with business-outcome telemetry, decision logs, traffic-shift controls, and recovery safeguards. The report includes de-identified operational evidence, including before/after windows, a representative incident timeline, shadow-mode validation records, policy-tuning history, score-normalization snapshots, provider-attribution examples, feedback-bias controls, and sensitivity analysis. The evidence suggests that adaptive provider routing can reduce dependence on incident-time interpretation when the operation is critical, telemetry volume is sufficient, and organizational controls exist for policy ownership, explainability, and safe traffic movement. The paper concludes with practitioner guidance and transferability conditions for teams considering similar architectures. © 2026

Title: Phygital pop-up stores: Measuring immersion, novelty, and post-visit purchase behavior using eye-tracking and biometrics
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Phygital pop-up stores hybrid retail environments fusing physical spaces with digital layers represent an accelerating frontier in contemporary retailing. However, the precise cognitive mechanisms through which these sensor-driven environments translate immediate sensory engagement into durable long-term consumer choices remain under-theorized. Drawing upon the Technology Acceptance Model, Expectation Confirmation Theory, and Trust Theory, this study develops an integrated model positioning consumer trust as a critical mediator between phygital experiential antecedents and downstream purchasing commitments. Primary data were collected from 612 adult consumers across the United Kingdom and Australia via a stratified intercept sampling protocol. Objective measures of consumer immersion were captured using eye-tracking metrics and galvanic skin response indices embedded within a structured self-report survey. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) reveals that while immersive experiences, novelty, interactivity, and enjoyment associate positively with retrospective post-visit purchase behavior within a 30-day window (R2 = 0.482), consumer trust functions as the dominant direct predictor (β = 0.274, p < 0.001) and an essential gatekeeper mediating the immersion–purchase pathway. Title: Advances in TMDs-Based Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers: From Structural Engineering to Multicomponent Synergy
Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered considerable attention as advanced electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) materials due to their unique layered structures, tunable electronic properties, and intrinsic defect-induced polarization mechanisms. This comprehensive review systematically summarizes recent advances in TMDs-based absorbers, with particular focus on two fundamental development strategies. The first involves multiscale structural design of pure phase TMDs spanning from atomic to submillimeter dimensions, achieved through precise defect regulation, phase engineering, and sophisticated morphological manipulation to optimize electromagnetic parameters and attenuation capabilities. The second strategy focuses on constructing multicomponent composite systems, incorporating dielectric matrices, magnetic elements, and multicomponent hybrids to achieve synergistic enhancement through interfacial polarization, conductive loss, and magnetic dissipation mechanisms. The review critically analyzes pioneering research achievements across various subfields while identifying specific challenges and opportunities within each domain. Future perspectives highlight emerging frontiers including atomic level interface engineering, inverse design of multicomponent and multiscale architectures, sustainable large-scale synthesis techniques, and development of multifunctional smart-response systems. This work aims to establish fundamental principles and provide forward-looking guidance for designing next-generation high-performance TMDs-based EMA materials with tailored functionalities. Title: Don't promise me, prove it: Leveraging blockchain affordances to reduce uncertainty and build consumer purchase confidence in sustainable fashion

Title: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer municipal plastics for enhanced environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical recycling of municipal plastic waste can reduce landfill burden, energy demand, and environmental impacts while recovering reusable polymers. The study objectives were to assess the performance of polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene using polymer-specific pre-processing methods, shredding, thermal consolidation, and compression moulding. The assessment focused on waste minimization, material recovery, energy requirements, estimated carbon dioxide emission reductions, sustainability, and mechanical and thermal performance. METHODS: A total of 37 kilograms of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene was separately processed using polymer-specific treatment and compression moulding. Environmental performance was evaluated within a cradle-to-gate framework using secondary emission factors, and the Sustainability Index was derived from predefined parameters. Recycled materials were evaluated for mechanical and thermal properties. Exploratory one-way analysis of variance assessed polymer differences, with probability values adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. FINDINGS: Waste reduction and material recovery rates exceeded 95 percent for all polymers, with low-density polyethylene achieving the highest recovery of 99 percent. Low-density polyethylene also showed the lowest energy consumption of 0.95 kilowatt-hours per kilogram and the observed sustainability index of 82.6 ± 2.1, although polymer-specific differences in the Sustainability Index were not statistically significant. Polyethylene terephthalate showed the highest tensile strength (55.2 megapascals), compressive strength (83.4 megapascals), density (1.36 grams per cubic centimetre), and carbon dioxide emission reduction (2.10 kilograms of carbon dioxide per kilogram). High-density polyethylene showed intermediate performance. Analysis of variance indicated polymer-specific differences, with F-statistic values of 1.72–412.3 and probability values of <0.001–0.27. After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, most physical and mechanical properties, energy consumption, and carbon dioxide emission reduction showed significant differences, whereas landfill diversion and the Sustainability Index did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene achieved high material recovery while maintaining mechanical and thermal properties. The polymers showed differences in material recovery, energy consumption, carbon dioxide emission reduction, and evaluated material properties. Further evaluation using heterogeneous municipal plastic waste and larger-scale processing is required. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Mixed methods research: Critical review and guidelines for stronger design, integration, and contribution
Abstract: Mixed methods research has a prominent place in tourism and hospitality scholarship, yet adoption has advanced faster than methodological selectivity, which leaves many studies combining qualitative and quantitative strands without explaining why both strands were necessary, how the strands were related, or what integrated inference their combination alone made possible. Drawing on a critical review of 222 mixed methods studies published in leading tourism and hospitality journals, this article identifies dominant patterns, strengths and weaknesses, and underused possibilities. In response, the article offers a stage-based guide that links problem formulation, purpose selection, design fit, sampling bridges, strand roles, integration, divergence handling, reporting architecture, and contribution development. Title: Fostering creativity through interdisciplinary teaching: A meta-analysis of effectiveness
Abstract: Interdisciplinary teaching is widely promoted to cultivate students’ creativity, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis synthesized 55 quantitative studies (70 effect sizes, 7490 students) from 2013 to 2024, applying random-effects models using Hedges’ g. Creativity outcomes were decomposed into three theoretically grounded dimensions: creative thinking process, creative practice ability, and creative personality and psychology. Results indicated a large overall positive effect ( g + = 1.090, 95% CI [0.913, 1.266]), with very high heterogeneity ( I 2 = 96.017%). Title: Security testing of RESTful APIs: Approaches and research challenges
Abstract: RESTful APIs have become a fundamental component of modern cloud-native and microservice-based applications, enabling seamless integration between distributed services. Since these APIs often expose sensitive data and business logic through publicly accessible endpoints, they have become attractive targets for cyberattacks. Recent security incidents and the growing number of API-related vulnerabilities demonstrate that traditional web application security mechanisms are insufficient for protecting RESTful APIs. Although numerous testing approaches have been proposed, existing research remains fragmented and often focuses primarily on functional validation rather than systematically addressing security vulnerabilities and adversarial exploitation patterns. This survey provides a comprehensive review of RESTful API testing approaches with a particular focus on those identifying security vulnerabilities. Based on a systematic analysis of 69 primary studies, we examine common RESTful API vulnerabilities and present a structured taxonomy that distinguishes between application-level weaknesses and configuration or deployment-level issues. We further analyze the attack patterns that exploit these vulnerabilities and review state-of-the-art testing approaches, including specification-based, model-based, property-based, and AI/ML-driven techniques. In addition, we analyze existing tools, datasets, and evaluation metrics used to assess the effectiveness of RESTful API testing methods. Finally, the survey identifies several critical research gaps that limit the effectiveness of current approaches, particularly around authenticated, context-aware testing and the detection and validation of logic-based security violations. We discuss emerging trends and outline potential research directions, including dependency-aware testing frameworks and AI-driven techniques for automated vulnerability discovery. This work aims to guide researchers and practitioners toward developing more systematic and robust frameworks for RESTful API security testing. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Machine Learning Parameters Identification for a New Unit Power-Logistic Quadratic Lindley Model
Source title: Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice
Abstract: This paper introduces a new two-parameter distribution for modelling unit interval data. It is named the Unit Power-Logistic Quadratic Lindley (UPLQL) model. It is constructed by applying a power-logistic transformation to a flexible baseline distribution known as the quadratic Lindley. The resulting density can take several shapes; decreasing, unimodal, right skewed, or left skewed making it suitable for a wide variety of proportional data. Closed-form expressions for the cumulative distribution function (CDF), probability density function (PDF), and hazard rate function are formulated, while the quantile function (QF) is derived in a semi-closed-form. Mathematical properties including moments, Lorenz and Bonferroni curves, order statistics, stress-strength reliability, and stochastic order are derived. Eight frequentist estimation methods are compared through an extensive Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), and a Bayesian analysis using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is also carried out. An amortised tree-based estimator (ATE) that predicts the parameters directly from a set of features is developed. It can be turned into a fast Bayesian tool using a parametric bootstrap. The performance of the UPLQL model is evaluated on two data sets, the flood-level proportions and petroleum reservoir measurements. In both applications, the new distribution performs competitively with established unit distributions and offers a good combination of flexibility, interpretability, and computational efficiency. © Grace Scientific Publishing 2026.

Title: Continuous Fabrication of Bioinspired All-Biomass Aerogel Fibers for Thermal Insulation
Abstract: Aerogel fibers have been considered as a promising solution for thermal protection textiles due to their high porosity and low thermal conductivity. However, the scalable production of sustainable and mechanical strong aerogel fibers remains a critical challenge. Here, inspired by the porous core–shell structure of polar bear hair, we report a continuous strategy to fabricate all-biomass aerogel fibers featuring an encapsulated core–shell architecture using silk fibroin as the core and cellulose as the shell. This tunable structure, with radially aligned sheet-like pores and adjustable shell thickness, is achieved through hydrogen bond-driven cellulose contraction and alcohol-induced curing of sheet-like silk fibroin. Such a porous architecture effectively suppresses convective heat transfer and promotes a multi-reflective effect for infrared radiation. The resulting fibers exhibit good mechanical robustness with a tensile load of a single aerogel fiber is up to 200 g without reinforcement. Meanwhile, the aerogel fiber maintains high porosity (79.78%), low thermal conductivity (52.4 ± 4.2 mW m−1 K−1), and low density (0.193 ± 0.01 g cm−3). Furthermore, an aerogel glove fabricated from these fibers demonstrates good thermal insulation. These results provide new insights for the design of biomimetic aerogel fibers with core–shell architecture, offering a scalable and eco-friendly pathway toward advanced wearable thermal management. Title: Wearable Electronics for Precision Diagnosis Through Advanced Manufacturing and Integration
Abstract: Wearable electronics are rapidly transforming healthcare by enabling continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and molecular signals directly at the point of need. This shift supports a transition from episodic, generalized care toward precision diagnosis, where individualized, longitudinal data guide early detection, risk stratification, and treatment decisions. Central to this transformation is the convergence of advanced manufacturing and heterogeneous integration strategies, which enable the development of compact, multimodal, and highly conformable diagnostic platforms. In this review, we examine how advances in materials engineering, micro/nanofabrication, and system integration have transformed wearable devices from single-parameter sensors into fully integrated, multimodal diagnostic systems. We outline key architectures and transduction mechanisms and highlight manufacturing approaches such as printing, 3D fabrication, photolithography, and laser writing. We emphasize heterogeneous integration strategies that combine sensing, electronics, power, and communication into skin-conformal platforms for long-term use. These advances enable precision diagnostics through continuous monitoring, multimodal data fusion, and individualized baselines. We also outline key challenges to clinical translation and discuss future directions toward robust, scalable, and clinically actionable systems, providing a strategic outlook for next-generation wearable electronics in precision diagnosis. Title: The impact of entrepreneurship education on sustainable entrepreneurial intentions: A quasi-experimental study
Abstract: In this paper, we examine how a semester-long sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship course shapes sustainable entrepreneurial intention (SEI) through individual sustainability orientation (ISO). Grounded in an adaptation of the Theory of Planned Behaviour, ISO is conceptualized as a multidimensional construct encompassing sustainability-oriented (SO) values, SO motivation, awareness of sustainability issues, and SO self-efficacy, dimensions expected to mediate educational effects on SEI with different temporal sensitivities. We implemented a quasi-experimental design across two graduate introductory entrepreneurship courses at two Canadian universities: one redesigned around sustainability mechanisms (treatment, N = 112) and one covering standard content (comparison, N = 47). Pre- and post-test surveys were conducted. Results show no direct effect of the treatment on SEI and no change in SO values, which were high at baseline. However, the treatment significantly increased students’ sustainability awareness, self-efficacy, and, unexpectedly, motivation. Among these, changes in awareness and self-efficacy were positively associated with changes in SEI. These findings indicate that semester-long interventions can reliably influence proximal cognitions (awareness and self-efficacy), while deeper dispositions such as values, and to a lesser extent motivation, likely require longer-term or more immersive exposure. Theoretically, this study conceptualizes ISO as a temporally layered construct that helps explain why prior findings on education–SEI links are mixed. Methodologically, it demonstrates the value of coupling quasi-experimental designs with pedagogical reporting. Practically, it highlights workable mechanisms, such as sustainability-anchored projects, sustainable business modeling, and impact-oriented pitches, that strengthen awareness and SO self-efficacy. These insights encourage moving beyond outcome-level evaluations toward understanding how entrepreneurship education can foster SEI. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Negotiation and relationships: Insights from adjacent, psychologically-grounded literature
Abstract: Negotiations often unfold within ongoing relationships, making relationships integral to negotiation processes and outcomes. Yet, despite repeated calls for greater attention to relational dynamics, behavioral negotiation research has largely relied on paradigms that minimize the role of relationships. We review research from adjacent, psychologically-grounded literature (e.g., on close relationships, marketing, strategy, and operations) that conceptualize negotiation as embedded within ongoing relationships. We show that negotiations in relationships unfold under distinct starting conditions that shape negotiators’ interpretations, judgments of appropriateness and risk, and the interplay between negotiation processes, outcomes, and the longer-term relationship. As a result, negotiations in relationships often involve managing both objective and relational interests simultaneously, producing beliefs, behaviors, and outcomes that differ from dominant findings in behavioral negotiation research. Title: The effectiveness of industrial gamma and e-beam sources, to inactivate B. pumilus spores in the presence of liquid water and considerations for validation of sterilization dose in accordance with ISO 11137
Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of industrial electron beam (e-beam) and gamma irradiators in inactivating Bacillus pumilus spores at varying levels of water availability. Commercially available B. pumilus spore strips were exposed to three hydration conditions: dry, immersed in saturated NaCl solution, or immersed in purified water, and subsequently irradiated. Gamma operated at a dose rate of 1 kGy/h, while the dose rate of e-beam was 1800 kGy/h. The results showed that gamma and e-beam irradiation were equally effective ( p = 0.111) in inactivating dry B. pumilus spores. These findings suggest that, provided the validated minimum dose is delivered, the dose may be transferred between industrial radiation sources without compromising product sterility, assuming no liquid water is present. In contrast, e-beam was more efficient than gamma in inactivating spores in saturated NaCl solution ( p = 0.007) and spores in water ( p = 0.009). It was observed that spore resistance increased with increasing water availability. The protective effect of water may have important implications for dose qualification strategies in sterilization processes. In the industrial sterilization of medical devices, the dose is often qualified by using Method 1/VDmax25, defined in ISO 11137. Method 1/VDmaxdose setting relies on the assumption that the product bioburden exhibits resistance to ionizing radiation that is consistent with the Standard Distribution of Resistance (SDR). If due to the presence of water, the resistance of the bioburden exceeds that of the SDR, Method 2 of ISO 11137-2:2013 should be used instead. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Dual-Ion Co-Storage via Solvation Structure Tuning Toward Ultrafast and Durable Zinc-Organic Batteries
Abstract: Aqueous Zn-organic batteries are promising due to the sustainability and tunability of organic cathodes. However, the critical challenge in their practical application lies in dissolution, degradation, and sluggish kinetics, ultimately degrading the cycling stability and rate capability. Title: Exploring the linkage between entrepreneurial education and entrepreneurial intentions among university students in Morocco
Abstract: The Moroccan labor market continues to struggle with the incorporation of its university graduates and the interest in entrepreneurship as an employment option is growing. Title: Reframing destination stability: how scale reshapes tourism volatility in the Balearic Islands
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourism destinations are often described as spatially differentiated systems, with coastal areas portrayed as more stable and inland areas as more volatile. Yet, it remains unclear whether these differences arise from location per se or from underlying structural properties of destinations. This paper develops a structural perspective on destination stability by examining the association between tourism-system scale and supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility at the municipal level in the Balearic Islands. Once scale is controlled for, the widely assumed coastal-inland divide in volatility largely disappears, and the independent contribution of spatial location becomes negligible. These findings indicate that structural stability in regulated accommodation capacity is strongly associated with tourism-system scale rather than being solely attributable to geographical location. The paper contributes to destination marketing and management by: (i) using supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility as an indicator of structural destination stability, (ii) providing evidence of a negative association between municipal tourism-system size and supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility, and (iii) qualifying spatially grounded interpretations of coastal stability. Title: MambaFusion: Registration-assisted lumbar CT-MRI image fusion via Mamba and dynamic feature modeling
Abstract: Medical images play a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis, yet a single imaging modality often fails to provide complete anatomical and pathological information. Multimodal image fusion addresses this limitation by integrating complementary information from different modalities. In this study, a CT-MRI registration and preprocessing procedure was first introduced to reduce spatial mismatch between lumbar CT and MRI images. The MRI volume was registered and resampled into the CT coordinate space, ensuring spatial consistency before image fusion. Title: Will this time be different? Just transition pathways in eastern and Southern Africa’s critical minerals sector
Abstract: The global energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for critical minerals required for renewable energy technologies like solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems. However, the future translation of mineral reserves into equitable socio-economic development in the region depends on policy frameworks and governance systems that promote inclusive participation, recognition, and benefit-sharing. This paper examines pathways for inclusive economic transformation, analyzing the conditions required to ensure mining-affected communities benefit equitably from the critical minerals boom. We employ a justice-centered framework of distributional, procedural, recognition and restorative justice to analyze five countries (Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa, Zambia, Malawi, and Burundi) through stakeholder interviews with 43 actors and document and policy analysis, including Malawi and Burundi, whose emerging sectors are largely absent from the peer-reviewed record. Across the five cases the four dimensions are not encountered as separate problems. Findings suggest that employment opportunities do not always reach local populations, revenue mechanisms face transparency challenges, consultation processes have limited influence over outcomes, customary tenure is inconsistently recognized, and environmental legacies often persist without adequate remediation. Title: Not that simple: How can generative artificial intelligence be used to develop college students’ entrepreneurial ability?
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become increasingly relevant to entrepreneurship education, yet its association with college students' entrepreneurial ability remains contested. Based on questionnaire data, our empirical findings show that both routine and innovative use of GenAI are positively associated with entrepreneurial ability. Moreover, we find that potential and realized absorptive capacity mediate this relationship, while interaction analyses indicate that these associations are stronger at higher levels of design thinking. These findings contribute to the entrepreneurship education literature by revealing the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which GenAI use enhances college students’ entrepreneurial ability. Title: Determining the robust drivers of CO2 emissions in Africa: Machine learning and panel econometric evidence on the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis
Abstract: One of the primary greenhouse gases linked to global warming is carbon dioxide. This study investigates the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions in 29 African countries over the period 1990–2023 using a two-stage machine learning and econometric framework. In the first stage, Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms are employed to identify the most important drivers of carbon dioxide emissions. The results indicate that Random Forests provide the highest predictive performance among the machine learning models. In the second stage, the variables identified by the machine learning analysis are incorporated into second-generation panel estimators that account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. Specifically, long-run and short-run relationships are examined using the Common Correlated Effects Autoregressive Distributed Lag estimator, while Augmented Mean Group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, and Fixed Effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are employed as robustness checks. The findings reveal that oil consumption is positively associated with carbon dioxide emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption is negatively associated with carbon dioxide emissions. The results provide limited but supportive evidence for the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, with income and income-squared terms exhibiting the expected signs and the estimated turning point falling within the observed income range. Robustness analyses based on oil-exporting and non-oil-exporting country groups, as well as an alternative carbon-intensity measure, confirm the central role of fossil fuel dependence and renewable energy adoption in shaping environmental outcomes across Africa. These findings highlight the importance of accelerating renewable energy deployment, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable development strategies to achieve long-term environmental sustainability in African economies. © 2026 The Authors.
