Title: Political elites and access to economic opportunities in China's rural market transition
Abstract: Understanding whether political elites maintain advantages in accessing economic opportunities during market transitions is crucial for assessing the distributional consequences of market-oriented reforms. This study examines whether political status provides rural households with advantages in accessing production resources and income opportunities during China's recent wave of marketization, and how these advantages vary with the degree of market development. Using three waves of the China Family Database spanning 2015–2019 and employing an instrumental variable approach, we find that political elites maintain persistent advantages in accessing economic opportunities. As marketization advances, the sources of elite advantage shift from agriculture to commercial activities. While advantages in agricultural production weaken, reflecting reduced state-controlled resource allocation channels, advantages in business operations strengthen consistent with elites converting political capital into entrepreneurial opportunities. Our findings suggest that rural marketization in China reallocates rather than reduces opportunity gaps. Title: Flexible computational loads as demand-side resources for surplus renewable energy: A review of siting criteria, thermal management, and operational strategies
Abstract: Renewable curtailment often occurs behind local transmission constraints, yet studies rarely examine whether flexible loads are located where surplus arises. This review assesses when Bitcoin mining, deferrable artificial-intelligence and machine-learning (AI/ML), and high-performance-computing (HPC) workloads can use otherwise-curtailed electricity. A PRISMA-informed search, citation tracking, targeted searches, and institutional records produced a 99-record source set. The synthesis follows five steps: verify surplus, match workload flexibility, screen site and thermal feasibility, select an operating pathway, and bound claims. The positive-part Normalized Surplus Index is proposed as a screening concept. A California Independent System Operator audit shows that balancing-area records cannot support nodal NSI without pre-curtailment availability and boundary-consistent absorption and export allocations. Siting criteria include electrical access, communications, cooling and water, land and environmental constraints, and heat sinks; local stakeholder elicitation is required for weighting. Reviewed models support rapid downward interruption of controllable Bitcoin-mining loads, whereas AI/ML and HPC flexibility is slower and schedule-dependent. Surplus absorption requires separately verified upward activation in the same location and time window. No operator-grade nodal validation, site ranking, field deployment, or grid-service qualification is demonstrated. Flexible compute is therefore a conditional demand-side resource, not a general curtailment solution. © 2026

Authors: Ma H.; Wang C.; Mao Y.; Yang L.; Wu H.; Fang R.; Xu W.
Title: Interfacial charge redistribution regulates surface hydroxyl dynamics during photocatalytic nitric oxide oxidation
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: Water can replenish reactive surface hydroxyls during photocatalytic nitric oxide (NO) oxidation, yet excessive hydration blocks adsorption sites. Here, Ag2O was deposited on hydroxyl-rich zinc hydroxystannate (ZnSn(OH)6, ZSOH) to couple interfacial charge transfer with dynamic surface-hydroxyl evolution under visible light. The optimized sample removed 69.8% of NO after 30 min and exhibited repeatable activity over five light-on/off cycles. At relative humidities of 5%, 50%, and 95%, NO removal reached 74.3%, 61.8%, and 51.3%, respectively. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, work-function calculations, and differential charge density revealed electron redistribution from ZSOH to Ag2O, while time-resolved photoluminescence, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and photocurrent measurements demonstrated improved carrier separation and transport. Electron spin resonance detected enhanced formation of photogenerated electrons, •O2−, and •OH. Density functional theory further showed that Ag2O coupling strengthened H2O adsorption and elongated the average adsorbed O-H bond. In-situ infrared spectroscopy revealed irradiation-induced redistribution and depletion of surface hydroxyls, followed by water-driven partial restoration of the O-H environment. These results support an interfacially mediated hydroxyl consumption–regeneration cycle in which charge redistribution promotes carrier utilization and reactive oxygen species generation, whereas adsorbed water restores reactive hydroxyl environments. At high humidity, competitive water adsorption increasingly restricts NO and O2 access. This work identifies interfacial electronic regulation of dynamic surface hydroxyls as a strategy for photocatalytic NO oxidation under variable humidity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Tourism's temporal pathways: A deceleration framework
Abstract: This research introduces Tourism Deceleration as a theoretically grounded framework for understanding temporal recalibration in tourism. Building on social acceleration theory and consumer deceleration framework, we conceptualize tourism deceleration as a situated temporal negotiation through which travelers recalibrate pace, attention, mobility, digital connectivity, and presence. Using hybrid deductive-inductive qualitative content analysis supported by LLM-assisted coding and human validation, we analyze 367 unique Reddit posts and 21,554 comments related to slow travel and long-term travel. The findings show that decelerated travel is often negotiated through practical, social, and personal constraints rather than simply chosen as a preferred travel style. Episodic deceleration remains the most explicit form of decelerated travel, while extended duration often intersects with embodied practices, reduced mobility pressure, and selective negotiation of digital technologies. Title: From cox to DeepHit: A comprehensive analysis of aircraft longevity using time-varying and machine learning models
Abstract: Estimating the economic useful life (EUL) of commercial aircraft is governed by extreme right-censoring: with over 70% of 35,212 aircraft still in service, retired-only analysis underestimates longevity through exclusion bias, while full-fleet analysis must work from relatively few observed retirements. We argue that this censoring, rather than the choice of model, sets the limit of what can be estimated, and we address it with a staged strategy comprising nonparametric Kaplan-Meier estimation, Cox models with time-varying coefficients, and a DeepHit neural survival network, each introduced to overcome a specific limitation of the previous stage. In individual aircraft-model × usage cells, estimated median EULs range from roughly 25–30 years for passenger jets to 29–42 years for their cargo counterparts, and cargo aircraft outlive passenger aircraft within every estimable model pair (87.7% vs. 33.2% 30-year survival across the pooled fleet). Leasing is associated with later retirement (24.2% lower estimated hazards for passenger aircraft and 42.6% lower estimated hazards for cargo aircraft), and, in pooled passenger-aircraft models, the estimated Airbus–Boeing contrast reverses over the lifecycle, with Airbus aircraft facing higher early but lower late retirement risk; this contrast may partly reflect differences in the manufacturers’ model composition. The censoring constraint becomes especially apparent at the finest resolution: many recently introduced types and modern freighter cells have too few retirements for reliable model-level estimation, motivating a pooled model that shares information across aircraft types. DeepHit, using a learned type embedding and lagged oil prices as leading predictors, attains the strongest predictive accuracy (C-index 0.89 vs. 0.64–0.77 for the Cox-family models), an indicative gain rather than a strict like-for-like ranking because the models are scored on different samples and representations. Title: Student perceptions of generative AI in accounting education: A thematic analysis
Abstract: Generative AI has outpaced pedagogical and ethical guidance in accounting classrooms, leaving students and educators uncertain whether it supports or undermines the discipline's dual emphasis on procedural accuracy and professional judgment. To address this problem, this study examines how 92 business undergraduates perceive generative AI tools, notably ChatGPT, in accounting education, drawing on in-class, handwritten survey responses. Findings show that students view AI as a useful yet uncertain resource: valuing its speed, accessibility, and support while raising concerns over cheating, fairness, unclear institutional policies, and overreliance. Four interconnected themes emerged: Practical Affordances and Engagement, Ethical Tensions and Integrity, Curricular and Institutional Context, and Reflective Learning and Active Engagement. These results suggest student perceptions are shaped less by technology alone than by the pedagogical and ethical conditions of its introduction. Theoretically, the study identifies an augmentation–formation paradox specific to disciplines that combine codifiable procedure with professional judgment, which is advanced tentatively as extending the boundary conditions of paradox theory in education, a proposition that requires further empirical testing. Thematic analysis using a hybrid inductive–deductive coding strategy served as the primary analytic approach, supported by supplementary lexical analyses. The study contributes to management and accounting education by demonstrating that responsible AI integration requires clear guidance, reflective learning, and explicit alignment among AI use, assessment design, and academic integrity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Covalent Organic Framework Membranes through Sequential Imine Exchange for Precise Molecular Separation
Abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with high crystallinity hold great promise in precise molecular separation, but often suffer from the intercrystalline defects and thus poor membrane-formation ability. This study reports a sequential imine exchange strategy to fabricate highly crystalline, defect-free COF membranes for precise molecular separation. Two functional amines (aromatic and aliphatic amines) are employed in highly reversible imine exchange reaction to separately conduct crystallization and defect remedy processes according to their different energy gaps. Aromatic amine, which serves as COF framework building unit, undergoes the first-step imine exchange for high crystallinity because of its lower energy gap. Afterward, the hyperbranched aliphatic amine with abundant amino groups undergoes the second-step imine exchange, affording the tight connections between adjacent crystals and the excellent membrane-formation ability. Accordingly, the COF membrane exhibits high permeance (344 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for water, 462 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for methanol) and rejection (> 99.9% for Congo red and Alcian blue). Meanwhile, the membrane is endowed with an ultrahigh separation factor (> 528) for mixed dye aqueous solutions and large-scale processability (> 290 cm2). This work offers a new strategy to fabricate highly crystalline and defect-free COF membranes, revealing their large potential in diverse practical applications. Title: Driving sustainable development goal alignment through green consumption marketing and public mind
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development demands synchronized efforts across socioeconomic and environmental domains, specifically targeting poverty alleviation, food security, and environmental stewardship. Although sustainable consumption patterns and ecological marketing act as established catalysts for environmental transitions, the specific socio-civic pathways translating micro-level pro-environmental behaviors into macro-level policy alignment remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, the study objectives were to evaluate the direct and indirect pathways through which green consumption behavior and green marketing drive local alignment with the sustainable development goals through the mediating role of the public mind among residents in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand. METHODS: A quantitative survey design was executed to gather data from 400 residents across administrative districts in Nonthaburi Province using proportionate stratified random sampling. The researchers collected primary data through structured questionnaires employing a 5-point Likert scale. Analytical procedures encompassed descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to validate construct relationships and assess overall structural model fit. FINDINGS: The results of structural equation modeling indicate that both green consumption behavior and green marketing significantly influence the realization of local sustainable development goals, operating through both direct pathways and indirect pathways mediated by public consciousness. The public mind demonstrated the strongest direct influence on sustainable development goals realization (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), followed by direct impacts from green consumption behavior (β = 0.35, p < 0.01) and green marketing (β = 0.28, p < 0.01). Additionally, green consumption behavior was the primary driver of public mind activation (β = 0.37, p < 0.01), surpassing green marketing (β = 0.27, p < 0.01). The validated structural model accounted for substantial variance in sustainable development goals alignment (R^2 = 0.97) and the public mind (R^2 = 0.77). CONCLUSION: Green consumption behavior and green marketing are critical precursors to cultivating a collective public mind, which bridges individual eco-conscious actions with macro-level alignment of Sustainable Development Goals. Municipal authorities ought to embed the mobilization of public ecological awareness into environmental governance policies. Furthermore, this structural framework offers a scalable model adaptable to other rapidly urbanizing provinces in Southeast Asia. Title: Building sustainable influencer partnerships within the creator economy

Abstract: Influencer marketing has become an integral part of retail branding strategies. Title: Why skilled migrants stay or leave host countries: A belongingness theory perspective
Abstract: While skilled migrants have a high propensity to quit their jobs and leave host countries, little is known about why some skilled migrants leave while others stay. Title: The impact of consumer culture positioning on multinational brand premium: The moderating role of global identity
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Multinational brands often charge higher prices in emerging markets than in their home markets. Although such multinational brand premiums can improve profitability, they may also invite consumers to compare prices across countries and evaluate the premium as unfair. This research examines how consumer culture positioning (CCP) shapes consumers' willingness to pay a multinational brand premium through price fairness perceptions, operationalized as perceived price unfairness, and how this process depends on consumers' global identity. Experiment 2 replicates this pathway and examines chronic global identity as a boundary condition. Experiment 3 further tests the moderation through situationally activated global versus local identity. The results generally show that GCCP, relative to LCCP, reduces perceived price unfairness and increases willingness to pay a premium. The fairness-based indirect effect becomes stronger as chronic global identity increases and when global identity is situationally activated. Title: TikTok as a stage: How short video creators’ identity performance drives engagement with tourism experiences
Abstract: Destinations are increasingly collaborating with short-form video creators to engage consumers. Through Goffman's dramaturgical lens, this study explores how creators' performed identities in travel videos relate to audience responses. Combining machine learning and AI-powered analyses of over 10k short-form videos and 176k viewer comments with a controlled experiment, we identified four identities that creators performed in these videos (the “showman,” “diarist,” “docent,” and “photographer”) and classified them at scale. Title: Recursive self-regulation in genAI-assisted experiential learning: A task-contingent model
Abstract: Existing literature on generative AI (genAI) in business education has examined students’ attitudes, motivation, and the ethics of genAI use, alongside ongoing debate about whether genAI over-reliance may diminish self-regulated learning (SRL). However, how students self-regulate their learning while working with genAI during authentic tasks remains under-explored. This study addresses this gap by examining (RQ1) how students' self-regulatory strategies manifest during genAI-assisted learning and (RQ2) how these strategies change through genAI interaction. A thematic analysis was conducted of 34 metacognitive reflections generated across two scaffolded, four-stage experiential learning activities in a Lean Startup unit. Findings inform a three-stage AI-mediated recursive loop model, comprising monitoring, strategic adoption, and limitation identification, that extends cyclical models of self-regulated learning by showing how regulation may be initiated within the task by genAI-generated suggestions. Within this structured, reflective learning context, students indicated evaluative judgement and metacognitive regulation, providing preliminary evidence that scaffolded genAI activities can elicit active rather than passive engagement. GenAI-supported cognitive deepening was task-contingent, emerging most strongly during applied refinement tasks. Title: Complex adaptive governance for sustainable tourism villages: Explanatory insights from combined polycentric and chaos theoretical perspectives
Abstract: Sustainable tourism villages face complex governance challenges because they must simultaneously support economic development, protect local culture, preserve ecological resources, and respond to changing social conditions. Existing studies have examined sustainable tourism governance mainly from administrative, community-based, or institutional perspectives, but less attention has been given to how distributed authority interacts with nonlinear adaptive dynamics in village-level governance systems. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated framework that combines polycentric governance theory and chaos theory. Using a quantitative explanatory design, survey data were collected from 590 stakeholders involved in tourism village governance across four regencies and one city in Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that institutional diversity has the strongest association with sustainable tourism village governance, followed by decentralization and local autonomy, bifurcation and cosmology, community participation, flexibility and adaptability, edge of chaos and the butterfly effect, and self-organization and strange attractors. The model yields a very high coefficient of determination, which suggests a close within sample fit between the proposed constructs and the observed perception data. This result is interpreted cautiously because the study is cross-sectional and several constructs are conceptually proximate. The study contributes to governance theory by showing that sustainable tourism village governance can be understood as both polycentric and complex-adaptive. Practically, the findings suggest that policymakers and tourism village managers should strengthen multi-actor coordination while maintaining flexibility to respond to uncertainty and local change. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Retreat in monastery stay tourism: the role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ connectedness and behavioural intention
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Monastery stay tourism is an emerging niche within spiritual and transformative tourism, offering immersive experiences that facilitate personal and emotional growth. Despite its rising popularity, limited research has explored how such experiences shape tourists' emotional bonds, identity formation, and revisit intention. Drawing on mindfulness theory, this study examines the role of mindfulness cultivated during Buddhist monastery retreats in influencing emotional solidarity, experience self-connection, place identity, and behavioural intention. Data were collected from 430 visitors and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The PLS-SEM results underscore the critical role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ social interactions, emotional attachment to the destination, and self-connection, all of which significantly impact their intention to engage in spiritual retreats. Emotional solidarity and self-connection are found to significantly influence place identity and future behavioural intention. The MGA findings indicate that generational and experiential segmentation reveals that Generation Z is more responsive to mindfulness and experience self-connection, while older cohorts are more influenced by emotional solidarity. Repeat visitors report stronger mindfulness effects across all outcomes, whereas first-time visitors rely more on emotional bonding. Title: Contextualized learning theory in practice: An assessment study of cultivating procedural vis-à-vis conceptual fluencies in operations management fundamentals through simulations
Abstract: Contextualized learning theory promotes effective learning by placing new information in meaningful contexts; however, despite its desirability among educators, identifying practical ways to apply this theory in specific classroom teaching remains an ongoing challenge. To that end, undergraduate business students often find operations management topics challenging to contextualize because of the inherently complex integration of theoretical concepts and methodical procedures that characterize the subject. Accordingly, instructors strive to identify viable instructional tools to help students overcome this challenge and achieve parallel mastery of the intertwined quantitative and qualitative aspects of operations management fundamentals. This paper presents the results of a comparative experimental study examining the effectiveness of simulation-assisted instruction in promoting contextualized learning in an introductory operations management course. The empirical results based on a quasi-experimental design showed that computer simulations enable students to experience contextualized learning, thereby enhancing their performance and fluency in understanding and applying OM concepts and techniques. On that note, performance-based assessment of learning outcomes revealed that students' conceptual fluency, as a reflection of their contextual efficacy, improved the most when simulations were used. Moreover, students' procedural fluency, as evidenced by their technical efficacy, was simultaneously improved, albeit to a lesser extent, when simulations were employed. Perception-based assessment of learning outcomes showed similar improvement patterns; however, unlike the performance-based results, these improvements did not reach statistical significance. The findings provide valuable insights into the utility of such instructional tools through a methodical inquiry into the objective and subjective assessments of polydimensional learning outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Decoupling Ion–Dipole Interactions via Competitive Coordination for Durable Dendrite-Free Zinc Metal Batteries
Abstract: Abstract: The aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are famous for high-safety and high-energy-density, but limited by severe challenges around the Helmholtz plane layer such as the strong ion–dipole interactions between Zn2+ and H2O, resulting in slow desolvation processes and limited transport kinetics as well as corresponding higher barriers. To reconstruct the ion–dipole surroundings, the interface chemistry of employing a high permanent dipole moment of L-Carnosine (L-CN) has been proposed, weakening the interactions between Zn2+ and H2O to realize a crowded Zn2+-conductive structure, accelerating the desolvation kinetics. As revealed, the strong affinity between L-CN and Zn2+ enables the L-CN molecules to repulse H2O, reconfiguring the inner Helmholtz plane layer, thereby inhibiting the active water molecular to form hydrogen evolution reactions. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells with Helmholtz plane modulation achieve a long lifespan up to 7000 h, a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.72%, and a high stabilization at high depth of discharge (85.4%). The assembled Zn//V2O5−x full cell with optimal electrolyte delivers the capacity of 289 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g−1 under an N/P ratio of 3.98. Impressively, the large-scale pouch cell with optimal electrolyte stabilizes for 200 cycles, offering the bright future of reconstructing Helmholtz plane for achieving high-performance AZMBs. Title: Ballistic transport in nanoscale devices
Abstract: Ballistic transport refers to the condition where charge carriers traverse a conductor without scattering, where conduction is governed not by bulk properties but by how electrons are injected, transmitted, and collected at the boundaries. This review gives a unified and critical overview of ballistic transport in a wide range of nanoscale systems such as 1D/2D heterostructures, topological insulators, inorganic heterostructures, molecular junctions (MJs), perovskites, nanowire, nanosheet transistors etc. In these systems, charge carriers move over nanoscale length with near-zero momentum and phase-randomizing scattering. Starting with a historical and conceptual overview of ballistic transport, the conversation explains how the gradual reduction of device sizes below the elastic and inelastic mean free paths fundamentally invalidates diffusive transport models and requires a quantum-coherent description based on transmission eigenchannels, contact-limited resistance, and nonlocal electrostatics. We also discuss the key experimental signatures and theoretical ideas used to identify ballistic behavior, including conductance quantization, length-independent resistance, and nonlocal transport features. Finally, we critically evaluate the significant challenges that hinder the clear identification and technological utilization of ballistic transport and also outline future perspectives that are anticipated to convert ballistic transport from a mesoscopic phenomenon into a foundational principle for next-generation nanoelectronics and quantum devices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Arora L.; Jain S.
Title: Seeing through the mind: Explainable multimodal AI for depression detection—A review
Abstract: Depression detection using multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, transitioning from traditional machine learning techniques to deep learning architectures built on pre-trained transformer encoders. These systems integrate textual, acoustic, visual, and physiological signal streams through early, intermediate, late, and hybrid fusion strategies to improve predictive performance. However, a significant gap persists in model interpretability: post-hoc attribution frameworks (such as SHAP and LIME) dominate recent work, accounting for over 70% of studies published in 2024–2025, while clinician-centered validation is reported in only about 18% of the full reviewed corpus. Consequently, existing explanations are rarely validated for explainability quality dimensions; for example, SHAP attributions are known to degrade under inter-modality collinearity, and reported systems frequently lack alignment with established diagnostic criteria (e.g., DSM-based or PHQ-9 symptom structures). To close the gap between predictive accuracy and clinical utility, this review jointly synthesizes multimodal datasets, feature extraction strategies, machine learning and deep learning taxonomies, fusion strategies, and explainability techniques across 72 included studies. Finally, we outline critical future directions, emphasizing standardized XAI benchmarks, clinician-in-the-loop validation studies, and knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic reasoning. © 2026

Title: Techno-economic analysis of hydrogen production utilizing offshore wind energy using the AHP method and the Weibull distribution approximation. A case of Sakhalin Island
Abstract: The study is devoted to assessing the suitability of the Sakhalin Island offshore zone for the development of a wind energy complex, with a focus on the potential production of green hydrogen. In the course of the research, the hierarchy analysis method was applied along with fuzzy logic. Criteria influencing the placement of wind farms were selected, experts in the field were interviewed to compile pairwise comparison matrices, after which the weights of these criteria were obtained. Using fuzzy logic functions, the absolute values of the parameters were unified. The territories where the construction of wind farms is undesirable were also taken into account. As a result, the final data set was obtained using the weighted linear combination method. As a result, it was possible to identify 4 zones with the best indicators of suitability for the construction of wind farms. The territories in the Gulf of Patience near the port of Poronaysk look the most promising. Based on the data collected, 8 promising locations within 4 zones have been identified. For each location, the potential amount of electricity and green hydrogen that can be produced has been calculated using the Weibull distribution model, with 6 different methods to parameter estimation. Six different turbine models have been used in the analysis. Additionally, LCOE (Levelized Cost of Energy) and LCOH (Levelized Cost of Hydrogen) calculations were conducted. As a result, the minimum LCOE calculated was 0.087 $/kWh and the lowest LCOH recorded was 7.4 $/kg. The Vestas V236-15.0 MW wind turbine demonstrated optimal performance for the study area. If actively invested in this area, this area could become an important hub for hydrogen trading in the Asia-Pacific region. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Survival of Contractor Consortiums in the Road Construction Industry during Economic Crisis
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Road construction industries worldwide are periodically exposed to economic crises, which are cyclical in nature and often characterized by high inflation, currency depreciation, resource shortages, and institutional inefficiencies. In such conditions, traditional procurement methods frequently struggle to maintain project continuity, prompting the emergence of local contractor consortiums as a more resilient alternative. This study examines how contractor consortiums in the road construction sector adapted to recent economic crises and sustained operations amid unprecedented challenges. A qualitative research approach was adopted, involving 14 semistructured interviews with industry experts. Manual content analysis identified key adaptive measures, including financial pooling, shared equipment and labor, agile internal coordination, and proactive engagement with public authorities. These mechanisms enabled many consortiums to continue project delivery despite severe economic and operational constraints. However, the effectiveness of these measures was constrained by rigid legal and contractual frameworks, limited digital integration, fragmented stakeholder collaboration, and delayed institutional responses. To enhance future resilience, the study recommends modernizing contractual systems, strengthening digital adoption, and improving public-private coordination. The findings contribute to construction management research in crisis contexts by demonstrating the viability of consortium-based procurement and providing practical guidance to support the long-term sustainability of local contractor consortiums in the road construction sector. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Tuning oxygen-proton coupling of oxygen electrodes to match electrolyte transport in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
Abstract: Understanding how oxygen-electrode functionality interacts with electrolyte transport is essential for advancing reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs), yet their coupling remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal an electrolyte-dependent performance reversal arising from the interplay between oxygen-proton coupled reaction pathways and electrolyte transport. Surface functionalization of BaCe0.5Pr0.3Y0.2O3−δ (BCPY) oxygen electrodes with Pr0.5Ba0.5CoO3−δ (PBC) and Ni-substituted Pr0.5Ba0.5Co0.5Ni0.5O3−δ (PBCN) perovskite coatings selectively tunes surface defect chemistry and reaction pathways. PBC promotes lattice-oxygen activation and oxygen-vacancy-mediated processes, whereas Ni substitution in PBCN suppresses vacancy formation while enhancing proton hydration through strengthened Co–O covalency and optimized adsorption of oxygen intermediates. Consequently, PBC-BCPY delivers superior performance on BaZr0.8Yb0.2O3−δ (BZYb) electrolytes with limited proton conductivity, whereas PBCN-BCPY outperforms on highly proton-conductive BaZr0.1Ce0.7Y0.1Yb0.1O3−δ (BZCYYb) electrolytes. Benefiting from the optimized coupling between electrode surface functionality and electrolyte transport, the PBCN-coated BCPY electrode achieves a peak power density of 1.88 W cm⁻2 and a current density of 2.57 A cm⁻2 at 700 °C and 1.3 V on BZCYYb, while maintaining stable operation for 300 h at 600 °C. Title: Natural nano-fish bone as novel Pickering stabilizers: the emulsifying property
Abstract: Particles in the micrometer or nanometer range are widely used as stabilizers in Pickering emulsion systems. Nano-fish bone (NFB) could be an excellent stabilizer for Pickering emulsions, as it has the advantages of environmental friendliness and others. In this work, we prepared NFB particles through wet media milling treatment to investigate the mechanism behind the effect of adding NFB and peanut oil (PO) on Pickering emulsion formation and stability. The results suggested that increasing NFB resulted in increased particle coverage on the droplet surface, increased emulsion apparent viscosity, and improved stability. Similar changes in both apparent viscosity and emulsion stability were observed as the amount of PO increased. Therefore, the emulsifying properties and packing behavior of Pickering emulsions could be affected by NFB and PO content. Title: Rheologically Engineered 3D-Printed Highly Loaded Magneto-Dielectric Absorbers for Device-Level Electromagnetic Compatibility
Abstract: Highly loaded magneto-dielectric composite systems are promising for achieving strong electromagnetic loss and structural design flexibility, yet their processability and geometric controllability remain extremely challenging. Herein, a rheologically engineered direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing strategy is developed. Graphene (Gr) is introduced to reconstruct the particle-loading network, which synergistically improves the ink’s yield behavior, shear-thinning property, structural recovery, and a magnetic–dielectric synergistic loss system is constructed with carbonyl iron powder (CIP). Title: Beyond tool adoption: designing cognitive scaffolds in individual preparation to support critical thinking in generative AI integrated learning
Abstract: The integration of GenAI into higher education risks promoting passive information acceptance over critical thinking (CT), a challenge that is acutely felt in ill-structured problem-solving contexts such as engineering design. While cognitive scaffolds are recognized as a solution, limited research provides process-oriented evidence on how they mediate student engagement with GenAI. To counter this automation bias, this study introduced a novel instructional framework that integrated the Preparation for Future Collaboration (PFC) paradigm with the Target-Criteria-Source-Analogy (TCSA) cognitive strategy to structure GenAI-supported learning. By analyzing the critical thinking patterns of 77 engineering undergraduates across high-, medium-, and low-performing groups, Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) identified distinct cognitive co-occurrence patterns across GenAI-supported preparation and subsequent AI-free collaboration. High-performing students showed stronger connections among Analysis, Evaluation, and Self-regulation, a pattern we interpretively describe as a “Triangulation Loop,” whereas low-performing students showed stronger connections between Interpretation and Analysis, described as a “Descriptive Loop.” The latter pattern was consistent with greater reliance on AI-generated information. Within the integrated PFC-TCSA instructional design, these observed patterns were characterized by stronger evaluative and self-regulatory co-occurrences, providing practical implications for designing human–AI collaboration. Title: Behavioral Economics as a Driver of Healthcare System Reform: Methodological Approach
Abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to develop and apply the Behavioral Economics in Health index as a methodological tool for assessing the role of behavioral strategies in healthcare reform, with particular attention to their impact on healthcare expenditure, life expectancy, and system-level adaptation in countries with varying levels of institutional maturity and economic capacity. Methods The research used system-dynamics-based simulation modeling using behavioral and economic parameters, followed by statistical analysis of the results. Results The AnyLogic simulation results showed that, under an intensive behavioral integration scenario for 2024 to 2034, per-capita health expenditure decreased by USD 200 in Ukraine and USD 190 in Poland. In these countries, the initial levels of behavioral integration were the lowest—0.51 and 0.59, respectively—and the 10-year increase was 0.30. This fact ensured a steady reduction in expenditure throughout the entire modeling period without significant fluctuations. In Denmark, where the initial behavioral integration level was higher (0.88), the decrease amounted to only USD 26 per person, indicating a limited effect of further behavioral interventions in an already prevention-oriented healthcare system. Conversely, in the United States, where the integration index was even higher (0.91), expenditure increased by USD 20.72 per capita. Conclusions These findings indicate that the maximum economic effect of behavioral strategies is achieved in countries with low initial levels of integration and limited resources. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: An integrated analytical framework for natural gas pricing: combining multi-source drivers, forecast enhancement, and model interpretability
Abstract: With the global pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), accurate forecasting and mechanistic interpretation of natural gas pricing have become increasingly important. As a transition fuel in the shift toward a low-carbon energy system, natural gas plays a vital role in balancing energy accessibility and environmental sustainability. However, rising economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks present significant challenges to effective price forecasting and policy formulation. In response, we develop a data-driven analytical framework for natural gas pricing that integrates feature engineering and forecast enhancement to achieve accurate point-interval forecasts and investment timing. Leveraging advanced explainability techniques, the framework systematically uncovers the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in global gas market drivers. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional models in predictive accuracy and reveals important lag effects and interaction mechanisms among influencing factors. These findings validate the framework's ability to support pricing decisions and risk hedging for energy enterprises, and to provide scientific evidence for regional energy policymaking through quantification of heterogeneity. Title: When health labels increase indulgent food purchase intention
Abstract: Health labels are widely used in front-of-package communication and are generally expected to facilitate healthier decisions. We examine whether such labels can also increase consumers' indulgent food purchase intention. Across six studies, health labels attached to indulgent products were associated with greater attentional or motivational salience (Study 1a), higher digital-ad click-through rates (CTRs) (Study 1b), a higher likelihood of selecting an indulgent product in an incentive-compatible raffle (Study 1c), and stronger purchase intentions (Studies 1d–3). Authors: Zeng Y.; Liu Y.; Mei L.
Title: Curriculum greenwashing in business statistics education: Institutional decoupling in responsible management education
Abstract: Business schools increasingly state commitments to responsible management education (RME), yet institutional commitment may not be consistently reflected in pedagogical change. This study examines curriculum greenwashing as a possible divergence between RME language in curriculum artifacts and corresponding evidence in teaching practice and student learning, without assuming deliberate intent. Drawing on institutional theory and decoupling, we test whether signatory status in the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME) is associated with declarative, procedural, and consequential integration in undergraduate business statistics courses. Longitudinal multilevel data were collected from 215 students and 45 faculty members across 30 institutions across three waves. PRME status was positively associated with RME content in syllabi, whereas associations with reported teaching and student learning gains were not detected. Faculty-reported practices were positively associated with student learning gains. The PRME status × faculty quantitative teaching self-efficacy interaction was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory probing indicated a positive PRME association only at high self-efficacy. The study contributes a three-level audit framework for evaluating how institutional RME commitment is reflected across curriculum representation, reported teaching practice, and student learning, while underscoring the value of evidence beyond syllabus language alone. © 2026

Title: Recurrent and eroding challenges in creative tourism: A longitudinal study of entrepreneurial resilience among urban handicraft artisans
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of creative tourism in emerging economies, the temporal nature of the challenges facing artisans—and the resilience strategies they employ—remains poorly understood. Grounded in the processual entrepreneurial concept, this study explores how handicraft artisans understand the challenges they face and how they enact resilience in response. Adopting a longitudinal interpretivist approach, the study examines the entrepreneurial resilience of urban handicraft artisans in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, across a period of compounding crises, including the pandemic, political instability, and socioeconomic volatility. The study identifies a novel “recurrent–eroding” dichotomy as a framework for understanding challenge temporality and three resilience enablers, namely personal resources, social support networks, and operational responses. Theoretically, the study introduces new typologies of entrepreneurial challenges and extends resilience theory in creative tourism. Practically, it provides critical insights for policymakers, advocating for institutional shifts from crisis-response measures to strengthening accountable support mechanisms, market linkages, and protections for cultural work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Embodied cognition and the luxury hospitality experience of in-flight wine in premium cabins
Abstract: This study explores how first- and business-class passengers experience in-flight wine as luxurious, even though flying reduces taste and smell. Drawing on embodied cognition theory, we argue that passengers do not simply judge wine by its quality. They build a sense of luxury by noticing how the airline tries to compensate for sensory limits, by feeling that the service fits their bodily experience, and by responding emotionally. We surveyed 500 premium-cabin passengers and used two analytical approaches: structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis. The results show two related paths to luxury: a cognitive path, in which the service feels consistent with the passenger's bodily state, and an affective path, in which the service creates positive emotions. For first-class passengers, both paths had to reach a minimum level for luxury to emerge. For business-class passengers, the cognitive path was more important, and positive emotions were less essential. Authors: Liang Y.; Chen R.; Zeng Y.; Yin S.
Title: Beyond participation: Creativity and entrepreneurial mindset across instructional modes and learner-level digital conditions in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education is often examined as a uniform educational exposure, although its associations with student development may depend on instructional mode and learner-level digital conditions. This study compares six entrepreneurship education formats and examines their associations with two self-perceived outcomes—creativity and entrepreneurial mindset—while assessing whether these relationships vary by perceived digital literacy and functional social media use. Drawing on survey data from 1181 graduating students at a multidisciplinary university in Guangdong, China, we use propensity score matching to improve comparability between participants and non-participants on observed characteristics and estimate interaction models to assess conditional relationships. The results indicate that entrepreneurship education is more consistently associated with entrepreneurial mindset than with creativity. Business plan competitions, training programs, and practical workshops generally show comparatively strong associations, particularly relative to entrepreneurship courses, although public lectures are also notably associated with entrepreneurial mindset. Perceived digital literacy displays a selective and format-dependent moderating relationship with creativity but does not consistently moderate the relationship with entrepreneurial mindset. Functional social media use shows no stable moderation in the primary binary models, while supplementary continuous-measure models reveal some operationalization-sensitive patterns. These findings indicate that entrepreneurship education is best understood as a heterogeneous set of learning experiences whose associations with student development vary across instructional modes, developmental outcomes, and learner-level digital conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly being integrated into on-site heritage tourism, yet little is known about how visitors evaluate hybrid experiences combining physical heritage environments with VR-mediated reconstructions. Using a multi-stage scale development process with data collected at a heritage museum in Hue, Vietnam, the study develops and validates the OTE measurement instrument. The findings show that OTE, reflected through emotional, cognitive, and functional dimensions, strengthens visitors’ memory formation and revisit intention. Theoretically, the study advances immersive tourism research by conceptualizing and validating OTE as a higher-order experiential construct for hybrid technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Title: Designing sustainability communication across behavioral effort levels: How AI-generated micro-videos shape pro-environmental intentions
Abstract: The sustainability communication literature treats communication formats as functionally substitutable, overlooking how effectiveness may depend on the effort required to perform targeted behaviors. Drawing on processing fluency theory, this research uses perceived behavioral effort and procedural demands as an organizing lens for examining message effectiveness. Focusing on AI-generated micro-videos, the study examines how different formats influence hotel guests’ perceptions and pro-environmental intentions. Across three experiments, Study 1 demonstrated that dynamic AI-generated videos outperformed static signage, although the effect could not be attributed solely to AI generation. In Study 2, instructional clips enhanced perceived message fluency and task–technology fit for lower-effort behaviors, but not pro-environmental intentions. In Study 3, instructional clips significantly enhanced all three outcomes for higher-effort, rule-based behaviors. The study enriches sustainability communication theory by highlighting the value of explicit instructional guidance and offers actionable recommendations for designing hospitality sustainability initiatives in unfamiliar tourism service settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: How they collaborate matters: collaboration modes and task fit in human-AI recommendations
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Human-AI collaboration is increasingly used in online product recommendation, yet it remains unclear how consumers interpret different role configurations and when such configurations facilitate adoption. Drawing on mind perception theory, we argue that collaboration mode signals the collaborative system's task-relevant capability profile, and that its effectiveness depends on whether this profile fits the judgment-support requirements of search versus experience goods. Evidence from one field experiment and two scenario-based experiments indicates that AI-dominant collaboration is more effective for search-good recommendations, whereas human-dominant collaboration is more effective for experience-good recommendations, and that this fit effect is mediated by perceived diagnosticity. In addition, AI empathy functions as a compensatory interaction cue, improving consumers' evaluations of AI-dominant collaboration in experience-good contexts by enhancing perceived diagnosticity and recommendation adoption intention. Title: Food hypersensitivity communication across physical and online foodservice menus in Brazil: fragmented regulation and consumer experiences in a mixed-methods study
Abstract: Inadequate communication of food hypersensitivity in foodservice settings is a recognised risk to consumer safety, yet in Brazil no national regulation governs disclosure in non-prepackaged foods. This study characterises how food hypersensitivity is communicated through physical and online foodservice menus across Brazilian cities, and whether communication differs by the presence of local legislation. A convergent mixed-methods study assessed food hypersensitivity communication in 1034 menus (323 physical; 711 online) from 18 Brazilian cities (seven with specific legislation, 11 comparators). Menus were classified by format: no information; ingredient-only; emphasised (typographic highlighting); or symbol/code-based (icons, codes or matrices). Four focus groups with 18 participants explored experiences of adults with food allergy, intolerance or coeliac disease, and parents of children with food allergy or coeliac disease. Most menus provided some information, predominantly ingredient-only (physical: 76.2%; online: 88.0%); few provided none (6.5%; 1.0%). Warning messages were uncommon (physical: 11.1%; online: 0.1%). Explicit food hypersensitivity information was more frequent in regulated than unregulated physical menus (regulated: 24.5%; unregulated: 12.7%; p < 0.001). Higher average customer expenditure predicted explicit information (OR = 3.46), and the effect of local regulation depended on establishment type (interaction p < 0.001). Regulation was associated with explicit information among independent establishments (OR = 8.29) but not among chains (OR = 0.55), which provided it at comparable levels regardless of regulatory context. No regulatory effect was observed online, where local laws rarely apply. Consumers valued clear, visually salient formats — icons and complete ingredient descriptions — and identified hidden hypersensitivity-relevant ingredients in composite dishes and inconsistent staff guidance as key barriers, particularly on delivery platforms. This is the first assessment of food hypersensitivity communication in Brazilian foodservice, showing that subnational regulation is associated with more explicit physical-menu communication among independent establishments. Establishments require structured communication and staff training; delivery platforms need mandatory disclosure fields and standardised warnings; policymakers should prioritise structured allergen fields on delivery platforms, with a national framework as a longer-term objective. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Chen N.; Huo L.
Title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread
Abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction–diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals’ offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. In contrast, when the suppression effect is strong, migration-driven information dissemination significantly reduces the probability of infection, thereby further suppressing the outbreak. Title: Wastewater heat recovery systems for sustainable building energy efficiency and decarbonization: A comprehensive review with practical insights
Abstract: Growing energy demand and carbon emissions pose a major challenge to the building environment, particularly in addressing heating and cooling needs sustainably. In this context, wastewater is recognized as an unconventional and largely untapped thermal energy resource due to its consistent supply and generally stable temperature. Wastewater heat recovery has the potential to significantly improve building energy efficiency and boost decarbonization efforts. This review provides a comprehensive and system-level assessment of wastewater heat recovery technologies for building- and district-scale applications, with particular emphasis on heat extraction locations, heat exchanger configurations, and wastewater source heat pump systems. Rather than treating individual components in isolation, the study integrates heat exchanger and heat pump technologies within a unified framework to support practical design and implementation decisions. State-of-the-art literature covering wastewater characteristics, recovery locations, heat exchanger technologies, and combined wastewater heat exchanger-heat pump systems is critically analyzed through comparative evaluation of performance indicators, benefits, and limitations. Key recovery locations, including building outlets, sewer networks, and wastewater treatment plants are examined in terms of thermal potential, operational constraints, and system compatibility. The review highlights that appropriately selected heat exchangers and wastewater source heat pump configurations can significantly improve energy recovery efficiency while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Finally, practical recommendations are provided to guide the selection, installation, and integration of wastewater heat recovery systems, identifying fouling control, system optimization, and data-driven design as critical factors for advancing wastewater as a viable unconventional thermal energy resource in modern building energy systems. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Individual entrepreneurial orientation in Spanish university students: The role of critical thinking disposition and intellectual styles in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: This study proposes a model that links students' disposition toward critical thinking (DTCT), Type I intellectual styles (oriented toward creativity, cognitive complexity, and autonomy) and Type II intellectual styles (oriented toward structure, conformity, and rule adherence), and individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) in higher education. DTCT improves the effect of Type I styles on IEO, but not with Type II styles. These findings suggest that strengthening DTCT is a central pathway through which entrepreneurship education can enhance students' IEO. Title: Brand stereotypes, information processing, and consumer acceptance of Chinese automobiles: The moderating roles of perceived brand globalness and brand credibility in an emerging market
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Stereotypes about Chinese products persist in many developing economies, even as Chinese manufacturers have substantially upgraded their technological capabilities and product quality. However, the cognitive pathways linking systematic and heuristic information processing to consumers’ stereotype-based perceptions of brand warmth and competence remain underexplored in the evaluation of high-involvement foreign products. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, stereotype content model, and signaling theory, this study develops and tests a process-based framework explaining how information processing routes shape stereotype-based brand perceptions, which in turn influence product evaluations and purchase intentions toward Chinese automobiles in Vietnam. A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. A qualitative phase with 20 in-depth interviews was conducted to explore consumers' cognitive processes and refine the theoretical framework. Subsequently, survey data from 638 Vietnamese consumers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings demonstrate that systematic information processing strengthens perceived brand competence and warmth, whereas heuristic processing weakens both dimensions, thereby reinforcing brand stereotypes. Perceived brand competence and warmth enhance product receptivity, judgment, and quality, which collectively drive purchase intention. Perceived brand globalness weakens the negative effects of heuristic information processing and amplifies the positive effects of systematic information processing on stereotype-related perceptions. Brand credibility strengthens the conversion of product-level evaluations into purchase intention. Theoretically, this study integrates HSM, SCM, and ST to clarify the sequential relationships linking information processing, stereotype-based brand perception, product evaluation, and purchase intention. Title: Integrated system dynamics modeling for sustainable fisheries provisioning services
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fisheries provisioning services deliver food production, livelihoods and ecosystem functions, but are increasingly under pressure from environmental degradation, declining fishery resources and socio-economic stressors. Traditional paradigms in fisheries governance often exhibit a deficiency in accounting for the multidirectional feedback loops linking ecological systems with socio-economic dynamics. The objectives of this study were to develop an integrated system dynamics model to assess interactions between these dimensions and identify management options to improve fisheries provisioning services through long-term scenario simulations. METHODS: A system dynamics model was integrated, consisting of social, environmental, and economic sub-models using primary and secondary data from 2018-2023. The model includes population, fishermen, floating net cages, alternative employment, willingness to be a fisher, water quality and aquatic conditions, fish restocking, capture fisheries production, fisheries productivity, fish processing innovations, income, costs, and fisher's income. The model was verified and validated using the mean absolute error and average variation error metrics. Subsequently, predictive simulations were projected to 2045 under current, moderate, and optimistic scenarios. FINDINGS: Actual capture fisheries production declined by 88.9 percent, from 588,100 kilograms in 2018 to 65,035 kilograms in 2023 and was projected to decline to 31,179 kilograms by 2045 under current conditions. Under the moderate and optimistic scenarios, the number of floating net cages was modeled with an annual reduction rate of 30% and 35%, respectively. Production recovery commenced in 2027 under the moderate scenario and in 2026 under the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, target water quality conditions were achieved by 2041 and 2037, respectively, while fisher's net income reached positive values by 2034. CONCLUSION: The integrated system dynamics model underscores the potential for the sustainability of fishery production services through coordinated actions across social, environmental, and economic dimensions. The faster realization of target outcomes under the optimistic scenario highlights that proactive, coordinated interventions effectively expedite ecological restoration, fisheries output, and socioeconomic progress. Title: How certification credibility and benefit framing shape heterogeneous consumer responses to sustainable products in e-commerce

Abstract: On e-commerce platforms, sustainable products succeed or fail on a compressed product page where certification logos, benefit descriptions, and platform trust cues compete for attention. Retailers treat these cues as interchangeable signals, yet they address two different questions: can the product be trusted, and is it right for me? Signalling theory answers the first through costly, verifiable certification; goal-framing theory answers the second through benefit claims activating competing motivations. Whether they operate as one mechanism or two remains unresolved in retailing research. Using a discrete choice experiment with 477 Chinese consumers analysed through aggregate conditional logit, latent class analysis, and trust-stratified models, we show they are separable strategic levers. The certification credibility hierarchy (dual and international premiums above the domestic schemes) holds broadly across all three motivational segments, whereas benefit-framing valuation differs sharply between them, and this segment-level dissociation is the evidence for their separability. Platform trust does not significantly moderate certification premiums. Latent class analysis reveals a dual-motivated majority (53.5 per cent) that stated self-classification systematically understates, making choice-derived rather than self-reported segmentation essential for targeting. Extending goal-framing theory, the study's central contribution shows certification quality as a novel external cue: superior certification shifts dual-motivated consumers' default health preference toward environmental framing, narrowing it to near-parity, with a ¥16.68 break-even threshold at which the two framings reach indifference. Title: Teaching AI governance in management education: A serious game for accountable decision-making under uncertainty
Abstract: Management education increasingly needs ways to prepare students for AI governance, yet students have limited opportunities to practise the organisational judgement involved in deployment decisions. An exploratory evaluation across two undergraduate cohorts used matched pre-test/post-test data (N=67), post-session evaluations, and descriptive artefact analysis of team-produced Model Cards (n=15). Title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
Abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Drawing on tourism's anthropological lineage and interdisciplinary dance scholarship, we develop the Dance Ecosystem for Destinations—a seven-biome framework that distinguishes encounter-level value realization, portfolio-level accumulation and circulation, and cross-cutting technological mediation. The framework expands tourism management's conceptual and diagnostic capacity by linking these biomes to questions of experience design, stewardship, governance, value distribution, and evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of a design thinking education program for kindergarteners: A mixed-methods study
Abstract: Children as young as three can engage in oral and visual planning when creating tangible objects from materials, yet it remains unclear whether such design competencies can be systematically strengthened in early childhood to cultivate future design thinkers and innovative creators. To evaluate a research-informed design thinking (DT) education program, we conducted a mixed-methods study. The quantitative component involved a quasi-experiment with 133 children ( M age = 5.22, SD = 0.86) from a Chinese kindergarten (intervention group: n = 68; business-as-usual comparison group: n = 65), where the intervention group received an eight-week DT program. Each child’s DT competence was assessed immediately before and after the intervention, followed by play-based interviews with 12 children (six per group). Authors: Kang K.; He M.
Title: Financing assistance and concession strategies of the transnational supply chain under liquidity shock
Abstract: How to deal with financial distress caused by liquidity shocks has become an urgent problem for firms. We provide a framework on how to clarify the role of financing assistance and concession strategies in the context of transnational supply chains and aim to help managers understand how to choose strategies. With a small liquidity shock, the buyer provides financing assistance to the distressed supplier, resulting in a bailout effect. When the cross-effect of tax difference and vertical shareholding is large, buyer financing can hedge bankruptcy risk more effectively. With a large liquidity shock, the distressed supplier files for bankruptcy. When the reorganization cost is small or moderate, the distressed supplier reorganizes, and concession effect and bidirectional predation behavior occur in the reorganization process. When the reorganization cost is large, the distressed supplier goes into liquidation. The results provide suggestions for financing and bankruptcy decisions of firms under liquidity shock. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Integrating theory of planned behavior and value-belief-norm framework to explain voluntary carbon offsetting intentions in aviation: Evidence from Vietnamese air passengers
Abstract: The aviation industry faces growing environmental criticism for its high greenhouse gas emissions, necessitating both technological and behavioral solutions to mitigate climate change. This study examines passengers’ willingness to pay for voluntary carbon offsetting programs by developing and empirically testing an integrated model combining the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Values-Beliefs-Norms (VBN) framework. Using data from 342 Vietnamese airline passengers, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze both direct and indirect relationships among key constructs. Results confirm that biospheric values significantly shape awareness of environmental consequences, moral responsibility, and personal norms, which in turn directly influence behavioral intention. Within the TPB framework, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are strong predictors of the intention to participate in voluntary carbon offsetting, with perceived behavioral control exerting the largest effect. Mediation analysis reveals that attitudinal and normative pathways bridge moral and cognitive antecedents with behavioral intention, underscoring the complementary roles of rational and moral motivations. The integrated TPB-VBN model demonstrates considerable explanatory power, providing a useful framework for understanding pro-environmental behavior in aviation. This research extends theoretical understanding by linking ethical and volitional determinants of sustainable consumption and offers managerial insights for airlines and policymakers to design effective carbon offset communication, education, and engagement strategies. Title: How social media content shapes enrollment intention: Distinguishing firm-generated and user-generated effects through TPB and self-identity
Abstract: The increasing reliance on social media has transformed how prospective students gather and evaluate information when selecting universities. This study examines how firm-generated content (FGC) and user-generated content (UGC) influence students' behavioral intention to enroll in private universities through psychological mechanisms grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and self-identity. Specifically, the study investigates both direct and indirect effects of FGC and UGC on behavioral intention, mediated by attitude toward behavior, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and self-identity. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed, with data collected from 295 final-year high school students in Banten, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that FGC has a significant direct and indirect effect on behavioral intention, whereas UGC does not have a significant direct effect but appears to operate primarily through indirect pathways. Among the mediators, subjective norms emerge as the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, followed by attitude toward behavior and self-identity. In contrast, perceived behavioral control does not significantly influence behavioral intention. The findings suggest that FGC and UGC function through distinct mechanisms. While institutional content can directly shape behavioral intention, user-generated content primarily influences intention through social and psychological processes. These results highlight that the effectiveness of social media communication depends not only on information exposure but also on how information is cognitively evaluated, socially validated, and integrated into individuals' self-concept. This study contributes to the literature by distinguishing between different types of social media content and extending the TPB framework with self-identity in the context of higher education decision-making. The findings provide insights for understanding how digital communication influences complex behavioral decisions in contemporary educational environments. © 2027 Malque Publishing, All rights reserved.

Authors: Liu J.; Zhang Y.; Li Z.; Wang Z.; Liu J.
Title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
Abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Yoganandan G.; Monisha S.R.
Title: From brand hate to behavioral response: A recourse-contingent exit-voice-loyalty-neglect framework for digital consumer markets
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Three decades of brand hate research have mapped what triggers consumer hate and catalogued how hateful consumers respond, avoiding, switching, complaining, retaliating, subverting, without connecting these two halves through one behavioral logic. This paper closes that gap by importing the Exit-Voice-Loyalty-Neglect (EVLN) framework into the brand hate domain and extending it with a boundary condition the literature has ignored: structural recourse availability. Brand hate's dimensional profile, whether anger, contempt, aversion, or fear dominates, depends on whether its trigger is relational (betrayal, transgression, ideological incompatibility) or structural (algorithmic, platform-based, institutional unfairness), and this profile sets a default EVLN response tendency. Whether that tendency is realized depends on structural recourse, the inverse of switching costs, platform dependence, and powerlessness. When recourse is blocked, Exit tendencies redirect toward Voice where a channel exists, and toward Neglect, termed informed helplessness, where none does. We develop eight propositions specifying this redirection process, including a measurement-validity proposition showing informed helplessness is indistinguishable from loyalty in standard satisfaction measures, and a release proposition explaining how dormant hate resurfaces when conditions change. The framework helps managers and policymakers identify trapped haters and sets an agenda for measuring them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
