Title: Determinants of visit intention to Lake Toba geopark: The roles of publicity, destination awareness, destination image, and word of mouth
Abstract: Tourism research has increasingly emphasized the importance of communication and perception factors in shaping tourists’ behavioral intentions, particularly in sustainable tourism destinations such as geoparks. However, limited studies have comprehensively examined the interplay between destination publicity, word of mouth (WOM), destination awareness, destination image, and visit intention within the context of UNESCO Global Geoparks. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the relationships among these variables in the context of Lake Toba Geopark, Indonesia, by applying the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework. A quantitative approach was employed using a structured online survey distributed to 425 respondents who had previously visited Lake Toba Geopark. The collected data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS. The findings reveal that destination publicity does not significantly influence destination awareness or destination image. Similarly, destination awareness does not directly affect tourists’ visit intention. In contrast, WOM significantly influences destination awareness, while destination awareness significantly enhances destination image. Furthermore, destination image emerges as the strongest determinant of visit intention. These findings indicate that tourists’ behavioral intentions are shaped more strongly by interpersonal communication and psychological perceptions than by conventional publicity exposure. This study contributes theoretically by extending the application of the SOR framework in geopark tourism through the integration of publicity, WOM, awareness, and image variables into a single model. Practically, the findings suggest that tourism stakeholders and destination managers should prioritize strategies that encourage positive WOM, strengthen destination awareness, and enhance destination image through authentic tourist experiences and digital engagement. Ultimately, destination image plays a central role in encouraging tourists’ intention to visit Lake Toba Geopark. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Predictors of Death Related to Drug Use Disorder and Interpersonal Violence in North Africa
Abstract: Fatal interpersonal violence and deadly drug use disorder are serious social issues resulting from criminal behavior, which require effective intervention policies. Prior research on African countries is limited, and the potential association between the two issues, as described in the literature, has not been investigated. In this study, a statistical analysis was performed with R packages to identify factors that predict the death patterns related to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence, and to show empirical evidence for the association between drugs and violence in North Africa. Data on annual counts of deaths attributed to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence between 1990 and 2023 were collected, and a bivariate copula modeling approach was adopted to account for the dependence of the two counts. The findings show that socioeconomic factors, including per-capita gross domestic product, youth unemployment rate, and urban population, are significant predictors of these death counts, and statistical tests show a positive relationship between deaths related to drug use disorder and deaths caused by interpersonal violence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: How do sustainability capabilities create retail performance over time? dynamic evidence from U.S. and Chinese retailers
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how sustainability-oriented technological innovation, sustainable supply chain management, and corporate social responsibility relate to environmental and manager-reported organisational performance in retail firms over time. Drawing on the natural resource-based view, institutional theory, and stakeholder theory, the study analyses a 12-wave monthly panel of 2410 retailers in the United States and China, comprising 26,998 firm-month observations. A multi-group hierarchical Bayesian continuous-time dynamic structural equation model estimates within-firm relationships, effects over one-, three-, and six-month intervals, time-varying mediation, and country differences. Technological innovation predicts environmental performance in both countries, but it strengthens sustainable supply chain management only in China. Sustainable supply chain management predicts organisational performance in both countries. Corporate social responsibility predicts environmental performance in both countries, while its direct short-run organisational effect is positive in the United States and negative in China. Environmental performance converts into organisational performance, and all three proposed indirect effects emerge, only in China during the focal six-month window. Exploratory analysis identifies integration-driven accelerators, evidence-driven pragmatists, and weakly-coupled drifters. Title: Association of observed ramp-electrification status with APU runtime and turnaround performance: A staggered difference-in-differences analysis at a tropical ASEAN hub
Abstract: Ramp electrification can reduce aircraft auxiliary power unit (APU) use during turnaround, but operational evidence from tropical airports remains limited and sensitive to treatment-timing and implementation definitions. This study presents a replacement reanalysis of 7122 de-identified turnarounds across 20 stands at a tropical ASEAN hub from 1 March to 28 June 2025. Fourteen stands exhibited an observed transition to active treatment status, six remained never observed treated, and five first-observed treatment-date groups were identified. Because official commissioning records were unavailable, treatment timing was defined by the first observed active-treatment timestamp rather than independently certified go-live dates. A cohort-by-event interaction regression incorporated stand and calendar-date fixed effects and adjusted for aircraft body class, carrier, time of day, wet-day status, temperature, relative humidity, and rainfall. Supported post-treatment cohort-event coefficients were aggregated using cell-count weights, yielding a turnaround-weighted post-treatment estimand across the realized distribution of observed post-treatment turnarounds. Inference used CR1 stand-clustered covariance and a 9999-replication restricted-residual wild-cluster bootstrap- t . Observed treatment status was associated with a 5.874 min/turn reduction in APU runtime (95% CI −6.586 to −5.162; p < 0.001; wild-bootstrap p = 0.0001), approximately 32.0% of the eventually treated pretreatment mean. At 6.5 kg CO2e/min, this corresponds to 38.18 kg/turn of gross avoided APU-related CO2e, a deterministic transformation rather than a net-emissions estimate. Average turnaround time was +0.657 min/turn (95% CI −0.539 to 1.853; p = 0.281; wild-bootstrap p = 0.353), with variation across group-specific estimates, including +6.15 min/turn for the single-stand second treatment group; these differences are interpreted cautiously because post-treatment support and follow-up varied across groups. Joint pretreatment tests were not statistically significant for APU runtime ( p = 0.157) or turnaround time ( p = 0.528), although the earliest pooled APU lead was individually positive. The findings support a consistent association between observed electrification status and lower APU runtime while requiring caution regarding counterfactual comparability, causal interpretation, operational variation, and net-carbon interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Historical document restoration via an Adversarial Frequency-aware Guidance Network
Abstract: Historical document restoration aims to recover clean and readable document images from complex degradations such as stains, ink corrosion, background noise, and missing strokes. Existing methods mainly improve restoration backbones, but often overlook how to expose the model to challenging yet residual-bounded degradations during training. To address this issue, we propose AFG-Net, a frequency-domain hard-sample learning framework for robust historical document restoration. The key idea is to use input-restoration residuals as online degradation cues, enabling the model to focus on degradation components that remain difficult to recover. Specifically, an adaptive frequency mask generation module constructs hard samples by selectively recombining residual degradations in the Fourier domain, while a complementary-mask objective regularizes frequency selection and improves degradation diversity during training. In addition, we design the restoration branch with a text-structure-aware restoration backbone to better preserve character strokes, text lines, and layout structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that AFG-Net achieves superior restoration performance in terms of image fidelity, OCR-oriented readability, and computational efficiency. © 2026

Authors: Ma C.; Shi J.; Zhang L.; Fan A.
Title: Green by association? Restaurant presence on food-waste reduction platforms as a hybrid sustainability signal for brand equity
Abstract: Food-waste reduction platforms allow restaurants to redistribute surplus food, but their branding implications remain unclear. Drawing on signaling theory, we conceptualize restaurant presence on these platforms as a hybrid sustainability signal that embeds sustainability and commercial meanings within the same marketplace cue. Across three experiments, we examine whether this hybrid signal enhances restaurant brand equity through green brand image and whether consumer residence and restaurant type condition its effects. Study 1 shows that platform presence enhances brand equity, partially through green brand image. Study 2 replicates the main effect and provides directional evidence that the premium of platform presence may be stronger among urban than rural consumers. Study 3 shows that this effect depends jointly on consumer residence and restaurant type, and that mediation through green brand image is evident primarily for full-service restaurants. These findings identify platform presence as a hybrid, context-dependent sustainability signal with branding implications. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Design and simulation of a renewable energy-based microgrid for Accra Technical University
Abstract: Rising electricity costs, coupled with the unreliability of the supply, are big challenges facing higher learning institutions in developing nations, where the use of fossil fuels in centralized power generation systems limits the efficiency of the systems in providing sustainable power services. In the case of Ghana, the challenges are more pronounced in urban-based institutions where the availability of electricity is essential in the conduct of learning, research, and administrative activities. This study outlines the design and techno-economic optimization of the microgrid system, powered by renewable energy, for Accra Technical University (ATU) in Ghana, with the aim of providing reliable energy services while minimizing the cost of energy production and its impact on the environment. Using HOMER PRO, the study developed the microgrid model, where the optimized microgrid is composed of a solar–battery microgrid, comprising 3400 solar panels, Schneider Core inverters, and lithium iron phosphate battery systems, where the simulation results indicate the ability of the microgrid system to generate energy that meets 100% of the energy demand, with the expected energy generated per annum being 3.35 GWh, while the autonomy of the battery is expected to be 68.5 h. Economically, the optimized design realizes a Net Present Cost of GHS 17.1 million and a Levelized Cost of Electricity of GHS 0.350/kWh, which reflects a significant reduction in electricity cost compared to traditional grid-connected supply. The optimized configuration supplies the full campus electricity demand primarily from solar-based generation supported by battery storage, thereby reducing dependence on conventional grid electricity and improving the environmental performance of the institution. Apart from the cost savings, the suggested microgrid design enhances the reliability of electricity supply, reduces the risk of power outages, and realizes a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, which aligns with the renewable energy goals of Ghana. The results prove that renewable energy-based microgrids for university campuses are technically viable and economically justifiable. This paper also presents a model that can be followed for developing reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective microgrids for universities in developing countries. © 2026 The Authors. Title: ThreatNet: A multi-class dataset and LLM-based framework with class-imbalanced fine-tuning for life threat detection
Abstract: Detecting life-threatening intent in online text is an increasing challenge as social media increasingly influence public conversation. Current models often face challenges related to insufficient data, class imbalance, and domain variability between platforms. This study proposes ThreatNet, a manually annotated multi-class dataset that contains a variety of linguistic indicators and different intensities of threats sourced from multiple online sources. Using this benchmark, we perform a comprehensive empirical evaluation of seven instruction-tuned LLMs (Flan-T5, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-4B-IT, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-Instruct-7B, Zephyr-7B-Alpha, Phi-3-Mini-3.8B) and four transformer baselines (BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, DeBERTa). We analyze the impact of class imbalance mitigation strategies, few-shot prompting (0, 4, 8, 16 shots), and model scale. Experimental results, reported with standard deviations over five runs, show that Flan-T5 achieves 85.67% ± 0.81% macro-average F1 on ThreatNet, while LLaMA-3.1-8B attains 97.12% ± 0.38% accuracy on the YouTube-Threat-Corpus. These results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its usefulness for life-threatening intent detection. Title: Perceived authenticity of AI-generated tourism video and destination attractiveness: An entity-referent correspondence perspective
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Grounded in the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how three authenticity dimensions of AI-generated destination portrayals, true-to-ideal, true-to-fact, and true-to-self, relate to destination attractiveness via parallel and sequential pathways of place imagination and mental simulation. Analysis of 406 participants exposed to an AI-generated tourism video reveals that true-to-ideal and true-to-fact authenticity show significant direct effects on destination attractiveness, whereas true-to-self authenticity operates entirely indirectly, consistent with a meaning-making route. Title: Biomimetic Gradient Porous Core–Shell Fibers with Enhanced Gas Sensing for CO-Temperature Dual-Mode Early Fire Warning
Abstract: Early fire detection systems that are highly sensitive are essential for reducing the impact of fire disasters. However, their development still faces significant challenges due to the lack of capability for simultaneous monitoring of both temperature and gas. Herein, we propose a facile coaxial wet-spinning strategy to fabricate a dual-parameter fiber sensor capable of simultaneously detecting carbon monoxide (CO) and temperature for early combustion warning. The gradient porous sheath constructed by gradient-induced phase separation technology exhibits gradually decreasing pore sizes from outer (> 10 μm) to inner (< 3 μm) regions. This structure demonstrates a significant enhancement in the fiber sensor’s sensitivity to CO, achieving a 15% higher response compared to non-gradient porous structures (ΔR/R0 = 0.95%/ppm; detection limit of 10 ppm), with the response time reduced to 19.28 s, surpassing the response speed of most fire-warning fibers. Additionally, this fiber sensor can rapidly monitor abnormal temperature increases, enabling flame alarm functionality within 3 s. It also achieves precise real-time temperature detection within the range of 50–300 °C, exhibiting high sensitivity (20.6 μV K−1) and a strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.99). This work highlights the significant potential of gradient pore in enhancing CO sensing and offers a novel perspective for the design of ultrafast early fire-warning fiber sensors. Title: Cognitive appraisal of illegitimate tasks and research creativity: dual reflective processing pathways in graduate education
Abstract: Although graduate students frequently encounter illegitimate tasks—assignments perceived as inconsistent with their research roles—little is known about how such tasks influence research creativity and through what cognitive mechanisms. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), a dual-pathway model is proposed in which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity through problem-solving pondering and affective rumination, with supervisor–student relationship quality as a moderator. Data were collected from 389 graduate students in Chinese universities using a two-wave survey design, and the hypothesized moderated mediation model was tested using hierarchical regression analyses supplemented by the PROCESS macro. Illegitimate tasks were associated with increased affective rumination, which interfered with sustained creative engagement. However, under high-quality supervisor-student relationships, illegitimate tasks were more strongly related to problem-solving pondering, which facilitated creative thinking. Title: Exploring the role of green human resource management in enhancing employee well-being and job satisfaction in the it sector
Abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has received a growing academic interest with organizations starting to incorporate the sustainability of the environment into their strategic human resource management. The present paper offers a synthesis and systematic review of the existing body of literature to identify the impacts of GHRM practices on employee well being, job satisfaction as well as environmental performance, especially in the IT industry. A systematic literature review was conducted. The sources of records were Google Scholar (n = 317) and Scopus (n = 312), which returned 629 preliminary studies. After applying inclusion criteria based on peer-review, relevance and timeframe criteria, 156 articles were selected for detailed analysis. Literature was grouped based on the Ability-Motivation-Opportunity (AMO) framework to assess the performance of GHRM practices in the main HR functions. The results show that green training and development (80% implementation impact; 90% environmental impact) and reward management (85% implementation impact; 90% environmental impact) have the greatest correlation with the employee engagement and sustainability outcomes. The other contribution made towards the development of a psychological green climate and the encouragement of organizational citizenship behaviour towards the environment (OCBE) is recruitment, job design, and performance appraisal. Nevertheless, there are gaps of measurement structures and multi-level empirical validation of sectors. The research finds out that holistic integration of GHRM between HR functions boosts employee motivation, job satisfaction, and performance on organizational sustainability. Title: Applied economic reasoning in air transport management: A question- and concept-level analysis of an airport business course
Abstract: Economic reasoning underpins business decision-making. Yet how it is taught and assessed in air transport management education remains underexplored. Drawing on final-exam data from an Airport Business course for non-specialists at a Japanese university, this study identifies aspects of assessed economic reasoning that appeared relatively more demanding. At the question level, the higher-difficulty side concerned airport network financing, restructuring, and public support, whereas the lower-difficulty side addressed charge pass-through, the club-good characteristics of small-airport services, and concession-contract risks. At the concept level, government failure, incentives, and user-pays lay on the higher-difficulty side, while demand and costs, price discrimination, and public, private, and club goods fell on the lower-difficulty side. This concept-level pattern did not follow a simple foundational–advanced distinction, with positions varying across institutional contexts and concept co-occurrence. Title: Inner-supportive destinations for psychologically vulnerable solo travelers: A framework of narrative reconstruction and reintegrative stabilization
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: This study examines how inner-supportive destination experiences support psychological reconstruction among solo visitors reporting self-identified emotional disruption. Drawing on constructivist grounded theory and 30 in-depth interviews with domestic solo visitors to Da Lat, Vietnam, the research identifies a process through which pre-travel emotional disruption is gradually reorganized through destination experience. Findings show that participants did not travel merely for leisure or stress relief, but because burnout, grief, relational rupture, life transition, or identity uncertainty had unsettled their self-understanding. Inner-supportive affordances, including temporal deceleration, sensory softness, perceived safety, and supported solitude, reduced defensive pressure and created conditions for regulated emotional exposure. This exposure enabled narrative re-authoring, through which distressing experiences were reinterpreted and integrated into a more coherent self-understanding. Based on these accounts, the study proposes the inner-supportive destination framework, explaining how destination affordances, regulated emotional exposure, narrative re-authoring, participant-attributed reintegrative stabilization, and boundary conditions relate within a contingent process. Theoretically, the study extends destination marketing and management by distinguishing narrative reconstruction from restoration, healing, or emotional elevation. Practically, it offers guidance for designing vulnerability-sensitive destinations that support autonomy, low-pressure engagement, and safe solitude without making therapeutic claims. The findings invite broader applications of inner-supportive design across wellness, cultural, nature-based, and urban retreat contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From airplanes to classrooms: A cross-domain literature review of seating assignment models and methods
Abstract: Seating assignments play an important role in customer-focused managerial decisions, yet existing studies are frequently limited in scope to isolated application domains. Co-citation analysis reveals that research communities operate in separate networks despite addressing similar challenges using mathematical programming, heuristic approaches, stochastic simulation, and other operational research methods. Our cross-domain synthesis identifies technique transfer opportunities previously invisible due to research silos, such as applying restaurant group-seating strategies to airline passengers traveling together or entertainment venue considerations to dining table assignments. Authors: Wang Z.; Liu W.; Chen L.; Jin Z.; Sun J.
Title: From fabrication to function: Electrochemical characterization of hyaluronic acid-based biomimetic hydrogels in aqueous ethanol
Abstract: Oral flavor perception currently relies predominantly on human sensory evaluation, and artificial sensory systems capable of mimicking oral interfaces remain limited. While hydrogels have been explored as soft substrates, most are designed as passive matrices or signal transducers. Here, we move beyond conventional hydrogel sensors by reconstructing a chemically relevant oral mimetic interface using two indispensable and physiological components of the oral cavity: hyaluronic acid (HA) and mucin. Inspired by biology, we investigate a biomimetic hydrogel that combines human tongue–like properties with electrochemical responsiveness and apply it to aqueous ethanol systems. We demonstrate that this hydrogel functions not merely as a structural mimic but as a dynamic electrochemical interface. Comprehensive characterization of its structure, rheology, and biosafety confirms its suitability as a biomimetic material. Electrochemical analyses further demonstrate its capability to operate as a responsive interfacial in aqueous ethanol environments. The hydrogel exhibits solid-like viscoelastic behavior and good biocompatibility, providing a stable and secure soft interface for studies related to artificial sensory systems. Overall, this work establishes a biomimetic hydrogel for oral-inspired sensing and advances artificial sensory systems toward mechanisms rooted in interfacial biophysics rather than solely pattern-based recognition. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microwave effects on the flavor and storage quality of ‘Nongke Nuo 336’ sweet corn
Abstract: Microwave (MW) technology, characterized by its convenience and efficiency, has demonstrated significant effects on extending the shelf life of agricultural products. This study investigated the impact of MW on flavor compounds, gene expression, and metabolic processes in sweet corn. The results indicated that after 6 days of storage at room temperature, MW-treated corn maintained 12.22% soluble solids content, reduced weight loss by 9.71%, and slowed the rate of hardness increase by 41.55%. Simultaneously, it reduced the expression of genes such as α-amylase (ZmAMY1), thereby hindering the conversion of sugars into starch. MW treatment significantly downregulated the expression of key enzyme genes involved in abscisic acid biosynthesis (ZmZEP, ZmCHIL2, and ZmCFAT), delaying postharvest senescence in sweet corn. Furthermore, MW treatment upregulated the expression of antioxidant enzyme-related genes, including peroxidase (POD), among others, enhancing the stress resistance of sweet corn and thereby extending its shelf life. Metabolomics analysis further revealed that MW treatment activated the corn's defense system, leading to the accumulation of isoquercitrin, and hyperoside, which improved its stress resistance. Notably, esters, ketones, alcohols, aldehydes, and methylated compounds, which are the main flavor components, significantly enhanced the flavor characteristics of sweet corn. These findings provide valuable insights into the effects of MW on the storage quality and flavor of sweet corn. © 2026

Title: Integrating Business Impact Analysis, Scenario-Based FMEA, and Business Continuity Planning in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing: A Product-Level Case Study
Abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the product-level integration of Business Impact Analysis (BIA), scenario-based Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and Business Continuity Planning (BCP) for a selected finished medicinal product. Twenty-five de-identified scenarios, were assessed using predefined 1–4 scales for severity, frequency, and detectability; RPN was calculated as S × F × D. Results: IT and Technology had the shortest recovery requirement (MTD 48 h, RTO 24 h, WRT 24 h). Twelve scenarios were low risk and 13 were medium risk; none was high or critical. Material-transport interruption and adverse commercial and market conditions had the highest RPN of 16. Thirteen scenarios required additional controls. Sensitivity analysis showed that selected medium risks could move to high risk after a one-level score increase. Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as highly versatile interfacial materials in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), offering tunable molecular structures, favorable energy-level alignment, high optical transparency, and minimized non-radiative recombination losses. Subsequently, the fundamental aspects of SAMs are systematically discussed. Finally, the remaining challenges and future prospects of SAMs in inverted PSCs are discussed, with particular emphasis on interfacial stability and long-term operational reliability. Title: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
Abstract: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. Title: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COIN: CLICKBAIT’S INFLUENCE ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION IN SOCIAL MEDIA
Abstract: As social media increasingly operates within algorithm-driven attention economies, clickbait has become a pervasive engagement tactic. However, prior research has not fully explained the psychological mechanisms linking clickbait to downstream consumer behavior. Existing studies have also largely treated clickbait as an isolated persuasive cue, overlooking its dynamic interactions with other elements in social media ecosystems. When headline-induced motivations align with the gratifications delivered by the content, perceived intrusiveness and reactance are attenuated. Title: Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) in business and management education for developing AI and prompt literacy
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into organizational practice has created an urgent need for business and management education to move beyond tool exposure toward meaningful skill development. This study develops and implements a Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) approach that embeds GAI within active learning environments to support students' AI literacy and prompt literacy. A central feature of the approach is the use of structured scaffolds, particularly the RACE framework (Role–Action–Context–Explanation), which guides students in designing prompts, evaluating AI outputs, and linking responses to theoretical concepts. The approach was implemented in an undergraduate Organizational Behavior course (n = 93) using an explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative results indicate significant improvements in both AI literacy and prompt literacy, including gains in knowledge, application, and ethical awareness. Qualitative findings show that students engaged with AI iteratively and reflectively, using it as a “co-thinker” to refine prompts, assess output quality, and connect AI-generated insights with course theories. Cognitive and metacognitive engagement emerged as dominant, while collaborative and ethical dimensions, though less prominent, contributed to students’ developing awareness of responsible AI use. Title: Inflow modeling strategies designed to enhance the ecological sustainability of hydroelectric reservoir operation planning
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid global expansion of water infrastructure alters major rivers, causes severe biodiversity declines, and destabilizes aquatic ecosystems. Amid intensifying eco-hydrological pressures, accurate prediction of reservoir inflow remains imperative to safeguard downstream aquatic ecosystems, yet data-sparse tropical environments chronically impair the generalizability of deep learning architectures due to pronounced overfitting. The study objectives were to evaluate three statistical inflow modeling frameworks, representative of design-era hydrological understanding, against the observed 1998–2023 flow regime to identify the most reliable forecasting approach for supporting environmental-flow-informed reservoir operation planning under monsoonal variability. METHODS: Using a multi-decadal hydro-meteorological dataset from 1998 to 2023 ( n = 312 monthly time steps) at Karian Reservoir in Banten Province, Indonesia, three primary modeling approaches were tested: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average, Markov Chain, and Multiple Linear Regression. To rigorously assess model diagnostics and predictive performance across historical drought and wet regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient, Kling-Gupta efficiency, and operational trajectory metrics were integrated. FINDINGS: Deterministic multiple linear regression achieved the highest overall predictive accuracy with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.74, a Kling-Gupta efficiency of 0.64, and a superior operational trajectory guideline correlation of 0.85. The observed enhancement in model efficacy stems from the methodical integration of lagged streamflow predictors that effectively characterize catchment-scale moisture persistence. Conversely, the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model exhibited the weakest diagnostic capability (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.62; Kling-Gupta efficiency = 0.60) due to systematic overestimation of dry-season baseflows, risking artificial inflation of safe water availability. Meanwhile, the stochastic Markov yielded a commensurate aggregate Kling-Gupta efficiency score of 0.66 and exhibited a superior proficiency in replicating long-term probability distributions. CONCLUSION: While Multiple Linear Regression shows the strongest performance for monthly operational scheduling, the Markov Chain model offers a complementary probabilistic framework for screening extended seasonal drought risk. Independent out-of-sample validation against a held-out 2019-2023 period revealed substantial performance degradation for both models (Multiple Linear Regression Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.61 to 0.02; Markov Chain Nash-sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.28 to -1.01), directly evidencing non-stationary rainfall-inflow relationships. Ultimately, these results establish that the evaluated models serve as an initial decision-support tool for raw water allocation planning, though their sustained operational reliability necessitates systematic recalibration. Title: Waiting for Uganda’s first commercial ‘Pearl Sweet’ oil: Discourses on social and environmental impacts and safeguards
Abstract: Uganda discovered approximately 3.5 billion barrels of commercially recoverable oil reserves in 2006 and is poised to become a major oil producer in Sub-Saharan Africa. In assessing progress towards full–scale oil production, expected by the end of 2026, Uganda’s President referred to the country’s commercial crude oil as “pearl sweet”, highlighting its medium-to-heavy, highly waxy characteristics, relatively low sulphur content, and ease of refining. Despite the anticipated economic benefits, considerable debate persists regarding the potential social and environmental impacts of oil development and the adequacy of safeguards ahead of full–scale production. Drawing on experiences from established oil–producing countries, this paper examines how environmental and social impacts are framed, how safeguards are prioritised, and what this implies for Uganda’s emerging oil sector. Anchored in environmental justice and political ecology, the study adopts a sequential integrative design combining a systematic literature review with empirical insights from twelve purposively selected stakeholders in Uganda’s oil-producing districts and national regulatory institutions. The literature review used Boolean search strings that connected terms within conceptual blocks using OR and combined blocks using AND, following a PRISMA-guided process across Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar and institutional data bases. Of 1800 records identified, 95 key sources were retained for analysis. The findings indicate that, although Uganda has initiated several safeguards measures including oil–spill preparedness training, buffer zone enforcement, afforestation, and resettlement programs – implementation remain fragmented, under–resourced, and heavily centralised. Comparative analysis further indicates limited integration of international climate frameworks, including the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement, into national oil governance. We argue that Uganda’s challenge is not simply the absence of safeguards, but the persistence of centralised, uneven, and under–resourced governance arrangements that constrain the translation of international safeguard commitments into effective national practice. This study contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while also intersecting with SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Unpacking the pathways from green intellectual capital to green recovery performance: The power of employee voice and intrinsic motivation
Abstract: Our paper proposes and tests a moderated mediation model that examines how green intellectual capital relates to green recovery performance, highlighting green promotive and prohibitive voice behaviors as mediators and intrinsic motivation to share knowledge as a moderator. Results based on time-lagged data gathered from FLEs in environmentally certified Spanish hotels revealed that the association between green intellectual capital and green recovery performance operated through green voice behaviors. Both green promotive and green prohibitive voice behaviors mediated the green intellectual capital-green recovery performance link. However, intrinsic motivation to share knowledge strengthened only the promotive pathway. This finding underscores an asymmetry in how motivational states condition the translation of intangible resources into recovery behaviors. Title: Charging station planning strategy considering imbalanced distribution of response propensity
Abstract: With the advancement of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, Electric Vehicle (EV) participation in grid scheduling has become a growing trend. This paper addresses the heterogeneous response propensity of EVs under different operating states by proposing a charging station planning strategy that accounts for the imbalanced distribution of planning-relevant EV response characteristics. Firstly, an improved synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) based on driving routes is introduced to tackle the data imbalance among EVs with different states of charge (SOC). By generating synthetic samples, this method enhances the accuracy of charging station planning under imbalanced data conditions. Next, an improved Mean Shift algorithm is proposed for charging station siting, which considers differences in the planning-level response propensity of EVs under different SOC states, thereby reducing the distance required for EVs to respond to grid scheduling. Finally, a capacity configuration strategy is designed to optimize charging station capacity by comprehensively considering the charging and discharging demands of EVs in the area and their response characteristics. Validation using real data from Chicago demonstrates that the proposed strategy effectively reduces EV response distance in scheduling, achieving an 8.3% reduction in response distance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Psychological safety as a driver of student learning outcomes in team-based learning environments: The mediating role of teamwork quality
Abstract: With the rise of constructivist approaches, team-based learning (TBL) has gained popularity as an instructional design in the field of management education. The extant research indicates that the positive effects of TBL on student learning outcomes, which many studies report, might depend on individual as well as social-contextual drivers. In this paper, we introduce psychological safety and the quality of teamwork processes as two important social-contextual drivers of student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Based on research on team processes and TBL, we argue that psychological safety fosters student learning outcomes because of its positive effect on intrinsic motivation and group interaction. We further hypothesize that the relationship between psychological safety and student learning outcomes is mediated by the quality of teamwork processes within the student teams. A field study based on a computerized business simulation involving 169 undergraduate management students, nested within 44 teams, at a German university supports our hypotheses. We contribute to research on constructivist learning and TBL by introducing psychological safety as an important driver and the quality of teamwork processes as a mediating mechanism for student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Our study also has practical implications for the design, support, and facilitation of psychologically safe team-based learning environments. © 2026

Title: The power of gastronomic cultural capital: How local food culture shapes residents' recommendation intention
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: While destinations increasingly leverage cultural capital for competitiveness, research predominantly focuses on top-down promotions of monument-centered heritage, neglecting the distinct social logic of gastronomic culture. Grounded in cultural capital theory, this study aims to examine how Hong Kong's tea restaurants food culture translates into residents' recommendation intentions toward culturally diverse individuals. It untangles the core inquiries: how everyday food culture fosters attachment; how this attachment subsequently shapes cultural identity and confidence; and how nostalgia and knowledge moderate these psychological pathways. Additionally, it identifies which specific tea restaurant's food culture dimensions serve as the primary drivers. Utilizing an empirical sample of 615 Hong Kong residents, this research adopts a PLS–SEM–ANN approach. The PLS–SEM analysis confirms that cultural identity and confidence act as pivotal mediators, while the complementary ANN analysis reveals that gastronomic identity, exceeding mere sensory flavour, is the predominant driving dimension. Empirically, nostalgia amplifies the culture–attachment link, and knowledge strengthens the attachment–confidence relationship. These findings advocate for a paradigm shift in destination marketing: beyond institutional campaigns, mobilizing residents as active cultural transmitters is crucial for gastronomic tourism, establishing a scalable mechanism for everyday cultural capital transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Rational Design of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Oxygen Electrocatalysis: Recent Advances and Mechanistic Insights
Abstract: Due to the excessive consumption of fossil fuels and the increasingly severe global environment, the world urgently needs to develop new clean and renewable energy sources. However, these energy sources have intermittency and instability, so it is necessary to vigorously develop efficient and large-scale energy conversion and storage technologies such as fuel cells, water electrolyzers, and metal–air batteries based on the core reactions of oxygen evolution reaction and oxygen reduction reaction. Because of their excellent molecular designability and structural tunability, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) show great potential for applications in this field. In this review, we first classify COF-based electrocatalysts based on the nature of active sites. Subsequently, strategies including structural design and functional synthesis for improving performance of COF-based electrocatalysts in the field of oxygen catalysis are systematically reviewed. Importantly, mechanism discussion of the performance improvement is highlighted. Finally, we put forward prospects for the future research directions, challenges, and development opportunities in this field. Title: When service environments signal ideology: Customer responses to ideological cues
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Service environments increasingly contain visible cues that communicate political engagement, religious identities, LGBTQ + affiliation, environmental advocacy, and other collective values. Although servicescape research has traditionally emphasized atmospheric, aesthetic, and functional cues, less is known about how customers interpret ideological cues embedded within routine service encounters. Drawing on servicescape research and social identity theory, this research examines how ideological servicescape cues are associated with customer discomfort, avoidance intentions, and stated store-choice decisions. Three preregistered, scenario-based experiments in a coffee shop context examine ideological cues displayed through employees and the physical service environment. Study 1 shows that political cues generate greater discomfort than environmental and lifestyle cues, although they do not differ significantly from religious or LGBTQ + cues. Study 2 shows that matching political cues displayed across employee and environmental touchpoints generate greater discomfort than political cues displayed through a single source, while perceived authenticity does not account for this association. Study 3 shows that political cues are associated with lower stated store choice than environmental cues, particularly when matching political cues appear across employee and environmental touchpoints. Across studies, customer discomfort statistically accounts for part of the association between ideological cue conditions and avoidance intentions or stated store-choice decisions. The findings extend servicescape scholarship by showing that politically charged symbolism may shape customer responses through both cue content and cue-source configuration. Because the studies rely on scenario-based experiments and stated responses, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of observed marketplace behavior or realized financial outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine
Abstract: In this study, an experimental and machine learning-assisted investigation was conducted on a modified single-cylinder direct-injection Compression Ignition (CI) engine operating in acetylene dual-fuel mode using copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticle-enhanced waste plastic oil (WPO) blends. The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Experimental investigations were performed using WPO10 and WPO20 blends containing 50 and 100 ppm CuO nanoparticles under acetylene flow rates of 5 and 10 LPM. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. Title: The power of morality: The effect of moral appeals on tourists’ attitudes in rural tourism destinations
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Rural tourism has become an important tool for rural-revitalization and poverty alleviation, which has been increasingly framed as a moral narrative in public discourse. However, destination marketing often prioritizes utilitarian attributes while overlooking the role of moral appeals. Drawing on affective events theory, this study employs two experiments to examine the effects of moral appeals on tourists' attitudes, the underlying mechanism, and boundary conditions. The findings reveal that moral appeals significantly enhance tourists' visit intention and perceived value of rural destinations, with anticipated guilt mediating this relationship. Notably, these effects are more pronounced in low-quality destinations than in high-quality ones. Specifically, in rural destinations with low quality, high-intensity moral appeals are more effective than low-intensity ones in enhancing tourists’ visit intention and perceived value. Title: From LinkedIn to labor statistics: Using Revelio microdata for labor market research in developing economies
Abstract: We explore the use of Revelio data—obtained primarily from LinkedIn profiles—as a source of labor force microdata in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where large-sample, high-frequency, employer-linked alternatives are largely unavailable. To address the selection inherent to LinkedIn usership, we employ ILO labor statistics to construct five sets of country-year-specific weights that alleviate non-representativeness across occupation, industry, occupation × education, industry × education, and industry × firm-size cells. We further validate these weights using national census data where they are available and not used for ILO labor statistics. The weighted dataset provides a balanced monthly panel with coverage across most LMICs. We also discuss remaining limitations of the dataset, including within-cell selection and self-reporting errors, and suggest techniques to alleviate them. Despite imperfect coverage, Revelio offers improved temporal and geographical resolution as well as cross-country comparability and is especially useful for studying the role of firms in economic development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation for single-phase-to-ground fault type identification in distribution networks
Abstract: Single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults are the most frequent fault type in medium-voltage small-current grounding distribution networks. Due to arc suppression coil compensation and nonlinear grounding behaviors, fault currents are weak and highly nonstationary, making accurate fault type identification challenging under complex operating conditions. This paper proposes a physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation framework based on the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) for SPG fault type identification. A typical 10 kV distribution network model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate multi-scenario fault samples. HHT is applied to construct complementary dual-modal features, including time–frequency energy maps and instantaneous temporal evolution sequences. A parallel Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture is developed to model spectral–spatial patterns and temporal dependencies, while channel and temporal attention mechanisms are introduced for adaptive feature enhancement. Results show that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 99.2% across five fault types. Under additive white Gaussian noise with signal-to-noise ratios down to 5 dB, the accuracy remains above 93.6%. These simulation-based results indicate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance within the modeled PSCAD/EMTDC scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge of the Arhuaco People on Water Management in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
Abstract: This article analyzes the role of Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) of the Arhuaco people in water management in the upper Ariguaní river basin, in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (Colombia), in a context of accelerated socio-environmental transformation. From an ethnohydrological approach, the study adopts a mixed-methods design that integrates community surveys, participatory techniques, spatial analysis of land use change (2000–2023), and dynamic socio-hydrological modeling. The results show that traditional water knowledge is mainly based on ritual practices and indigenous norms guided by indigenous spiritual authorities, while coordination with state institutional frameworks is limited. Spatial analysis shows a loss of forest cover and expansion of agricultural uses around the sacred sites that sustain TEK. Modeling indicates that, although indigenous norms slow the deterioration of the system, only co-governance scenarios can cushion pressures and avoid trajectories of collapse. Taken together, the findings show that the effectiveness of TEK depends on its articulation with multiscale governance arrangements. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Bridging the implementation gap in MCABC inventory management: from a taxonomy to practical archetypes
Abstract: Despite increasing demands for resilient and sustainable supply chains, inventory management often relies on outdated single-criterion analyses. While multi-criteria ABC (MCABC) analyses provide a theoretically mature assessment of resilience-sustainability-benefit trade-offs in inventory, their adoption remains limited due to fragmented methodologies, lack of standardization, and unclear design guidance. This study addresses this gap by developing a taxonomy of eight dimensions and 25 characteristics to structure the MCABC analysis design space. Using a dataset of 108 configurations, cluster analysis identifies six recurring archetypes that serve as implementation-ready templates for inventory analysis. Archetype 2: artificial intelligence (AI)+-driven cluster minimalist enables rapid, cost-focused inventory structuring with minimal data and no expert input. In contrast, Archetype 1: AI+-driven complex ranker uses expert-weighted multi-criteria analysis to support holistic and sustainability oriented inventory strategies. The taxonomy and archetypes provide a unified framework for researchers to theorize inventory design trade-offs and for practitioners to apply scalable blueprints for mature inventory analyses. © 2025 The Author(s). Title: Decoding entrepreneurial intention: A systematic review, theoretical framework synthesis, and research trajectories
Abstract: Entrepreneurial intention (EI) is a critical psychological construct for understanding the precursors of entrepreneurial behavior. Despite a surge in empirical research over the past decade, the literature on EI remains fragmented across theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and contextual applications. This study systematically reviews 53 peer-reviewed articles on entrepreneurial intention published between 2018 and 2025 to synthesize theoretical frameworks, methodological patterns, key findings, and future research directions. Guided by the PRISMA approach, the review reveals the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as the predominant model, frequently integrated with constructs from Social Cognitive Theory, Technology Acceptance Model, and moral or contextual frameworks. Quantitative cross-sectional designs dominate the methodological landscape, often involving university student samples and the use of structural equation modelling techniques for hypothesis testing. Findings consistently confirm the central role of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and self-efficacy in predicting EI, while more recent studies highlight the growing significance of emotional intelligence, cultural influences, institutional support, and entrepreneurship education. However, the review identifies key limitations, including the overreliance on student-based samples, a lack of longitudinal and experimental designs, and limited generalizability to actual entrepreneurial behavior in real-world settings. Additionally, contextual diversity across emerging and developed economies remains underexplored. In response, the study proposes five future research trajectories: theoretical expansion beyond dominant models, increased adoption of behavioral and longitudinal approaches, broader contextual and demographic inclusion, pedagogical innovation in entrepreneurship education, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration. By mapping evolving trends and gaps in EI research, this review provides a foundation for more dynamic, inclusive, and practically relevant scholarship in entrepreneurship studies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Survival analysis of U.S. regional airline routes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
Abstract: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, U.S. regional airlines have faced substantial operational challenges, including reduced flight activity, fleet restructuring, rising labor costs, and persistent pilot shortage. Between 2019 and 2024, domestic departures by regional airlines declined by nearly 24% from 3.81 million to 2.92 million, while passenger enplanements fell by 19% from 165.2 million to 133.7 million. Mainline carriers temporarily increased their reliance on regional partners during the pandemic but subsequently reduced regional operations during the post-pandemic recovery. Against this backdrop, we examine the determinants of route survival in U.S. regional airline markets during and after the pandemic. Using airline-route panel data for 2017–2024, we estimate Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying route-performance covariates. The results show that routes operated by independent regional airlines face significantly higher discontinuation hazards than those operated by wholly-owned subsidiaries of mainline carriers. Routes serving large hub airports exhibit higher survival probabilities, underscoring the importance of network connectivity beyond local market size. Support through the U.S. Essential Air Service (EAS) program is also associated with greater route survival, while larger aircraft are linked to improved route persistence, consistent with post-pandemic upgauging and capacity consolidation. The analysis also accounts for market demand conditions and operational characteristics, including population, per capita income, unit cost, stage length, and aircraft size. This study extends the literature by examining how ownership structure, network position, route performance, and EAS support jointly relate to regional route survival following the COVID-19 pandemic. Title: HAD-TAM: Health insurance anomaly detection via truncated affinity maximization with degree-normalized scoring
Abstract: Substantial financial losses are incurred annually as a result of medical insurance fraud, driven by subtle behaviors such as false diagnoses and over-prescription. Although heterogeneous graph structures can be exploited by existing graph neural network-based methods, they often rely on manually selected meta-paths, and the identification of structural anomalies remains a persistent challenge. To address these challenges, Health insurance Anomaly Detection via Truncated Affinity Maximization (HAD-TAM) is proposed as a health insurance fraud detection method, wherein degree-normalized anomaly score-guided meta-path selection is first combined with dual-threshold edge pruning to capture structural anomalies. First, the meta-graph with the highest degree-normalized anomaly score is selected by the model to highlight structures potentially indicative of fraud. Second, non-homophily edges are iteratively pruned by the model using both global and local thresholds to suppress noise and preserve meaningful structure. Finally, the neighborhood affinity of normal nodes is maximized by the model to better separate them from anomalies and improve fraud detection accuracy. Experimental results show that HAD-TAM outperforms eleven advanced baseline methods on two real-world medical insurance datasets, achieving a 2.41% improvement in AUROC and a 1.06% improvement in AUPRC. Furthermore, it exhibits good generalization to public datasets such as Amazon and Reddit. © 2026

Title: Municipal utilities and SDG adoption: Evidence from Austria and Germany
Abstract: This paper explores how municipal utilities (MUs) in Austria and Germany adopt and integrate the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into their strategies, strategic projects and management controls (MCs). MUs have a long tradition of delivering public infrastructure services, such as energy, water, and public transport, in the two focus countries. As important municipal enterprises, MUs must position themselves on a continuum between their public mission and their business orientation, and therefore act in a financially sustainable manner. Taking SDG adoption seriously is in line with the public mission orientation. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the study investigates whether MUs engage with the SDGs symbolically or substantively. The research is based on nineteen semi-structured interviews conducted with representatives from sixteen MUs, allowing for an in-depth qualitative analysis of strategic alignment, project implementation, and related MCs. The findings reveal considerable variation in SDG integration, showing that most MUs are still in an early, emerging stage of adoption, which is still at a symbolic level. By providing empirical insights from two countries with long-standing traditions of municipal service provision by local government-owned public utilities, the study contributes to the limited literature on SDG adoption in municipal enterprises and enhances understanding of the legitimacy dynamics shaping SDG practices in local state-owned entities. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Enhancing repeat patronage in beauty clinics: An integrated model of trust and consumer perceptions
Abstract: This study aims to explain how trust drives repeat patronage in the beauty clinic industry by examining the roles of service quality, price fairness, and influencer credibility. A quantitative explanatory approach was applied using survey data from 360 beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS to test direct and indirect relationships among variables. The results show that perceived service quality, perceived price fairness, and influencer credibility each have positive and significant direct effects on both repurchase intention and brand trust, and that brand trust itself significantly and positively drives repurchase intention. Brand trust also partially mediates the effects of all three antecedents on repurchase intention, indicating that consumers' evaluations of service, price, and influencers shape repeat patronage both directly and through the trust these evaluations help to build. These findings suggest that improving service quality, price fairness perception, and influencer credibility can enhance consumer trust in a brand, which ultimately increases repurchase intention in beauty clinic services. This study is limited to beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. Beauty clinic managers should focus on trust-building strategies through consistent service quality, transparent pricing, and collaboration with credible social media influencers to foster long-term consumer relationships. This study provides an integrated model that empirically demonstrates the mediating role of brand trust in the beauty clinic industry. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Banks and informality: Two perspectives of microenterprises’ balance sheets
Abstract: Our paper studies how the nationwide expansion of bank branches affects the performance of informal microenterprises. We exploit the Branch Authorization Policy (BAP) in India, which directed banks to open branches in “underbanked” districts. Using a regression discontinuity design, we find that microenterprises in underbanked districts report higher value-addition, revenues, and productive assets, but no increase in local registration. However, borrowings on the enterprise balance sheet do not increase. The household balance sheet offers a second perspective that reconciles these findings: households in underbanked districts increased their bank borrowings for non-farm business by an amount comparable to the increase in microenterprise productive assets. Micro-entrepreneurs thus accessed bank credit as households rather than as enterprises, weakening a key incentive to formalize and helping explain how expanded access to finance can coexist with persistent informality. © 2026

Title: Improving spectral reproducibility in SERS analysis of exosomes via surface charge-modulated and biofunctionalized gold nanoparticles
Abstract: This study introduces an improved SERS platform for analyzing exosome heterogeneity. We compared three gold nanoparticle substrates: negatively charged citrate-Au NPs (cit-Au NPs), positively charged cysteamine-Au NPs (cyst-Au NPs), and anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs. Conventional cit-/cyst-Au NPs yielded fluctuating SERS signals due to random exosome localization, limiting accurate heterogeneity assessment. In contrast, anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs specifically anchored exosomes via CD63 targeting, producing highly reproducible spectra. Principal component analysis (PCA) confirmed significantly reduced spectral variance with the antibody-based approach, with 95% confidence ellipses showing substantially tighter clustering compared to charge-based substrates. Theoretical simulations and sensitivity tests further showed the cyst-Au NPs strategy achieved a detection limit of approximately 1.3 × 103 particles/μL, while cit-Au NPs and anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs exhibited LODs of 7.9 × 103 and 8.1 × 104 particles/μL, respectively. Notably, the PCA plot for the biofunctionalized strategy revealed two distinguishable circles, potentially indicating the presence of exosome subpopulations or distinct CD63 epitope distributions. By integrating surface charge control with biofunctionalization, this work enables reproducible, sensitive SERS detection, offering a reliable platform for exosome heterogeneity analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Determination of discount rates in business valuation and public project evaluation: A systematic review from the perspective of international finance and financial theory
Abstract: The discount rate plays a central role in business valuation and public project appraisal because it links risk to the valuation of future cash flows and guides the efficient allocation of resources. However, the global literature lacks methodological consensus and shows significant divergences between private and social approaches, as well as between developed and emerging economies. The present study aims to synthesize the main theoretical and empirical approaches used to determine discount rates from the perspective of international finance. A systematic literature review was conducted following the prisma protocol. Searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, sciencedirect, ssrn, and jstor, using boolean search strings related to “discount rate”, “wacc”, “capm”, “social discount rate”, and “country risk premium”. Studies published from 2000 to 2025, in english and spanish, were included. Only studies with a clear methodological foundation in finance and economics were considered. The analysis was carried out through a qualitative thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature indicates the predominance of the wacc and asset pricing models as the primary references for estimating private discount rates, and reports the increasing use of multifactor models and country risk premiums in the international context. For public projects, the literature identifies two main approaches: the social rate of time preference and the social opportunity cost of capital. The studies also suggest substantial heterogeneity across countries, with generally higher discount rates in emerging economies. No single discount rate is universally applicable; instead, its estimation depends on the local institutional context, the objectives of the investment, and the nature of the risks being evaluated. These findings should be interpreted in light of the qualitative nature of the synthesis. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Targeted Modulation of Zn Deposition Behavior toward High-Performance Stable Zn Anodes
Abstract: Dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions at the Zn metal anode remain critical obstacles to the commercialization of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Zn anode design regulates Zn deposition behavior from its thermodynamic and kinetic roots and is therefore recognized as a pivotal strategy to address the above bottlenecks. However, Zn deposition evolves through a complex multistage nucleation-growth process, and the structure–property relationship between the anode designs and practical Zn deposition behavior remains to be elucidated. This review focuses on Zn deposition substrate and functional interphase engineering, systematically elucidates the microscopic mechanisms and key regulatory targets of Zn deposition at each stage, and establishes a multidimensional regulation framework covering atomic tuning, interfacial modification, and spatial confinement. Based on this framework, we summarize three core design strategies, namely zincophilic regulation, lattice-matched effects, and three-dimensional structural engineering, and provide in-depth elucidation of the working mechanism and structure-property relationship of each strategy. By correlating these fundamental principles with the latest research advances in the field, we highlight the paradigm shift from empirical trial and error to rational material design. Finally, we outline the prevailing challenges and future research directions for Zn anode design, aiming to provide actionable insights for the development of advanced dendrite-free Zn anodes toward high-performance AZIBs. Title: Optimal carbon quota allocation for power system decarbonization: a two-stage peer-to-peer market framework
Abstract: Amid the global pursuit of deep decarbonization, effectively harnessing demand-side resources has emerged as a crucial strategy, particularly as end-user consumption is a primary driver of carbon emissions. However, existing demand-side carbon policies often impose a significant financial burden on consumers and struggle to utilize carbon quota resources to achieve effective emission reductions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel two-stage framework for carbon quota allocation to advance the decarbonization of power systems. The first stage introduces an allocation strategy that accounts for the heterogeneous low-carbon potential among different consumers, thereby regulating the supply-demand dynamics of the secondary carbon market. The second stage establishes a peer-to-peer carbon market based on a double-auction mechanism to support efficient and transparent rule-based trading. Within this market, an optimal bidding model is formulated to capture the strategic interactions among participants. To solve this complex optimization problem, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is developed, which incorporates a centralized reward mechanism to improve computational tractability. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework. © 2026

Title: From search results to generative answers: A mixed-methods study of credibility assessment and trust formation in AI Overviews
Abstract: Generative search shifts information evaluation from comparing ranked documents to assessing synthesised answers. This study examines how users’ perceptions of answer quality are associated with trust and credibility in Google AI Overviews and explores whether visible interface cues may foster trust without systematic source verification. Study 1 analysed survey data from 510 Spanish users using a consistent partial least squares structural equation modelling approach. Study 2 combined eye tracking and interviews with 20 Spanish users. The model explained 75.7% of the variance in trust and 91.0% of the variance in credibility. Clarity and context (β = .419, p < .001) and access to additional information and supporting sources (β = .335, p = .002) showed the strongest observed associations with trust, whereas response immediacy was not significant (β = .008, p = .874). Trust (β = .834) and perceived usefulness (β = .229) were positively associated with credibility (both p < .001), which, in turn, was associated with recommendation following (β = .877) and intention to use (β = .553; both p < .001). Eye tracking recorded no analysable fixations on the AI-error warning, while the interviews indicated that participants in this subsample did not routinely verify the displayed sources and often interpreted visible references as indicators of reliability. Taken together, Study 1 identifies associations between perceived answer-quality cues, trust, and credibility, whereas Study 2 suggests that visual prominence and visible references appeared to operate as authority cues for some participants and may encourage reliance without active source verification. © 2026 The Authors. Title: AI guest personalization as driver of hotel performance and hotel guest behavior: A dual-model analysis
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven personalization is reshaping hotel operations, yet evidence on its financial effects and guest acceptance mechanisms remains limited. This study adopts a dual-perspective design combining hotel-level performance modeling with guest-level behavioral analysis. Study 1 examines revenue dynamics using Interrupted Time Series (ITS), SARIMA forecasting, and TOPSIS, comparing AI-driven and non-AI-driven hotels based on publicly documented implementations of AI personalization. Findings indicate heterogeneous short-term responses but more consistent differences in long-term revenue stability and predictability. Study 2 develops a Diffusion of Innovation–based structural model extended with trust in AI as a mediator, using survey data from 1396 hotel guests. Relative advantage and compatibility increase trust and adoption intention, whereas complexity reduces them; trust partially mediates these effects. Title: Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods for stiff differential equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods (TASE-TSRK) for solving stiff ordinary differential equations, inspired by the technique presented in Calvo et al. [1]. The objective of the methods is to improve the stability characteristics of explicit TSRK methods by pre-multiplying the vector field with a suitable TASE operator. In this work, the related order conditions are analyzed, and then a complete study of stability properties is carried out for TASE-TSRK methods with order k ≤ 4. By appropriately selecting the free parameters of the TASE operator family, we demonstrate that the 2nd-order method is strongly A-stable, the 3rd-order and 4th-order methods can be nearly strongly A-stable. Some numerical experiments are performed to show that the new TASE-TSRK schemes are competitive with TSRK methods and potentially more advantageous for stiff problems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Real-World Cost of a Bundle Payment Strategy for Thyroid Oncological 90 Days Treatment: A Time-Driven Activity-Based Cost Analysis
Abstract: Objectives Continuous increases in the incidence of thyroid cancer emphasize the requirement for effective management policies. This study estimated the cost of a bundle reimbursement strategy for thyroid oncological treatment and compared it with a real-world cohort of patients. Methods This retrospective single-center microcosting study was conducted in 2 steps: (i) thyroid oncological surgery bundle design and (ii) real-world cost variability between the estimated bundle and a cohort of patients. The bundle was designed based on clinical guidelines and the center’s thyroid oncological surgical experience, represented by clinical registry data on 8381 cases. Time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) was applied to estimate the bundle’s cost, using data from a real-world cohort of 29 patients. The estimated and measured cost data were compared descriptively, and cost variability was analyzed using linear multiple regression. Results The thyroid cancer bundle covered care from preparation for surgery through postsurgical monitoring, including standard medications, exams, and involvement of health professionals. The estimated cost for the thyroid bundle was R$20,288 (US$3757), with the surgery accounting for 90% of the costs. The mean bundle cost based on the real-world cohort of patients was R$19,448 (SD 6690), with 33% of costs justified on hospital facilities. Patient’ age and length of hospital stay were identified as cost drivers. Conclusion This study is unique in evaluating the economic impact of adopting a bundle reimbursement strategy for one thyroid cancer treatment. Applying TDABC demonstrated the value of accurate costing for evaluating pricing and increasing the chances of achieving sustainability through an innovative care and payment strategy. © 2026 The Authors.
