Title: IMPORTANCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS IN CAMPUS MANAGEMENT
Source title: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
Abstract: Campus managers need to balance the competing claims of different stakeholders of higher education institutions (HEIs). Previous studies in general management have indicated that the decision-making processes are highly related to stakeholders’ attributes (power, legitimacy and urgency). However, such studies have not yet been conducted in the field of campus management. Therefore, this paper aims to identify the importance of key stakeholders in campus development and relevant key performance indicators (KPIs) that are essential for decisionmakers in determining and explaining how their efforts are progressing towards achieving various stakeholders’ goals. To explore the underlying importance of campus stakeholders, a theory on stakeholder salience and a questionnaire survey among Polish public HEIs were employed. In turn, to identify various KPIs, the content analysis of institutions’ strategies was conducted. Empirical research suggests that in Polish public HEIs, authorities and academic staff continue to be regarded as the most important stakeholders (at different stages of the building’s life cycle, respectively). This contrasts with the growing market-oriented approach seen in higher education globally. Title: Why travelers prefer humans over artificial intelligence (AI): Developing and testing an AI aversion model in tourism
Abstract: As tourism businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance traveler decision-making, a persistent reluctance to rely on AI-generated recommendations has emerged as a critical barrier. This research addresses this gap by developing and validating an AI aversion model that identifies the factors driving traveler resistance to AI-generated recommendations. Using a mixed-methods approach, this research uncovered five core drivers rooted in the perceived absence of human nature attributes: lived experience, emotional engagement, contextual understanding, domain specific knowledge, and proactive engagement in communication. Twenty-three items were developed and validated in a multicultural context. Additionally, we revealed that individual differences (i.e., rational vs. emotional personalities) play a moderating role, which can offer a way to mitigate the negative impacts of AI. Title: Developing instrument to measure the glass ceiling phenomenon among female academics in Indonesia
Abstract: The persistence of the glass ceiling phenomenon in academia indicates the necessity of developing a contextually valid and reliable measurement instrument, particularly within Indonesian higher education institutions. Instruments developed in different cultural settings are often unable to fully capture the structural and sociocultural dynamics influencing female academics' career advancement in Indonesia. This study aims to develop and validate a comprehensive measurement instrument that reflects these contextual specificities and improves measurement accuracy in assessing career advancement barriers. A quantitative research design was employed using a survey approach. Instrument development was conducted through the integration of two established questionnaires originating from India and Europe, followed by contextual adaptation. Data were collected from female lecturers employed at Catholic universities in Indonesia. The two preliminary questionnaires were administered to the same initial group of female academics. For the final validation, the integrated instrument was administered to the initial respondents together with additional participants, resulting in a larger validation sample. The measurement model was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with SmartPLS. Reliability and validity were assessed through composite reliability, Cronbach's alpha, average variance extracted, and discriminant validity criteria. The findings indicate that the newly developed instrument demonstrates strong reliability and validity across all dimensions, with acceptable thresholds achieved for composite reliability and convergent validity. Compared to the adapted international instruments, the final instrument exhibits higher cultural relevance and improved measurement precision. Several dimensions were more accurately captured, particularly those related to organizational culture, informal networks, and discriminatory promotion practices, indicating a stronger alignment with the Indonesian academic environment. The study contributes to the refinement of measurement approaches in gender-related research by providing a robust and context-sensitive instrument. The instrument is expected to support future empirical studies and institutional policy evaluations aimed at reducing gender disparities in academic career advancement and leadership positions in Indonesia, while also enabling more accurate diagnosis of structural and cultural barriers. Title: Breaking the cycle of malice: Influence mechanism and intervention of social exclusion on malevolent creativity in adolescents
Abstract: Creativity is the core driving force for humans to break through existing boundaries and promote continuous social progress, and its positive impacts have been widely recognized. However, creativity also has a dark side, namely, malevolent creativity, which poses significant potential harm to society. Therefore, it is necessary and meaningful to conduct research on malevolent creativity to prevent its negative impacts. Based on the 4P model of creativity, this study explored the impact mechanism between social exclusion and malevolent creativity (Study 1) and the effectiveness of a group counseling intervention for self-concept clarity (Study 2). Study 1 conducted a field questionnaire survey (N = 1567). The results showed that social exclusion not only directly increased malevolent creativity, but also indirectly predicted it through the independent mediating effects of reduced self-concept clarity and heightened negative emotions, as well as through the serial mediating effect whereby reduced self-concept clarity led to increased negative emotions, which in turn predicted malevolent creativity. Trait mindfulness moderated the impact of social exclusion on self-concept clarity, with higher levels of trait mindfulness alleviating the negative effects of social exclusion on self-concept clarity. Study 2 utilized a group counseling intervention (N = 30) and demonstrated that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in self-concept clarity and a significant decrease in malevolent creativity after the intervention. The study's conclusions provide educators with references and insights for correctly understanding the impact of social exclusion and for offering interventions to enhance self-concept clarity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Enhanced Antibiotics Sieving by Exfoliated TiS2 Membranes via Surface Functionalization and Passivation
Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanolaminate membranes hold great promise for molecular sieving due to their two-dimensional capillary structures, which facilitate size-restricted diffusion. However, many transition metal sulfides exhibit intrinsic instability and are highly susceptible to oxidation, which severely limits their durability under reverse osmosis operating conditions. In this work, we introduce a stable 1T phase titanium disulfide (TiS2) constructing nanolaminate membranes from Group IVB, enabling the formation of tunable capillary channels and achieving a permeance up to 46.8 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Experiments confirm that water-initiated hydrolysis, rather than direct oxidation by molecular O2, dominates the degradation of TiS2, while alkyl-chain hydrophobic barriers effectively suppress this water-triggered degradation. The enhanced surface hydrophobic properties simultaneously improve antioxidation stability and ensure sustained performance over 30 filtration cycles and 15 days of continuous operation. Functionalized membranes further reached 96.9% rejection for diverse antibiotics, such as sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and rifampicin. This work opens new avenues for exploring emerging TMD materials in the efficient and reliable removal of trace antibiotics from water, contributing to safer water resources and promoting sustainable ecological practices. Authors: Xie L.; Bian Y.; Jin P.
Title: A novel hierarchical optimal control strategy for hybrid energy storage considering smoothing wind power fluctuations and compensating prediction errors
Abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power, its inherent intermittency and prediction errors pose significant challenges to the stable operation of power systems. To fully leverage the rapid dynamic response of supercapacitors and the high energy density of lithium-ion batteries, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical optimal control strategy for a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to smooth wind power fluctuations and compensate prediction errors. The upper layer model introduces the concept of virtual energy storage (VES) and proposes a novel power extraction strategy based on model predictive control to obtain the total VES power, which is considered as the HESS power. The middle layer model establishes a novel power optimal allocation strategy based on the improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise and the grey relational analysis. The strategy realizes the decomposition, reconstruction and correction of li-ion battery (LB) and supercapacitor (SC) power. It avoids the problem of LB and SC power in the opposite direction at the same moment. The lower layer model builds a multi-objective optimal configuration model considering the life loss of HESS, which is solved by the improved multi-objective slime mould algorithm based on generalized opposition-based learning. Finally, some indicators are proposed to assess the effects of smoothing and compensation, simulations are conducted using actual data from western China. Results indicate that, compared with Case 1 using the conventional HESS power allocation strategy, the proposed strategy increases the modeled HESS lifetime from 4.54 years to 14.39 years, corresponding to an improvement of 216.96%, while the configuration satisfaction degree reaches 0.6941. © 2026

Authors: Zhang B.; Guo Q.; Li H.; Wang Y.; Li Q.; Liu H.; Qiao S.
Title: Bioinspired Molecular Magnetic Field-Responsive Catalyst for On-Demand Switching of 2e− and 4e− Oxygen Reduction
Abstract: Achieving precise and on-demand steering of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) pathway between the efficient 4e− route to H2O and the valuable 2e− route to H2O2 remains a pivotal challenge in electrocatalysis. Herein, we address this challenge by designing a bioinspired molecular magnetic field-responsive catalyst (MMFR-C) via magnetic single-atom-anchored Salen-based covalent organic frameworks (MSA-Salen COFs) onto magnetic nanoparticles (single/multi-domain Fe3O4). Mimicking cytochrome c oxidase, the MMFR-C employs MSA-Salen COFs as an ordered proton-transfer channel and well-defined N2-M-O2 moieties as enzymatic O2 activation sites, with Fe3O4 providing a built-in magnetic field for remote regulation of the active-site electronic structure. The bioinspired MMFR-C exhibits switchable ORR pathways. Relative to the pristine Co-Salen COF (26% H2O2 selectivity, n = 3.48), the MMFR-C integrated with a single-domain Fe3O4 exhibits a remarkably enhanced H2O2 selectivity of 63.9% (n = 2.72), while that with a multi-domain Fe3O4 diverts the ORR pathway toward the 4e− route (n = 3.67). (i) We elucidate that the uniform magnetic field from the single-domain Fe3O4 in MMFR-C favors orbital hybridization between its active N2-M-O2 moieties and the *OOH intermediate, with moderate *OOH adsorption suppressing O–O scission and thus steering ORR selectivity toward H2O2. (ii) In contrast, the enhanced specific magnetism from its multi-domain Fe3O4 core optimizes the d-band center of MMFR-C’s active sites, stabilizes triplet O2 adsorption, and reduces spin-forbidden transition barriers, thereby facilitating O–O cleavage and diverting its ORR pathway to the 4e− route. Title: Coupled supply and demand forecasting in platform accommodation markets
Abstract: Tourism demand forecasting is methodologically mature, but it usually treats accommodation supply as fixed, exogenous, or slow-moving. This Progress in Tourism Management article develops a narrated, conceptually focused review of forecasting in platform-mediated short-term rental markets, where supply is elastic, decision-driven, and jointly shaped with demand through pricing, information design, host participation, and policy intervention. The article reframes realized booked nights as a constrained outcome generated by latent demand, effective supply, and matching frictions. It synthesizes tourism forecasting, revenue management, two-sided market economics, causal inference, and compositional time-series methods; articulates a three-layer coupling framework spanning intervention, behavioral, and informational channels; and uses a stylized model experiment to illustrate one supply-shock failure mode. The contribution is a theoretical and methodological map: where platform accommodation forecasting has developed, what remains under-specified, and how future work can validate coupled supply–demand forecasting. It does not attempt a completed comparative empirical evaluation. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Falk J.; Popp B.
Author full names: Falk, Jonas (60975228500); Popp, Bastian (56037564000)
Title: Why (not) subscribe? Drivers and barriers of grocery replenishment subscriptions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Subscription models are gaining importance across retail sectors, yet a picture of consumers’ evaluations of replenishment subscriptions for regularly needed products, particularly groceries, is still lacking. Drawing on perceived value theory and technology acceptance research, this study proposes a value-risk framework for replenishment subscription adoption. It contrasts four value-related drivers (time efficiency, supply reliability, cognitive relief, and cost efficiency) with four corresponding risk-related barriers (time concerns, supply mismatch concerns, lock-in concerns, and financial concerns) and examines their effects on perceived usefulness, attitude, and ultimately usage intention. Two structural models, a ‘drivers model’ and a ‘barriers model’, were estimated using quota-representative surveys in Germany (N = 493) and the UK (N = 339), complemented by multigroup analysis. The results show that subscription evaluations are inherently ambivalent: positive and negative evaluations coexist, but drivers account for considerably more variance in perceived usefulness and attitude than barriers, while financial and supply mismatch concerns still exert strong negative effects. Convenience proves multidimensional: while cognitive relief outweighs time efficiency as a driver of perceived usefulness, distinct barrier facets also show different relevance. The cross-country comparison reveals common patterns alongside differences. Retailers are advised to communicate the benefits of subscriptions more concretely rather than through generic convenience claims. However, relying just on benefit communication is insufficient: adoption also hinges on actively mitigating perceived risks, with messaging tailored to a market's maturity and familiarity. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises: The roles of technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality in an ai-driven business environment
Abstract: The tourism industry is experiencing unprecedented transformation driven by digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and the rapid evolution of smart tourism ecosystems. At the same time, tourism enterprises face growing pressure to enhance service quality while controlling operational costs and improving managerial responsiveness. In this context, management accounting effectiveness has become a critical capability for supporting strategic decision-making and maintaining sustainable competitiveness. Although previous studies have examined digital transformation and accounting systems separately, limited attention has been paid to how technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality jointly influence management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises operating in emerging economies. Addressing this research gap, the present study investigates the effects of these three determinants on management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism enterprises. Grounded in the resource-based view, contingency theory, dynamic capabilities theory, and sociotechnical systems theory, the study adopts a mixed-method research design consisting of expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. Data were collected from 315 tourism enterprises, with chief accountants, general accountants, and management accounting personnel serving as key respondents. The data were analyzed using SPSS through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The empirical findings demonstrate that technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality all exert positive and statistically significant effects on management accounting effectiveness. Among these determinants, information technology infrastructure emerges as the strongest predictor, followed by technology readiness and data quality. These findings indicate that tourism enterprises equipped with integrated digital infrastructure, advanced technological capabilities, and high-quality accounting data are better positioned to generate timely, accurate, and strategically relevant management accounting information in AI-enabled business environments. This study extends the literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging economy and contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital transformation and management accounting. The findings also offer practical implications for tourism managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen digital accounting capabilities, improve managerial decision-making, and enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of tourism enterprises in the era of AI-driven business transformation. Title: An advanced integrated cross-sectoral model for formulating government strategies on energy consumption management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions toward achieving net-zero emissions in the future
Abstract: This study aims to develop a model that identifies alternative scenarios for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by examining the interrelationships among the circular economy, socio-cultural, and environmental sectors, with the ultimate goal of supporting Thailand's net-zero emissions target. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study provides a foundation for developing integrated national management strategies that promote long-term sustainability. A novel model, referred to as the Path–Probit–Logit–ARx Model (Path Analysis–Probit–Logit Model based on Autoregressive with Exogenous Variables), was developed to address the study objectives. The findings reveal that, during the period 1992–2025, the circular economy sector experienced continuous growth, which directly contributed to the steady expansion of the socio-cultural sector. The growth of both sectors also exerted a positive influence on the environmental sector. Furthermore, the environmental sector was found to have a direct positive effect on the socio-cultural sector, indicating a bidirectional relationship between these two sectors. This finding suggests that environmentally responsible societies can promote long-term ecosystem development and that environmental and social development should progress concurrently. Based on the analysis, the study identified the adoption of electric vehicles as the most sensitive and effective scenario for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Under this scenario, the growth rate of final energy consumption is reduced to 33%, while greenhouse gas emission growth decreases to 53.73%, remaining below the critical threshold of 590.05 Mt CO2 equivalent and thereby meeting the government's target. To enhance the policy relevance and credibility of the findings, a focus group consisting of 15 experts was conducted to validate the results. The experts confirmed the appropriateness and accuracy of the proposed scenario and agreed that it is suitable for promoting sustainable development in Thailand. However, they emphasized the need for immediate action and strong governmental support to ensure effective implementation. Therefore, the findings of this study can support evidence-based decision-making and strategic planning, contributing to the development of Thailand's long-term national strategies through 2065. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Reducing the weighted tool replacement problem to min-cost flow on a linear-size graph
Abstract: We study the Weighted Tool Replacement Problem (WTRP), where a fixed sequence of n jobs must be processed using a tool magazine of capacity C, and each tool is associated with insertion and deletion costs. Our main contribution is a new exact reduction of WTRP to a min-cost flow problem that avoids the quadratic-size network of the classical Privault-Finke construction (with running time O(C3n2)). Starting from a packing formulation of WTRP, we build a flow network with O(n) nodes and O(Cn) arcs, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm with running time O(C2n+Cnlogn). Computational experiments show speedups of at least one order of magnitude over established exact approaches for WTRP, including the Privault-Finke method and the algorithm of Crama. Finally, we embed the proposed flow-based routine into a state-of-the-art heuristic for the Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem (SSP), thereby extending it to weighted replacement costs. Compared to natural Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation adapted to the weighted setting, the resulting method achieves substantially improved objective values on large instances, with improvements of up to 4.2× under identical time limits. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Human Factors and Safety Communication in Engineering Safety Performance: A Predictive PLS-SEM Model for Petrochemical Operations
Abstract: Petrochemical operations are complex engineering systems in which safety performance depends not only on technical safeguards and process controls but also on human and organisational factors that influence how workers perceive, interpret, and respond to safety requirements. Despite advances in engineering controls and occupational safety management systems, incidents continue to occur, highlighting the need to integrate human factors into engineering safety management. This study develops and evaluates a predictive model of engineering safety performance by examining the effects of two culturally embedded human factors, religiosity and fatalism, together with safety communication effectiveness in Malaysian petrochemical operations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 463 employees and contractors from major petrochemical facilities in Malaysia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. The structural model showed that religiosity significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.442, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while fatalism significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.378, p < 0.001). In contrast, safety communication effectiveness did not directly predict safety performance (β = −0.006, p = 0.954). The model explained 74.7% of the variance in safety communication effectiveness and 61.2% of the variance in safety performance. These findings demonstrate that engineering safety performance in high-risk petrochemical operations cannot be addressed solely through technical controls and communication systems. Integrating culturally embedded human factors with organisational safety mechanisms provides a more comprehensive approach to engineering safety management and supports the development of human-centred safety interventions for complex industrial operations. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. Title: A graph-based direct association strategy with fuzzy interpretability for linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality
Abstract: Existing coke quality prediction methods mainly rely on a two-stage prediction strategy, where blended coal properties are first estimated from individual coal properties and then used for coke quality prediction. This process inevitably introduces information loss and accumulated prediction errors, which limit the prediction accuracy and reliability of these models in practical coal blending applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes, for the first time, a graph-based direct association strategy linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality. Each coal blending scheme is transformed into a graph structure, where individual coal samples are regarded as graph nodes and their corresponding coal properties together with blending ratios are used as node features. Different graph neural network models are further investigated to directly learn the relationship between individual coal properties and coke quality indicators, namely Coke Reactivity Index (CRI) and Coke Strength after Reaction (CSR). A total of 306 coal blending schemes are used for model development and evaluation. Experimental results show that the proposed one-stage graph-based framework outperforms traditional two-stage prediction methods. Among different graph neural network models, the graph attention network achieves the best overall prediction performance, obtaining mean absolute errors of 2.06 and 2.60 for CRI and CSR prediction, respectively. The t-SNE visualization further demonstrates that the proposed one-stage framework can learn more discriminative feature representations than the traditional two-stage framework. In addition, the proposed framework demonstrates good robustness under blending conditions with different numbers of coal types and can provide interpretable analysis through feature importance and node importance visualization. Title: Exploring the determinants of student loyalty in islamic higher education: An empirical study from Indonesia
Abstract: This study investigates the determinants of student loyalty in the context of Islamic higher education in Indonesia, focusing on the role of religiosity and student satisfaction. As competition among higher education institutions intensifies, particularly in Yogyakarta, understanding the drivers of student loyalty becomes essential for institutional sustainability. Drawing upon relationship marketing theory and the service-dominant logic perspective, this research examines whether religiosity directly influences student loyalty and whether student satisfaction mediates this relationship. A quantitative approach was employed via a structured questionnaire distributed to 190 respondents, consisting of final-year students and alumni from private Islamic universities in Yogyakarta. The data were via structural equation modelling-partial least squares (SEM-PLS). The findings reveal that religiosity significantly influences student satisfaction, which in turn positively affects student loyalty. However, religiosity does not directly influence loyalty, indicating that satisfaction plays a critical mediating role. These results underscore the importance of cultivating religiosity-based values in higher education service delivery, as well as ensuring continuous improvement in student satisfaction to strengthen loyalty. The study contributes to the literature by integrating religiosity into the service quality and loyalty framework, offering both theoretical insights and managerial implications for Islamic universities in Indonesia. Despite its notable contributions, this study is constrained by its focus on private Islamic universities within a single regional context, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. Future investigations are encouraged to employ longitudinal designs or comparative analyses encompassing diverse types of higher education institutions and broader geographical areas to enhance the external validity of the proposed model. Additionally, incorporating complementary constructs such as institutional trust, perceived value, and university reputation could provide a more comprehensive understanding of the multifaceted processes underlying student loyalty within faith-based higher education environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Diversification or concentration? Supply chain configuration responses to decoupling risk
Abstract: This study investigates corporate supply chain configuration strategies in the context of perceived decoupling risk. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2023, we employ textual analysis to construct a firm-level index of perceived decoupling risk. Building on this index, we empirically examine its effect on corporate supply chain configuration strategies. The findings reveal that a higher level of perceived decoupling risk prompts firms to pursue greater supply chain diversification, leading to a significant decrease in supply chain concentration; notably, the diversification response is concentrated among firms facing high-intensity risk perception, while low-intensity risk perception is associated with minimal supply chain adjustment. Further analysis reveals that this negative association is attenuated by both executive risk preference and the level of corporate investment irreversibility. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the reduction in supply chain concentration is more pronounced for firms with high overseas revenue exposure, those in strategic emerging industries, and small-scale enterprises. Additionally, this impact is amplified during periods of heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly following the U.S.-China trade frictions in 2018, and is more pronounced in the upstream ends of supply chains. Finally, we find that the proactive supply chain diversification triggered by decoupling risk significantly enhances firms' operational resilience after a three-year adjustment period, demonstrating a long-term benefit for corporate stability. By quantifying firms’ subjective perception of decoupling risk and confirming its significant impact on supply chain configuration, this study provides novel micro-level evidence on firms’ supply chain behaviors in response to external environmental uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Subgroup testing for change-plane Cox models in heterogeneous credit risk data
Source title: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference
Abstract: Change-plane analysis has emerged as an effective tool to detect subgroups with distinct effects on the response of interest. Notably, the change-plane Cox model has gained significance in the subgroup analysis of survival data. Testing for the existence of a change plane can provide valuable insights into optimal decisions for the specific subgroups. However, classical supremum testing methods often suffer from limited efficiency in practical. To address this drawback, we propose a novel testing procedure designed to enhance statistical power. Our approach calculates the weighted average of the squared score test statistic (WAST) over the space of parameter that defines the subgroup, significantly improving power in practice. Moreover, we derive the asymptotic distributions of the test statistic under both the null and local alternative hypotheses. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by extensive simulation studies, exhibiting better size control and higher power than existing testing approaches. Additionally, we illustrate the practical application of our approach using the Lending club loan dataset and the German credit dataset, showing its ability to identify subgroups with different default risks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Explicit reward mechanisms for local flexibility in renewable energy communities
Abstract: Incentivizing flexible consumption of end-users is key to maximizing the value of local exchanges within Renewable Energy Communities. If centralized coordination for flexible resources planning raises concerns regarding data privacy and fair benefits distribution, state-of-the-art approaches (e.g., bi-level, ADMM) often face computational complexity and convexity challenges, limiting the precision of embedded flexible models. This work proposes an iterative resolution procedure to solve the decentralized flexibility planning with a central operator as a coordinator within a community. The community operator asks for upward or downward flexibility depending on the global needs, while members can individually react with an offer for flexible capacity. This approach ensures individual optimality while converging towards a global optimum, as validated on a 20-member domestic case study for which the gap in terms of collective bill is not more than 3.5% between the decentralized and centralized coordination schemes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Economic design of residential solar resources under uncertainty: An adaptive robust optimization approach for EV households
Abstract: The integration of residential PV systems with electric vehicles (EVs) offers significant opportunities to enhance self-consumption, reduce reliance on the grid, and lower household energy costs. Effective PV system sizing, however, is challenged by uncertainties in PV generation, household electricity demand, and EV charging behavior. While traditional approaches often ignore uncertainties or assume predefined values for uncertainties, this paper develops an adaptive robust optimization framework for sizing residential PV systems in EV-integrated households, explicitly accounting for operational uncertainties and calibrating the uncertainty parameters using a Genetic Algorithm. The proposed model explicitly incorporates multi-source uncertainty using a budgeted adaptive robust optimization approach. Investment decisions, such as PV capacity, are modeled as here-and-now variables, while operational variability is captured as wait-and-see decisions responding to uncertainty realizations. To mitigate the inherent conservatism of robust optimization and identify optimal uncertainty settings, a Genetic Algorithm–based calibration is integrated. The GA iteratively searches for the best combination of uncertainty parameters through simulation-based evaluation, balancing robustness and economic efficiency. Title: Influencer beware: The buffering role of sponsor–influencer fit in the commercialization-authenticity trade-off
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly commercialize their online presence through sponsored content, understanding how sponsorship intensity shapes consumer responses has become important. Drawing on attribution and congruence theories and the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how sponsorship levels influence audience engagement and purchase intentions through perceived personal authenticity (PPA) and whether these effects depend on sponsor–SMI fit. Three experimental studies were conducted to test the proposed relationships. The results show that higher sponsorship levels reduce consumers’ intention to follow influencers and share their content. Sponsor–SMI fit attenuates the negative effect of sponsorship intensity on PPA. Thereby mitigating its adverse effects on consumer engagement and purchase intentions. We further demonstrate that sponsorship level affects consumer responses indirectly through PPA and that this indirect effect is contingent on sponsor–SMI fit. These findings advance the influencer marketing literature by applying the ERC framework to distinguish the different authenticity types and their impact on consumer behavior. Title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
Abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Transforming value of sustainability in urban development: Reconfiguring logistics service in the construction industry
Abstract: Urban development depends on construction activity to improve sustainability, yet the logistics required to move materials, equipment, waste, and workers remains insufficiently integrated into urban planning. This paper examines how construction logistics can be integrated into municipal urban planning by analysing how actor groups perceive its impacts and coordinate value creation across fragmented urban systems. The study applies a qualitative interactive research design based on a Swedish construction logistics project. Data were collected between August 2022 and March 2024 through eight semi-structured group interviews, joint workshops, actor-specific validation workshops, and a final synthesis workshop with developers, main contractors, suppliers, and trade organizations. The analysis combines iterative thematic coding with value configuration theory. The findings show that suppliers emphasize efficiency and climate savings, main contractors focus on project efficiency and safety, developers stress sustainability, accessibility and accountability, while trade organizations highlight knowledge-building and sector coordination. These differences create misalignment because societal benefits are often separated from project-level costs. Four conditions are identified as central: clearer procurement requirements, stronger logistics knowledge, scalable logistics service designs, and systematic follow-up of time, cost, and emission effects. The paper concludes that municipalities should use procurement, planning requirements and follow-up mechanisms to enforce construction logistics values in urban planning. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A blockchain-enabled distributed service configuration approach for distributed smart manufacturing systems
Abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, distributed manufacturing (DM) paradigms, exemplified by cloud manufacturing (CMfg), have garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. These paradigms aim to achieve the precise matching of geographically dispersed manufacturing resources with personalized demands. However, existing research on service configuration predominantly relies on centralized information architectures, which pose critical challenges such as single point of failure (SPoF), data privacy leakage risks, and limited scalability. To address these issues, this paper investigates how blockchain technology can be leveraged to enable trustworthy collaboration and distributed decision-making in DM systems. Specifically, we propose a Blockchain-enabled Cyber-Physical Network (BCPN) architecture and design a complete and executable business process tailored to service configuration requirements. Furthermore, a systematic solution is developed that integrates several key components, including a reputation evaluation contract, a service pre-screening contract, a proof of reputation (PoR) consensus mechanism, a distributed service configuration contract, and a backward time propagation smart contract based on breadth-first search (BFS). Authors: Lin X.; Yang M.; Liu C.; Agag G.
Title: How retailers build authenticity over time: A longitudinal study of transparency, frontline brand enactment, customer-company identification, and sales growth
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Retailer authenticity is treated as a commercial asset, yet its relevance may depend on identity conversion. This longitudinal study separates retailer-controlled evidence from customers' higher-order authenticity judgments and from the self-definitional response that follows. Retailer transparency supplies informational evidence concerning disclosure, clarity, accuracy, and candor, whereas frontline brand enactment supplies behavioral evidence that employees embody the retailer's professed identity. Three waves of matched survey data from 10,214 loyalty customers nested in 208 stores in China are linked to a 12-month archival comparable-sales-growth window beginning during the closing month of Time 3. Multilevel longitudinal structural equation modeling indicates temporally ordered positive associations from Time 1 transparency and frontline brand enactment to Time 2 authenticity, from Time 2 authenticity to Time 3 customer-company identification, and from store-level identification to follow-up sales growth. The direct authenticity-growth association is not reliable after identification is modeled. The authenticity-identification association is stronger at higher prestige, recorded frontline interaction frequency, and brand familiarity, consistent with proposed conditions of cue diagnosticity and identity relevance. The study's central contribution is an evidence-judgment-identity-performance account: the observed pattern links authenticity with commercial performance through identification, without establishing that this is its only pathway or that a direct premium is absent. Title: Hot war tourism: The touristification of unresolved conflict
Abstract: This article conceptualises hot war tourism as the touristification of unresolved conflict: configurations in which conflict continues materially to shape civilian vulnerability, security and visitor access while conflict-affected places and experiences acquire experiential, representational or market value. A critical integrative review clarifies its boundaries with dark, battlefield, military, risk, recovery and solidarity-oriented tourism and identifies five dimensions: temporal immediacy, spatial proximity, commodification, moral and motivational ambiguity, and governance and responsibility. Ukraine and Syria illustrate contrasting active-war witnessing and recovery–normalisation configurations. A relational framework locates war-related tourism according to the degree of unresolved conflict and the intensity of touristification, while a multi-actor governance framework specifies responsibilities for access, risk disclosure, representation, consent, platform accountability, humanitarian non-interference and escalation. The concept links tourism value production to unresolved harm and provides a basis for analysing when conflict-related visitation requires facilitation, restraint or restriction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java: The roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, innovation capability, and ESG
Abstract: This study examines the determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java by analyzing the roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) implementation, innovation capability, and organizational performance. Social enterprises in emerging economies increasingly face challenges in maintaining long-term sustainability due to resource limitations, institutional uncertainty, and dynamic social demands. Although previous studies have explored intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, ESG practices, and innovation capability separately, limited empirical research has integrated these variables into a comprehensive sustainability model within the context of social enterprises in emerging economies, particularly Indonesia. Therefore, this study seeks to address this gap by developing and testing an integrated model of social enterprise sustainability. This research adopts a quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data were collected from 200 owners and managers of social enterprises operating across six provinces on Java Island. The findings reveal that entrepreneurial orientation has a strong and significant effect on innovation capability (β = 0.699, p < 0.001), while ESG implementation significantly influences social enterprise performance (β = 0.402, p < 0.001). Intellectual capital and entrepreneurial orientation significantly contribute to innovation capability, whereas ESG implementation directly improves organizational performance and sustainability. Furthermore, innovation capability acts as a crucial mediating variable that strengthens the relationship between strategic organizational resources and sustainability outcomes. Social enterprise performance also demonstrates a significant mediating role in achieving long-term sustainability. These findings highlight the importance of innovation-driven strategies, knowledge-based resources, and ESG-oriented governance in strengthening the resilience and sustainability of social enterprises. Title: Reflection quality and psychological safety as mechanisms of development in virtual management education
Abstract: This study examines the mechanisms linking behavioral participation in virtual management education to developmental learning outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning theory (ELT), this study investigates whether reflection quality mediates the relationship between behavioral participation and student development and whether team psychological safety moderates the participation–reflection relationship. Data were collected from an eight-week multicultural virtual leadership program involving 74 business students working in nine multicultural teams. To reduce common method concerns, this study integrated six independent sources of evidence: instructor activity logs, coded reflection reports, pre- and post-program competency surveys, psychological safety ratings, peer evaluations, and instructor-assessed team-performance scores. The findings indicate that higher behavioral participation is associated with deeper reflective responses. Reflection quality is more consistently associated with gains in cultural intelligence (CQ) and global leadership competency than participation alone. Furthermore, the relationship between participation and reflection is stronger in teams characterized by higher psychological safety, highlighting the importance of supportive learning environments in fostering reflective practices. Because reflection depth and post-program outcomes were assessed at the same measurement occasion, the mediation findings are interpreted as theory-consistent associative evidence rather than causal proof. Overall, the results are consistent with a sociocognitive extension of ELT, in which experiential learning is shaped not only by individual cognitive processing but also by the interpersonal safety of the team environment. For management educators, the findings emphasize three design priorities: systematic monitoring of behavioral participation, scaffolding and assessing reflection quality, and intentionally cultivating psychologically safe learning environments to enhance developmental outcomes in virtual management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The impact of digital marketing on consumer attitudes and behavioural responses: The role of perceived value and financial considerations in the decision-making process
Abstract: Digital technologies influence consumers across need recognition, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase activity. This study examines how six features of digitally mediated promotion—informativeness, personalisation, interactivity, entertainment, credibility, and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)—shape attitudes and subsequent behavioural responses among Albanian consumers. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey yielded 487 valid responses from adults residing in Albania who had recently used online channels in purchase-related activity. The conceptual model integrates the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the Theory of Planned Behaviour, and the customer-journey perspective. Measurement and structural relationships were assessed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples; supplementary analyses tested mediation, moderation, age-group differences, and stage-specific effects. Results: Credibility was the strongest predictor of attitude (β = 0.291), followed by positive eWOM (β = 0.245) and informativeness (β = 0.230). Attitude positively predicted purchase intention (β = 0.597), online engagement (β = 0.467), and recommendation intention (β = 0.517), while purchase intention predicted self-reported purchasing (β = 0.553). Attitude mediated the effects of all six promotional features on purchase intention. Media literacy strengthened the informativeness–attitude relationship (β = 0.109), whereas age-group differences were not significant. Influence was greatest during information search and alternative evaluation. Title: From eco-signals to green trust: How tourists evaluate sustainability credibility through online reviews

Abstract: Growing sustainability claims in tourism have intensified concerns about credibility and greenwashing. Title: Can a transversal adaptation of teaching materials foster students’ entrepreneurial intentions? A quasi-experimental exploration in a statistics course setting
Abstract: We propose that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content within other curricula may be an effective approach to foster students' entrepreneurial intentions. A qualitative follow-up exploration with seven participants suggested that the data collection itself may have prompted students to reassess their attitude toward entrepreneurship. Title: Human capital development through community digital centers for inequality reduction in Thailand
Abstract: Driving human capital development through community digital centers to reduce inequality requires multiple interrelated factors and components to ensure successful implementation. Title: Exploring digital culture: A bibliometric review using keyword co-occurrence and performance analysis
Abstract: Digital culture has become a central organizational phenomenon shaping how firms navigate digital transformation, emerging technologies, and sustainability pressures, yet prior research remains fragmented across disciplines and contexts. This study provides the first large-scale bibliometric mapping of digital culture research from an organizational perspective. Using the Scopus database, we analyzed 212 publications published between 2008 and 2025. Bibliometric techniques and VOSviewer were applied to examine (i) annual publication trends, (ii) thematic structures through keyword co-occurrence networks, (iii) influential knowledge producers across authors, affiliations, and countries, and (iv) document type distribution to infer field maturity. The results show a clear acceleration after 2020, culminating in more than 60 publications per year by 2025, indicating that digital culture has shifted from a niche conceptual topic to a consolidated research stream. Document type analysis further indicates a field dominated by journal articles (68.0%), supported by book chapters (18.5%) and conference papers (11.0%), while reviews remain scarce, suggesting strong empirical expansion but limited synthesis. Title: Social and Spiritual Aspects Affecting Psychosocial Well-Being Among Early- and Late-Stage Oral Cancer Patients Presenting with Restricted Oral Functioning
Source title: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research
Abstract: Objective: There is increasing awareness of the diverse negative effects of cancer stage on the psychosocial well-being of patients with oral cancer. This study examined the role of social support and spiritual aspects in predicting psychosocial well-being among the early-and late-stage Malaysian oral cancer patients with restricted oral functioning, to inform a holistic model of cancer care. Material and Methods: Secondary data analysis was performed based on a health-related quality of life dataset among 96 oral cancer patients, collected from the Functional-Assessment of Cancer-Therapy–Head and Neck, Version 4.0 instrument between 2008 and 2015. Descriptive analyses, including correlation, were performed, followed by a hierarchical multiple regression using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) Version 25.0. Results: The multivariate analyses indicated moderate-strong relationships between the mean scores for oral functioning, social support, spiritual aspect, and psychosocial well-being among a cohort of both early (n=31) and late-stage (n=65) patients attending three visits: pre-treatment, 1 month, and 3 months post-treatment. However, only oral functioning and social support were found to be significant predictors of patients’ psychosocial well-being; with social support being the most significant predictor for both groups. In addition, social support was a mediator of oral functioning at pre-treatment among the late-stage group. Conclusion: These findings provide insights into how social support and spiritual aspects can contribute to improved psychosocial well-being among patients with compromised oral functioning. The results could potentially outline new provisions for a better holistic care model for oral cancer patients in Malaysia. © 2027 JHSMR.

Title: Dynamic hierarchical population-based differential evolution with parameter control and hypervolume diversity for numerical optimization
Abstract: A hierarchical differential evolution algorithm with individualized restart is proposed. In each generation, the population is split into an elite layer and an ordinary layer by an adaptive, progress-dependent threshold derived from normalized fitness deviations, and the two layers are evolved by different mutation operators and parameter-generation rules. Scaling factors and crossover rates are adapted from a success-history memory weighted by successful difference-vector magnitudes, supported by an archive whose members are aged out over time. A volume-based diversity indicator, combined with per-individual stagnation counters, triggers dimension-wise reinitialization of unproductive individuals, while a piecewise-decreasing population size concentrates the remaining budget on refinement. To validate the optimization performance of the proposed HPHD-DE algorithm, we selected six high-performing DE variants as competitors, including two champion algorithms L-SRTDE and RDEx, and conducted comparative experiments on 88 test functions from three well-known testbeds. The experimental results show that although the overall performance of HPHD-DE is inferior to L-SRTDE and RDEx, it significantly outperforms the other five competitors. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Beyond Technology Readiness Levels: Developing and Evaluating an Industry 5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework for Regulated Life Sciences Manufacturing
Abstract: Purpose: Regulated life sciences manufacturing organisations face increasing pressure to adopt Industry 5.0 (I5.0) innovations while maintaining patient safety, product quality, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. Existing assessment models provide useful perspectives on technical maturity, expectation dynamics, and organisational innovation capability, but do not fully assess whether an innovation is ready to progress responsibly in a regulated, multi-stakeholder environment. This paper develops an I5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework and presents a preliminary practitioner-informed evaluation of its use in regulated life sciences manufacturing. Methods: This paper uses design science research structured through the Double Diamond process. The framework was developed through literature review, advisory feedback, subject matter expert input, practitioner workshops, case-based application, surveys, and thematic analysis. Evaluation was conducted with a small, purposively selected cohort of 16 practitioners from a single educational-industry programme. Results: The framework comprises three linked tools: the Innovation Maturity Assessment, Innovation Maturity Rubric, and Innovation Readiness Levels. Across two exploratory workshops involving 16 experienced practitioners, participants reported that the framework supported clearer discussion of readiness and improved visibility of adoption risks. In Workshop 2, descriptive feedback indicated that 91% of respondents viewed Innovation Readiness Levels as clearer than Technology Readiness Levels, 82% found the framework useful for comparing innovation timelines, and 75% would recommend it. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary practitioner feedback rather than sector-wide validation. Conclusion: The findings support the conceptual distinction between innovation readiness and technology readiness and indicate the need to assess technical, regulatory, organisational, stakeholder, and societal dimensions together when evaluating I5.0 innovation in regulated manufacturing. Title: Towards a digital skills framework for the energy sector: Evidence from the Australian LNG industry
Abstract: Digital innovations have become increasingly widespread in almost every industry, and Australia’s energy sector has not been immune to this. It therefore follows that the coordination of energy exports like liquified natural gas (LNG) across government, industry, and community stakeholders will be largely dependent on the ability of these constituents to share digital information between and among each other in useful timeframes. However, the success of these integrated data systems will hinge on the ability of the energy sector’s workforce to use these technologies effectively, but it is increasingly coming into focus that the industry’s workers have very uneven levels of proficiency with digital technologies. By synthesizing earlier digital skills frameworks from other industries and adding qualitative evidence distilled from 42 interviews with a broad range of employees throughout a midsize Australian LNG company, this paper puts forward a digital skills framework for the energy sector which identifies five skill areas that will be required in 2030: (1) data analytics, (2) digital communication and collaboration, (3) digital security, (4) digital ethical and social responsibility, and (5) digital innovation. The required level of proficiency that will be required in 2030 for each of these skill areas is then assessed for different discipline groups throughout the industry. We conclude by explaining how the presented framework can be used as an assessment tool for identifying skill gaps throughout the energy sector, and exploring the policy-related implications of the findings. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Combining multiple endogeneous information sources for improved efficiency in covariance and correlation matrix estimation

Abstract: This paper proposes efficient covariance and correlation matrix measures using high-frequency data. The proposed matrix measures are the multivariate extension of the Parkinson volatility measure that incorporates High, Low, Open and Close price information distinct from the classical approaches based solely on one information type such as closing price information when constructing the sample covariance matrices. The proposed novel matrix measures facilitate new developments for multivariate time series modelling of dependence structures, including the extension of volatility models such as Conditional Autoregressive Range models to multivariate settings. Model results will provide important risk measures to practitioners for portfolio or investment strategies that deal with a large number of stock assets. Through simulation studies, the proposed matrix measures are shown to perform well under heteroskedastic variance conditions and are positive semi-definite. Title: Large language models in Scrum management: A practitioner survey of use, perceived benefits, risks, and human–AI collaboration
Abstract: Context: Scrum management includes knowledge-intensive activities such as backlog refinement, event preparation, and stakeholder alignment. Large language model (LLM) chat assistants may support these activities, but empirical evidence remains limited. Objective: This study investigates practitioners’ self-reported LLM use in Scrum management, perceived benefits and risks, and expectations for human–AI collaboration. Methods: We conducted a practitioner survey, and the results are based on a final analytic sample of 79 respondents who reported using LLM chat assistants in Scrum management. Closed-ended items were analyzed descriptively; open-ended responses underwent thematic coding. Results: In this sample, 48.1% reported daily or almost daily use, and 79.7% rated their LLM knowledge as at least qualified. Reported use centered on backlog refinement, event summarization, and Scrum-practice exploration. Perceived benefits included productivity (77.2%), reduced repetitive-task time (75.9%), and artifact quality (74.7%). Reported problems included almost-correct outputs (65.8%), hallucinations (54.4%), privacy concerns (50.6%), and content-validation difficulty (46.8%). Most respondents envisioned human-led or balanced human–AI collaboration (81.0%); 65.8% selected the no-role-replacement option. Title: Surfactant-Derived Nitrogen-Bridged MoS2/C Heterostructures for Robust Lithium-Ion Storage
Abstract: Structural stability, ionic transport, and electronic conductivity are the major challenges of layered transition-metal dichalcogenide/carbon nanocomposites (LTMD/C) for lithium-ion storage. Herein, to address these challenges, a quaternary ammonium surfactant-mediated strategy is proposed to simultaneously construct porous MoS2 architectures and in situ generate nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) layers chemically coupled to MoS2 via interfacial Mo–N bridges. The resultant N-bridged MoS2/C heterostructures (denoted as MoS2–N–C) exhibit excellent structural robustness, expanded interlayer spacing, and improved charge-transfer kinetics. As an anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), the optimized MoS2–N–C700 electrode delivers remarkable cycling stability (~ 100% capacity retention after 800 cycles at 0.5 A g−1) and excellent rate capability. Moreover, lithium-ion supercapacitors (LISCs) based on the as-prepared MoS2–N–C composite achieve an ultrahigh power density of 3500 W kg−1, and excellent cycling stability over 10,000 cycles. The cycling performance in both LIBs and LISCs surpasses that of most previously reported MoS2/C nanocomposites and conventional carbon-based anodes. This surfactant-derived interfacial bridging structure design offers a general platform for developing robust LTMD/C heterostructured electrodes for energy storage systems. © Crown 2026.

Title: Will the deepening of interdependence network coupling increase the robustness of the network?
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Modern networks are increasingly interdependent, with a typical example being the coupling relationship between communication networks and power networks. As smart grids evolve and coupling intensifies, the overall security of the networks faces significant challenges. Some real-world cases have indicated that increasing the coupling strength between networks may increase the vulnerability of networks to failures. Many researchers have studied the coupling relationship in interdependent networks from various perspectives, including modeling the coupling relationship, considering load flow and developing strategies for failure mitigation and recovery. However, there is currently limited research on the specific effects of coupling strength on network robustness. This paper focuses on the interdependence between communication networks and modern power grids and investigates the influence of coupling strength on network robustness by constructing a cascading failure model. Through simulations on power-communication networks, three main conclusions are drawn: (1) Deepening the coupling strength does not necessarily increase network robustness; in some cases, excessive coupling can decrease the network’s robustness to cascading failures. Title: Examining perceptual spillover effects in social media influencer marketing effectiveness: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA approach

Results from the Stage 1 serial mediation model suggest that SMI social attractiveness is directly associated with purchase intention and indirectly associated with purchase intention through brand attitude. Title: Financial leverage in business sector profitability: A review
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between financial leverage and corporate profitability in a context of heightened economic uncertainty following the COVID-19 pandemic, a period during which organizations have been compelled to redefine their financing strategies in order to preserve sustainability and financial performance. The primary objective was to systematically analyze recent empirical evidence on the impact of financial leverage on corporate profitability. To this end, a systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, using the Scopus database. The search strategy incorporated terms related to financial leverage, financing, profitability, and firms, while the 2020–2025 period and the explicit inclusion of key topic-related concepts were established as the main eligibility criteria. From an initial total of 7,587 identified records, a rigorous screening process was carried out based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in the final selection of 36 articles for qualitative analysis. The study employed synthesis matrices, bibliometric analysis, and keyword co-occurrence networks, which made it possible to identify trends, predominant methodological approaches, and the main findings. The results indicate that companies rely on a combination of internal and external financing sources, including bank credit, bond issuance, informal financing, and fintech tools. In general, financial leverage has a positive effect on indicators such as ROA, ROE, and ROI, provided that adequate financial planning, cost control, and efficient debt management are in place. However, in SMEs or firms with high levels of indebtedness and limited managerial capacity, the impact may be negative or statistically insignificant. It is concluded that financial leverage constitutes a strategic tool for enhancing profitability, provided that it is managed prudently and within a comprehensive financial risk management framework. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: High-Spatiotemporal and Multimodal Soft Tactile Interface with Layered Architecture for Simultaneous Structural and Thermal Perception
Abstract: Advanced robotic systems require tactile perception to interact reliably with objects in environments where visual information is limited by occlusion, illumination variations, and focusing issues. However, conventional tactile sensors are limited to single-stimulus recognition and face fundamental challenges in scalability and functionality, as miniaturizing sensor pixels reduces baseline signal levels and degrades the SNR. This study presents a high-spatiotemporal and multimodal soft tactile interface for simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles, fabricated through a layered architecture enabled by additive manufacturing. The proposed interface incorporates a 3D-stacked capacitive pressure sensor that combines buried interdigitated capacitors and a parallel-plate capacitor, and a reduced graphene oxide based temperature sensor within the same pixel area. The 3D-stacked electrode architecture enhances baseline capacitance within a miniaturized pixel footprint, and a via-free, interlayered interconnection scheme resolves wiring complexity in the temperature sensor array. Each sensing layer operates through independent transduction mechanisms, enabling the simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles with minimal cross-interference. The fabricated multimodal array can spatially resolve both contact geometry and localized thermal distributions with high-spatiotemporal resolution. Furthermore, by applying a tactile scanning strategy in robotic perception, the platform successfully identifies geometric features and surface thermal profiles of target objects even under vision-limited conditions. This study provides a scalable and robust foundation for multimodal tactile perception in advanced robotic manipulation and human–robot interaction. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Enhancing communication competence and managerial skills through virtual reality based experiential learning in management education
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising pedagogical modality in higher management education, offering immersive, risk-free environments that simulate the complexity of real-world organizational interactions. Title: Alkaline-thermal and enzymatic pretreatment of PLA/PBAT plastics boosts methane production from anaerobic co-digestion with food waste
Abstract: The co-treatment of food waste (FW) and biodegradable plastics in anaerobic digestion (AD) is challenged by the slow degradation of polylactic acid and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PLA/PBAT) blends. This study systematically evaluated alkaline-thermal (AT) and enzymatic pretreatment of two PLA/PBAT plastics—starch-containing (PLA/PBAT/ST) and mineral dust-containing (PLA/PBAT/MD)—followed by anaerobic co-digestion with FW. AT pretreatment significantly enhanced methane production. The highest cumulative methane yield (223.40 ± 5.62 mL/g VS) was obtained with PLA/PBAT/MD pretreated at 140℃, a 25.2 % increase over the untreated control (CK-MD), while PLA/PBAT/ST showed an 8.6 % increase (197.60 ± 2.49 mL/g VS). Enzymatic pretreatment led to only marginal improvements. Scanning electron microscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that AT at 140℃ induced extensive surface erosion, pore formation, and ester bond cleavage, thereby increasing surface hydrophilicity and microbial accessibility. Title: Is green product trade a pathway to better air quality in China?
Abstract: This study evaluates whether green product trade can serve as an effective pathway to improving air quality in China. Using panel data for 28 provinces from 2010 to 2021, we are the first to jointly examine the impacts of green trade on six major air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NOx, and CO2) while simultaneously identifying both its temporal dynamics and spatial spillover effects within a unified empirical framework. We construct an integrated green-product trade database combining the APEC, OECD, and World Bank classifications and employ System GMM and the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to address spatial-temporal dependence. The results show that a 1% increase in green trade reduces PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by approximately 1.1%. Moreover, green imports in neighboring provinces generate strong spatial spillovers, lowering local PM2.5, PM10, CO, and SO2 emissions by about 5%. We also find that green imports exert significantly stronger pollution-reduction effects than green exports, suggesting an import-driven technology-upgrade mechanism typical of developing economies. These findings provide robust evidence that green trade contributes to China's environmental improvements and offer important policy insights for emerging economies seeking to leverage green globalization for sustainable, lower-emission development. Title: When crowds converge: Link between events and crime
Abstract: This study draws on environmental criminology to conceptualize planned events as bounded opportunity contexts that temporarily reshape urban activity. Using high-dimensional fixed-effects Poisson models and a panel of 154,561 events in Houston, Texas, we estimate reduced-form associations across event attributes and offense types. The event-crime association is statistically detectable but economically modest. Formal comparisons reveal selective offense heterogeneity, with the Crimes Against Society coefficient exceeding the Violent Crime coefficient. Public opportunistic crime also shows stronger associations than private opportunistic and non-opportunistic crime, but not Other Crime. Event size exhibits significant heterogeneity, with the largest events showing stronger associations than those in all lower-attendance categories. Event type, day-type context, duration, and recurrence are not statistically distinguishable. Adjustment for contemporaneous foot traffic attenuates the event coefficient. The findings suggest proportionate, targeted situational prevention rather than generalized security escalation in urban destination safety planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chain performance, ripple effects, and viability
Abstract: We simulate impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chains (SCs). First, we articulate the specific features that frame a global energy crisis as a unique type of SC large-scale systemic shocks characterized by a long-term disruption existence, disruption propagations (i.e., the ripple effect), a combination of immediate and delayed effects, cross-industry ripple effects, and mutual interrelations of SC and economic impacts. Second, we demonstrate how simulation-based methodology can be used to examine and predict the impacts of global energy crises on SC performance using the example of the Strait of Hormuz blockage and anyLogistix software. The major observation from the simulation experiments is that global energy crisis impacts resemble the COVID-19 pandemic patterns and ripple effects in 2020–2022 with reduced logistics capacities, delivery delays, and production shutdowns, supplemented by inflation effects observed in tariff turbulences in 2025. Other important factors influencing the shock impacts and propagation mechanisms are the duration of the energy crisis and SC viability. We observe that viable SCs with greater variety in production, supply, logistics, and energy structures are better able to absorb shocks. The outcomes of this research can be used by decision-makers to predict the operational and long-term impacts of global energy crises on SCs and to develop viability strategies. Our models are readily available to be used in practice for SC stress testing. They offer recommendations on proactively building adaptability and reconfiguring in response to disruptions to survive in a world without a reliable energy supply, incorporating large-scale systemic shocks into operational models. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Rheo-tribological measurements and trained sensory panel texture perception across size-controllable whey protein microgels
Abstract: Protein microgels have gained attention as potential fat replacers and texture modifiers due to their ability to modulate viscosity and lubrication. In this study, whey protein microgels with controlled particle sizes (6 and 20 μm) were incorporated at different inclusion levels (15-45%) into fat-free dairy milk to evaluate their effects on rheological behaviour, tribological performance, and trained sensory texture perception. A combined instrumental-sensory approach was used to establish relationships between microgel structure, lubrication mechanisms, and perceived texture attributes. Sensory evaluation was conducted using a trained panel (n = 13), assessing thickness, smoothness, graininess, creaminess, and astringency. Viscosity and coefficient of friction were measured using a tribo-rheometer with stainless steel and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) geometries. Viscosity measured at oral-relevant shear rates showed a strong positive correlation with perceived thickness (r = 0.959), confirming bulk shear viscosity as a key determinant of thickness perception. Tribological-sensory relationships varied with surface geometry. Stainless steel measurements showed correlations with smoothness (r = - 0.798) and graininess (r = 0.789), while creaminess correlated with friction at intermediate sliding speeds (r = - 0.856). In contrast, PDMS tribology showed the strongest relationship with thickness perception (r = - 0.953) and greater sensitivity to particle size. Larger microgels (20 μm) promoted smoother and less grainy textures, whereas smaller microgels (6 μm) increased graininess, likely due to aggregation within the dairy matrix. Overall, rheological and tribological measurements provided mechanistic and predictive insight into how microgel size and concentration influence perceived texture, supporting the rational design of fat-reduced and healthier products. © 2026 The Authors.
