Authors: Wang X.; Xue B.
Title: Artificial intelligence-supported learning and academic performance: Evidence from Chinese universities
Abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence tools into university learning environments has generated urgent but as yet inadequately answered empirical questions about the direction, magnitude, and mechanisms of their effects on student academic performance. This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of AI-supported learning and academic performance in Chinese higher education, drawing on a large-scale survey-administrative data linkage of 1080 undergraduate students across 12 universities spanning five academic disciplines in the 2021-2022 academic year. The study integrates technology acceptance theory, self-regulated learning frameworks, and human capital theory within a unified analytical design employing structural equation modelling, hierarchical regression with moderation testing, mediation analysis with bootstrapped confidence intervals, and a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences specification exploiting staggered institutional AI policy adoption. Core findings establish that AI usage intensity exerts a positive and statistically robust effect on cumulative GPA (standardised beta: 0.284, p < 0.001), mediated primarily through self-regulated learning enhancement (indirect effect: 0.138, 95% CI: 0.094-0.182) and cognitive engagement (0.121, 0.081-0.161). A statistically significant positive interaction between AI usage and prior academic achievement reveals that above-average students benefit more from AI tool adoption than below-average students, raising equity concerns that are empirically corroborated by significant disparities in digital literacy and AI access across socioeconomic subgroups. The difference-in-differences analysis, exploiting staggered university-level AI policy rollout, yields an intent-to-treat GPA effect of 0.18 grade points (p < 0.01), consistent with the primary regression findings. Subgroup analyses document significant effect heterogeneity by discipline, gender, institution type, and first-generation student status, with STEM and business students showing larger effects and first-generation students showing the largest absolute AI benefit but remaining the most digitally underserved group. A GPA trajectory analysis using six-semester longitudinal data confirms that early AI adopters achieved significantly steeper positive GPA trends following AI tool introduction compared with non-adopters. These findings collectively call for policy frameworks that integrate active AI literacy development, equitable access provision, and academic integrity governance into a coherent institutional AI-in-education strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Assessing the viability of urban rooftop photovoltaic systems under new regulatory frameworks in Brazil via an evolutionary real options approach
Abstract: The transition towards decentralized and sustainable urban energy systems requires robust decision-making frameworks that account for policy changes, market uncertainties, and investment flexibility. This study applies an Evolutionary Real Options Approach (EROA) to evaluate the economic viability of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems in Brazil under the New Mark of Distributed Generation (NMDG), a regulatory change that alters incentives for net metering. By incorporating stochastic volatility models, such as the Heston model and Geometric Brownian motion (GBM) with jumps, this work quantifies the impact of regulatory changes on investment timing and system sizing decisions. Results indicate a significant reduction in financial returns and a delay in investment decisions under the new regulation. The introduction of the new regulation has led to reductions in returns of approximately 18% and 23% for the Heston and GBM with jumps models, respectively. In terms of decision sequences, the Heston model presents increased opportunities for phased investment due to its greater flexibility. On the other hand, the GBM with jumps model encourages immediate investment in a complete solar system. The new regulation results in a delay of 6 to 12 months at entry points, regardless of the chosen model. These findings contribute to the understanding of urban energy transitions, policy impacts on decentralized generation, and investment dynamics in sustainable urban infrastructure. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Overcoming geothermal development barriers in Indonesia: A narrative policy review of sedimentary basin-based geothermal development
Abstract: Indonesia possesses the world's largest geothermal resource potential, yet its utilization remains disproportionately low. This study conducted a narrative policy review and strategic assessment using the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework to identify the key barriers to geothermal development and formulate strategic recommendations using the TOWS (Threats, Opportunities, Weaknesses, Strengths) matrix. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach based on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2011 and 2026. The analysis identified four major constraints to conventional volcanic geothermal development: high exploration risk and capital expenditure (CAPEX), land-use conflicts with protected forests, electricity tariff policies linked to coal-based generation costs, and persistent social resistance (NIMBY/Not in My Backyard syndrome). The findings indicated that diversifying geothermal development toward non-volcanic back-arc sedimentary basins, particularly through co-production with mature Oil and Gas (O&G) fields, provided a practical pathway to reduce exploration risk, lower infrastructure costs, minimize permitting conflicts and social resistance, and improve project economics. This approach could potentially reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) to below USD 0.07/kWh. Based on the TOWS analysis, the study recommended a dual-track geothermal development strategy combining continued volcanic exploration with accelerated sedimentary basin development, supported by binary-cycle technology, brownfield O&G infrastructure reuse, Feed-in Tariff (FiT) reform, and international green financing. Collectively, these strategies could strengthen investment attractiveness and accelerate Indonesia's transition toward its Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 target. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Career plateau and multifaceted turnover pathways in the airline industry: Evidence from full-service and low-cost carrier cabin crew
Abstract: This study examines how career plateau influences stress, burnout, and multifaceted turnover intentions among airline cabin crew members by comparing full-service carriers (FSCs) and low-cost carriers (LCCs). Career plateau was categorized into hierarchical and job content career plateaus, and their psychological and behavioral impacts were assessed. Data were collected through a survey of 382 Korean cabin crew members with at least three years of experience and in-depth interviews with 14 participants. Quantitative results showed that a job content career plateau significantly heightened stress, leading to burnout. LCC crew members reported stronger turnover intentions, whereas burnout among FSC crew members did not necessarily translate into turnover intentions, suggesting that its effects may be constrained by organizational and labor market conditions. Qualitative findings revealed coping strategies such as goal adjustment and highlighted carrier-specific interpretations of turnover. Social support moderated the burnout–turnover link, buffering negative outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Polar-Twisted Electron-Transport Layer Simultaneously Breaks Efficiency-Flexibility-Cost Limits in Organic Solar Cells
Abstract: Perylene diimide (PDI)-based electron-transport layers (ETLs) are fundamental in governing charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and the operational longevity of organic solar cells (OSCs), yet their molecular design still lacks transferable principles. Here we present a PDI-ETL molecular design framework that couples bay-position engineering with polar, bulky side-chain modulation to improve additive-free alcohol solubility, suppress over-crystallization, and mitigate oxidative degradation. With this framework, H75-DMA suppresses reactive-oxygen-driven chemical evolution and interfacial trap accumulation, thereby stabilizing interfacial energetics and electron transport. Binary OSCs based on H75-DMA achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) above 20% and exhibit improved mechanical toughness and bending durability in flexible devices. Its smooth, high-surface-energy interface also induces continuous growth of ultrathin metal cathodes, leading to increased light-utilization efficiency in flexible semitransparent OSCs. In addition, H75-DMA enables cathode substitution from Ag to Cu while retaining about 97% of the PCE of the Ag-based devices, thereby improving cost-effectiveness at the device level. Authors: Chen J.; Wang S.; Ke W.; Zhang J.
Title: When culture speaks through E-commerce chatbots: How collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles shape impulsive buying
Abstract: E-commerce chatbots increasingly provide product advice during online shopping, yet it remains unclear how culturally framed recommendation language shapes impulsive buying. Drawing on cultural dimensions theory, cultural priming theory, and constructivist interpretation, this study conceptualizes collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles as message-level cultural language cues rather than as measures of consumers’ stable cultural orientation. Across four experiments with 880 participants, we show that a collectivistic persuasive style increases impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as socially supported and behaviorally acceptable choices, which strengthens social conformity. By contrast, an individualistic persuasive style reduces impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as choices requiring confirmation against personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit, which strengthens self-referencing. The findings further identify two boundary conditions. Human labeling strengthens the collectivistic pathway through social conformity by making group-oriented language more likely to be treated as socially relevant advice, whereas AI labeling shifts source perception toward algorithmic advice and strengthens the individualistic pathway through self-referencing by increasing attention to personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit. Low algorithm accessibility strengthens the collectivistic pathway, whereas high algorithm accessibility strengthens the individualistic pathway. These findings show that chatbot recommendations do more than transmit product information. They shape how consumers interpret the perceived source, social relevance, and personal applicability of recommendations, thereby influencing whether recommendations are quickly accepted as purchase decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Microbial succession and genome-resolved metabolic functions shape flavor evolution during sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation
Abstract: Sauce-flavor Baijiu (SFB) fermentation is characterized by a unique multi-round solid-state process, during which complex microbial succession drives flavor formation. However, the functional differentiation and metabolic mechanisms of microbial communities across successive fermentation rounds remain poorly understood. In this study, the physicochemical properties, microbial assembly, and metabolic profiles of fermented grains (FG) were investigated across seven production rounds (R1-R7). The results revealed that as fermentation rounds progressed, the FG environment evolved toward elevated acidity and reduced pH, driving a directional shift in the microbial community from an initially diverse assemblage to a structure dominated by acid-tolerant Acetilactobacillus, which established pronounced ecological dominance in later rounds. Metabolomic analysis further indicated that this dynamic adjustment of microbial structure drove the evolution of the flavor profile, specifically manifesting as differential accumulation of compounds such as esters, alcohols, and pyrazines across the various rounds. Co-occurrence network analysis demonstrated that positive microbial interactions significantly predominated within the fermentation system, and that community function exhibited a convergent trend as the rounds increased. Furthermore, 158 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were recovered, and metabolic reconstruction elucidated the potential contributions of genera such as Pediococcus, Bacillus, and Oceanobacillus to key metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, phenylalanine metabolism, and pyrazine biosynthesis. Title: Multi-agent collaboration strategies for tourism demand forecasting
Abstract: With the advancement of LLM-based agents, multi-agent collaboration has attracted growing interdisciplinary attention. However, its effectiveness in business planning and decision-making remains underexplored. Therefore, this study proposes different multi-agent collaboration strategies and examines their effectiveness in such business tasks as tourism demand forecasting. The results based on Hong Kong daily inbound tourist data show that there is variability in agent forecasting performance guided by different strategies. The parallel collaboration significantly outperforms both non-collaboration and chain collaboration. Meanwhile, the performance of chain collaboration depends on agent number, independent forecasting ability, and agent order. Furthermore, heterogeneous multi-LLM collaboration consistently exceeds homogeneous multi-role collaboration. Title: Zwitterionic Ionogels Resolving the Trade-Off Between Mechanical Strength and Autonomous Self-Healing for Iontronics
Abstract: Simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness and autonomous self-healing in ionogels remains a fundamental challenge for durable, skin-like electronics. Conventional approaches often improve mechanical strength by introducing rigid or densely cross-linked polymer networks, but such strategies inevitably restrict polymer chain mobility and hinder dynamic bond reconfiguration required for healing. Here, a zwitterionic side-chain engineered tough ionogel (ZESTI) is developed to overcome this trade-off through molecular-level design. Hydrophilic zwitterions are covalently grafted onto a hydrophobic polyurethane backbone to preferentially interact with the ionic liquid through ion–dipole interactions and thereby regulate its distribution. This architecture simultaneously facilitates dipole–dipole interactions for mechanical reinforcement and ion–dipole coordination for efficient self-healing under ambient conditions. As a result, ZESTI exhibits an exceptional combination of tensile strength (10.40 MPa), stretchability (1606%), toughness (56.03 MJ m−3), and ambient self-healing efficiency exceeding 83%, while maintaining high ionic conductivity via enhanced ion hopping. When constructed as a self-reporting packaging interface, ZESTI provides stable protection and state perception under sharp contact and restores signal output after mechanical damage through self-healing. This work offers a generalizable design strategy that reconciles mechanical toughness with dynamic functionality in ionogels, establishing a general design paradigm for next-generation self-sustaining iontronic devices. Title: Geopolitical tensions and foreign R&D subsidiaries’ innovation performance: Evidence from emerging economy MNEs
Abstract: In an era of intensifying geopolitical rivalries, emerging economy multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face unprecedented challenges in sustaining cross-border innovation, particularly as technological competition becomes increasingly entangled with national security agendas. Integrating the literature on geopolitics in international relations with EMNE subsidiary innovation, this study investigates whether and to what extent inter-country geopolitical tensions influence the innovation performance of EMNEs’ R&D subsidiaries in advanced economies. Using a sample of Chinese listed firms’ foreign R&D subsidiaries, we find that escalating geopolitical tensions between home and host countries significantly reduce the innovation output of these subsidiaries. Furthermore, the number of host-national innovation partners of a foreign R&D subsidiary can help mitigate the negative effect of geopolitical tensions on its innovation pursuits, while its local same-parent sisters can exacerbate this adverse impact. Our study enhances the understanding of how international politics affect EMNE subsidiary innovation and advances the political risk literature by revealing the role of subsidiary-level networks in shaping firm vulnerability to geopolitical disruptions. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: When animated avatars outperform: Leveraging avatar endorsers to enhance consumer adoption of AI-designed products
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) plays an increasingly important role in marketing, acting as both a product designer and an endorser, yet research predominantly examines these roles in isolation. This study addresses this gap by investigating how consumers’ adoption of AI-designed products is jointly shaped by textual designer disclosure (i.e., AI- vs. human-designed) and visual endorser cues (i.e., human-like vs. animated avatars). This research proposes that consumers integrate these two modalities into a single evaluation, and their adoption intention is shaped by the congruence between textual and visual cues. Study 1 (N = 240) demonstrates the congruence effect: for an AI-designed product, consumers show higher adoption intention when it is endorsed by an animated (vs. human-like) endorser, whereas the effect is reversed for human-designed products. Study 2 (N = 156) illustrates that perceptual curiosity serves as a mechanism: AI's involvement in design stimulates curiosity, which is then sustained by presenting the endorser in a congruent, animated form. Study 3 (N = 156) validates the mediating effect of perceptual curiosity alongside cognitive mechanisms, i.e., perceived trustworthiness and uncanniness. Study 4 (N = 340) examines how this congruence effect varies across consumers with different dispositional traits and shows that this effect is stronger among those with high anxiety about AI. These findings make a theoretical contribution by introducing designer-endorser congruence as a determinant of product adoption in AI-mediated marketing, and by identifying curiosity as an alternative affective mechanism that complements prior information-processing perspectives. Title: Assessing second-price auctions for parcel exchanges in last-mile logistics
Abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has led to multiple carriers operating in the same regions, creating opportunities for collaboration. However, logistics companies typically operate independently, leading to inefficiencies. Horizontal cooperation, where carriers share resources and infrastructure, can improve efficiency and reduce costs. This study explores the requirements for a parcel exchange framework through a game-theoretic lens. We focus on auction-based mechanisms to facilitate horizontal cooperation, optimize exchanges, and minimize delivery costs and emissions. Our approach prioritizes ensuring that carriers report accurate marginal delivery costs while maintaining business privacy. First, we define the key properties of an exchange mechanism for redistributing parcels among carriers. Our analysis reveals a conflict between incentive compatibility and budget balance when non-free disposal is enforced. Among the mechanisms considered, the Vickrey–Clarke–Groves (VCG) mechanism is the most suitable, though it tends to overpay carriers. The rationale for using VCG is that we consider incentive compatibility and allocation of all parcels more important than budget balance to ensure long-term participation of carriers and delivery fulfillment. In a computational study, we analyze a VCG-based parcel exchange under realistic settings. The experiment considers several parcel carriers within a region with heterogeneous market shares. In the simulated auctions, carriers compute marginal costs for the parcels, and the winner determination problem is solved via a linear program. A random parcel assignment serves as proxy for noncooperative behavior. The results demonstrate that second-price premium reward payments are typically moderate and that second-price compensation for allocated parcels remains superior to noncooperative last-mile parcel logistics. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: A feature selection layer approach for multi-class classification on neural networks
Abstract: In the age of data-driven decision-making, deep learning models have become powerful tools for uncovering patterns and making predictions that influence many aspects of society. However, their broader adoption in scientific and business applications is often limited by a lack of interpretability. Feature weighting methods, which assess the relevance of individual features, are among the most widely studied approaches for improving interpretability. While post hoc techniques have advanced significantly, especially in modeling nuanced relationships between features and labels in multiclass problems, embedded methods typically fall short in this regard. Embedded techniques integrate feature relevance learning directly into the model training process, but they are often unable to capture label-specific relationships. To address the limitation, we propose multiple extensions to this Feature Selection Layer, an embedded feature weighting mechanism for neural networks. Through extensive experimentation, we identify the most effective extension and benchmark it against established feature weighting methods. Our results show that the proposed method matches existing techniques in identifying globally relevant features and outperforms them in capturing label-specific relevance. By leveraging the internal dynamics of the trained neural network, the method reveals how individual features contribute to the prediction of specific labels, requiring no post-processing beyond the training process. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Fu Y.; Fan Y.; Yang Z.
Title: Filling in the gaps: Digital platform economies and the agglomeration of urban consumption amenities
Abstract: The spatial agglomeration of restaurants and retail establishments provides a physical platform for consumers searching for differentiated local goods and services. However, the rapid penetration of digital platforms, such as Yelp and Meituan, has substantially lowered search frictions and fundamentally changed the search behavior of consumers. This paper establishes a directed consumer search model to investigate the impact of the introduction and merger of digital platforms on urban agglomeration and provides empirical evidence with novel datasets on merchant relocation, platform registration, and consumer reviews. It is found that (1) digital platforms drive merchants to locate in cluster locations with lower horizontal and vertical accessibility; (2) digital platforms complement urban agglomerations regarding business density, diversity, and clustering patterns. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Beyond green claims: a social-ecological assessment of cruise tourism sustainability
Abstract: Cruise tourism sustainability discourse prioritises vessel level innovation, marginalising destination level social ecological impacts. To address this, we develop a structured literature based conceptual model of cruise mobility as a coupled global and local social ecological system. Supported by AI assisted extraction and synthesis of multidisciplinary literature, this paper constructs a governance-oriented framework. The analysis identifies two interacting dynamics: a reinforcing expansion loop where revenues stimulate infrastructure and deepen dependency, and a degrading acceptance loop where cumulative stress erodes tolerance. Presented as heuristic formalisation devices, these loops help explain why vessel efficiency alone cannot prevent destination level degradation. We translate these findings into a five-pillar governance framework featuring capacity thresholds, social monitoring, economic diversification, power rebalancing, and multi-level coordination. Title: Charge-Carrier Behavior and Molecular Interface Engineering in Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
Abstract: Molecular interface engineering has become increasingly important for improving the efficiency and stability of perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). Although highly emissive perovskite materials have advanced rapidly, their translation into high-performance devices remains limited by interfacial losses, unbalanced charge injection, and instability under electrical operation. In this review, we first discuss charge-carrier behavior in perovskite materials and devices, with emphasis on radiative and non-radiative recombination, carrier accumulation under injection, and the device-level consequences of interfacial constraints. We then examine the development of interfacial molecular strategies in PeLEDs, including self-assembled monolayers and related interfacial molecules, and summarize how such molecular layers influence charge injection, interfacial recombination, local electronic structure, and film formation at both charge-injection interfaces. On this basis, we further consider the implications of these interfacial effects for molecular regulation in light-emitting devices, with particular attention to electronic regulation under bias, chemically persistent passivation, and structural compatibility with emissive-layer formation. By connecting carrier physics, interfacial function, and molecular regulation, this review aims to provide a clearer framework for understanding and developing molecular interfacial strategies for high-performance PeLEDs. Title: Redox-Active Ligand-Stabilized Lithium Iron Phosphate Nanoparticles for High-Performance Lithium-Ion Battery Cathode with High Capacities and Long-Term Stability
Abstract: Developing cathodes that simultaneously deliver high capacity, superior rate capability, and long-term cycling stability remains a major challenge in lithium-ion batteries. Here, we report a high-performance textile cathode constructed via interfacial interaction-mediated assembly of high-energy porphyrin (PP) ligand-stabilized LiFePO4 nanoparticles (LFP NPs). For this, 19 nm LFP NPs with olivine-type intercalation mechanism were covalently integrated with amine-functionalized PP to enable multi-electron redox activity, followed by encapsulation with multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) multilayers. Subsequent thermal annealing transformed the MWCNT layers into a covalently cross-linked conductive network. As a result, the textile cathode delivers an unprecedented specific capacity of ~260 mAh g−1 at ~0.1 C, excellent rate capability, and retains over 93% of its initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 1 C with nearly 100% Coulombic efficiency. Title: Ethical reasoning and responsible use of ChatGPT in higher education: Integrating technology acceptance and moral cognition
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT into higher education has raised important questions about how students evaluate the ethical implications of AI-assisted academic practices and whether those evaluations are linked to intentions to use these tools responsibly. While previous research has largely focused on technology adoption and acceptance, it has paid less attention to the relationship between ethical reasoning and intentions to use these tools responsibly. This study develops and tests an integrated framework that combines the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and moral cognition theory to examine how technology perceptions and academic and cognitive factors relate to students’ ethical reasoning and intentions to use ChatGPT responsibly. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design among business and management students in Oman and analysed the data using structural equation modelling. The findings indicate that perceived ease of use, academic pressure, and moral disengagement are positively associated with ethical reasoning, whereas perceived usefulness is not significantly associated with ethical reasoning. Ethical reasoning is positively associated with behavioural intention to use ChatGPT responsibly. In contrast, ChatGPT usage does not significantly moderate the relationship between academic pressure and ethical reasoning. These findings suggest that students’ responsible-use intentions are associated with their ethical evaluations of ChatGPT-assisted academic practices, while conventional technology acceptance perceptions and usage frequency alone offer a more limited explanation of ethical reasoning. The study contributes to emerging research on responsible generative AI use by extending TAM beyond conventional adoption outcomes and integrating it with a moral cognition perspective. It highlights the relationship between ethical reasoning and responsible-use intentions while distinguishing ethical evaluation from technology acceptance and usage frequency. The findings also provide context-specific evidence from Omani higher education, while recognising the limitations of the cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, and a context-specific sample. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Deep contrastive multi-view spatio-temporal clustering for stock volatility prediction
Abstract: Forecasting extreme stock volatility from candlestick patterns, investor commentary, and macroeconomic indicators requires reconciling views with different noise levels, temporal scales, and statistical distributions. We formulate this problem as cluster-guided multi-view forecasting: the representation and clustering modules learn latent market regimes from historical input windows, while a cluster-to-class mapping calibrated only on the training period assigns the regimes to future-return classes. We propose DCMVC-TRANS, which couples domain-adversarial low-level alignment with instance- and cluster-level contrastive objectives, Transformer-based cross-view interaction, quality-aware view weighting, and local–global assignment alignment. This coupling is designed to preserve complementary view information while preventing a noisy or dominant view from determining the consensus representation. Experiments on 238 small- and mid-cap stocks show that DCMVC-TRANS obtains the best three metrics at the 5-day horizon, the best accuracy at the 20-day horizon, and the best recall and F1-score at the 60-day horizon among the compared methods. Long-only backtests further show the highest Sharpe ratio at all three horizons. These results support the use of cluster-guided heterogeneous representation learning for robust stock volatility prediction. © 2026

Title: Supporting initial teacher education student creativity and critical thinking using active constraints in assessment: A scoping review
Abstract: Assessment design plays a critical role in shaping student learning in higher education, particularly in disciplines where creativity is both a learning outcome and a pedagogical approach. In Initial Teacher Education (ITE), this role is intensified, as assessment tasks often function as the primary site of learning for time-poor students and simultaneously model pedagogical practice for future teachers. While constraints are frequently embedded within assessment tasks, their role in supporting creativity remains under-theorised and inconsistently articulated in the literature. This scoping review examines how constraints are used within assessment tasks that aim to foster creativity and/or critical thinking in social sciences, humanities, education and creative arts courses in higher education in order to consider implications for enhancing creativity through assessment tasks in ITE. Using a scoping review framework, 28 empirical studies published since 2000 were identified and analysed thematically. Six key themes emerged: the role of prior experience, constraints as catalysts for creativity, task design and flexibility, rubrics and scaffolding as support structures, the domain-specificity of creativity, and the presence of “invisible architectures” in task design. Findings indicate that constraints function as powerful pedagogical mechanisms when they are intentionally designed, aligned with disciplinary practices, and calibrated to student readiness. However, many studies prioritise creative outcomes without sufficiently detailing the task conditions that shape them. Drawing on these findings, the paper positions constraints as active contributors to assessment design and introduces a design-oriented framework to support educators in making constraints explicit and pedagogically purposeful. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Artificial intelligence and generative AI in entrepreneurship education: A systematic review of competency development, entrepreneurial intention, and the sustainability disconnect
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education increasingly deploys artificial intelligence (AI), yet claims that it builds entrepreneurial competence and advances sustainability rest on an unexamined evidence base. This review asks what that evidence supports, and what it does not. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and Web of Science searches yielded 21 empirical studies with approximately 7800 unique participants across 14 countries. Studies were stratified as generative, broader or analytical AI, quality was appraised item by item with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and every conclusion was tested by sensitivity analysis. CIMO logic specified the question; TCM-ADO organised the synthesis. AI was positively associated with entrepreneurial intention in every study that measured it, but its magnitude cannot be established: the largest estimates come from the lowest-quality studies, and few report uncertainty estimates. Competency development, the assumed mechanism, rests almost entirely on non-generative AI studies and is untested for generative systems. Self-efficacy operates as a boundary condition, raising an equity concern no study measures. Nominal relevance to the Sustainable Development Goals is widespread, yet none measured a sustainability outcome or named an environmental goal. It supplies a stratified, quality-weighted evidence base and shows that closing the sustainability gap requires theory and instruments, not more intention surveys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance. © 2026

Title: Investigating the interplay between public art, urban design, and national identity: Case of the UAE
Abstract: Public art and culturally responsive urban environment play a crucial role in shaping national identity, particularly in culturally diverse and rapidly evolving societies like the UAE. This study examines how different forms of public art, their integration into urban spaces, and digital platforms influence perceptions of national identity. Grounded in Social Identity Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and Public Space Theory, it employs structural equation modeling (SEM) and thematic analysis using data from 543 respondents across UAE emirates. The SEM model explains 40.3% of the variance in Perceived National Identity (PNI), emphasizing the significant role of public art and digital platforms in cultural engagement. Mediation analysis highlights the importance of interactive experiences in strengthening cultural connections, while thematic analysis identifies cultural integration, community involvement, and sustainability as key themes. Findings suggest that combining traditional Emirati artistic elements with modern digital technologies enhances inclusivity and engagement. However, the limited direct impact of urban design on national identity highlights the need for culturally relevant elements to maximize its effectiveness. By integrating quantitative and qualitative insights, this study offers clear implications for policy and practice by recommending participatory planning, integration of heritage-based design elements and use of digital platforms to enhance cultural visibility and engagement. It provides a practical framework for urban planners, cultural policymakers, and designers to develop inclusive public spaces that reinforce national identity in the UAE. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Motivations in Chinese costume travel photography: An evolutionary psychology perspective
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourist photography has shifted from passive sightseeing to active narrative construction. Existing research has revealed the proximate motives of such behavior centered on identity construction, but the ultimate motives remain underexplored. Using a qualitative research design, this study explores motivations in Chinese costume travel photography by applying three interpretive lenses derived from evolutionary psychology, namely performative affiliation, temporary status, and scripted exploration. The findings indicate that participants' motivations are satisfied in Chinese costume travel photography as follows: temporary immersion and affiliation are gained from symbolic imitation and contextual co-performance; contextualized status enhancement is acquired by enacting ideal identities and collecting digital validation; and novelty seeking is met through experiences grounded in symbolic imagination and pre-arranged scripts. This study provides insights into the ultimate drivers of tourists’ surface motivations and the possible satisfaction mechanisms of deep evolutionary motives in Chinese costume travel photography. It also offers practical insights for tourism experience design and marketing by focusing on the satisfaction of deep motives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Bolstered Interfacial Field Chemistry for Deep Fast-Charging Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
Abstract: Deep fast-charging capability has become the core pursuit for practical applications of aqueous zinc metal batteries, yet it is critically impeded by unfavorable interfacial field evolution at the electrode/electrolyte interface under high-current–density conditions. The coexistence of sluggish Zn2+ desolvation, competitive H2O reduction corrosion, uneven electric field, and concentration field collectively leads to poor rate performance. To tackle these issues, a bolstered interfacial field chemistry strategy was developed via sulfosuccinic acid to precisely regulate the physicochemical and electrochemical properties within the inner Helmholtz plane. The tuned interfacial field comprises a homogeneous distribution of interfacial ions and electric fields, promoting fast desolvation and interfacial electron transfer. Consequently, the modified Zn||Cu asymmetric cells deliver an outstanding average Coulombic efficiency of 99.48% over 1600 cycles at 2 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, the modified Zn||Zn symmetric cells demonstrate exceptional stability under challenging conditions of 5 mA cm−2, 2 mAh cm−2 (over 1600 h), and 10 mA cm−2, 10 mAh cm−2 (over 675 h, depth of discharge = 17.08%). Impressively, a substantial cumulative capacity of 3500 mAh cm−2 is attained at 10 mAh cm−2 and a 56.93% Zn utilization rate. Besides, the enhanced Zn (10 µm) ||I2 (10.87 mg cm−2) full cell sustains over 1490 cycles at 1 A g−1 with 77.13% capacity retention and a harsh N/P ratio of 2.31. Remarkably, the Zn (10 µm) ||I2 pouch cell achieves over 680 cycles with an ultralow N/P ratio of 2.04. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Advanced optimization problems and solution methods for renewable energy integration - A bibliometric review
Abstract: The worldwide shift to sustainable energy supply has led to extensive incorporation of renewable energy sources into modern power systems incorporating specifically with wind-turbine and solar-photovoltaic systems. The stochastic and intermittent nature of such renewable energy sources, however, poses significant challenges in their operation and planning, especially regarding optimization and system coordination. This paper provides a detailed overview of various advanced optimization problems and solution methods for the integration of renewable energy in today's power systems. The study divides important optimization problems into three categories: active and reactive power management, uncertainty modelling and real-time stochastic operation of power systems. Coordination of active and reactive power resources is a critical issue that needs to be addressed to ensure voltage stability and reliability of the grid with high penetrations of renewables. The review also explores the concept of stochastic energy and reactive power markets, which entails optimizing ancillary services like voltage support and reactive power dispatch together, considering interactions between transmission system operators and distribution system operators. Moreover, the traditional optimization techniques such as linear programming, nonlinear programming and mixed-integer programming are compared with the new ones such as the intelligent and hybrid techniques. The current review is a structured reference which combines technical analysis with bibliometric analysis and indicates future research directions to develop resilient, intelligent and market-oriented power system optimization frameworks. © 2026 The Authors. Title: From fragmentation to integration: Rethinking the measurement of responsible management education
Abstract: Responsible Management Education (RME) has become a central agenda within business schools, as institutions seek to prepare graduates capable of addressing complex sustainability and societal challenges. Despite its growing prominence, approaches to evaluating RME remain fragmented, with studies measuring diverse educational, institutional and societal outcomes using inconsistent conceptualisations and indicators. This study systematically reviews the contemporary literature to examine how RME is currently measured and develop a more coherent conceptual framework for evaluation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature review of 62 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 using the Scopus database—an AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop thematic synthesis identified and consolidated 328 measurement-related concepts. The synthesis identified five complementary measurement domains: implementation, learning, behaviour, performance and impact, alongside five stakeholder groups: students, educators, institutions, industry and society. Building on these findings, the study proposes the Integrated Responsible Management Education Measurement Framework (IRMEF) as a multidimensional conceptual evaluation architecture that organises these domains and stakeholder perspectives. Rather than representing an empirically validated measurement model, the IRMEF provides a common conceptual vocabulary for organising existing approaches and guiding future evaluation and empirical validation. It provides a foundation for greater theoretical coherence and methodological consistency while supporting business schools, accreditation bodies, and policymakers seeking more balanced, multidimensional, and contextually appropriate approaches to RME evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Negotiating the contested: A framework for studying social issue negotiations
Abstract: Negotiation research has yielded useful insights on how to manage economic and business interactions by highlighting the importance of information sharing, trade-offs, and integrative solutions in achieving mutually beneficial outcomes. However, these approaches inadequately explain why negotiations over social issues such as immigration reform and climate change can remain deadlocked despite sustained efforts to reach agreement. Drawing upon recent research, we introduce an organizing framework that identifies three common features of such negotiations: moralization, identity threat, and public contestation. Moralization frames issues as matters of right and wrong, reducing willingness to compromise; identity concerns transform policy disagreements into threats to group membership and self-concept; and public scrutiny increases reputational risks and constrains flexibility. Together, these dynamics hinder engagement, value creation, and the quality of agreements. We review emerging interventions—including moral reframing, perspective sharing, high-quality listening, informal dialogue, and third-party mediation—that may mitigate these barriers. We conclude by highlighting the need for research examining how moral, identity, and public pressures interact across levels of analysis to shape social issue negotiation processes and outcomes. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Guo R.; Wang Y.; Gong T.; Li C.
Title: Advancing family bonding: A conditional framework from immersion to communitas
Abstract: A gap still exists between mobile social media-embedded modern family tourism and family relationship improvement. From a communitas perspective, this study proposes a conditional immersion-communitas relationship improvement framework to address this gap. Evidence from multi-wave surveys, an eye-tracking experiment, focus group interviews, and multiple field experiments shows that: (1) social media notification management is a key precondition for relationship improvement; compared with notification-off, visual, or auditory models, haptic notifications better sustain relationship improvement through the full chain mediation of immersion and communitas; (2) happiness experience type (eudaimonia vs. hedonia) moderates the immersion maintenance mechanism, with hedonia family members relying more on notification management; (3) family structure (intragenerational vs. intergenerational) also moderates the process: the positive effect of communitas on family relationship improvement is stronger in intergenerational families than in intragenerational ones. This study advances understanding of modern family tourism and offers practical implications for both individual management and external intervention. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: ID-free STFormer: An identity-free spatio-temporal transformer for day-ahead EV charging demand forecasting
Abstract: Day-ahead electric vehicle (EV) charging demand forecasting at the traffic analysis zone (TAZ) level is challenging owing to strong spatial heterogeneity and long-tailed demand distributions. Existing models commonly use node-identity embeddings to represent spatial heterogeneity; however, their direct injection into predictive representations may encourage location-specific memorization and local overfitting under long-tailed demand. We propose the Identity-Free Spatio-Temporal Transformer (ID-Free STFormer), which excludes explicit node-ID embeddings from the temporal forecasting representation while retaining spatial adaptation through graph-based feature aggregation. The model combines a fixed physical graph for local proximity, an adaptive graph for global context, and a Transformer-GRU module for 168-h-input to 24-h-ahead forecasting. Experiments on the UrbanEV dataset covering 275 TAZs in Shenzhen show that ID-Free STFormer achieves the lowest root mean square error (RMSE) and the highest coefficient of determination R2=0.91, reducing RMSE by 15.7% over the strongest graph-based baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ID-free modeling for peak-sensitive forecasting on fixed urban TAZ networks and motivate further validation across cities and unseen regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Development and characterization of an active and smart gelatin-alginate based packaging enriched with eggplant anthocyanin-rich extract
Abstract: Bio-functional films were developed based on a gelatin-alginate hydrocolloid matrix, incorporated with anthocyanin-rich powder extracted from eggplant peels at different concentrations (0.5-2 mg/mL). The incorporation of anthocyanin-powder induced significant modifications in the physicochemical and structural properties of the films. FTIR, XRD and DSC/TGA analyses revealed that anthocyanins promoted intermolecular interactions within the matrix, leading to a reorganization of the polymer structure, reduced crystallinity and enhanced thermal stability. These structural changes were associated with more homogeneous morphology and modified mechanical behavior, as evidenced by variations in tensile strength and elongation at break. In addition, anthocyanins incorporation significantly improved the optical properties, reducing lightness (L*) and yellowness (b*), and increasing redness (a*) of the films as well as the total color difference (ΔE), and subsequently, increasing their opacity, contributing to the global enhancement of the light barrier of the films.Regarding functional properties, the incorporation of anthocyanin-powder enhanced biological properties of the films in a dose-dependent manner at multiple endpoints: increased antioxidant activities against DPPH, ABTS and reducing power, in addition to antibacterial capacities against Gram positive (Bacillus cereus and Staphylococcus aureus) and Gram negative (Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherishia coli) bacteria, which was directly associated with their phenolic content. Moreover, the films exhibited pronounced pH-responsive colorimetric behavior and high sensitivity to ammonia, enabling rapid and visible changes in color which highlight their potential as intelligent indicators for monitoring food freshness.Overall, our findings demonstrate that gelatin-alginate films incorporating anthocyanin extract powder from eggplants peels holds as promise dual-functionality as smart and active packaging, suitable for real application on food products in order to enhance the quality and extending their shelf-life. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jin X.; Mou S.
Author full names: Jin, Xiaoyu (60968617900); Mou, Shandong (55551657500)
Title: Justifying membership fees through quality and pricing in a competitive supply chain
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: While membership-based retail has experienced substantial growth, how membership stores can justify membership fees through product quality remains underexplored from a supply chain perspective. This study examines a supply chain consisting of a manufacturer, a membership store, and a traditional retailer, where consumers differ in their perceived value of exclusive membership services and may exhibit the sunk cost effect generated by the prepaid membership fees. We investigate how this behavioural mechanism affects retail pricing and the manufacturer's quality investment. The results show that the sunk cost effect not only reshapes the membership store's pricing strategy but also affects the manufacturer's quality investment decision, thereby enabling the membership store to justify its membership fee. The equilibrium outcomes are jointly determined by the membership store's competitive advantage and the perceived membership fee. Based on these two dimensions, we derive a strategic decision matrix comprising four equilibrium regimes. We use several business cases to help understand how membership stores can adjust their quality and pricing decisions according to their specific characteristics to justify membership fees. This study thus translates analytical results into a managerial framework and provides managerial insights for membership stores’ strategic decision-making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Noncovalent interaction-driven self-assembly endows interfacial β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils with inhibitory activities against lipid-hydrolyzing enzymes
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: Pancreatic lipase (PL) and cholesterol esterase (CE) are dominant lipid-hydrolyzing enzymes involved in the digestion and absorption of lipids, making them attractive targets for obesity prevention. β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) can transform into amyloid fibrils with potential inhibitory activity against PL and CE because of its amphiphilic and self-assembling properties. In this study, Dielectric Barrier Discharge atmospheric cold plasma treatment was employed to regulate the fibrillation process of β-LG (P-β-LGF) at three stages of fibril growth, namely, the initial stage (t0), the end of the lag phase (t0.1), and the exponential phase (t0.9). P-β-LGF exhibited enhanced β-sheet content, increased surface hydrophobicity, enhanced colloidal stability, and superior emulsifying and foaming properties. Furthermore, the elongated fibrillar morphology of P-β-LGF with a high aspect ratio and large specific surface area facilitated multivalent binding to the surface of enzymes, which resembled a “grape-on-a-vine” arrangement with enhanced inhibition at the oil/water interface. P-β-LGF exhibited competitive inhibition towards PL and mixed-type inhibition towards CE, indicating structure-specific enzyme inhibition mechanisms that collectively reduced lipid hydrolysis by interfacial behavior. Results demonstrated that P-β-LGF delayed in vitro lipid digestion by modulating enzyme activity effectively, indicating its potential as a functional ingredient for obesity management and lipid-lowering food applications. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Zhuang Y.; Liu J.; Wang X.; Su R.; Yifan D.; Fang L.
Title: One cart, many channels: How real-time inventory visibility shapes trust and purchase continuity in cross-border omnichannel retail
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study isolates inventory data latency as an operational primitive of omnichannel retail, evaluating its impact on cross-channel purchase continuity and consumer trust. Utilizing a dual field design, a randomized customer-level feature-flag experiment was coupled with a staggered rollout of real-time inventory visibility (RTIV) infrastructure across 142 store nodes, capturing 812,406 sessions from 96,318 loyalty customers. Multilevel logistic regressions and Cox survival frameworks demonstrated that transitioning from a 4-h batch baseline to a 60-s real-time window significantly increased checkout completion rates from 34.7% to 41.9% (F = 256.63, p < 0.001; OR = 1.71) and suppressed the instantaneous hazard of cart abandonment by 26% (HR = 0.74, p < 0.01). Parallel mediation profiling confirmed that this operational lift functioned through behavioral trust restoration rather than technical page-rendering speed; real-time visibility systematically minimized programmatic verification loops, reducing behavioral Price-Check Exits from 22.6% to 9.8% (F = 190.45, p < 0.001). Cross-level interactions showed that performance gains concentrated heavily within time-sensitive buy-online-pickup-in-store paths (OR = 1.45, p < 0.01). High-dimensional stacked Difference-in-Differences models and price dispersion sensitivity matrices confirmed the causal robustness of these findings against localized promotional, competitive, and pricing confounders. Financially, the empirical conversion lift offsets upfront cloud and micro-services infrastructure costs, projecting a clear 13.8-month capital payback horizon. This study replaces traditional psychometric scales with objective digital trace logs, proving that underlying data processing latency acts as a structural constraint on corporate conversion velocity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The evolution of remote operating centres: Towards a new geography of mining
Abstract: In mining ‘remoteness’ was once a measure of isolation from other activities and communities. With the adoption of new digitalization technologies, ‘remote operations’ now more often refers to the management, monitoring and control of mining equipment, processes and infrastructure from locations which are geographically separate from the immediate extraction site. This paper reviews the evolution of remote operating centres in the sector and explores the nature and implications of the new geography of mining that they are helping to create. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Integrated energy recovery assessment from municipal wastewater treatment plants: a comparative techno-economic and risk study of activated sludge and UASB systems for electricity, biomethane, and hydrogen using the SIAELA and SIATER software
Abstract: Municipal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) hold substantial untapped energy-recovery potential through biogas valorization into electricity, biomethane, or hydrogen. This study presents the first systematic, integrated techno-economic and probabilistic risk assessment comparing two dominant treatment technologies, the Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket (UASB) reactor and the Activated Sludge System (ALS) with anaerobic sludge digestion, applied to Itajubá, Minas Gerais, Brazil (93,073 inhabitants). Two purpose-built, INPI-registered platforms were used: SIATER v2.0 (BR512026004510-0) for UASB and SIAELA v2.0 (BR512026004511-8) for ALS, each integrating eight modules from population projection to Monte Carlo risk analysis (5,000 simulations) and financial-leverage optimization. The ALS generates 3.9 times more methane (1,410 vs. 362 m3CH4/d) and 2.4 times more electricity, with an LCOE of US$0.276/kWh (UASB) vs. US$0.223/kWh (ALS). SMR hydrogen costs US$8.96–9.56/kg, above fossil parity (US$1.91/kg). Even with voluntary carbon credits (VCS AMS-I.D), neither route reaches a positive NPV: the best SIATER case (grid metering plus carbon) gives NPV = −US$210,720 (IRR = 6.82%; PB = 10.7 yr). CAPEX dominates risk in both systems (Spearman ρ = −0.94 for SIATER; −0.80 for SIAELA). Scale-sensitivity analysis (20,000–1,000,000 inhabitants) shows that neither route reaches a positive NPV at any scale under the Fisher hurdle rate; the UASB route's IRR rises with scale but never reaches the 24.71% MARR, whereas the ALS approaches grid-parity LCOE only at large scale. Results guide utility planners pursuing energy self-sufficiency in mid-sized Brazilian municipalities. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Lim W.M.
Author full names: Lim, Weng Marc (57193912670)
Title: From academic integrity to credential integrity: What does management education certify once artificial intelligence can produce the work?
Abstract: The debate on generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in management education has centered on whether students may use AI, yet the larger question is what student work can still prove. Once AI can draft and polish a case analysis, an essay, or slides, polished work stops being strong evidence of what a student can do. This article calls the resulting problem credential integrity (i.e., whether a business school can defend what its degree certifies when AI may have produced the graded work). Policies on detection, disclosure, and originality cannot solve this problem, given that all three ask who produced the work and leave intact the assumption that good work proves a capable student. In response, this article draws on assessment scholarship, policy research, and validity theory to propose a verified-judgment architecture in which high-stakes certification rests on unaided command of core concepts and methods, reasoning defended when questioned, positions reconsidered when challenged, learning transferred to changed conditions, and accountable decision making. The architecture is translated into program-level responsibilities for school leaders and redesigned assessments for teachers, neither of which requires a ban on AI or the false belief that an AI-free submission proves learning. A reality check of 84 business schools shows how far practice is from this standard, given that schools describe AI access, curriculum integration, and faculty development more fully than any proof of what the degree certifies and only one school in seven reports a safeguard (e.g., a defended capstone or work kept free of AI). © 2026 The Author

Title: E-recruitment adoption and candidate's intention to apply: The mediating role of person-organization fit and the moderating role of digital literacy
Abstract: E-recruitment is increasingly recognized as a strategic digital tool that enables organizations to attract and communicate with potential candidates more efficiently. As organizations continue to shift from traditional recruitment methods to internet-based platforms, understanding how job seekers respond to these systems has become increasingly important, particularly among Generation Z applicants who are highly exposed to digital technologies. However, despite the widespread adoption of e-recruitment, many candidates still fail to complete online job applications. Prior research has mainly emphasized the organizational benefits of e-recruitment, while limited attention has been given to the psychological and individual mechanisms through which e-recruitment adoption shapes candidates’ intention to apply (ITA). This study aims to examine the effects of perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) of e-recruitment on ITA among Vietnamese final-year students and recent graduates. It also investigates the mediating role of person–organization fit (POF) and the moderating role of digital literacy (DL). Adopting a quantitative approach, the study used convenience sampling and collected survey data from 368 valid respondents in Vietnam through a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that PU and PEOU positively influence both POF and ITA. POF significantly enhances ITA and mediates the relationships between e-recruitment adoption and application intention. In addition, DL significantly strengthens the effects of PU and PEOU on both POF and ITA. These findings highlight the importance of designing informative and user-friendly e-recruitment systems while recognizing DL as a critical condition influencing applicant responses in digital recruitment contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: On the interplay between multi-instance BPMN collaborations and the environment
Abstract: Nowadays, business processes are increasingly influenced by information from the surrounding physical environment and vice versa. This is especially evident in the presence of multi-instance participants able to move in and interact within a physical environment. In this regard, BPMN is a widely accepted standard for representing multi-party business processes in terms of collaboration diagrams, offering an expressive and understandable notation. However, BPMN, as well as its extensions, overlooks the support for the physical environment. In this paper, we describe the interplay between BPMN collaborations, including multiple instances of the same participant, and the physical environment. Specifically, we extend the BPMN meta-model with environmental concepts, defining environmental BPMN collaboration models. To facilitate a deeper understanding of the dynamics of these models, we provide a formal account of their semantics, addressing the handling of multiple instances of the same participant and incorporating time as a factor influencing process execution during interplay with the environment. Beyond defining a novel formalization, we propose BEAR, a tool that implements the formal semantics and supports modeling, animation, and debugging of environmental BPMN collaborations, extended to support multi-instance participants and time progression. We illustrate our findings through a fire-extinguishing multi-instance collaborative scenario. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Fundamentals of power system resilience: Concepts, models, and decision-making under extreme events
Abstract: Power systems are being reshaped by decarbonization, digitalization, and high shares of renewables. At the same time, increasingly severe extreme conditions expose the limits of traditional reliability frameworks, calling for risk-aware, resilience-oriented approaches to address high-impact, low-probability (HILP) events. In this context, this paper presents a comprehensive overview of the foundations of power system resilience. It revisits the transition from reliability to resilience, formalizes key concepts and metrics, and introduces advanced approaches for resilience assessment, including fragility-based modeling, cascading failure analysis, and tail-risk indicators. The paper further examines resilience-oriented investment planning, operational strategies across all event phases, and the role of distributed energy resources, microgrids, and cybersecurity. The analysis highlights that resilience extends reliability by focusing on extreme conditions, fundamentally reshaping decision-making and requiring coordinated strategies across infrastructure, operation, and governance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: From personality to prestige: A dual-method analysis of masstige consumption using PLS-SEM and fsQCA
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: “Masstige”, a new trend in marketing, represents a hybrid concept that stands for ‘prestige or luxury for the masses’. With the growing number of high-end middle class, there is a tendency among the people to have a premium product which is in between exclusive luxury and midrange products, accompanying with high quality and exclusivity at a reasonable price. However, research is limited about how internal psychological factors and external motivational factors affect consumer attitude and consumption of masstige brands. Hence, this study aims – to explore the status of masstige among the popular smartphone brands in Bangladesh using MMI (Masstige Mean Index), and to investigate the influence of internal (personality traits) and external (perceived product quality and perceived prestige value) factors on consumer attitude and consumption behavior of masstige brands. Besides, this study examines the moderating effect of materialism in the association between consumer attitude and masstige consumption. In total, 418 responses were gathered in study 1 to identify the masstige status of smartphone brands in Bangladesh and 341 responses were collected in study 2 from the same country utilizing a structured instrument and analyzed with PLS-SEM and fsQCA. The findings of study 1 represent that iPhone is appeared as masstige category; whereas, the outcomes of study 2 indicate that except neuroticism, all personality traits along with product quality and prestige value have positive impact on attitude towards masstige brands, which in turn affects the masstige consumption. Moreover, materialism strengthens the influence of consumers' attitude towards masstige consumption. The fsQCA results identified eight different configurations that successfully lead to masstige consumption. Additionally, the analysis highlighted five essential elements of perceived prestige value, conscientiousness, extraversion, openness, and attitude as necessary for achieving high levels of masstige consumption. In the milieu of masstige literature, this study strengthens the theory of masstige consumption by integrating the theory of personality traits. This study provides practical guidance for the marketers of masstige brands to uphold consumers' attitude and accelerate their masstige consumptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Traditional or simplified Chinese? Exploring the use of linguistic variants in tourism linguistic landscape
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: By employing a two-phase mixed-method research design (i.e. survey and interviews), this study investigates residents' and tourists' perceptions of the effectiveness of language variants of Chinese characters in public signage within Macao's tourism landscape. The findings reveal that while simplified Chinese may be favored for its practicality, traditional Chinese retains significant cultural and identity values among residents and enhances the travel experiences by signally authenticity. Additionally, the research highlights perceived cultural erosion among the local community and concerns over prioritizing tourists' needs at the expense of local identity. This study extends linguistic landscape scholarship by illustrating how script variants within a shared language carry distinct practical and symbolic meanings for different stakeholders. Finally, this research proposes an exploratory needs–affect–attachment framework and a theoretically informed model of tourism power relations to conceptualize these dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Stochastic inversion of multivariate uniform-distribution-preserving transformations
Abstract: A multivariate transformation of the unit cube with component transformations that are piecewise continuously differentiable and uniform distribution preserving (udp) is considered. A stochastic inverse transformation is defined using randomization to overcome the non-injective nature of the udp transformations. The inverse transformation preserves the uniform margins of a random vector distributed according to a copula and yields different copulas for different randomizations. A copula density transformation result for the multivariate stochastic inverse is proved and illustrated in the bivariate case. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Uncovering creative metacognition patterns in TVET innovation education: insight from an epistemic network analysis of students’ self-reflective assessments
Abstract: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) increasingly position creativity as a teachable competence in innovation and entrepreneurship education, yet little is known about how Creative Metacognition (CMC) elements are structurally interconnected and activated to facilitate creativity in TVET learners. To address this gap, this study provides an exploratory epistemic network analysis on structural mapping of CMC in TVET innovation and entrepreneurship course. Forty TVET learners completed a three-stage authentic Creative Problem-Solving task focused on venture design for a remote region. Their self-reflective assessments were segmented into 1,506 theory-driven semantic fragments and coded into Creative Strengths (CS), Creative Restrictions (CR), and Creative Contextual Knowledge (CK). Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) was employed to model the co-activation patterns and relational intensity among CMC elements. Results show that students with high scores exhibited a stronger connection between CS and CK, suggesting that contextual knowledge was framed as creative affordances. In contrast, low-scoring students demonstrated a stronger connection between CR and CK, suggesting that situational reasoning was more often associated with perceived barriers and may reflect constrained idea development despite contextual awareness. The study also provides evidence of associations between reflective CMC configurations and creative performance, offering implications for reflective scaffolding and TVET entrepreneurship task design. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Strategies of Designing High-Efficiency Electrolyte Additives for Aqueous Magnesium Batteries: A Review
Abstract: With the development of next-generation energy storage systems focusing on green, safe, and sustainable devices, aqueous magnesium (Mg)–air batteries have emerged as promising candidates owing to the intrinsic merits of the Mg metal anode, including low cost, large volumetric capacity, a highly negative electrode potential, and excellent safety. However, the high self-discharge rate and formed discharge products substantially impair the practical discharge performance of Mg anodes with poor anode utilization efficiency and low cell voltage. While anode alloying and electrolyte additive strategies can help mitigate this issue, designing highly efficient electrolyte additives that are compatible with the established anode remains a challenge. This review summarizes recent progress toward understanding the role of electrolyte additives for aqueous Mg batteries, provides insights into the discharge mechanism of Mg-based anode materials in different types of additive-containing electrolytes, and offers strategies for designing high-efficiency mixtures of electrolyte additives. Moreover, a highly promising direction of AI-supported and robotic workflows for the future fast design of advanced electrolyte additives for aqueous Mg batteries is discussed. Title: Extruded cornmeal improves freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough by restricting water mobility
Abstract: In frozen cereal-based foods, water is not only a structural plasticizer but also a destructive phase-change medium. Temperature fluctuations during frozen storage promote water migration and ice recrystallization, which weaken the gluten-starch matrix and lead to cracking, water loss, and textural deterioration. Existing strategies mainly rely on gluten reinforcement or hydrocolloid addition, whereas starch-rich non-gluten ingredients are often regarded as formulation diluents because they disrupt dough network formation. This study investigated whether extrusion can convert cornmeal into a functional water-state regulator that improves the freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough. Wheat flour (CK), wheat flour containing 15% native cornmeal (NC-15) and wheat flour containing 15% extruded cornmeal (ECM-15) were compared. ECM-15 significantly reduced freezable water content (from 71.85% in CK to 51.63%, a reduction of 28.14%) and melting enthalpy, and showed the lowest water loss throughout five freeze-thaw cycles. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) analysis revealed restricted water mobility in ECM-containing dough, indicating that extrusion-modified starch immobilized water fractions that would otherwise contribute to freezing and migration. Consistently, ECM-15 exhibited higher water-holding capacity, swelling power and farinograph water absorption, together with lower pasting viscosity and setback. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman analyses indicated that these effects arose from extrusion-induced amorphization and short-range disordering of starch, rather than simple cornmeal addition. Notably, this improvement was achieved despite reduced dough mixing stability, indicating that extrusion-induced water-state regulation offers a label-friendly strategy for frozen dough improvement, distinct from conventional gluten reinforcement. More broadly, physically modified cereal ingredients can be designed as functional phase-state regulators in frozen staple foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets. © 2026
