Authors: Liu M.; Liu G.; Guo C.; Sun H.; Ta N.; Wu J.; Yang W.; Li M.
Title: Potato LAI estimation by enhancing spectral features of reflectance and fluorescence to improve application potential among different varieties
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Abstract: Accurate leaf area index (LAI) estimation of potato crops is of great importance for precision management in potato cultivation. Vegetation indices (VIs) derived from spectral reflectance are widely used for LAI estimation but suffer from saturation under high LAI conditions, limiting accuracy and robustness across varieties. Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence in the near-infrared region (SIFNIR), closely linked to canopy photosynthetic activity and light absorption, provides complementary information for LAI estimation. However, heterogeneous light radiation and structural differences among canopies interfere with SIFNIR extraction. To address these challenges, we propose an approach that enhances and integrates spectral reflectance and fluorescence features to improve LAI estimation across 40 potato varieties. Seven VIs were calculated and their saturation effects were discussed. SIFNIR was extracted based on Three-band Fraunhofer line discriminator (3FLD) method and normalized by absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (APAR) and canopy coverage (Cov) to reduce radiative and structural effects. Potato LAI estimation models of different varieties were constructed using the Random Forest (RF) method. The results showed that (1) NLI and MSAVI were reliable VIs for assessing potato canopy growth. (2) APAR and Cov showed stronger relationships with LAI, and SIFNIR normalized by these factors could reduce interference from canopy structure. (3) The RF model of reflectance and fluorescence feature fusion achieved the best performance, with prediction set Rp2 of 0.68, 0.70, 0.68, 0.70, and RMSEp of 0.50, 0.45, 0.50, 0.45 for all varieties, early season, mid-season and late season varieties, respectively. These results demonstrate the application potential of reflectance and fluorescence fusion to improve potato LAI estimation, and provide support for precise management in potato cultivation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Green power markets in selected Latin American countries: Experiences and trends
Abstract: Latin America is undergoing a significant transformation of its electricity systems as countries strive to advance their energy transitions through cleaner technologies, new business models, and strengthened policy frameworks. Despite long-standing reliance on hydropower, the region has experienced both a rapid expansion of non-hydro renewable capacity and, unexpectedly, a parallel growth in thermal generation. However, comparative understanding of how renewable energy policies and emerging green power markets have evolved across the region remains limited. This paper addresses this gap by analyzing the emergence and evolution of green power markets across twelve Latin American countries, examining renewable energy policies, green electricity products, and the mechanisms that shape market development. We compare policy design, investment incentives, and the deployment of wind, solar, biomass, and geothermal technologies, as well as the role of auctions, fiscal measures, grid-access regulations, and energy attribute certificates (EACs). Our findings reveal convergence in the types of policy instruments adopted, but substantial differences in their implementation and green power market development. Overall, market development remains limited and fragmented. The analysis suggests that deeper renewable integration will require clearer long-term policy signals, stronger regulatory coordination, and incentives that mobilize both public and private actors. EAC systems present an opportunity to complement this transition, but their effectiveness depends on regulatory stability, transparency, and market participation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Covalent Organic Framework-Anchored Carbon Nanotubes Enabling Ultra-Thin Robust Polyimide Films for High-Specific-Power Flexible GaAs Solar Cells
Abstract: Free-standing polymer films that are ultra-thin, lightweight, and robust hold significant promise for applications in flexible electronics. However, their performance has been constrained by the challenge of simultaneously enhancing mechanical strength and reducing density. Herein, an ultra-thin and robust polyimide (PI)-based covalent organic framework-modified multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT-COF) film is demonstrated for high-specific-power flexible GaAs solar cells. The film exhibits a high Young’s modulus of 1.53 GPa, a tensile strength exceeding 97.53 MPa, and a low density of 0.73 g cm−3, representing a 45.1% reduction in density. The incorporation of 3D interconnected layered and porous MWCNT-COF significantly enhances the film’s mechanical properties while reducing its density. The synergistic effects of robust MWCNTs and covalently bonded COF layers, combined with the thermally stable PI molecular structure, impart exceptional strength and lightness to the film. Computational studies further confirm that COF-grafted MWCNTs effectively modify the polyamide acid matrix, substantially improving the mechanical properties of the PI films. Moreover, flexible dual-junction and triple-junction GaAs solar cells were successfully fabricated using 6 µm-thick MWCNT-COF/PI composite films, delivering outstanding specific powers of 8998 and 7749 W kg−1, along with efficiencies of 26.6% and 31.5% (AM0), respectively. These results underscore the potential for high-performance applications in space and energy systems. This work offers valuable insights into the development of high-performance flexible GaAs solar cells based on ultra-thin and robust PI films for a wide range of applications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: AI-Driven Acceleration of Nanomaterials Development: Advanced Computational Tools and Techniques
Abstract: Nanomaterials, which range in size from 1 nm to 100 nm, have special physical, chemical and electrical characteristics that make them extremely promising for use in environmental technologies, electronics, energy and medicine. The discovery and development of nanomaterials has been greatly expedited in recent years by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and sophisticated computer techniques. This review examines how machine learning (ML) and AI techniques, along with computational methods like density functional theory (DFT), Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, can be used to predict material properties and optimize synthesis processes. Research indicates that when compared to conventional trial-and-error methods, AI-assisted models can improve prediction accuracy for nanomaterial attributes while cutting computational screening time by up to 60–80%. Furthermore, faster identification of ideal synthesis conditions and material architectures is made possible by AI-driven automation and robotic experimentation platforms. Notwithstanding these developments, problems with toxicity assessment, environmental effect assessment and AI model interpretability still exist. All things considered, the combination of AI and computational modeling offers a strong foundation for boosting nanomaterial innovation and aiding in the creation of safer and more effective materials for upcoming technological uses. © 2027, World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Dynamic event-triggered adaptive cooperative control for robotic manipulator with output constraints and model uncertainties
Abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive fuzzy-based dynamic event-triggered adaptive cooperative control to address the challenge of achieving high-performance control for robotic manipulators under model uncertainties and output constraints. This strategy designs a signal-processing-based backstepping control scheme and an energy-transformation-based error port-Hamiltonian (EPH) control scheme, respectively. The uncertain dynamics of the system are approximated through adaptive fuzzy logic systems, while the output of the system is constrained by boundary constraints gain. Furthermore, an adaptive cooperative control mechanism is designed, which dynamically adjusts the weighting between the two control schemes. This mechanism integrates the advantages of the fast response from the signal-processing-based scheme and the minimal energy consumption from the energy-transformation-based scheme. This paper also proposes a dynamic event-triggered control (ETC) mechanism, whose triggering threshold adaptively adjusts according to the system state, achieving dynamic matching between the triggering frequency and the system status. Theoretical analysis shows that all signals in the closed-loop system are bounded, the output does not violate the constraints, and the ETC mechanism avoids Zeno behavior. Experimental results verify that the proposed method can achieve high-precision trajectory tracking under disturbances and output constraints, while effectively reducing the control signal update frequency, demonstrating excellent comprehensive performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: A knowledge graph and hierarchical learning framework for food safety risk identification and traceability: A case study on meat products
Abstract: Food safety risk analysis is challenged by fragmented information among regulatory standards, production processes, and inspection data, which limits the integrated understanding of risk characteristics and potential origins. This study proposes an integrated framework for food safety risk identification and traceability by integrating knowledge representation and data-driven inference. A dual-layer knowledge graph (DLKG) was constructed to bridge food safety standards (as constraint knowledge) with Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP)-based process knowledge (as a mechanism layer), enabling cross-layer reasoning from detection indicators to Critical Control Points (CCPs). To address imbalanced and long-tail distributions in inspection data, a Hierarchical Cascade Ensemble Learning (HCEL) model was developed to perform hierarchical risk identification, including category recognition and fine-grained indicator inference, with attention-based feature representation and a Top-k constraint strategy. A large language model was further employed to organize model outputs and retrieved knowledge into coherent textual outputs, without contributing to decision-making. Using 5995 non-compliant meat-product records, HCEL achieved 91.99% Top-1 and 98.42% Top-2 accuracy for risk-category identification, with Macro-F1 and Macro-Recall exceeding 85%. Hit@3 and MRR for specific risk indicators reached 83.82% and 73.51%, respectively. Temporal out-of-sample validation showed some performance degradation when 2024 inspection data were used for testing, but HCEL generally maintained better performance than the comparative models. The proposed framework enhances the identification and interpretation of non-compliance patterns and may support risk-oriented inspection prioritization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The Fragility of Collective Action in Community Forest Management: Social Feedbacks, Trust, and Cooperation Dynamics
Abstract: In community forest management, cooperation is rarely a one-time decision. It depends on whether local actors continue contributing time, labor, and resources year after year. We examine this problem with a system dynamics model that follows changes in trust, reputation, reciprocity, perceived benefits, and free-riding. The model adapts an earlier structure to the case of ejido La Loma, Mexico. The case material guided several modeling decisions, especially the choice of variables and the interpretation of the scenarios. It did not, however, provide enough information for full empirical calibration. The simulations show that trust and reputation may sustain cooperation even as participation declines. Over time, however, the loss of active members can weaken monitoring and place collective action at risk. One result is particularly relevant: a favorable starting point does not guarantee long-term stability. We use the model to think through these possible trajectories, rather than to forecast La Loma''s future. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Materials–Structure–Hardware–Algorithm Co-Driven Hierarchical Optimization for Flexible Sensors
Abstract: Flexible electronics represent a paradigm shift in modern electronics, with flexible sensors serving as pivotal components in these systems. Despite significant advances driven by innovations in materials, structures, hardware, and algorithms, conventional design approaches that focus on optimizing individual hierarchies have inherent performance trade-offs, limiting further development. This review contends that future performance enhancements can no longer rely solely on breakthroughs in separate components. Still, it must adopt a new co-design paradigm spanning the “materials–structure–hardware–algorithm” hierarchy. In this review, we systematically organized the research landscape and representative advances across these four key hierarchies, analyzed the importance and recent breakthroughs in hierarchical synergy, and established a forward-looking theoretical framework to foster innovation and development in the field of flexible sensing. Authors: He X.; Choi Y.; Su Y.; Fan D.; Cui L.; Lei J.
Title: Beyond the accession event: Joint regional membership duration and completion of cross-border acquisitions
Abstract: Cross-border acquisition (CBA) completion is often hindered by institutional barriers, imposing substantial costs on deal participants. While regional integration aims to reduce such barriers, prior research predominantly treats regional integration as a discrete accession event, leaving post-accession adaptation dynamics and their underlying mechanisms underexplored. Drawing on new institutional economics and social learning theory, we argue that joint regional membership duration increases CBA completion likelihood, with country-dyadic M&A stock serving as the mediating carrier via the sequential pathways of institutional alignment and social learning. We further examine how initial regulatory distance and cultural distance condition this mechanism. Using a sample of 8009 announced CBAs across the European Union (2010–2022), we find support for the mediation pathway and show that both regulatory and cultural distance weaken this indirect effect. This study advances the literature by moving beyond discrete event-based integration framing and refines the understanding of cross-national distance within integrated regional blocs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Shi J.; Zhu L.
Title: Assessing drone freight demand in intercity mountainous corridors: A discrete choice modeling approach with capacity-constrained simulations
Abstract: The low-altitude economy, as an innovative economic model utilizing low-altitude airspace resources, is reshaping traditional transportation systems through applications like drone logistics, demonstrating pronounced advantages in complex terrains. While existing research predominantly focuses on macro-level airspace deployment, meso-level demand analysis, and micro-level route optimization of drones in passenger transportation, the meso-level demand analysis lacks consideration of drone capacity constraints and the impact of drone allocation across different modes and regions on service levels and traffic volume in freight transportation. This study adapts established discrete choice models to a novel and complex context by explicitly integrating strict capacity constraints into the demand simulation—an aspect largely overlooked in existing applications. Based on stated preference data from four typical mountainous intercity freight corridors in Fujian Province, China, market shares of pure-drone, pure-road, and drone-road intermodal modes are simulated under varying service attributes. Key findings reveal: (1) Shippers across different corridors exhibit significant variations in their preference for drone modes, which correlate with cargo attributes and drone capacity; (2) Competitiveness enhancement requires prioritizing capacity reallocation to corridors with higher cargo unit value and total cargo value (such as the Fuqing-Fuzhou corridor) and reducing waiting time. In particular, the value of cargo transported by drones (including pure-drone and drone-road intermodal modes) increases from 7.87 million Chinese Yuan in the current scenario to 44.57 million Chinese Yuan in the multi-factor optimization scenario (capacity reallocation + waiting time reduction + freight subsidies). This study theoretically offers a quantitative method to understand the relationship between drone service levels and modal share under capacity constraints, and practically provides decision-making support for developing strategies to enhance the competitiveness of drone transportation in various freight corridor scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Territorializing the sea: fragmented operational control in offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia
Abstract: The expansion of offshore tin mining transforms the sea into a space of extraction, yet territorial claims over this space do not necessarily translate into operational control. Studies of territorialization have largely focused on the formation of claims rather than on the processes through which such claims are converted into operational control. This article examines the territorialization of offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia, through three interrelated analytical moments: territorial claims, securing access, and operational control. This qualitative study draws on fieldwork comprising interviews with 23 informants and observations, supplemented by a review of relevant literature and an analysis of regulatory documents, corporate reports, and news coverage. The findings show that exploration and regulatory arrangements produce epistemic and legal claims over marine space but do not, in themselves, enable mining operations. Companies and their local networks must still secure access by cultivating and representing support, engaging village institutions and local intermediaries, negotiating benefits, and making personal approaches to key actors. Their success varies across locations, shaped by local power relations, actor legitimacy, and fisher resistance. Consequently, operational control is contingent, partial, fragmented, and continuously negotiated: mining operations can proceed in some locations, whereas elsewhere territorial claims remain in force without being translated into operational control. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Store coolness in luxury fashion: Antecedents, outcomes, and the moderating role of price consciousness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: In the context of luxury fashion stores, this study investigates the mediating role of the dimensions of store coolness (extraordinary, subcultural, iconic, and high status) in linking service quality of employees, store display, and store creativity with customers' behavioral intention and positive word-of-mouth (WOM). Additionally, the study examines whether price consciousness moderates any of these relationships. To gain a deeper understanding of how coolness is perceived in luxury fashion stores, we collected customer insights through interviews with 16 frequent store visitors. We then tested our proposed model using a survey administered to shoppers immediately after they visited luxury stores (N = 213). Our results indicate that the extraordinary and subcultural dimensions of coolness positively mediate the effects of store display and creativity on behavioral intention and positive WOM. However, the iconic dimension did not play a mediating role, while the high status dimension negatively mediated these paths, including those involving service quality. Finally, we found that price consciousness weakens the path from store creativity to the studied outcomes via the extraordinary dimension. Building on these findings, we provide managerial insights for designing luxury fashion store experiences that foster store coolness and positive customer responses. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Integrated utilities for Net-Zero: empirical evidence and policy framework for the global energy–water–digital transition
Abstract: This study develops and empirically validates an integrated framework linking energy, water, and digital infrastructures as mutually reinforcing drivers of global sustainability. Using a balanced panel of 45 countries (25 OECD and 20 emerging economies) from 2000–2023, we construct a Triple Transition Readiness Index (TTRI) and estimate dynamic panel models (System GMM) to test the Triple Transition Hypothesis. Results confirm strong complementarities: digital infrastructure amplifies the decarbonisation and efficiency gains of energy and water transitions. A simultaneous 10 % increase in renewable-energy deployment and broadband penetration reduces CO2 intensity by an additional 0.9 %. Emerging economies display greater synergies, revealing leap-frogging potential. The paper introduces the Triple Transition Efficiency Frontier (TTEF) and the Integrated Utility Governance (IUG) model, showing how coordinated regulation and investment across utilities accelerate cost-effective progress toward net-zero targets. Findings provide actionable insights for integrated policy design in the global sustainability transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Unveiling research trends in artificial intelligence adoption based on the UTAUT: A bibliometric analysis supporting SDGs and future outlook
Abstract: The development of AI adoption across disciplines has become a major global concern, especially with the UTAUT model that runs concurrently. This study aims to map research trends on AI adoption within the UTAUT model in conceptual, intellectual, and social structures. The research utilises a bibliometric approach from the Scopus database for the period 2018-2025 on related topics. Data analysis was conducted descriptively using Biblioshiny (Rstudio). The study found a very positive and significant development in research on AI adoption within the UTAUT model across various disciplines, aligning with the SDGs, particularly points four, nine, and seventeen. The countries that contributed most were China and the USA. Interesting themes for studying the development of UTAUT model implications include social influence, performance expectancy, behaviour, perceived risk, digital literacy, and AI anxiety. In SDG 4, the adoption of AI in higher education is crucial by incorporating perceived risk and digital literacy to achieve effective personalised learning. In SDG 9, organisational and corporate levels within managerial structures are important for combining structural and psychological factors that influence AI adoption. AIMDSS in the healthcare sector is essential for supporting health innovation and infrastructure. Meanwhile, for SDG 17, discovering best practices for AI adoption across various fields needs to be accelerated, particularly in Africa, South America, and most of Eastern Europe. The implications of this research point to the development of institutional guidelines for AI adoption and the exploration of the UTAUT model. By highlighting the evolving role of contextual, ethical, and governance-related factors, this study provides a foundation for aligning AI adoption strategies with sustainable development objectives and informs future empirical and policy-oriented research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Diffusion-based cross-modal generation for audio-driven facial expression and emotion recognition
Abstract: The combination of speech signals and facial expressions can be very useful for the research. If facial expressions can be developed using speech signals, then it will be very easy to recognize the state of human. Generation of facial expressions from audio signals required a cross model correlation. There are some predefined methods which are not very robust as represented in existing results. This paper proposes a framework based on Diffusion-based Contrastive Learning with Multimodal Fusion (DCL-MF). The framework can generate facial expressions as well as emotion recognition. In order to enable robust and discriminative cross-modal feature learning, the suggested framework uses different learning to align audio and visual representations within a shared emotion-aware latent space. A diffusion-based generative model gradually synthesizes high-fidelity and temporally coherent facial expressions driven by speech signals, trained on these aligned embeddings. To further improve emotion recognition performance, a multimodal fusion module combines audio messages with the generated facial features. Benchmark audio-visual emotion datasets such as CREMA-D, RAVDESS, and IEMOCAP are used to assess the efficacy of the suggested DCL-MF framework. Through typical emotion recognition accuracies of 82.6% on CREMA-D, 85.1% on RAVDESS, and 78.4% on IEMOCAP an improvement of 3%–6% over current baselines—experimental results show that DCL-MF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. Additionally, better Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) scores, which show more realistic and emotionally consistent facial dynamics, demonstrate that the suggested model achieves superior facial expression generation quality. These findings demonstrate that the suggested DCL-MF framework is efficient and scalable for audio-driven affective computing applications by combining diffusion-based generation with contrastive cross-modal alignment, which greatly improves both facial expression synthesis and emotion recognition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Multi-horizon solar irradiance forecasting under variable sky conditions through CNN–TCN feature learning and XGBoost
Abstract: Multi-horizon solar irradiance nowcasting is highly sensitive to rapidly varying atmospheric conditions. Traditional statistical models such as persistence and autoregressive integrated moving average are computationally efficient but often degrade under strong atmospheric variability, whereas physical models based on numerical weather prediction remain constrained by spatial resolution, initialization delay, and computational cost. Machine learning methods such as extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) improve nonlinear regression performance, but when used alone they do not explicitly capture temporal dependencies. Deep learning models, including convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal convolutional network (TCN), can learn temporal patterns, yet maintaining stable accuracy across multiple forecast horizons remains challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a hybrid CNN–TCN–XGBoost framework in which CNN and TCN extract multi-scale temporal features and XGBoost performs horizon-specific regression. The model is evaluated over forecast horizons from 1 to 30 min using independent 2018 and 2021 datasets covering clear-sky, mixed, overcast, and highly variable atmospheric regimes. The results show notable improvements over the 2-State benchmark, including normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) reductions of approximately 8% at 2 min and 22% at 10 min in the aggregated 2018 evaluation, while preserving smooth error growth with increasing horizon. Day-level validation across six representative atmospheric regimes provides further evidence of regime-dependent forecasting performance: on a highly variable day, error reductions reach about 38% at 10 min and 29% at 30 min, while on a stable clear-sky day the reduction reaches nearly 87% at 30 min. For the clear-sky subset, nRMSE is typically below 0.016 and remains below 0.032 even on the most challenging day. Therefore, the proposed CNN–TCN–XGBoost framework is best interpreted as a model that provides strong short- and intermediate-horizon performance and best or near-best accuracy across most evaluated regimes, while long-horizon performance remains dependent on atmospheric regime across diverse atmospheric conditions. These findings make it a promising solution for reliable real-time solar irradiance forecasting and photovoltaic operation. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Expand or carve up? Evaluating market dynamics of premium airline entry with extended synthetic control methods: Evidence from STARLUX airlines
Abstract: This study examines the effects of STARLUX Airlines' entry as a newly established premium full-service carrier on Taiwan's international air transport market. Using the synthetic control method (SCM) and an extended SCM framework, the analysis evaluates changes in passenger demand following the airline's entry, encompassing both single and multiple treated units, including individual routes and interconnected markets. A conditional growth model was subsequently employed to distinguish market expansion from demand redistribution. Results indicate that although only 9 out of 24 treated markets showed statistically significant expansion, STARLUX's entry still revealed latent demand and contributed meaningfully to overall market growth despite the relatively small size of STARLUX as compared to its primary competitors, China Airlines and EVA Airways. This effect was particularly evident in business-oriented and transfer-focused segments, while some tourism-driven and politically sensitive markets saw limited or negative responses. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the demand-side influence of premium airline entry, extending SCM to multi-unit and network-based applications, and providing a replicable framework for evaluating airline market interventions in liberalized environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Chatbot service quality in omnichannel retailing: Effects of ChatbotSQ on decision confidence and customer behavior
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: AI chatbots are increasingly being embedded in omnichannel retail ecosystems; however, research on how chatbot service quality relates to customer behavior is limited. In this paper, we conceptualize chatbot service quality (ChatbotSQ) as a formative construct comprising six dimensions: functional, integration, interface, safety, emotional, and personalization quality. Drawing on means-end chain theory, we examine decision confidence as a mechanism underlying the association between chatbot service quality and customers' share of time with the chatbot and omnichannel ecosystem lock-in and explore the moderating role of chatbot comfort level. We use partial least squares structural equation modeling, importance-performance map analysis, and necessary condition analysis to analyze survey data from the United States (N = 345) and Saudi Arabia (N = 302). The results show that chatbot service quality is positively associated with customers' share of time with the chatbot and omnichannel ecosystem lock-in in both countries. These relationships are mediated by decision confidence, which also emerged as a necessary condition for achieving both behavioral outcomes. Chatbot comfort level significantly moderates the relationship between ChatbotSQ and decision confidence in Saudi Arabia but not in the United States, indicating that this boundary condition is context-sensitive across the two samples examined. We also validate a condensed six-item ChatbotSQ measure that provides a parsimonious alternative for research and practice. These findings advance retailing research by showing that AI chatbot service quality is associated with behavioral outcomes through customers’ decision confidence. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Beyond positive attitude: What motivates stem undergraduates to engage in classroom discussions?
Abstract: Fostering active participation in classroom discussions remains a persistent challenge in higher education, particularly in STEM fields where lecture-based instruction remains prevalent. While positive attitudes are often considered an important predictors of participation in classroom discussions, this study examines a broader set of psychological factors associated with STEM undergraduates’ intention to participate in classroom discussions. We propose and test an integrated model incorporating attitude, subjective norms, perceived need, and self-efficacy. Using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) on data from 550 undergraduates from engineering-focused universities, the study examines the motivational factors associated with participation intention and willingness to recommend classroom discussions. Perceived need and self-efficacy showed the strongest statistical associations with both outcomes. Subjective norms were positively associated with participation intention but not willingness to recommend, whereas attitude did not demonstrate a significant unique effect in the full model. Additional analyses suggest that this pattern reflects the stronger explanatory role of perceived need when considered alongside students’ general evaluations of classroom discussions. These findings highlight the importance of perceived learning value and confidence in predicting students’ participation in classroom discussions and provide context-specific implications for discussion-based teaching in engineering education. Title: Non-covalent interactions between pectin and volatiles modulate flavor formation in goji berry (Lycium barbarum L.) during pulsed vacuum drying
Abstract: Pectin plays a crucial role in modulating the flavor attributes of goji berry. This study investigated dynamic variations of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), non-volatile organic compounds (NVOCs), and pectin fractions, as well as their interactions in goji berry during pulsed vacuum drying (PVD), focusing on the chelator-soluble pectin (CSP) fraction. The results showed that 121 differential VOCs (DVOCs) were identified throughout the PVD process. The transition from stage III to V, during which rapid moisture migration occurred, was determined as the critical period for flavor formation. NVOCs involving soluble sugars, organic acids and amino acids affected VOC profiles. CSP exhibited substantial nanostructural rearrangement and interconnected network reconstruction, showing strong negative correlations with key aroma-active compounds such as acetic acid and octanal. It was further revealed that CSP interacted with acetic acid predominantly through hydrogen bonding, while octanal binding likely involved both hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding. These non-covalent interactions inhibited pectin aggregation, reduced particle size, and promoted the formation of stable porous fibrous microstructure that may facilitate flavor retention. Therefore, these findings indicate that pectin regulates flavor formation during PVD not only through structural transformation but also via non-covalent interactions with VOCs. Title: Advancing bibliometric analysis: Evidence-based guidelines with insights from senior journal editors
Abstract: Bibliometric analysis is a powerful means of evaluating research. This article employs a sequential mixed-methods approach to enrich the understanding of bibliometric analysis and presents a structured guide to maximize the technique's benefits. A thematically synthesized narrative commentary on bibliometric review papers, based on input from 53 senior editorial members of leading hospitality and tourism journals, constitutes the study's foundation. Our evidence-based guidance provides scholars with a roadmap for conducting state-of-the-art bibliometric analyses. Title: Should generative AI be responsible to users? Developing and validating the user-generative AI psychological contract scale
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As GenAI becomes increasingly embedded in AI-enabled service interactions, users' evaluations of AI are extending from functional performance to expectations regarding responsibility and obligation. Drawing on Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) theory and psychological contract theory, this study defines the user–generative AI psychological contract (AIPC) as users' beliefs about the responsibilities and obligations GenAI should fulfill toward them during ongoing interaction and develops a corresponding scale. Study 1 used purposively recruited interviews (N = 26) to identify the construct content domain. Study 2 used two nonprobability online-panel samples of active GenAI users (N = 507 and N = 506) to develop the items and examine the factor structure, reliability, and construct validity. Study 3 used the same 506-case sample employed for structural validation in Study 2 to provide an initial test of the nomological network among AIPC, AI anthropomorphism, and co-creation intention. Results indicate that AIPC consists of three dimensions—the functional support contract, relational collaboration contract, and ethical safety contract—and forms a 16-item scale. Users reported the strongest expectations regarding ethical safety. Anthropomorphism was indirectly associated with co-creation intention through functional support and relational collaboration, but not through ethical safety. The findings extend psychological contract theory to user–AI relationships and provide a measurement tool for studying responsibility expectations toward GenAI. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Molecular and environmental indicators of Listeria monocytogenes persistence in food processing facilities: a multi sector approach
Abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a foodborne pathogen capable of persisting in food processing environments. This persistence results from interactions between strain-specific traits and environmental conditions. This study aimed to identify molecular and environmental indicators associated with L. monocytogenes persistence across high-risk food production sectors. Three environmental sampling events were conducted in nine facilities from seafood, vegetable, and pork (n = 3 each) sectors. In total 1097 samples were analysed for the presence of L. monocytogenes, the temperature, and surface characteristics, pH, humidity, temperature, and surface characteristics. L. monocytogenes was detected in 114 samples (≈10%), with the highest prevalence observed in the vegetable sector. Isolates were characterized by Whole Genome Sequencing and classified into persistent or transient clusters based on core genome multilocus sequence typing profiles. Persistent clusters were defined by ≤ 7 allelic differences and repeated detection across at least two sampling events, whereas transient isolates were detected only once. We identified 13 persistent clusters including 67 isolates, of which 42 were assigned to CC121, 9 to CC5, 5 to CC31, 4 to CC101, 4 to CC155, and 3 to CC412. Pangenome analysis identified several loci enriched among persistent isolates, including prophage-related loci, genes encoding transport systems such as TatA, TatC and EfeO, and genes involved in stress response mechanisms. Persistence was associated with higher total microbial counts and high humidity, with persistent isolates mainly detected under conditions exceeding 5–6 log CFU/mL of total microbial counts and 80% relative humidity. Overall, results highlight persistence arising from the interplay between bacterial genetic traits and environmental conditions, emphasizing the importance of integrated approaches for monitoring and control in food processing environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A novel Index-Organized storage model for modern in-memory database systems
Abstract: Large-scale data-intensive applications require high-throughput real-time data processing. Modern in-memory database systems maintain the primary data copy in main memory and support fast concurrent transactions and analytics on recent data. However, under hybrid workloads with long-running queries, pointer-chasing overhead becomes a major bottleneck that prevents these systems from sustaining high performance.In this work, we investigate the pointer-chasing bottleneck in modern in-memory database systems and propose a novel Index-Organized storage model for efficient reads and writes. Its key innovation is storing the latest versions within the leaf nodes of the tree index, combined with a cacheline-aligned node layout and cache-prefetching-assisted version chains, improving pointer chasing performance. We present three optimizations, i.e., pending version table, fine-grained memory management, and Index-SSN algorithm for supporting efficient transaction processing. We implement Index-Organized on an open-source in-memory database system. Experimental results show that Index-Organized achieves up to a 3× speedup over conventional row-store, column-store, and hybrid row-column storage models. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: 40 years of equity sensitivity: A theoretical and meta-analytic review of relations, roles, and remaining questions
Abstract: Organizational scholars have studied equity sensitivity (ES) for nearly half a century. Yet, a lack of synthesis in the ES literature suggests important questions remain regarding our understanding of the concept, its nomological network, the theoretical role(s) it may play in shaping employee attitudes and behaviors, and its relations to adjacent theories of equity and organizational justice. In the current work, we address these questions via a theoretical and meta-analytic review of the ES literature encompassing 117 articles, 144 samples, and 36,177 participants. In synthesizing the literature, we (1) describe and alleviate existing tensions surrounding the construct's conceptualization, (2) provide empirical insights regarding the construct's associations and relative importance in the prediction of key workplace outcomes, and (3) present an integrative model of ES's potential theoretical moderating role in equity and justice relationships. Our work provides clarity regarding ES's nomological network and offers critical directions for future scholarship. Specifically, we draw special attention to opportunities for new work exploring ES's potential as a key linking mechanism among equity and organizational justice theories. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: IrMn-Cluster-Based Artificial Metalloenzymes with Radiosensitized Systemic Antitumor Responses to Prevent Malignant Tumor Metastasis and Recurrence
Abstract: Developing radiosensitizing agents to amplify tumor-eradicating effects on primary, regional recurrence, and distant metastases plays a transformative role in modern cancer care. Here, we report the de novo design of biocatalytic artificial metalloenzymes with an IrMn-cluster-based redox center (IMM) to achieve radiosensitized systemic antitumor responses for preventing malignant tumor metastasis and recurrence. Notably, our findings indicate that Mn-organic ligands substantially enrich the electron density of Ir clusters, thereby optimizing their interaction with oxygen species and markedly enhancing the production of both reactive oxygen species and molecular oxygen. When combined with radiotherapy, the IMM effectively amplifies DNA damage and induces pronounced apoptosis by alleviating intratumoral hypoxia. This shift reprograms the tumor microenvironment, enhancing radiosensitivity and facilitating the infiltration and activation of intratumoral CD8⁺ T cells and dendritic cells. Moreover, when integrated with anti-PD-1 therapy, this coordinated therapeutic regimen elicits potent systemic immune responses and durable antitumor memory, effectively suppressing tumor recurrence and metastasis while markedly improving therapeutic efficacy and long-term survival. We anticipate that this conceptual design could offer a promising and translationally relevant nanomedicine platform for radiotherapies. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Fitria D.; Nugraheni D.R.; Herdiansyah H.; Qamruzzaman M.
Title: Consumer awareness, participation, and accessibility in sustainable electronic waste management
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid increase in electronic waste has created increasingly complex environmental and health challenges, especially in developing countries like Indonesia. The study objectives were to examine how household awareness and accessibility of electronic-waste management facilities are associated with consumer participation, controlling for socioeconomic factors, demographics, and the region's spatial characteristics. METHODS: This study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design to examine household consumers living near electronic waste management facilities in Indonesia. To analyze the data, Spearman's rank correlation was employed to evaluate variable relationships, ordinary least squares regression to estimate the associations of awareness and accessibility with participation levels, Kruskal-Wallis test to examine group differences, and Geographic Information System-based spatial analysis to describe the spatial patterns of facility distance, accessibility, and electronic waste management participation. FINDINGS: Consumer awareness of the consequences of electronic waste showed a significant positive correlation with the intention to manage electronic waste, with a correlation coefficient of 0.340, but showed no significant correlation with actual behavior, with a correlation coefficient of only 0.067. Accessibility showed a significant positive correlation with both intention and actual behavior, with correlation coefficients of 0.197 and 0.416, respectively. Accessibility had the largest reported regression coefficient for actual behavior ( β = 0.449 ), followed by awareness of consequences ( β = 0.182 ). The Kruskal-Wallis test confirmed significant differences in intention and actual behavior across accessibility levels, with chi-square values of 11.67 and 35.91, respectively. Spatial analysis using the nearest neighbor method produced a nearest neighbor ratio of 0.60 with a z score of -10.01. Spatial analysis revealed that highly aware and active residents are significantly clustered rather than randomly dispersed, with the vast majority residing within a functional catchment area defined by 10 to 30 kilometer distances or 10 to 30 minute travel times from e-waste facilities. CONCLUSION: The findings underscore the need for electronic waste management policies that prioritise facility accessibility and spatially based approaches to strengthen community participation within a circular economy framework. Title: Neuroprotective, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuromodulatory effects of Calliandra portoricensis root bark ethanol extract against carbon tetrachloride-induced neurotoxicity in male Wistar rats
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Calliandra portoricensis (Jacq.) Benth. is used in the ethnomedicine of southwestern Nigeria in treating epilepsy, convulsion, pain, inflammatory disorders, fever and other neurological conditions. However, its neuroprotective potential has not been adequately investigated. Aim of the study: This study evaluated the neuroprotective, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuromodulatory effects of Calliandra portoricensis root bark ethanol extract (CPRBEE) against carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced neurotoxicity in male Wistar rats. Materials and methods: CPRBEE was characterized using phytochemical screening and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly allotted to seven groups (n = 5). Neurotoxicity was induced with CCl4 (1.3 mL/kg; 3:10 v/v in olive oil). Following induction, rats received vitamin C (200 mg/kg) or CPRBEE (10, 20, 30, and 40 mg/kg). Neurobehavioral performance, oxidative stress biomarkers, acetylcholinesterase activity, inflammatory cytokines, neuronal injury markers, trace metal concentrations, Nrf2, HO-1, NF-κB, BDNF concentrations, and histopathological changes were evaluated. Results: GC–MS analysis tentatively annotated several phytochemicals, including phytol, β-sitosterol, stigmasterol, squalene, and a vitamin E (tocopherol derivative) peak consistent with α-tocopherol. CCl4 exposure significantly increased lipid peroxidation, acetylcholinesterase activity, pro-inflammatory cytokines, NSE, GFAP, and NF-κB concentrations, while reducing antioxidant defenses, Nrf2, HO-1, and BDNF concentrations (p < 0.05). CPRBEE attenuated these alterations, improved behavioural performance, partially restored trace-element profiles, and reduced histopathological alterations, with the magnitude of effects varying across biomarkers and treatment levels. Conclusion: CPRBEE demonstrated neuroprotective activity against CCl4-induced neurotoxicity, potentially through attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation while preserving antioxidant and neurotrophic defenses, supporting its traditional applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Frequency-selective transmission of geopolitical risk to day-ahead electricity prices: Evidence from variational mode decomposition, wavelet transform coherence, and double machine learning
Abstract: Electric vehicles, AI data centres, and electrification are raising electricity-demand volatility, while post-2022 conflicts have repeatedly disturbed global fuel markets. This paper studies a hard empirical test: whether geopolitical risk reaches a regulated Chinese provincial market where price caps and administered fuel pricing mute indirect fuel-chain pass-through. In Guangdong day-ahead prices from 2021-11-01 to 2026-06-07, the aggregate signal is weak: 0.038 with the Caldara–Iacoviello composite GPR index and 0.112 with the GPR-threat sub-index. The muted average points to institutional attenuation, with transmission appearing only in selected horizons and fuel states. Variational mode decomposition and wavelet coherence indicate that the relevant relation is concentrated in a short-pulse 2–8 day band: GPR threats and prices co-move with same-band correlation 0.348, and phase arrows show threats leading prices. In the pure-fuel reference specification, double machine learning estimates a positive conditional association for the threat index of 0.078 CNY/MWh per index unit; the association remains positive across carbon, demand, weather, macro-financial, supply-side, bootstrap, and EPU robustness exercises. Walk-forward forecasting indicates statistically significant, state-dependent out-of-sample signal value under the Clark–West nested-model test, concentrated in high-risk periods. Leave-event-out DML counterfactuals show that crisis premia are compound states; within the fuel block, the dominant component follows physical chokepoints, gas for Russia–Ukraine and oil for Hormuz. A cross-market comparison reverses sign in coal-based Shanxi and is strongest in directly disrupted European markets, supporting fuel-chain exposure as the organizing mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Two pathways at once: An investigation of how reactance and ethicality shape student learning with AI
Abstract: Generative AI tools promise to expand student agency in management education, yet the same tool can help and hurt learning inside a single classroom. We argue this contradiction is the signature of two psychological pathways running in parallel. Drawing on the cognitive-affective-conative framework, we develop a dual-pathway serial mediation model in which a cognitive pathway runs from psychological reactance through autonomy perceptions to effectiveness judgments, while an affective pathway runs from ethical perceptions through emotional engagement to effectiveness judgments. Ninety-seven undergraduate management students participated in two AI-enhanced activities with different chatbot tools across one semester. Both pathways operated as predicted. More surprising was how the cognitive pathway changed across exposures. At first use, reactance traveled through autonomy, consistent with self-determination theory. By the second activity, reactance bypassed autonomy and suppressed effectiveness directly. The affective pathway remained stable across exposures. For management educators, ethical framing before a student's first AI encounter may do more work than redesigning the tools themselves to preserve student choice. As a single-cohort study using two researcher-built chatbots, the results are preliminary and point to hypotheses for multi-site replication rather than population estimates. © 2026

Title: Digital influences on green economic participation: The role of eWOM in shaping circular consumption among young vietnamese consumers
Abstract: Circular business models (CBMs) are increasingly recognized as a strategic mechanism for advancing sustainable consumption and supporting green economic growth, particularly in emerging economies where rising consumption intensifies pressures on natural resources and waste management systems. Concurrently, the rapid expansion of social media and digital commerce has elevated electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) to a central role in shaping how young consumers interpret, evaluate, and normalize sustainability-oriented business practices. Despite this growing intersection, limited empirical evidence explains how specific attributes of eWOM translate into consumers’ intentions to participate in CBMs, especially in developing-market contexts such as Vietnam. Addressing this gap, the present study adopts a quantitative approach using survey data from 1,142 young Vietnamese consumers to examine how core dimensions of eWOM influence information acceptance and, subsequently, participation intentions in CBMs within the retail sector. A rigorous multi-stage analytical procedure was employed, including reliability testing, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to validate the measurement model, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to assess the structural relationships among latent constructs. The results indicate that all four eWOM attributes positively influence information acceptance, which in turn significantly drives participation intention. Among these factors, relevance emerges as the most influential attribute, suggesting that sustainability-related messages are most effective when aligned with consumers’ personal needs, values, and decision contexts. The findings also confirm the mediating role of information acceptance in translating eWOM quality into behavioral intention. By validating both the measurement and structural models, this study enhances the robustness of IAM-based explanations in the context of circular consumption and extends the literature on digital influence in emerging markets. Practically, the study highlights the importance of designing relevant, credible, and comprehensive sustainability communication strategies. Title: Asymptotic behavior of systemic risk measures in a bidimensional compound risk model
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Consider a bidimensional compound risk model with stochastic premiums and returns, in which the claims within the same business line possess a specific weak dependence structure, while the accident-arrival processes across different lines are arbitrarily dependent. To assess the risk contagion between an insurer and each of its business lines, this paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of two specific systemic risk measures: conditional mean excess and systemic expected shortfall. Specifically, the former captures the insurer's instantaneous mean excess loss when a business line experiences a crisis, while the latter quantifies the corresponding business line's instantaneous expected loss contribution to the insurer's systemic distress. Within a regular variation framework, our asymptotic formulas illustrate how the heavy-tailedness of the claims influences these risk measures, whereas weak dependence exerts no contributory effect. Numerical studies are also conducted to verify the accuracy of the resulting estimates for these two measures, and to investigate the sensitivity of systemic expected shortfall with respect to several key parameters. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Abstract: Although loyalty programs and checkout charity are widely implemented across retail industries, the integration of reward point donations into online checkout charity remains rare, and consumer behavior in this context is not yet fully understood. While a few studies have explored reward point donations and generally reported positive consumer responses, to the best of our knowledge, little research has examined how reward point characteristics and situational factors influence consumers' willingness to donate. Title: Ultramicropore-Confined Solvation and Interphase Regulation Unlock High-Performance Hard Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
Abstract: Hard carbon (HC) anodes are promising for sodium-ion batteries, yet achieving high initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), large plateau contribution, and fast charge-transfer kinetics remains challenging due to insufficient control of micro–nanostructure and interphase chemistry. Here, we present a precursor-level molecular engineering strategy that simultaneously regulates sodium desolvation and interphase chemistry in HC. An iodine-mediated oxidative cross-linking process converts starch into spherical HC with uniformly distributed ultramicropores and carbonyl-rich surfaces. These nanoconfined pores are proposed to act as molecular sieves, preferentially excluding bulky solvent molecules while allowing PF6−-coordinated Na+ access, thereby favoring anion-enriched electrolyte structures under confinement. Surface carbonyls exhibit strong PF6− affinity, which may promote fluorine-rich inorganic interphases on pore surfaces. The synergistic effects of anion-selective adsorption and confined desolvation are suggested to favor thin and robust NaF-rich interphases at external surfaces and within nanoconfined pore regions, contributing to reversible interfacial reactions and rapid Na+ storage kinetics. Consequently, the HC delivers an ICE of 88.4%, a reversible capacity of 352.9 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, excellent rate capability (288.9 mAh g−1 at 5C), and 95.6% capacity retention over 200 cycles. This work offers a molecular-level design paradigm integrating efficiency, capacity, and kinetics in HC anodes. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Impacts of tourism development on residents’ quality of life: A dual spillover perspective
Abstract: Tourism development can influence residents’ quality of life through bottom-up spillover (i.e., mediation) across life domains and through spatial spillover across regions. Title: Transformational entrepreneurship education in the AI era: Reframing entrepreneurial readiness through AI literacy and digital entrepreneurial capability
Abstract: Artificial intelligence integration is reshaping entrepreneurship education and increasing the need for pedagogical approaches that prepare students to act under digital uncertainty. Drawing on Transformational Learning Theory, Growth Mindset Theory, and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines how Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy contribute to Entrepreneurial Readiness directly and through Digital Innovation Skills and Digital Growth Mindset, the complementary dimensions through which Digital Entrepreneurial Capability is conceptually expressed. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. Survey data from 698 Indonesian university students were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, followed by semi-structured interviews with 24 students. The findings show that Transformational Entrepreneurship Education was positively related to AI Literacy, Digital Innovation Skills, Digital Growth Mindset, and Entrepreneurial Readiness. AI Literacy was also positively related to both capability dimensions and Entrepreneurial Readiness. Both dimensions significantly mediated the relationships of Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy with Entrepreneurial Readiness, while the corresponding direct effects remained significant. Qualitative findings showed that reflective AI engagement, iterative experimentation, feedback, and persistence supported capability development, whereas passive AI reliance and limited scaffolding constrained capability translation. The study advances entrepreneurship education and AI Literacy research by reframing Entrepreneurial Readiness as an action-oriented outcome. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Setyowati M.S.; Hanum R.K.
Title: The effect of agricultural taxes and local agricultural policies on enhancing food security and environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Indonesia is currently working towards sustainability in line with Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Anticipated demographic growth to 10.8 billion by the year 2050 is expected to place unprecedented strain on global food security and production systems. The study objectives were to examine the biophysical factors, production inputs, economic conditions, socio-technological factors, agricultural business management, and agricultural tax policies regional agricultural policies and, ultimately, agricultural productivity. METHODS: This quantitative study employed structured questionnaires administered to a sample of 200 farmers in Surabaya. The instrument used a one-to-five Likert scale covering biophysical factors, economic factors, tax policy, tax morale, and agricultural productivity. Data was analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling version 3. The analytical procedure comprised three distinct phases: first, evaluating the outer model for convergent and discriminant validity; second, conducting reliability assessments; and third, testing the inner model via bootstrapping to determine the coefficient of determination, the effect size, and hypothesis significance. Hypothesis significance was determined using t-statistic values of at least 1.96 and p-values of no more than 0.05. FINDINGS: Four hypotheses were rejected: economic factor on regional agricultural policy (p-value 0.557), agricultural taxation policy on tax morale (p-value 0.072), tax awareness on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.058), and tax morale on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.208). The findings reveal that regional agricultural policies are substantially driven by three key dimensions: biophysical factors (beta coefficient of 0.251, probability value of 0.000), production inputs (beta coefficient of 0.253, probability value of 0.002), and agricultural business management (beta coefficient of 0.228, probability value of 0.007). Agricultural tax policy significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.229, probability value of 0.000), while tax administration efficiency also significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.345, probability value of 0.000) and tax morale (beta coefficient of -0.634, probability value of 0.000), since clarity on procedures, benefits, and regulations fosters public responsibility and awareness of taxpayer obligations and rights. CONCLUSION: Elevating agricultural output demands comprehensive frameworks characterized by active farmer participation, supportive regulatory policies, targeted outreach regarding tax frameworks, and enhanced coordination between industry stakeholders and governmental bodies. Regional agricultural policies and tax awareness significantly influence agricultural productivity. These findings offer practical insights for policymakers aiming to strengthen agricultural governance and tax compliance frameworks in support of sustainable rural development. Title: Moral responsibilisation in destination management: The strategic framing of civic practices by DMOs
Abstract: This paper examines moral responsibilisation as an emerging destination governance mechanism through which destination management organisations (DMOs) and local stakeholders mobilise visitors to support sustainability goals. Drawing on an intrinsic qualitative case study of the Danish DMO, Wonderful Copenhagen , we develop a practice theory-based model showing that responsibilisation extends beyond narrative persuasion to include the organisational and material reframing of civic conduct. Analysis of interviews, participant observation, documents, and netnography identifies four interrelated stages: interpellation, involvement, intervention, and institutionalisation. Together, these stages connect inspirational messaging with participatory experiences, reward schemes, and decentralised service design. The findings also reveal tensions around the relevance, inclusivity, and feasibility of emerging civic practices. Resistance to responsible subject positions stems from stakeholders’ differing interpretations, negotiations, and disengagement from DMO-prescribed roles. The study advances the understanding of responsibilisation as a practice-based mode of governance and offers insights that may inform destination managers in varied tourism contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang X.; Tinacci L.; Giusti A.; Kang H.; Deng W.; Li Y.; Sun Z.; Peng H.; Zou L.; Armani A.; Wen J.
Title: DNA authentication of shark meat products from a major Chinese e-commerce platform reveals trade-name opacity and traceability limitations
Abstract: Shark meat products are subject to a variety of regulatory and conservation frameworks, yet their characterization at the retail level is often constrained by the use of umbrella terms and limited species-specific information. In this context, the present study was designed as an exploratory case study examining shark meat products commercialized through a major Chinese e-commerce platform within a defined sampling period. Product descriptions, labeling information (including trade name, processing type, product presentation, declared production origin, and price), and molecular species identification obtained through DNA barcoding were jointly examined to characterize shark-derived products marketed through the platform. A total of 63 products were screened, and 165 tissue samples were analysed using COI and cytb markers. All products were marketed under generic umbrella terms, without scientific nomenclature, and prepackaged products showed variable labeling completeness. Molecular analyses detected at least one shark taxon in 61 of the 63 products examined, whereas the remaining two products contained billfish and batoid taxa. At the tissue level, 160 of 165 samples (97%) were assigned to shark taxa. Across all analysed samples, molecular identification revealed 12 species-level taxa, comprising 10 shark species (Alopias pelagicus, A. superciliosus, Carcharhinus brevipinna, C. limbatus, C. sorrah, Galeocerdo cuvier, Isurus oxyrinchus, Mustelus griseus, Prionace glauca, and Sphyrna lewini), one batoid species (Rhynchobatus australiae), and one billfish species (Istiophorus platypterus), together with three genus-level assignments including shark and billfish taxa (Scoliodon sp., Carcharhinus sp., and Kajikia sp.). The identified taxa include species listed as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, and Critically Endangered according to the IUCN Red List. The two products containing non-shark taxa represented cases of non-conformity between molecular identity and the available product information and therefore warrant discussion in relation to labeling practices. Overall, the findings illustrate the utility of molecular approaches for documenting species composition in online retail settings and provide an exploratory baseline for future investigations into species-level transparency, product information practices, and shark product commercialization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li Y.(.; Wan L.C.
Title: Touchable cultural heritage: How alternative touch experience facilitates visitors’ cultural inheritance behavior
Abstract: Touch is a fundamental human need, yet in cultural heritage tourism, it is strictly restricted to protect fragile artifacts. While essential for preservation, touch restrictions limit multi-sensory experience and impede deeper cultural participation. This research addresses this touch dilemma by introducing alternative touch experiences, wherein tourists touch surrogate objects (e.g., artifact replicas) that simulate the haptic attributes of authentic artifacts. Across four studies with qualitative, experimental, and field evidence, we found that alternative touch experiences enhance tourists’ psychological closeness to heritage, which in turn fosters cultural inheritance intentions and actual behaviors (e.g., cultural learning, cultural knowledge sharing, and donation to protect heritage). However, this touch effect diminishes when artifacts carry negative (vs. positive) superstitious associations. These findings offer a new theoretical perspective on enabling embodied experience within the traditionally sensory-restricted context, and highlight the role of sensory engagement in facilitating heritage appreciation and cultural inheritance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
Abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization: Proximal MM method and statistical error bound
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper concerns the group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization problems. We propose a proximal majorization-minimization (PMM) algorithm to tackle a class of equivalent difference-of-convex (DC) surrogate optimization problems. Under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz (KL) property, we establish the global convergence of the proposed algorithm and characterize its local (sub)linear convergence rate. Furthermore, for linear observation models with design matrices satisfying restricted eigenvalue conditions, we derive statistical estimation error bounds between the PMM-generated iterates (including their limit points) and the ground truth solution. To efficiently implement the PMM framework, we develop a proximal dual semismooth Newton method for solving the subproblems. Numerical experiments on both synthetic data and the UCI benchmark demonstrate the efficiency of our PMM method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang H.; Shan Q.; Zhang J.; Xiao P.; Liu A.
Title: An audio-visual fusion emotion generation model based on neuroanatomical alignment
Abstract: In the field of affective computing, traditional methods for generating emotions predominantly rely on deep learning techniques and large-scale emotion datasets. However, deep learning techniques are often complex and difficult to interpret, and standardizing large-scale emotional datasets are difficult and costly to establish. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Audio-Visual Fusion for Brain-like Emotion Learning(AVF-BEL). In contrast to conventional brain-inspired emotion learning methods, this approach improves the audio-visual emotion fusion and generation model through the integration of modular components, thereby enabling more lightweight and interpretable emotion learning and generation processes. The framework simulates the integration of the visual, auditory, and emotional pathways of the brain, optimizes the fusion of emotional features across visual and auditory modalities, and improves upon the traditional Brain Emotional Learning (BEL) model. The experimental results indicate a significant improvement in the similarity of the audio-visual fusion emotion learning generation model compared to single-modality visual and auditory emotion learning and generation model. Ultimately, this aligns with the fundamental phenomenon of heightened emotion generation facilitated by the integrated impact of visual and auditory stimuli. This contribution not only enhances the interpretability and efficiency of affective intelligence but also provides new insights and pathways for advancing affective computing technology. Title: Technostress in the age of digital transformation and AI: A bibliometric–systematic literature review for HRM research
Abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping human resource management through algorithmic recruitment, automated evaluation, predictive analytics, and generative tools. While these systems improve efficiency, they also intensify technostress through opacity, surveillance, reduced control, and digitally intensified work arrangements. Responding to a fragmented literature spanning both AI-enabled and broader digital work systems, this study provides a B-SLR that maps technostress in digital transformation while identifying AI-specific stressors as a key emerging stream for HRM research. Drawing on 194 Scopus-indexed articles, we combine performance analysis and science mapping to identify publication trends, dominant themes, and intellectual structures. The review shows how AI-specific stressors extend established technostress mechanisms and shift attention toward transparency, control, fairness, and responsible HRM design. We conclude with actionable implications for researchers and practitioners aiming to design more transparent, responsible, and sustainable digital and AI-enabled HRM systems. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Li X.; Meng H.
Title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Moving beyond traditional approaches that treat beauty (or ugliness) and cuteness as separate dimensions, we investigate their interactive effects through four studies: one field experiment and three online experiments, involving participants from both China and the United States. Our findings show that the combination of ugly-cute configurations can attenuate the purchase-intention disadvantage associated with ugliness-related aesthetic deviation, with this effect explained by perceived social value and moderated by consumption setting (public vs. private). Specifically, this effect is more pronounced in public consumption settings, where consumers are more likely to seek social approval and positive evaluation from others, thereby amplifying perceived social value in purchase decisions. These results advance the literature on product design and consumer aesthetics by identifying a psychological explanation underlying consumer responses to atypical aesthetics, and provide practical insights for designing products that generate perceived social value (e.g., feeling accepted, gaining approval, or being positively regarded by others). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Li X.; Zhou Y.; Sun W.; Lei X.
Title: Uncertainty-aware nodal carbon intensity based on sliced Latin hypercube sampling
Abstract: The variability of climate conditions leads to significant renewable uncertainty. With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, it becomes necessary to consider uncertainties in the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) of power systems. However, the renewable uncertainty though the power flow propagates to the carbon emission flow, making an unclear relationship between the renewable uncertainty and the carbon emission flow. In this paper, an uncertainty-aware nodal Carbon intensity method is proposed to handle this issue. An explicit matrix-form relationship linking renewable forecast errors, AGC-based generation dispatch, branch power flow variations, and NCI is established. In addition, a Jacobian-based local sensitivity expression is derived to characterize the local response of NCI to renewable forecast errors. Then, sliced Latin hypercube sampling (SLHS) is employed to estimate the statistical characteristics and probability distribution of NCI. Case studies performed on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method is capable of accurately accounting for the uncertainty in the nodal carbon intensity. © 2026
