Title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. For instance, a critically problematic scenario (TK4) received a low ISA of 0.34, signaling the need for immediate intervention, while a case with systematic violations (TK5) scored 0.55, near the predefined acceptability threshold of 0.5. ©2027 The author(s). Authors: Pan A.
Title: The AI-augmented collaborative learning model: A conceptual framework for integrating generative AI in business and management education
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) amplifies four tensions in business and management education: the threat to pedagogical coherence, the literacy-to-competency gap, pervasive ethical risks, and the assessment crisis. A first wave of practice-oriented frameworks – including the Human-Centric AI-First (HCAIF) framework and the Leeds Model – offers actionable roadmaps but lacks the theoretical architecture needed to explain the systemic classroom dynamics GenAI introduces. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by developing the AI-Augmented Collaborative Learning (ACL) Model, a second-wave framework organised around three research questions: (RQ1) which theoretical lenses explain the classroom dynamics that generative AI creates in business and management education; (RQ2) how can these be synthesised into an integrated pedagogical framework whose pillars address the four systemic challenges; and (RQ3) how can human-AI collaboration be operationalised as an assessable pedagogical meta-skill. Using Socio-Technical Systems Theory, Activity Theory, Actor-Network Theory, Constructivist and Experiential Learning Theories, and the AI-TPACK framework, the ACL Model specifies four interlocking pillars – Pedagogical Intentionality, Developmental Scaffolding, Ethical Guardrails, and Authentic Assessment. The paper's primary theoretical contribution is to relocate the unit of analysis from the individual student to the student-AI network and to define collaborative intelligence as the resulting meta-competency. A six-proposition validation agenda guides testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Familiar faces, honest answers? The impacts of enumerator familiarity and modality on survey responses
Abstract: Survey data can be distorted through mistrust, discomfort, or demand effects on the part of respondents. We test whether familiar enumerators – those with whom a respondent has completed a prior survey – influence data quality in a panel survey with small business owners in Uganda. We randomly assign respondents to a familiar or a new enumerator and cross-cut a second randomization to an in-person or phone-based interview modality. Across a broad set of outcome types, we observe few impacts of either survey method on means, distributions, or attrition. However, respondents are significantly more likely to give norm-congruent answers to new surveyors compared to familiar ones. The effect of familiarity does not interact significantly with a prior experiment conducted with the same sample, suggesting that familiarity influences estimates of levels but not of treatment impacts. These findings suggest that surveys by familiar enumerators can improve the measurement of sensitive beliefs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Polyhydroxy Molecular Regulator Enabled Interfacial Microenvironment Programming for Alkaline Zinc–Iron Flow Batteries
Abstract: Alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries (ZIFBs) are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost, intrinsic safety, and scalable architecture, yet their practical deployment remains hindered by hydrogen evolution and uncontrolled Zn deposition in three-dimensional porous electrodes. Here, we report that isomalt acts as a polyhydroxy molecular regulator that reconfigures the interfacial microenvironment of porous carbon felt, thereby endowing the porous electrode with a more deposition-directing function for reversible Zn plating/stripping. In the bulk electrolyte, isomalt reconstructs the local hydrogen-bond network, lowers water activity, and suppresses hydrogen evolution. At the carbon/electrolyte interface, its preferential lateral adsorption establishes a hydroxyl-rich interphase that homogenizes zincate transport and directs Zn growth toward a preferred (002) orientation, thus promoting compact and reversible deposition. This interfacial microenvironment programming markedly reduces the charge-transfer resistance and activation barrier of the Zn anode, enabling stable cycling for over 500 cycles at 20 mA cm−2. In full-cell tests, the optimized ZIFB delivers a high energy efficiency of 87.5%, substantially outperforming the pristine electrolyte. Beyond identifying a low-cost green additive, this work establishes polyhydroxy molecules as interfacial programming units for three-dimensional porous electrodes, offering a new design concept for directional metal deposition in aqueous flow-battery systems. Title: Techno-economic optimisation and operational assessment of hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids for remote communities
Abstract: Hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids represent a promising pathway for sustainable decarbonisation of remote communities; however, conventional techno-economic optimisation often overlooks the operational behaviour of hydrogen subsystems, leading to optimistic performance estimates and less practically deployable designs. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Hybrid Optimisation of Multiple Energy Resources (HOMER) Pro-based techno-economic optimisation with Python-based post-optimisation operational assessment. The framework evaluates operational indicators, including minimum-load compliance, start-stop cycling, large-ramp events, and hydrogen storage utilisation, using hourly dispatch data and literature-informed criteria. A scenario-based design-space exploration is conducted for a remote off-grid community in Australia, followed by operational feasibility screening and Pareto-based multi-objective analysis balancing economic performance, renewable energy utilisation, and electrolyser operation. The optimised reference configuration achieves zero operational CO2 emissions with a levelised cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.258 AUD/kWh and a levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of 6.77 AUD/kg. Post-optimisation assessment reveals that 5,912 h of reported electrolyser operation reduces to 4,775 h of acceptable operation; the excluded 1,137 h (19.2%) correspond to low-load periods, indicating an overestimation of effective electrolyser utilisation of up to 23.8%. Threshold sensitivity analysis identifies hydrogen tank near-full hours as the most sensitive indicator, while core screening outcomes remain stable under low-load and ramp-event threshold variations. Operational feasibility screening reduces the 22 candidate designs to 15 feasible configurations, demonstrating that techno-economic attractiveness does not necessarily ensure operational viability. The proposed framework provides a practical methodology for operational assessment and design selection of hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids, supporting informed planning and deployment of reliable, low-carbon energy systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Navigating CSRD compliance: Challenges in sustainability reporting for the real estate sector
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the challenges faced by the Norwegian real estate sector in complying with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), addressing a critical gap in understanding how these regulations impact sustainability reporting practices. The research seeks new insights into the barriers to implementing CSRD-compliant reporting, contributing to a deeper understanding of the sector's readiness and areas requiring improvement. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, utilizing a scoping literature review to map existing knowledge and semi-structured interviews with industry stakeholders to supplement findings. Data were collected from peer-reviewed articles, master's theses, and interviews with key stakeholders, and analyzed using thematic coding and qualitative analysis. The results reveal that the main challenges include limited knowledge of sustainability matters, difficulties in conducting Double Materiality Assessments (DMA), high costs, poor data systems, and administrative burdens. These findings provide evidence that while some companies proactively prepare for CSRD compliance, many, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), struggle due to resource constraints and a reliance on manual processes. This highlights significant implications for improving digital solutions and stakeholder collaboration. This research offers a novel perspective on sustainability reporting in the Norwegian real estate sector, providing valuable insights into the sector's preparedness and key barriers. The study's findings contribute to advancing digital reporting practices and support for SMEs, highlighting areas for future research and potential policy development to ease the transition to CSRD compliance. Title: Capacity Degradation Mechanisms, Recovery Strategies, and Challenges of Flow Batteries
Abstract: Redox flow batteries, by virtue of their advantages in power/capacity decoupling, high safety, and long cycle life, have become a strategic support for long-duration energy storage systems; however, capacity degradation remains a bottleneck for their commercialization. This review systematically identifies the multi-dimensional mechanisms of capacity degradation: including volume imbalance caused by transmembrane migration, inactivation and decomposition of active species, electrode degradation, and valence imbalance induced by side reactions. Targeting these challenges, the review deeply explores recovery strategies from physical repair to intelligent scheduling: covering the research and development of high-selectivity membranes, precise regulation of valence states, functionalized repair of electrodes, and model-driven predictive pathways integrating digital twins. Finally, current challenges such as characterization limitations and incomplete recovery rates are summarized, and future development directions for capacity recovery are envisioned. This review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical guidance for extending the system cycle life of flow batteries and improving capacity recovery efficiency. Title: Beyond compliance: Community development committees and the transformation of resource governance in Tanzania
Abstract: Resource-rich countries worldwide often face persistent imbalances in the redistribution of resource wealth. Although mineral extraction generates substantial revenues, these funds are typically centrally managed and redistributed, leaving host communities, who bear the social and environmental burdens of extraction, impoverished and marginalized. In Tanzania, despite provisions allowing Local Government Authorities to levy a 0.3% service charge on mining revenues and receive Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions intended to support local development, means of engaging host communities remain a challenge. Community Development Agreements (CDAs) have been identified as potential instruments to safeguard the interests of host communities. However, despite their widespread promotion, a critical gap remains in understanding how communities can effectively engage in, negotiate, and implement CDAs, particularly in contexts marked by power asymmetries. Communities are often poor, with limited knowledge of mining and the broader extractive industry, and with no access to decision-making power. This study addresses the gap by examining Community Development Committees (CDCs) as an inclusive, participatory institutional mechanism through which communities can effectively articulate their development priorities. Using semi‑structured interviews with 36 key informants across the mining value chain, including central government officials, mining representatives, and local communities, the study finds the CDC model as an effective approach for strengthening community voice, enhancing transparency, improving negotiations, and monitoring project implementations. Although grounded in Tanzania’s mining sector, the study offers insights relevant to other resource dependent economies seeking to foster more equitable social contracts. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: An applicable mechanism for regulating anti-etching performance through interface doping in periodic Y2O3-BaZrO3 films
Abstract: Plasma etching is widely used in the processing of semiconductor memory and the manufacturing of field-effect transistors, with precise transfer of nanometer level precision, high aspect ratio structures, and complex three-dimensional structures. However, halogen-containing reactive plasma can corrode the ceramic components of chambers, for example, generating YOF particles on the surface of yttrium oxide coating after high-energy plasma bombardment. In order to reduce the etching rate and minimize particle contamination, this work adopts an interface doping strategy to prepare Y2O3-BaZrO3 etch-resistant multilayered films through radio-frequency magnetron sputtering. Subsequent vacuum annealing of the films at 900℃ was performed to improve their atomic diffusion, crystallization, and density. 12-layer Y2O3-BaZrO3 film proved to be the hardest and most etch-resistant with the lowest relative etching rate (0.67 nm/min) under chemical plasma conditions (CF4/O2), compared with Y2O3 film (1.42 nm/min) and Y2O3-MgO composite film (0.91 nm/min). As chemical etching involves the formation of protective fluoride passivation layers such as Y-F, Ba-F and Zr-F, the surface stability is enhanced by the increased bonding energy of metal fluorides, indicating higher thermodynamic stability of the composite after adsorption of fluorine. Title: Guest-origin and temporal heterogeneity in online hotel reviews: A structural topic modeling analysis
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines whether the relative salience of hotel-review themes varies across guest-origin groups and review years. Structural Topic Modeling was applied to 29,304 Booking.com reviews from 144 hotels in Vietnam collected between 2022 and 2025. A seven-topic solution captured staff/location/breakfast satisfaction, room cleanliness and comfort, amenities and food, walkability, personalized hospitality, leisure settings, and booking/travel logistics. Probability-scale contrasts were standardized over the complementary metadata distribution, with hotel-clustered CR2 inference accounting for within-hotel dependence. Guest-origin heterogeneity was markedly more stable than temporal heterogeneity. Under hotel-clustered inference, 15 of 21 guest-origin contrasts met the within-family false-discovery-rate threshold, compared with 1 of 21 2022-referenced temporal contrasts; 11 guest-origin contrasts showed strong multi-specification evidence. The largest difference was a 27.6-percentage-point higher expected prevalence of the Room cleanliness and comfort topic in Domestic than Western reviews; Domestic reviews also showed an 18.4-percentage-point lower expected prevalence of Staff, location, and breakfast satisfaction. Asian reviews exhibited a distinct profile spanning amenities, walkability, personalized hospitality, travel logistics, and leisure-related content. Temporal evidence was less stable: the 2025–2022 increase in Personalized hospitality and attentive service attenuated after hotel fixed effects, although a separate 2023-referenced analysis identified six supported temporal contrasts. The findings show that guest-origin context is associated with persistent differences in what consumers discuss, whereas annual differences are more dependent on hotel composition and temporal reference. Title: Path-reliability analysis for perishable goods delivery in urban multigraph networks: Integrating non-instantaneous deterioration and failed-delivery risks
Abstract: With the rapid development of the instant retail business model, consumers have placed increasingly stringent demands on delivery speed and service quality in perishable goods distribution. In instant retail contexts, hot-chain delivery involves managing perishable goods characterized by non-instantaneous deterioration, where quality degradation progresses over delivery time in urban multigraph networks, thereby posing distinctive operational challenges. To address these issues, this paper defines path-reliability, denoting the reliability of a specific path between two customer nodes, to summarize path operating conditions, including congestion, reachability, and connectivity, and establishes a functional relationship between path-reliability and delivery delay time. On this basis, a perishable goods delivery (PGD) network model is developed under customer availability profiles, and a hybrid tabu search algorithm equipped with neighbourhood operators tailored to multigraph structures is proposed for its solution. The model is then validated on randomly generated benchmark instances as well as real-world operational data from a prefabricated-food distribution enterprise in Xi'an. The results indicate that in regions with dispersed customer distribution, multi-path planning combined with reliability assessment yields significant cost savings and risk reduction, whereas in highly clustered regions single-path planning is sufficient to achieve efficient resource allocation while simplifying computation and implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Can stablecoin instability threaten emerging tourism payment infrastructure?
Abstract: Stablecoins are increasingly discussed as an emerging form of digital tourism payment infrastructure. This study examines whether instability in stablecoins creates vulnerabilities in emerging tourism payment ecosystems by analysing the UST and USDC depeg events. Drawing on tourism systems theory, tourism resilience theory, and financial economics, the analysis combines high-frequency market data, on-chain transaction activity, and tourism payment indicators. The results show that depeg events degrade market quality by widening bid–ask spreads, reducing market depth, and increasing transaction costs. Large market participants also reduce risk-bearing and withdraw liquidity during periods of stress. In addition, depeg events strengthen dynamic correlations among closely linked stablecoins. Evidence from tourism payment activity suggests that severe depeg events may reduce the use of stablecoin-based payments within crypto-native tourism ecosystems. The findings suggest that instability in stablecoins may introduce settlement uncertainty and payment frictions within tourism ecosystems experimenting with blockchain-based payment infrastructure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ren J.-J.; Chai Z.-Y.; Li Y.-L.; Li J.-J.
Title: Adaptive auxiliary task generation and reinforcement learning-enhanced multi-task multi-population evolutionary offloading in IIoT
Abstract: Workflow-based computation offloading has become a fundamental technique for improving execution efficiency in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. However, heterogeneous workflow structures, complex task dependencies, and dynamic resource conditions make multi-workflow offloading a challenging multi-objective optimization problem. Existing evolutionary offloading methods generally optimize workflows independently and lack effective knowledge sharing mechanisms, resulting in limited search efficiency and potential negative transfer across heterogeneous tasks. To address these issues, this paper formulates multi-workflow computation offloading as a multitask multi-objective optimization problem and proposes an adaptive auxiliary task generation and reinforcement learning-enhanced multi-population MOEA/D (ATRL-MT-MOEAD). The proposed framework assigns each workflow to an independent subpopulation for collaborative evolution, introduces adaptive auxiliary tasks to accelerate convergence, and employs a reinforcement learning-based knowledge transfer mechanism to dynamically regulate inter-task information sharing while suppressing negative transfer. Experimental results on representative IIoT workflow benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently achieves the best optimization performance. Compared with the strongest baseline for each metric, the proposed method reduces the average IGD by 72.0%, GD by 80.4%, ACT by 16.8%, and AEC by 14.5%, while consistently achieving superior Pareto-front quality. These results verify that the proposed framework provides superior convergence, solution diversity, and optimization effectiveness for complex multi-workflow computation offloading in dynamic IIoT environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang X.; Seema
Title: SHG wave propagation in functionally graded piezomagnetic sandwich plates with imperfect interfaces: Analytical modeling and machine learning prediction
Abstract: Shear horizontal guided (SHG) waves in functionally graded piezomagnetic structures are highly sensitive to material gradation, interfacial imperfections, and magnetic boundary conditions, making them attractive for smart sensing and structural monitoring applications. This study develops an integrated analytical and physics-informed learning framework for SHG-wave propagation in a composite sandwich structure comprising two dissimilar functionally graded piezomagnetic layers coupled through a spring-membrane imperfect interface and subjected to surface mass loading. Analytical dispersion relations are derived for two distinct velocity regimes under magnetically open-circuit (MOC) and magnetically short-circuit (MSC) conditions. The effects of magneto-mechanical coupling, material gradation, interface characteristics, membrane inertial density, and normalized density on the dispersion response are systematically examined. The results reveal pronounced dispersive behavior and demonstrate that magneto-mechanical coupling, functional gradation, interface stiffness, membrane inertia, and magnetic boundary conditions provide effective mechanisms for controlling SHG-wave propagation. The analytical formulation is further integrated with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and a physics-informed Deep Operator Network (PI-DeepONet) for rapid prediction of the dispersion response. PI-DeepONet achieves R2=0.99970, compared with 0.99811 for ANN, and reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by approximately 69.6%, 73.1%, and 73.5%, respectively. The physics residual also falls below 10−3 over a substantial portion of the investigated wave-number range, while tests on unseen physical configurations demonstrate improved generalization. The proposed analytical–physics-informed framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient approach for SHG-wave analysis and offers potential for smart piezomagnetic sensors, acoustic-wave devices, and guided-wave-based structural monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Authors: Yang C.; Lu X.; Pan Y.; Zhang Q.; Yu R.; Yang R.; Liu H.; Duan M.; Li M.G.; Zhu Z.; Yang C.
Title: Hotspot to Homogeneous: Amorphous Interfacial Current Redistribution Enables Stable Solid-State Lithium-Metal Batteries
Abstract: Interfacial instability in oxide ceramic electrolyte (OCE)-based solid-state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) is conventionally attributed to chemical incompatibility or mechanical failure, yet the underlying atomic-scale mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we reveal that grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline OCEs function as bipolar interfacial hotspots, accelerating three degradation pathways: lowering barriers for Li dendrite nucleation and enabling electron-leakage-driven reduction at anode side, while generating localized overpotentials for cathode phase transformation. To deactivate these GB-driven hotspots, we develop a laser-induced amorphization strategy that constructs a GB-free amorphous interlayer capable of homogenizing Li+ flux and blocking electron migration. Applied to a representative sodium superionic conductor-type electrolyte, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3, this approach delivers substantially increased critical current density in Li symmetric cells (1.4 to 2.4 mA cm−2) with stable cycling over 2000 h, and achieves an exceptional capacity retention of 101.9 mAh g−1 after 800 cycles in LiCoO2 full cells operated at 4.5 V. The generality of this strategy is further validated on garnet-type and perovskite-type OCEs. This work introduces amorphous interfacial current redistribution as a universal paradigm for engineering stable interfaces, providing a critical atomic-scale interface engineering route to unlock high-voltage, dendrite-free SSLMBs. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Multicomponent Nitride/High-Entropy Alloy Heterostructures as Highly Active and Stable Electrocatalysts for Ampere-Level Water Oxidation

The protonation of Brønsted basic oxyanions facilitates the critical *OOH intermediate formation on N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH with near-optimal adsorption energy, substantially accelerating the oxygen evolution reaction kinetics. Consequently, the heterostructure electrode exhibits superior oxygen evolution reaction electrocatalysis in 1 M KOH solution, delivering ultrahigh current density of ~ 2.5 A cm−2 at low overpotential of 300 mV. Title: Assessing the environmental–economic viability of expressway photovoltaics in China: A spatio–temporal life cycle perspective
Abstract: Expressway corridors are increasingly considered for distributed photovoltaic deployment, but their environmental–economic viability depends strongly on local solar resources, infrastructure availability, grid structure, and future decarbonization pathways. This study develops an integrated framework that combines spatio–temporal assessment with environmental life cycle costing to evaluate the deployment potential and comprehensive benefits of expressway photovoltaic systems across 351 prefecture–level cities in China. The assessment covers service areas, rest areas, and expressway slopes under business-as-usual and carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenarios. Results indicate that expressway slopes provide the greatest installation potential, with 49.71% of cities supporting more than 200 MW. At the national-average level, expressway photovoltaic systems yield a net internal benefit of 317.05 USD/kW and a net environmental benefit of 249.48 USD/kW under the business-as-usual scenario. Inverter and monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic module production are the main contributors to environmental costs. Under the carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenario, grid decarbonization reduces the avoided environmental burden of photovoltaic electricity and delays the transition to positive net environmental benefits from 2035 to 2037. These findings support a shift from capacity-oriented expansion to region-specific life cycle planning, prioritizing corridors where solar resources, expressway availability, grid displacement benefits, and recycling infrastructure are jointly favorable. © 2026

Title: Biomimetic PD-1-Functionalized Immunostimulatory Nanomedicine Enables STING Activation and Durable Antitumor Immunity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade, largely because of an immunologically cold tumor microenvironment (TME) characterized by deficient antigen presentation and impaired cytotoxic T cell responses. Analysis of numerous HCC clinical cohorts, including our institutional datasets, reveals that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway activity is positively correlated with patient survival, enhanced antigen presentation capacity, and an immune-activated TME. However, achieving effective and controllable STING activation in immune-cold HCC tumors remains challenging. Here, we develop a biomimetic nanomedicine that integrates photothermal therapy (PTT), STING pathway activation, and immune checkpoint blockade to treat refractory HCC. A coordination nanomedicine MCI-NP is engineered by co-encapsulating the STING agonist MSA-2 and indocyanine green (ICG) via Cu2+-mediated chelation, enabling stabilized PTT-induced immunogenic cell death together with robust STING-driven innate immune activation. Further cloaked with PD-1-overexpressing cell membranes, MCI-NP@mPD-1 achieves an approximately fivefold increase in tumor accumulation compared with uncoated MCI-NP and enables localized PD-1/PD-L1 axis blockade. Following a single treatment, MCI-NP@mPD-1-based photothermal immunotherapy effectively suppresses primary tumor growth and significantly prolongs survival by remodeling the TME toward an immune-active state, while inducing durable systemic immune memory that effectively limited postoperative lung metastasis. Without introducing additional nanocarriers or excipients, MCI-NP@mPD-1 offers a promising therapeutic paradigm for photothermal immunotherapy of immune-cold HCC. Title: Business simulation games and ethical decision making confidence and intentions: The role of self-efficacy, reflective practice, and teamwork
Abstract: This study examines the potential associations between experiential learning via participating in a business simulation game and business students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. While simulation games have been widely recognized for their effectiveness in developing business competencies, their associations with ethical decision making confidence and intentions in a non-ethics related environment remain underexplored. Our findings suggest that participation in simulation games is associated with higher levels of students' teamwork and reflective practice capabilities that, in turn, were found to be positively associated with their ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Moreover, students who participated in simulation games reported higher self-efficacy which, however, was not found to have a significant relationship with ethical decision-making confidence and intentions. Title: Healthcare Resources, In-Hospital Management Measures, and Outcomes for Acute Ischemic Stroke in China: A Cross-Sectional Study
Abstract: Objectives To assess how province-level healthcare resource configuration relates to in-hospital management and outcomes for acute ischemic stroke in China. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of 1 055 971 adults with acute ischemic stroke treated at 1456 secondary and tertiary hospitals in the Chinese Stroke Center Alliance, 2015 to 2019. Hospital-level management and outcome measures were linked to province-level resource indicators from the China Health Statistics Yearbook, including physician:nurse ratio, nurse:bed ratio, density of medical institutions, and total health expenditure. Associations were estimated using patient-number–weighted linear regression models adjusted for hospital level, provincial gross regional product per capita, admission timing, and year, with cluster-robust standard errors at the province level. Results Substantial interprovincial variation was observed. Most healthcare resource indicators were not significantly associated with composite adherence, although physician:nurse ratio showed a borderline positive association (β = 0.018 per 0.1 increase, 95% CI, −0.0004 to 0.036). Secondary prevention adherence was positively associated with health expenditure (β = 0.007; 95% CI, 0.0003-0.014). For thrombolysis within 4.5 hours, physician:nurse ratio was negatively associated (β = −0.062; 95% CI, −0.119 to −0.006), whereas nurse:bed ratio was positively associated (β = 1.232; 95% CI, 0.066-2.397). In contrast, healthcare resource indicators were not clearly associated with in-hospital outcomes. Conclusions Healthcare resource configuration showed modest associations with stroke management but limited associations with in-hospital outcomes, suggesting that resource availability alone may not fully explain variation in stroke outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
Abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Boosting baijiu fermentation efficiency through designed microbial community coalescence: Enhanced substrate conversion and flavor output
Abstract: In this study, we designed a synthetic community (SynCom) for directedly monitoring the yield of phenolic compounds and other flavor compounds of Baijiu, through inoculating the coalescence of synthetic community and autochthonous starter culture (Daqu). Title: The potential for coordination between air and ocean transport in advancing Net Zero policies
Abstract: This study explores ways to achieve a modal shift in cargo transport markets for high-value commodities, with particular emphasis on shippers' awareness of climate change. Specifically, it aims to (i) provide insights for carriers in designing efficient cargo transport networks aligned with Net Zero policies; (ii) examine the robustness of the results by discussing the feasibility of sea-and-air services for high-value commodities while accounting for heterogeneity in shippers’ behavior; and (iii) inform policymakers in their efforts to support and facilitate such modal shifts. Third, if time-sensitive shippers with a high level of awareness of climate change occupy the major part of the market, ocean transport can become a feasible option for carrying high-value commodities. Title: Screening out ethics: How technology enables ethical fading in negotiations
Abstract: Negotiations are rife with opportunities and temptations to engage in unethical negotiating behavior. Such behavior is not always strategic or even intentional; rather, it can emerge from situational characteristics of the negotiation environment. One psychological process through which situational characteristics influence unethical behavior is ethical fading, a process that limits one's ability to recognize the ethical aspects of the situation and behave in line with one's ethical values. As technologies such as email, video conferencing, and artificial intelligence (AI) become increasingly common in negotiations, an important question is whether these technologies facilitate ethical fading. In this review, we explore the impact that technology and AI have on ethical fading and unethical negotiating behavior. We propose that technology and AI use in negotiations promotes three cognitive processes that facilitate ethical fading: psychological distance, cognitive offloading, and displaced accountability. We review how technology may serve as an antecedent to each of these processes and explain why these processes may facilitate ethical fading in negotiation contexts. Title: Local market framework considering flexible agents in energy communities: Theory and experimental validation
Abstract: In this paper, we experimentally test a local electricity market framework, considering both passive and active market participants as well as uncertainty from production, consumption and network flows. By solving a chance-constrained optimal power flow and expressing the uncertainty using generalized polynomial chaos, we can express nodal active and reactive power prices as polynomial chaos coefficients eliminating the need to perform computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations. In the day-ahead stage, this produces probabilistic nodal prices, giving prosumers the ability to make optimal strategies ex ante. In the realtime stage a simple measurement of the stochastic drivers is sufficient to calculate realtime nodal prices, avoiding the need to run near-realtime optimization routines. Title: Interface Contact Optimization via Phosphomolybdic Acid Enables 24.9% Efficiency in MoOX-Based Silicon Solar Cells
Abstract: The development of cost-effective carrier-selective passivating contacts is critical for enhancing the commercial feasibility of silicon compound solar cells. Molybdenum oxide (MoOX) has garnered considerable interest as a promising hole transport layer (HTLs). A key advantage of MoOX is high work function, in addition to the low-cost processability. However, in silicon photovoltaics, MoOX-based p-type contacts face fundamental limitations at hydrogenated amorphous silicon (i-a-Si:H)/MoOX interface, where oxygen vacancy defects lower work function, as well as, weak van der Waals-dominated interactions impair charge carry transport. To address these challenges, we introduced an ultrathin phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) interlayer at the i-a-Si:H/MoOX interface. PMA passivated oxygen vacancy defects, resulting in a notable improvement in open-circuit voltage from 713 to 730 mV, and 0.11 eV work function elevation via dipole formation; meanwhile, PMA strengthened the interfacial bonding energy, reducing saturation current density and contact resistance by 63% and 24%, respectively, contributing to a fill factor enhancement from 83.7% to 84.9%. In the end, we demonstrated a record efficiency of 24.9% for MoOX-based silicon solar cells, which provides valuable insights for developing high-performance MoOX HTL devices for dopant-free p-type contact technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Seven Sisters tourism under siege: Hybrid neural insights into stakeholder resilience
Abstract: Tourism stakeholders in insurgency-affected destinations navigate persistent insecurity that shapes their perceptions, adaptive behavior, and support for tourism in nonlinear ways. This study investigates how security-related perceptions influence tourism support in Northeast India's Seven Sisters region, a politically fragile zone characterized by prolonged insurgency. ANN modeling revealed a nonlinear inverted-U relationship between security visibility and stakeholder support, interpreted as a “ security-skepticism dilemma” grounded in Prospect Theory. Title: Reinventing the package holiday: Consumer preferences and optimal pricing for hotel room upgrades
Abstract: We examine a tour operator initiative enabling consumers to select their hotel room before departure for a supplementary fee. Using a stated-preference discrete choice experiment with 691 UK package holidaymakers, we estimate conditional and mixed logit models to identify drivers of upgrade acceptance, derive willingness-to-pay (WTP) estimates, and compute the uptake probability as a continuous function of the fee. Room facilities command the highest WTP (£8.04 per unit), and room location the second-highest (£3.67 per unit); hotel location is insignificant. The revenue-maximizing fee is £33.1 per person, yielding a predicted uptake of 54.1%. Latent class analysis identifies three consumer segments with distinct price sensitivities, and segment-specific revenue optima reveal meaningful variation across hotel categories, lengths of stay, and party types, supporting differentiated fee structures. Title: Using vertical integration to safeguard against unfavorable bargaining position
Abstract: This paper examines the effect of a change in bargaining power on the decision to engage in vertical integration. Market contracts are inherently incomplete; when contingencies arise, firms rely on conventions to facilitate non-contractable adaptations. The perceived flexibility of informal agreements increases as the firm’s bargaining power weakens. Using data on the U.S. airline market (2006-2011), I find that buyers (mainline carriers) are more likely to vertically integrate when they have low bargaining power vis-à-vis suppliers (regional partners). Title: Mapping the global landscape of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship: A bibliometric review (2000–2025)
Abstract: Mentorship is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of women’s entrepreneurial participation and success. However, existing scholarship remains fragmented, conceptually inconsistent, and unevenly distributed across global contexts. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship, examining peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 globally. To enhance methodological robustness and address limitations associated with narrow keyword selection, a multi-stage search strategy was employed using the Scopus database. A total of 878 records were identified through the Scopus database. The final dataset includes 621 articles, allowing for a detailed analysis of publication trends, geographic distribution, authorship patterns, and thematic development within the field. The findings reveal a significant concentration of research output in the Global North, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, with comparatively limited representation from developing regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa. Thematic analysis indicates strong clustering around mentorship, coaching, entrepreneurial ecosystems, and capacity building, highlighting both conceptual convergence and fragmentation. Furthermore, the results show that mentorship is frequently embedded within broader entrepreneurial support frameworks rather than examined as a standalone construct. In response, this study advances a Gendered Social Capital and Learning framework to provide a more integrated understanding of mentorship processes in women’s entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the literature by offering a robust, data-driven overview of the field, identifying key gaps in geographic and theoretical coverage, and highlighting the methodological implications of keyword selection in bibliometric research. The findings provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to design more inclusive and contextually relevant mentorship interventions for women entrepreneurs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Yao H.; Chen Z.
Title: How autonomy-supportive environments and growth mindset foster creativity efficacy in middle school students? Evidence from a large-scale survey in China
Abstract: This study examines the associations between multi-source autonomy-supportive environments, growth mindset, and creative self-efficacy among Chinese middle school students, with particular attention to the mediating role of growth mindset and individual heterogeneity in these associations. Using large-scale survey data from 6146 middle school students in Suzhou, China, and drawing on Bandura's (1997) social cognitive theory and Self-Determination Theory, we employed structural equation modeling and quantile regression to investigate these relationships. The SEM results indicate that teacher, parental, and peer autonomy support are all positively associated with creative self-efficacy, with teacher and peer support showing stronger total associations than parental support. Growth mindset mediated all three associations, with the indirect effect proportion being highest for teacher autonomy support, followed by parental autonomy support and peer autonomy support. Quantile regression analyses revealed meaningful heterogeneity across the creative self-efficacy distribution: teacher and parental autonomy support showed stronger associations at lower quantiles, peer autonomy support peaked at moderate quantiles, and all associations weakened at higher quantiles. These findings contribute to the cross-cultural understanding of how multi-source autonomy-supportive environments relate to creative self-efficacy in a collectivist educational context, and offer practical implications for differentiated educational interventions targeting students at different levels of creative self-efficacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Anionic Bottom-Up Flux Orchestrated via Hard Carbon Surface Chemistry for Stable Sodium-Ion Batteries
Abstract: Hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries suffer from unstable solid-electrolyte interphase formation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and poor cycle stability. Herein, we demonstrate a molecular-level surface design that actively orchestrates an anionic bottom-up flux from the electrolyte bulk to the hard carbon interface. By engineering a synergistic pair of pyridinic-N and carbonyl groups on the carbon surface, we create a functional-differentiation microenvironment where pyridinic-N selectively anchors PF6− anions, while the cooperative carbonyl repels solvent molecules. This dual functionality establishes a sustained concentration gradient that drives a continuous reverse flux of anions toward the interface, fundamentally redirecting the electrolyte decomposition pathway from solvent-dominated to anion-preferential. The tailored surface lowers the PF6− decomposition barrier by over 70%, yielding a thin, inorganic-rich solid-electrolyte interphase dominated by NaF and Na2O. The optimized anode achieves 91.9% Coulombic efficiency with high reversible capacity of 368.2 mAh g−1, and 96.5% capacity retention after 5,000 cycles. A pouch cell assembled with NFPP cathode achieves an energy density of 239.1 Wh kg−1 and stable operation over 500 cycles, demonstrating strong practical potential. This work establishes active surface-guided anionic transport as a powerful strategy for interphase engineering in advanced sodium-ion batteries. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Elucidating the Respective Roles of Photochemical and Photothermal Effects in Photocatalytic Methanol Decomposition
Abstract: Photocatalytic reactions can be driven by both photochemical and photothermal processes. However, their individual contributions and synergistic effect remain to be clarified. Title: Can AI-generated images match human-generated images in inspiring travel? A visual feature analysis of audience perceptions and visit intention
Abstract: Generative AI tools can now create photorealistic destination images at low cost, yet whether such images motivate travel as effectively as human-generated images remains unclear. Title: Feelings of ease in generating ideas: My loyal companion that guides my mental action but does not help me generate more creative ideas
Abstract: The ability to generate creative ideas is an important skill for education. This study examined how feelings of ease in generating ideas act as a cue that allowed individuals to have information to monitor their mental action and make important metacognitive decisions while generating creative ideas. Participants were asked to generate four ideas to help deal with the problem of empty work offices during and after the pandemic of COVID-19. After generating each idea, participants reported their feelings of ease and evaluated the creativity of each idea. Title: Modified DEA-SBM efficiency-based diversion risk proxy assessment with peer similarity for decision support in aircraft diversion management
Abstract: Aircraft diversion is a critical component of aviation safety management, requiring close coordination among pilots, air traffic controllers, and airline operations teams. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, three real diversion cases in the Philippines are used as baseline scenarios. Title: Energy management systems for hybrid AC/DC microgrids: a problem-oriented review of system challenges and control architectures
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources introduces several system-level challenges for hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs), including power coordination, voltage regulation, uncertainty management, load–demand balancing, and energy storage coordination. Energy management systems (EMS) play a key role in addressing these challenges and ensuring reliable and efficient MG operation. Existing review studies mainly focus on methods and optimization techniques, while system challenges are not always clearly identified or examined from a structured perspective. Review and research studies are compiled in separate tables and categorized according to system challenges and the applied EMS approaches. The proposed classification explicitly covers rule-based, method-based, and objective-based EMS strategies and presents a multi-dimensional framework that links system challenges, control structures, and energy management approaches. Title: Task value, effort regulation and critical thinking: Towards a unified learning configuration in financial management education
Abstract: Financial Management requires students to integrate motivational, behavioural, and cognitive competencies to solve financial problems. However, existing research has predominantly examined these learner characteristics independently, providing limited understanding of how they coexist to shape learning. This study adopted a person-centred approach to identify distinct learning configurations based on task value, effort regulation, and critical thinking among Business students studying Financial Management. Title: Data-driven calibration sample selection and forecast combination in electricity price forecasting: An application of the ARHNN method
Abstract: Calibration sample selection and forecast combination are two simple yet powerful tools used in forecasting. They can be combined with a variety of models to significantly improve prediction accuracy, at the same time offering easy implementation and low computational complexity. While their effectiveness has been repeatedly confirmed in prior scientific literature, the topic is still underexplored in the field of electricity price forecasting. In this research article we apply the Autoregressive Hybrid Nearest Neighbors (ARHNN) method to three long-term time series describing the German, Spanish and New England electricity markets. Title: Gender Representation and Intercultural Competence in Iranian EFL Coursebooks from the 1960s to 2020s
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the representation of gender and intercultural competence in the images and texts of 15 Iranian secondary school English coursebooks, published over six decades. The representation of males and females in the books published in the 1970s was almost equal, followed by extreme and sudden changes in gender representation in the 1980s. However, the books published in and after the 2000s presented a balanced picture of males and females. The coursebooks dealt with intercultural competence in their texts and images very rarely, limiting this concept to religious issues and neglecting other aspects. Title: Perceived social entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial intention in times of crisis: Where moral obligation matters
Abstract: Social entrepreneurship education is widely promoted; however, the reflection of students' educational experience in social entrepreneurial intention remains insufficiently understood, particularly in institutionally fragile contexts. Drawing on survey data from 299 Lebanese university students, this study tests a moderated mediation model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Specifically, it examines whether personal attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control mediate the relationship between students' perceived social entrepreneurship education experience and entrepreneurial intention, and whether moral obligation conditions these pathways. More positive perceptions of the educational experience are associated with stronger intention indirectly through personal attitude and perceived behavioural control, while subjective norms show no significant effect, reflecting weakened normative reference points under prolonged crisis. Moral obligation operates selectively, strengthening the attitudinal pathway while leaving the control and the normative pathways unchanged. This study extends the mediated view of educational influence to social entrepreneurship education in a crisis setting, suggests that moral obligation may function as a conditional ethical amplifier, and shows how institutional fragility can affect the salient dimensions of TPB. Title: Technological, economic and environmental aspects of the production of sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker based on the mineral resources of Karakalpakstan; [Қарақалпақстанның минералдық ресурстары негізінде сульфатқа төзімді портландцемент клинкерін өндірудің технологиялық, экономикалық және экологиялық аспектілері]; [Технологические, экономические и экологические аспекты производства сульфатостойкого портландцементного клинкера на основе минеральных ресурсов Каракалпакстана]

Title: From sound to resonance: Club anthem attractiveness and fan–brand relationships
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Auditory branding plays an increasingly important role in sensory service experiences; however, limited research has examined how recurring auditory brand cues relate to consumer–brand relationship outcomes. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework as an organizing logic, this study examines associations among club anthem attractiveness (CAA), positive emotion (PE), post-exposure brand cognition (BC), and fan–brand resonance (FBR) in sports leisure services. Data were collected from a screened nonprobability online sample of 468 respondents in China. Participants listened to one of three standardized 90-s club anthem excerpts before evaluating CAA, PE, BC, and FBR. CAA was positively associated with both PE and BC, and these responses were positively associated with FBR. The two prespecified coefficient products were positive, whereas the residual direct CAA–FBR association was not significant. A separate balanced validation study (N = 450) supported CAA's empirical distinction from simple anthem liking, PE, BC, FBR, and prior brand attitude. CAA explained additional variance in PE and BC beyond simple liking and pre-exposure controls, while its incremental association with FBR was small. The findings indicate that evaluations of recurring auditory brand cues covary with consumer–brand relationship outcomes alongside affective and cognitive responses. This study extends auditory branding and sensory service literature by conceptualizing recurring branded sound as a service-embedded cue and examining theoretically ordered affective and cognitive associations. Title: Secondhand fashion subscription boxes: A necessary condition analysis of purchase intention determinants

Using a sample of 215 German participants, we found that most determinants are necessity-based bottlenecks. They must be present and reach a certain threshold. Title: Screen-Printed Li Arrays with Reinforced Interphase as Ultrathin Anodes for High-Energy–Density Liquid- and Solid-State Batteries
Abstract: High-energy–density lithium metal batteries, either liquid or solid state, require ultrathin Li anodes, but their implementation is hindered by poor Li processability in fabrication and inhomogeneous Li plating behaviours upon cycling. This work addresses these challenges through a mask-patterned discrete array using a molten salt-derived Li nanocomposite. The screen-printing strategy circumvents the poor wettability of molten Li on copper that causes high Li|Cu contact angle and non-uniform Li spreading, thus fabricating ultrathin Li foils with equivalent thicknesses below 30 μm. Concurrently, the molten salt-derived inorganic nanoparticles in Li favour homogeneous Li deposition and induce inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase to jointly suppress active Li consumption. The resulting Li array (10–28 μm) anodes demonstrate remarkable performance in both liquid- and solid-state systems, achieving high energy densities up to 504 Wh kg−1/1071 Wh L−1 and stable cycling over 260 cycles with high-loading cathodes. This integrated approach resolves both fabrication and cycling challenges of ultrathin Li anodes and offers an alternative solution for high-performance liquid-/solid-state batteries. Title: Beyond technological determinism: A multidimensional framework and research agenda for consumer trust in blockchain applications
Abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly integral to domains such as finance, supply chain, commerce and tourism, yet consumer trust remains a pivotal barrier to its widespread adoption. Studies on trust in blockchain contexts have significant conceptual and contextual limitations that inhibit a holistic understanding of trust formation. In this study, we draw on the antecedents, decisions, outcomes and theory, context, methods (ADO-TCM) framework to systematically review 53 high-quality multidisciplinary studies. We identify three critical issues: (1) technological determinism that conflates technical capability with consumer trust, marginalising psychological, social and institutional factors; (2) theoretical convergence around acceptance models that obscures blockchain-specific trust phenomena; and (3) a narrow geographic and domain scope that creates self-reinforcing knowledge hierarchies limiting generalisability across applications and cultures. To address these gaps, we propose a multidimensional trust framework integrating three dimensions: technological architecture trust, information source trust and social actor trust, reflecting blockchain's sociotechnical structure. Central to this framework is a four-paradigm typology that classifies trust into interpersonal, technology, institutional, and sociotechnical perspectives, revealing that the prevalence of technological determinism reflects theoretical inertia rather than genuine consensus. We complement this with three research themes: multi-level theoretical integration, innovative methodologies and contextual expansion. This study contributes to the information systems discourse by providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trust in complex sociotechnical systems beyond acceptance models. Title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism

Abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. Title: Registered Report Stage I: Signaling green, securing greenbacks: Sustainability claims and venture funding in hospitality & tourism start-ups

Title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Title: Silent Valleys: Unraveling the Causes and Strategic Pathways for Reverse Migration in Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand
Abstract: This study examines out-migration and the prospects for sustainable reverse migration in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand, addressing three objectives: identifying the main drivers of migration, synthesizing reinforcement strategies to reduce distress migration and support return, and linking causes and responses within a human-environment systems perspective. Title: Inside and out: Exploring how internal and external CSR perceptions influence hospitality employees’ service sabotage
Abstract: Although corporate social responsibility (CSR) has been shown to exert positive effects on hospitality organizations and their stakeholders, the interactive effect of internal CSR (ICSR) and external CSR (ECSR) perceptions on employees’ subsequent service behaviors remains unclear. Title: Mapping the intellectual structure of digital transformation research in SMEs: A decade of performance-oriented studies
Abstract: Despite their vital contribution to worldwide economic progress, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to environmental fluctuations, resource limitations, and swift technological shifts. In this context, digital transformation has emerged as a critical strategic mechanism through which firms seek to enhance competitiveness, resilience, and organizational outcomes. Although this topic has attracted considerable scholarly attention in recent years, the available literature is dispersed across different academic fields, theoretical viewpoints, and methodologies, making it difficult to gain a holistic understanding of the area's intellectual organization and progression. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to examine digital transformation and firm-level outcomes in small business contexts from January 2016 to January 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix through its Biblioshiny interface and VOSviewer. A final dataset of 186 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined using descriptive statistics, keyword co-occurrence analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation analysis, thematic mapping, and research trend analysis. The results indicate a strong and accelerating publication trend, with an annual growth rate of 17.46, particularly since 2020, highlighting the increasing strategic importance of digital technologies in response to economic disruptions and uncertainty. The analysis identifies four major thematic clusters: (1) performance-oriented outcomes, (2) technology - and capability-driven transformation, (3) organizational and sustainability-related performance, and (4) strategic and Industry 4.0-oriented transformation. In addition, emerging themes include digital readiness, dynamic capabilities, and business model innovation. While the literature frequently associates digital transformation with improved organizational outcomes, the findings also reveal persistent heterogeneity in results and highlight substantial risks and failure rates, especially among resource-constrained firms. By mapping the intellectual foundations, thematic structure, and evolution of this research domain, the study provides an integrative overview that supports theory development and informs future empirical research. The results also offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers who seek to understand and guide digital transformation initiatives in small business contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Development and validation of an ATP degradation model for predicting K-value progression in chilled greenling under variable temperature conditions
Abstract: Temperature fluctuations during refrigerated distribution can accelerate postmortem ATP degradation and complicate freshness management; therefore, a temperature-responsive model is needed to predict K-value progression under practical cold-chain conditions. The pooled variable A = ATP + ADP + AMP was modeled as converting to IMP and then to H = HxR + Hx through two first-order processes governed by empirical effective rate coefficients k1 and k2. The coefficients were calibrated at 0 and 5 °C, while 2.5 °C and intermittent 0–5 °C data were reserved for validation. Across the 24 observations reserved for validation, K-value predictions yielded an RMSE of 7.976 percentage points, an MAE of 5.180 percentage points, and an R2 of 0.885. During commercial transport, the representative prediction at approximately 51 h was 12.48%, compared with a measured group median of 11.97%, without parameter re-optimization. Title: The effect of rosé wine color: A conceptual replication and a generation-based extension
Abstract: Recent research on crossmodal correspondences from Jaud et al. (2025) highlighted the role of rosé wine color in shaping consumer responses. Title: Exemption or backfire? The double-edged effect of AI attribution strategy on brand trust in digital content moral crises

Abstract: Human-AI collaboration has become central to brand content production, but AI's black-box nature obscures responsibility in digital content moral crises. When such content is perceived as violating widely shared social values, brands increasingly attribute such incidents to AI errors. Prior research has mainly emphasized the responsibility-exemption role of AI attribution strategy, offering limited insight into its moral risks, mixed consequences, and underlying mechanisms. Drawing on the fact-value model, this study conducts five scenario-based experiments to examine how AI attribution strategy affects brand trust in this crisis context. The findings reveal a double-edged effect. At the factual level, this strategy increases consumers' perceived responsibility reduction, thereby producing an exemption effect that supports trust repair. At the value level, it also triggers perceived moral indifference, thereby producing a backfire effect that damages trust. This double-edged effect is moderated by public opinion and consumer traits. High negative electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) dispersion strengthens the perceived responsibility reduction path, whereas low negative eWOM dispersion strengthens the perceived moral indifference path. AI literacy strengthens the exemption effect by helping consumers understand AI-related technical limitations, whereas hostile attribution bias strengthens the backfire effect by leading consumers to question the moral motives behind the brand's technical explanation. This study advances crisis attribution research by examining AI attribution as a proactive brand communication strategy under attribution ambiguity and shows how it can reduce factual blame while raising value-based moral concerns. Title: Renewable electricity penetration and retail price dynamics: Global evidence on transitional costs of the energy transition
Abstract: The global expansion of renewable energy represents a structural transformation with profound macroeconomic and financial implications. Title: Recursive object-centric process discovery with fitness and rediscovery guarantees
Abstract: Digitized processes are an integral part of businesses to achieve their operational goals. Process mining aims to analyze such processes based on digital track records. These so-called event logs can be extracted from commonly used information systems. Traditionally, process mining remains limited as it requires individual business objects to define isolated process executions. However, in real-life processes, it is much more common to observe multiple business objects of various types that interact with each other. Object-centric process mining acknowledges this fact and fundamentally enhances traditional process mining techniques to analyze processes with interacting business objects. This analysis often requires a process model that describes the interacting control flows of all objects. Discovery algorithms are used to automatically construct such models from logs. For further steps, it is important that the discovery algorithm rediscovers a process model that is equivalent to the underlying business process. If it is impossible to rediscover the full behavior of a process, the discovered model should at least be fitting for the observed behavior. However, no existing object-centric discovery technique guarantees rediscovery or fitness. In this paper, we introduce a new algorithm that recursively constructs tree-structured object-centric models. We prove that our approach produces fitting models for all logs and rediscovers a subclass of processes within the used representational bias from logs that are sufficiently complete and free of incorrect recordings, unobserved or duplicated activities and loops. Title: The impact of technological developments on the changing role of HR(M): A scoping review and research agenda
Abstract: Due to technological developments, jobs disappear, new jobs arise, and existing jobs change. This leads to opportunities and challenges regarding human resource management (HRM) and the role of the HR function in the future of work. In this article, we explore how technological developments such as the use of smart technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and robotics influence HRM and the role of the HR function. Through a scoping review, we highlight the influence of technological developments across macro (societal), meso (organization/HRM) and micro (individual workers) level work themes. We specifically focus on the dynamic interplay between technological developments and HRM. At the meso level, the analysis zooms in on how technological developments influence HRM at the strategic, tactical, and operational levels within organizational contexts. Our findings inform a future research agenda comprising avenues aimed at deepening our understanding of the challenges and opportunities associated with technological change in the context of HRM. More specifically, we propose future research to explore how the HR function can prepare the organization, itself, and other stakeholders, including line managers and workers, for the impact of technological developments to enhance HRM for the greater good. Title: Attribution of causality following service failure on online retail platforms: The roles of governance structure and recurring failures
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online retail platforms are increasingly mediating customer–vendor interactions, yet research offers limited insight into how platform governance shapes service failure attribution, especially after recurring failures. Drawing on attribution theory, this paper examines how centralized versus diffused governance structures influence consumers’ attribution of causality to the platform after service failure and their responses to recurring failures. Study 1 analyzes customer reviews using computational text analysis and shows that customers recognize governance structures and attribute causality to the platform more often under centralized than diffused governance. Employing scenario-based experiments, Study 2 demonstrates that centralized (vs. diffused) governance leads to higher failure attribution to the platform. Finally, we show that attribution following single and recurring failures serially mediates the relationship between governance structure and repurchase intention after a recurring failure. Importantly, platform attribution exerts opposite effects across failure episodes: following a single failure and successful recovery, greater platform attribution increases repurchase intention by signaling platform accountability and resolution capability. However, following a recurring failure, greater platform attribution decreases repurchase intention because recurrence signals a stable, persistent cause and reduces attributional uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Hemisphere-aware Graph Convolution and 3D Structural Fusion for multi-modal fMRI brain-disorder classification
Abstract: Multimodal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data is a valuable source of information for precisely classifying neurological disorders, which is why it is widely used in the diagnosis of these diseases. However, traditional methods struggle to capture the spatiotemporal dynamics of the brain and single-modality approaches overlook voxel-level structural information. This limits the accuracy of imaging diagnoses of neurological diseases. This study therefore selected resting-state fMRI samples from the Autism Spectrum Disorder (ABIDE) and Parkinson's Disease (PPMI) datasets, proposing the multi-modal half-brain perception framework MSHAGL. This comprises a shared-weight half-brain–whole-brain graph convolutional network (CHW-GCN) and a three-dimensional structure encoder (GBConvNet3D). These are combined with multi-head gated fusion and redundancy suppression loss for joint optimization. Specifically, dynamic maps of the left and right hemispheres and the whole brain are constructed, cross-scale functional connectivity features are extracted, and 3D fMRI volumes are utilized to capture spatial structural patterns. Gating mechanisms achieve dynamic alignment and weighted fusion of temporal-structural features. In classification experiments on the ABIDE and PPMI datasets for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), the results demonstrate that hemispheric perception modelling and multimodal fusion effectively enhance diagnostic sensitivity and robustness while revealing abnormal connectivity and spatial activation patterns related to disease.
