Authors: Qi X.; Huang Z.; Chang W.
Title: Employee-led disclosure of anthropomorphism in tourism GAI failure recovery: A mind perception model from tourists and employees
Abstract: Generative AI (GAI) is increasingly mediating tourism service encounters, reshaping GAI failure recovery within a broader tourist–employee–GAI service configuration, in which GAI serves as the failure source, employees act as recovery agents, and tourists are the end recipients. Drawing on Mind Perception Theory, we theorize and test a post-failure recovery tactic in which employees intentionally foreground anthropomorphic aspects of the failing GAI during recovery interactions. Across six scenario-based experiments and two on-site simulation studies ( N = 2061), results provide convergent evidence that employee-led disclosure of GAI anthropomorphism (vs. control) improves recovery outcomes for both tourists and employees through mirrored mechanisms. Specifically, it increases tourist forgiveness by elevating perceived GAI experience and increases state employee satisfaction by elevating perceived GAI agency. These benefits weaken under high tourist anger or employees' perceptions of tourist anger and are further contingent on tourists' AI expertise and employees’ competitive versus collaborative mindset. The findings advance tourism research by offering parallel dyadic evidence on GAI failure recovery beyond a tourist-centric lens, extending Mind Perception Theory through stakeholder-contingent effects of perceived experience and perceived agency, and repositioning anthropomorphism in recovery as a co-produced mechanism jointly enacted through employee framing and available GAI interface affordances. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Invisible data infrastructure and cross-domain digital innovation: Evidence from data groups in China
Abstract: This study examines whether and how formalized data governance reshapes firms’ digital innovation by exploiting the staggered establishment of municipal data groups in China. Using a difference-in-differences design and Chinese A-share listed firms from 2008 to 2024, we find that municipal data group establishment significantly expands firms’ cross-domain digital innovation. This effect is stronger among state-owned enterprises, regulated industries, firms in cities with lower technological complexity, and regions with more developed market and factor environments. Additional analyses provide evidence consistent with several potential pathways: municipal data groups are associated with changes in R&D uncertainty, managerial innovation expectations, interregional collaboration, and innovation activities. Further analysis reveals a quantity–quality divergence: data group establishment increases patent output but is associated with lower average measured patent quality, particularly among firms receiving stronger innovation incentives. This pattern is consistent with multiple explanations, including incentive responses and innovation composition changes. Title: Balancing productivity and safety: a risk-aware framework for human-robot collaborative workflows
Abstract: This paper addresses the Assembly Line Balancing Problem (ALBP) in the context of Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC), integrating task failure risks through Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (PFMEA)-inspired framework. Title: Green architectural tactics in ML-enabled systems: an LLM-based repository mining study
Abstract: Context: The increasing adoption of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies raises growing concerns about their environmental sustainability. Developing and deploying ML-enabled systems is computationally intensive, particularly during training and inference. While prior research has proposed catalogs of sustainable practices (i.e., green tactics), there remains limited understanding of their adoption in practice and whether additional, undocumented tactics exist. Title: How should conversational recommendation agents organize candidate products? Matching recommendation set granularity with time pressure
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: With the widespread application of conversational recommendation agents (CRA) on e-commerce platforms, an increasing number of consumers use a CRA to support product choices. Existing research has mainly focused on the accuracy of CRA recommendations, with limited attention paid to how candidate products should be organized and whether this organization should be adapted to consumers' current decision contexts. Drawing on the product set granularity perspective and the heuristic–systematic model, this study examines the matching effect between recommendation set granularity (coarse vs. fine) and time pressure (high vs. low) on consumers' intention to adopt CRA recommendations and investigates the underlying psychological mechanisms. The results of three online scenario experiments reveal that consumers show higher adoption intention toward CRA recommendations featuring coarse recommendation set granularity under high time pressure and toward those featuring fine recommendation set granularity under low time pressure. The two matching effects operate through perceived fluency and perceived attractiveness, respectively. Furthermore, consumer knowledge affects the relative effectiveness of the two matching strategies: the match between coarse recommendation set granularity and high time pressure is more effective for consumers with low product knowledge, whereas the match between fine recommendation set granularity and low time pressure is more effective for consumers with high product knowledge. Title: Good listening as a wise negotiation tactic
Abstract: Listening is a foundational interpersonal skill. Effective listening is central to managing the dual demands of negotiation: competing over limited resources while sustaining cooperation and trust. Nevertheless, limited research has shed light on how to listen effectively in negotiation. Integrating research from psychology, communication, and negotiation, we identify three common listening traps that undermine negotiation effectiveness: negotiators tend to focus too much on: (1) the self (and too little on others); (2) resolving disagreement (and too little on exploring it); and (3) what is said (and too little on what remains unspoken). We propose three approaches for effective listening in negotiations: (1) listening to understand rather than persuade; (2) listening for movement and change; and (3) making listening observable through concrete verbal and nonverbal behaviors. We argue that high-quality listening improves both informational and relational outcomes by facilitating deeper information exchange, increasing trust, and supporting integrative agreements. By highlighting high-quality listening as a wise negotiation tactic, this article illustrates how negotiators can better navigate the tension between cooperation and competition in mixed-motive interactions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: When and why women ask (or do not): Taking stock of research on gender differences in negotiation propensity, behavior, and outcomes
Abstract: Evidence first emerged several decades ago that women are less likely than men to initiate negotiations and perform less competitively than men in negotiations. Researchers also have discovered moderators of these effects, including structural ambiguity, representation role, and gender salience and relevance. Furthermore, the anticipation of backlash has emerged as a potential mechanism to explain gender differences in negotiations. Yet, more recent research has revealed varied findings concerning whether gender differences, underlying mechanisms, and moderators have shifted, as well as the role of intersectionality. We review the research in this area and find that the nature of gender differences in negotiation is complex, with some recent research replicating certain past findings (e.g., gender gaps in negotiation behavior) but not others (i.e., gender gaps in negotiation propensity or moderation by representation role). Still other recent research has even revealed a reversal of gender gaps in negotiation propensity, with women being more likely than men to negotiate in certain cases, and that female negotiation counterparts are liked more than male negotiation counterparts, leading to greater counterpart satisfaction. We also consider the role of statistical power given the small-to medium-sized effects typically reported: Sample size may be another important reason for inconsistent findings in the gender and negotiation literature. Finally, we consider the potential for changing gender roles. Overall, we conclude that gender differences in negotiation performance outcomes persist and are influenced by situational nuances, but that these differences have been mitigated for propensity to initiate negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Hub-centric heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning for integrated automated guided vehicle dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling with finite-buffer constraints
Abstract: The integration of automated guided vehicle (AGV) dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling constitutes a challenging problem in flexible manufacturing systems, particularly when finite output buffers cause blocking effects and potential deadlocks. This paper investigates an integrated event-driven AGV dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling problem with finite-buffer constraints, aiming to minimize the makespan. In this study, dispatching refers to the real-time assignment of AGVs to transportation tasks, whereas scheduling refers to assigning workpieces to parallel machines and determining processing sequences. These two decision processes are strongly coupled through transportation, processing, and buffer interactions. To address the strong coupling among transportation, processing, and buffering decisions, this paper proposes a framework that integrates a hub-centric heterogeneous graph neural network (HCHGNN) with proximal policy optimization (PPO), termed HCHGNN-PPO. The manufacturing system is modeled as a hub-centric heterogeneous graph comprising four node types: orders, AGVs, waiting areas, and buffer areas. In this structure, AGVs serve as hub nodes that bridge task sources and processing resources. To leverage this, an HCHGNN encoder is developed to extract structured state representations via AGV-mediated message passing and learnable feature standardization. To improve training stability, a decoupled actor–critic architecture is introduced, in which the policy and value networks use independent graph encoders and optimizers. Moreover, a priority-based action-masking mechanism reduces the risk of buffer-induced blocking by prioritizing buffer-clearance operations, while an incremental reward based on minimum idle-time progression provides denser feedback for makespan-oriented learning. Extensive experiments on various benchmark instances demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional dispatching rules and representative deep reinforcement learning baselines. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework to generate effective scheduling decisions for complex integrated manufacturing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Unveiling the effects of multidimensional urban shrinkage on urban flood resilience: A case study of the Yangtze River Basin, China
Abstract: Climate change poses growing flood-management challenges for cities undergoing economic, demographic, and spatial decline. Using 1921 city-year observations for 113 prefecture-level cities in China’s Yangtze River Basin (YRB) from 2007 to 2023, this study develops a six-subsystem urban flood resilience (UFR) framework encompassing socioeconomic conditions, ecological environment, infrastructure, institutional support, spatial structure, and climate stress. These findings identify robust associations and scenario-dependent pathways rather than causal effects. Title: Capability, opportunity, and motivation for healthy eating: Exploring gender-specific pathways
Abstract: Women generally consume a healthier diet than men; however, both fall short of dietary guidelines. This conceptual replication tested the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation and Behaviour (COM-B) model for dietary behaviour, originally evaluated in a female-dominant sample, in a male-dominant sample (N = 1358; 67% male). Authors: Kim S.-H.
Title: What makes human service distinctly human in the AI era? Conceptualizing and measuring authentic relational service competency
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) service agents increasingly simulate human interaction, the basis for distinguishing human service has become theoretically ambiguous. While prior research consistently identifies authenticity as a key limitation of AI-enabled service, authenticity remains underdeveloped as a uniquely human service capability. Addressing this gap, we introduce Authentic Relational Service (ARS) as a distinct form of service through which frontline employees create genuine, contextually responsive, and relationship-centered customer interactions. We further conceptualize authenticity as a competency-based capability and develop a measure of Authentic Relational Service Competency (ARSC), which enables frontline employees to enact ARS. Using established scale-development procedures, this study identifies and validates four dimensions of ARSC: perspective-taking, patience, creativity, and agility. By conceptualizing and operationalizing Authentic Relational Service as a distinct human service capability, this research advances theory on human-AI service differentiation and provides a foundation for understanding uniquely human value creation in service contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Affordances and paradoxical engagement in virtual immersive learning platforms: A configurational analysis across demographic groups
Abstract: Virtual immersive learning platforms (VILPs), integrating immersive technologies, gamified design, and learning tools, enable meaningful engagement in learning while also creating possibilities for compulsive engagement. Drawing on a sociotechnical affordance perspective, this study examines how configurations of affordances are associated with meaningful and compulsive engagement and how these pathways vary across demographic conditions. Using a mixed-methods design, we first uncover the core affordances of VILPs and organize them within a sociotechnical perspective. We then employ a two-stage fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to examine affordance configurations associated with different engagement outcomes and the role of demographic conditions. The findings show that meaningful and compulsive engagement are associated with distinct combinations of affordances and these configurational patterns vary across demographic conditions. Authors: Deng G.; Ye T.; Liu J.; Xu Y.
Title: Synergy or backfire? Adding virtual influencers to advertisements featuring human influencers: The roles of sensory cues and temporal framing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: In recent years, virtual influencers (VIs) have emerged as a salient presence in brand communication. Firms are increasingly featuring them alongside human influencers (HIs) in advertising campaigns. Yet whether such HI–VI co-endorsement creates synergy or instead backfires remains unclear. Drawing on cue utilization theory and the elaboration likelihood model, this research examines how endorsement format, defined as advertisements featuring only HI(s) versus HI–VI co-endorsement, and advertising sensory cue type (distal vs. proximal) jointly shape consumers’ purchase intentions, and how this relationship varies across temporal frames (past vs. future). Results from four experiments (total N = 1293) show that advertisements featuring both an HI and a VI are more effective than advertisements featuring only HIs when distal sensory cues are emphasized, but less effective when proximal sensory cues are highlighted. These effects operate through two distinct mechanisms: perceived novelty explains the synergy associated with HI–VI co-endorsement under distal sensory cues, whereas perceived authenticity explains the advantage of advertisements featuring only HIs under proximal sensory cues. Moreover, future-oriented framing strengthens the novelty-based effectiveness of HI–VI co-endorsement, whereas past-oriented framing favors advertisements featuring only HIs through authenticity-based evaluations, particularly when proximal sensory cues are emphasized. By identifying when HI–VI co-endorsement succeeds or fails, this research extends endorsement theory from a source-substitution perspective to a hybrid co-endorsement perspective and provides practical implications for advertising strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Understanding conflict in protected areas: integrating justice considerations with economic perspectives
Abstract: Despite broad agreement on the urgency of sustainability transitions that protect biodiversity, conservation conflicts continue to rise. This paper examines environmental conflicts in protected areas (PAs), highlighting the overlooked link between conflict and justice. Existing frameworks often fail to distinguish between conflict manifestations and determinants, or to integrate justice theories with economic perspectives. This study provides a comprehensive review of the literature to support the analysis of PA conflicts and develops a robust framework that integrates justice considerations with the economic perspective. Conflicts are viewed as inherent to complex social–ecological systems, shaped by social relations and rights over ecosystem services. The framework is structured around three analytical axes: substance (what the conflict is about), process (how it unfolds), and relation (who is involved with-whom). It differentiates between how conflicts appear (i.e., manifestation) and what causes them (i.e., determinants), framed through distributive, procedural, and recognition justice. This perspective challenges linear assumptions that conflicts always stem from injustices, emphasizing their potential to drive institutional change. The framework offers a novel approach to assessing justice-conflict dynamics in PAs governance, providing comprehensive toolkit for promoting equitable conservation strategies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: ST-AHM: a soft-threshold sparse-attention hypergraph model with contrastive learning for session-based recommendation
Abstract: Session-based recommendation (SBR) predicts the next interaction from anonymous, short-lived behavioral sequences. A central challenge is to capture higher-order dependencies within sessions and collaborative information across related sessions while limiting weak contextual relations. We propose ST-AHM, a dual-channel model that jointly represents within-session and cross-session information. In the within-session channel, hypergraph convolution captures higher-order item dependencies. Hypergraph-specific sparse attention (HSPA) then averages scaled compatibility scores across attention heads before applying Sparsemax. This operation creates a consensus-based sparse support while retaining head-specific value projections, thereby reducing the propagation of weakly supported relations. An identity-free blank node summarizes the enhanced sequence and produces a context-dependent session-intent representation without relying directly on the last item. In the cross-session channel, Jaccard similarity between session item sets defines a relational graph. Relational graph convolution propagates collaborative information, and the blank-node representation acts as a blank-node-derived query for aggregating relevant cross-session context. A contrastive objective aligns valid interaction representations with the blank-node-augmented view of the same session and distinguishes them from shuffled representations. Across Tmall, Diginetica, and 30Music, ST-AHM outperformed the evaluated baselines, including DCL-BPM, DiffSBR, and MSGAT. Its average improvements were 19.23% for HR@10, 12.71% for HR@20, 23.19% for MRR@10, and 24.28% for MRR@20. These results support the joint modeling of within-session and cross-session information while reducing the influence of weak relations. Title: Non-intrusive appliance classification in smart grids using swin transformer mixtures
Abstract: As smart grids evolve, non-intrusive appliance classification has become an important enabler of demand-side energy management and grid intelligence. However, accurately identifying appliances from aggregate low-resolution power measurements remains challenging due to concurrent appliance operation, temporal variability, and similar consumption signatures across appliances. To address these challenges, we transform consumption windows into complementary time-series images to provide richer spatiotemporal representations and enable robust image-based learning and classification. We propose a Mixture of Swin Transformers (MoST) in which a pretrained Swin backbone extracts features from stacked multi-modal images while a mixture-of-experts transformer head performs adaptive appliance classification. To improve sample efficiency and accelerate convergence, we fine-tune ImageNet-pretrained Swin weights via transfer learning. For resource-constrained deployment, we further optimize MoST using Neural Architecture Search (NAS). Experiments on ENERTALK and REFIT show that MoST with multi-modal fusion outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 100% multi-class accuracy and over 94% multi-label F1-score. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Munir K.; Nand A.
Title: Circular economy approaches to sustainable food waste management in the hospitality and food services sector
Abstract: The Circular Economy (CE) as a model has become a widespread approach to promoting sustainability through the restoration and regeneration of products and materials within production and consumption. Despite the plethora of work done, research on the application of CE principles for food waste management in the hospitality and food services (HaFS) sector remains scarce. This study adopts a conceptual review approach and follows the PRISMA-ScR guidelines to address this gap through exploring the role of CE in reducing and managing food waste in the HaFS sector through a review of papers between 2015 and 2026. The findings indicate that collective efforts of both actor-internal (hospitality managers and staff) and actor-external (customers, local authorities and government) stakeholders are essential to achieve sustainable and circular practices. Additionally, a framework that supports managerial decision-making by aligning with external stakeholders to enable circular food waste management is proposed for adoption in the HaFS sector. Title: Personalized assignment of UAV rescue tasks: an integrated framework of content-based filtering and two-stage robust optimization
Abstract: This paper presents a novel integrated framework approach of content-based filtering and two-stage robust optimization for personalized assignment of UAV rescue tasks. Our approach differs from traditional UAV task assignment method in that (1) The personalized assignment of UAV task is established on the mining of “fine-grained” attributes such as hovering capability, payload capacity, wind resistance, and rainproof capability, etc; rather than simply considering “coarse-grained” attributes like cost, time, and capacity. (2) Pre-disaster airport positioning and UAV allocation are integrated with post-disaster task assignment into a single model, accounting for the uncertainty of disaster scenarios. In our approach: Text mining techniques are first employed to identify the “fine-grained” attributes of UAVs and rescue tasks. Subsequently, content-based filtering method is utilized to calculate the matching degree between UAVs and rescue tasks. Finally, a two-stage robust optimization model, incorporating constraints based on the matching degree parameters, is applied to optimize both pre-disaster UAV deployment and post-disaster task assignment plans. Our approach is applied in a real-world earthquake case study. The results verify the correctness and efficiency of the method. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Fan Y.; Wang M.; Zhang X.; Shi R.
Title: When products speak: The effects of product-as-subject anthropomorphic communication on consumer responses to carted products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Shopping cart abandonment is a pervasive challenge in e-commerce, with more than 70% of online shopping carts failing to convert into purchases. In this context, this research examines whether and how anthropomorphic communication directed at carted products influences consumers' responses to shopping cart reminders. Across five experiments, we find converging evidence that product-as-subject anthropomorphic communication enhances consumers' purchase-related responses to carted products. Study 1 shows that product-as-subject anthropomorphic communication generates stronger responses than both non-anthropomorphic and brand-as-subject anthropomorphic communication, while Study 2 demonstrates that these effects are robust across different levels of pity conveyed in the message. Study 3 identifies state empathy and perceived interestingness as parallel mediators. Study 4 further demonstrates that these indirect effects are stronger among consumers with an emotional (vs. rational) decision-making style. Finally, Study 5 extends the findings to behavioral responses, showing that product-as-subject anthropomorphic communication increases behavioral cart re-engagement and reduces consumers’ reported likelihood of cart abandonment. This research advances understanding of anthropomorphic communication in shopping cart contexts and offers actionable guidance for the design of shopping cart reminders. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Investigation of uncertainties associated with human judgment during the inspection and condition assessment of civil infrastructures
Abstract: Inspection of civil infrastructure components is a critical task to assess their condition states and plan for appropriate maintenance actions. The process of inspection, however, involves several sources of uncertainty that can influence how a component is rated by an inspector. Despite potential consequences, such uncertainties have remained largely unexplored. This motivated the current study to develop a holistic framework to first measure the agreement and consistency of condition state predictions provided by various inspectors through the inter-rater reliability and intra-class correlation methods. The study then advanced to understand how the provided condition ratings can be analyzed, updated, and aggregated, taking into consideration possible interactions among inspectors during an inspection task. The outcome was quantified based on the inclination of participating inspectors to make more conservative, realistic, or less conservative assessments. The cumulative prospect theory was then utilized to quantify how the risk tolerance of individual inspectors can influence the decision making process, both at the time of inspection and during the service life of civil infrastructure components subjected to inspection. In the absence of similar studies, this investigation’s findings helped improve how condition state ratings received from inspectors can be processed and incorporated into a decision making framework. While the exploration of the psychological roots of why various inspectors rate the same component differently remained outside the scope of this study, the quantification of contributing uncertainties is expected to guide future training programs to further enhance the quality of condition assessment and management decisions made based on inspection reports. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Safety concepts through a memetic lens
Abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. As a case, this paper traces the historic development of one of safety’s most influential and iconic safety concepts, the accident triangle, over nearly a century through successive cycles of replication, variation, and selection. Knowledge of factors that influence the adoption of safety concepts can contribute to the design of more effective concepts that attract attention and of social and organisational environments that are receptive of these concepts. In the end, provided the concepts in question are useful, this can contribute to enhancing safety and reducing harm. In addition, the insights gained in this paper can help safety professionals and academics to critically reflect on the development of safety concepts, to help them better understand how safety concepts evolve and can change meaning leading to various interpretations and reflect on what this means for their own adoption of concepts and eventually their practice. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Exploring generation Z nurses' experiences of shift work in intensive care units: A qualitative analysis
Abstract: Objectives: Generation Z nurses are entering the workforce with distinct expectations regarding work–life balance, professional recognition, and organisational support. Intensive Care Units (ICUs), characterised by rotating and night shifts, are associated with significant psychophysical and organisational demands. This study explored how Generation Z nurses perceive and manage ICU shift work and its impact on well-being, coping strategies, professional integration, and career sustainability. Methods: A qualitative interpretative descriptive study was conducted in ICUs of a tertiary-care academic hospital in northeastern Italy. Thirty Generation Z nurses working rotating 24-h shifts participated (mean age 25.2 years; mean ICU experience 1.7 years). Semi-structured interviews were conducted between June and September 2025, audio-recorded, and transcribed verbatim. Data were analysed inductively using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis. Coding was performed independently by two researchers and refined through team-based analytic discussion and consensus. Results: Three themes emerged: (1) Experiencing psychophysical imbalance; (2) Seeking stability in an unstable context; and (3) Navigating professional identity. Participants described fatigue, circadian disruption, sleep disturbances, and anticipatory anxiety related to shift work. Nurses adopted coping strategies including structured routines, emotional regulation, and digital boundary-setting. Peer support facilitated professional adaptation and resilience. However, limited organisational recognition, communication barriers, and perceived undervaluation of competencies contributed to disillusionment and uncertainty about future career development. Participants questioned the long-term sustainability of shift work and considered pursuing further education or alternative career pathways. Conclusions: Generation Z nurses experience ICU shift work as demanding and potentially unsustainable early in their careers. Organisational recognition, supportive leadership, and structured transition processes appear important to promote well-being, professional integration, and workforce retention. Implications for clinical practice: These findings highlight the need for supportive leadership practices, mentorship programmes, and structured transition pathways to support the well-being, professional development, and retention of Generation Z nurses in ICUs. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Zhou D.; Gong Z.
Title: Organizational responsibility attribution: Public responses to AI versus human failures in government services
Abstract: Existing research provides only limited insights into whether, compared to traditional human service failures, artificial intelligence (AI) failures in government services lead the public to attribute more responsibility to the service organization, and whether outsourcing necessarily alleviates organizational responsibility attribution. To advance this debate, this study conducted three pre-registered survey experiments. Study 1 (N = 1112) reveals that citizens attributed more responsibility to the service organization for AI service failures than to human service agents. The effect was mediated by the perceived service provider's controllability, rather than by counterfactual thinking. Study 2 proposed and tested two distinct pathways, namely the responsibility-transfer and controllability-transfer pathways. The objective was to explain how diminished controllability perceived at the individual service provider level increases the attribution of responsibility to the organization. Empirical evidence (N = 1084) supports the responsibility-transfer pathway. When citizens perceive that AI agents have less control over services than humans, they assign less responsibility to the AI agent and transfer more responsibility to the service organization. Study 3 (N = 1007) examines whether disclosing that the AI agent was externally developed mitigates the attribution of organizational responsibility. Compared to in-house AI systems, outsourcing to either a state-owned enterprise or a private enterprise, rather than to other government organizations, reduced organizational responsibility. In this study, this reduction was substantial enough to eliminate the disparity between AI and human service failures. This study advances theories of responsibility attribution in the digital era, highlighting the nuanced role of outsourcing transparency and the responsibility-transfer mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Pharmaceutical Import Forecasting for Supply-Chain Decision Support: A Comparative Evaluation of Fuzzy, Statistical, and Machine-Learning Models
Abstract: Purpose: Pharmaceutical supply-chain planning in import-dependent economies is sensitive to macroeconomic shocks, currency volatility, and global supply disruptions. This study evaluates a Dynamic Fuzzy Time Series (DFTS) candidate together with statistical and machine-learning benchmarks for annual pharmaceutical-import forecasting. Methods: Azerbaijan’s annual pharmaceutical-import observations for 2012–2023 are used for model development; the 2024 observation (USD 507.50 million) is reserved as an untouched external holdout. Model comparison uses a common rolling-origin/expanding-window protocol beginning with a 2012–2017 initial training window. RMSE is pre-specified as the primary loss, with MAE and sMAPE as complementary measures. The DFTS recency parameter rho is selected from {0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00}, and an optional log-space long-term blending weight alpha is selected from {0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00}, using pre-2024 rolling-origin RMSE only. The best DFTS setting was rho = 0.70 with RMSE = 120.17 million USD; adding the long-term log-trend component did not reduce RMSE, so the selected alpha was 0 and the hybrid candidate collapsed to the DFTS component. Its frozen 2024 forecast was USD 591.91 million, corresponding to a 16.63% absolute percentage error, compared with 10.51% for the naive benchmark. Conclusion: The revised evidence does not support a claim that the hybrid/DFTS candidate outperforms simple benchmarks on this short annual series. Authors: Zhao J.; Yang H.; Pan Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Wireless mobile charging for emergency electric vehicle routing: A mixed-integer and metaheuristic framework for in-motion energy transfer
Abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) become central to decarbonization efforts, the need for uninterrupted power supply in time-critical logistics, particularly in medical transportation, poses unique challenges for power systems integration. Conventional fixed or mobile charging infrastructure requires vehicle downtime, which makes them unsuitable for nonstop operations such as organ delivery. This work introduces the Wireless Mobile Charging Electric Vehicle Routing Problem, a novel framework in which mobile charging trucks wirelessly transfer energy to moving EVs via inductive coupling, eliminating the need for stationary charging stops. We formulate a mixed-integer programming model that co-optimizes routing and in-motion energy transfer between heterogeneous vehicle fleets under temporal and spatial alignment constraints. To address computational complexity, we develop a hybrid Bitmask Dynamic Programming and Large Neighborhood Search algorithm, tailored to arc-level charging decisions and dual-fleet synchronization. Experiments using real-world hospital logistics data from Singapore demonstrate significant runtime improvements and higher-quality solutions compared with commercial solvers. This study advances computational power system modeling by incorporating dynamic, motion-based energy delivery that is both time- and space-dependent. The results provide actionable insights into planning mobile energy infrastructure, enhancing demand-side flexibility, strengthening resilience in emergency logistics, and integrating wireless charging into urban power systems to support flexible and zero-carbon electrified mobility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Nature sells: How visual biophilia influences promotional effectiveness of service firms

Abstract: Amidst the crowded media environment and growing consumer disconnection from nature, leveraging biophilia - the innate human tendency to connect with nature - offers a compelling way for service firms to attract and engage consumers. This research advances service literature by examining the effects of direct and indirect biophilia in service advertising using schema congruity theory. Across two studies, we show that indirect biophilia led to more favorable ad evaluations compared to direct biophilia and no biophilia (control). Title: Comparing applicants’ self-presentation in artificial intelligence versus human interviews: The role of opportunity to perform and contingency-based interactivity
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly embedded in employment interviews. Although AI interviewers may enhance the efficiency and standardization of personnel selection, their effects on applicants’ authentic and inauthentic self-presentation remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on impression management theory, this study examines how AI interviewers, relative to human interviewers, shape applicants’ self-presentation and why differences arise. Across four studies, we find that applicants facing AI interviewers perceive fewer opportunities to perform than those facing human interviewers. This reduced opportunity to perform, in turn, weakens not only exaggerated self-enhancement but also authentic self-presentation and authentic self-enhancement. These findings indicate that AI interviewers do not constrain deceptive impression management. They also dampen the expression of genuine strengths and self-relevant information. The results also show that contingency-based interactivity can mitigate this disadvantage by enhancing applicants’ perceived opportunity to perform and narrowing the gap between AI and human interviewers. By identifying both the constraining effects of AI interviewers and the design conditions that can reduce them, this study advances the research on AI interviews and offers practical implications for the design of more effective AI-enabled interview systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Sun Y.; Shen X.
Title: FracBiNet: Fractional bilateral decomposition with heterogeneous dual-path modeling for cross-market stock index prediction
Abstract: Stock index levels are hard to predict one day ahead: daily series are noisy and near-integrated, with only a few thousand observations per market. We propose FracBiNet, a lightweight decomposition model with 4, 612 trainable parameters. Its core is a causal fractional bilateral kernel coupling a power-law temporal decay with an edge-preserving range gate. An innovation-whitening criterion on a dedicated learning-rate clock calibrates the kernel’s two parameters. Its latest level is the trend anchor, and a small additive-attention network models the residual. We evaluate under a leakage-free walk-forward protocol with eleven test folds (2014–2024) across CSI 300, S&P 500, and Dow Jones. Every baseline is tuned per fold under identical grids, with five seeds and Diebold–Mariano tests against persistence. First, FracBiNet is Pareto-efficient among learned models. It is the only one never significantly worse than persistence on any market; all eleven baselines are significantly worse on at least two of three. Title: Bridging Transparency Gaps in Construction Claims through Blockchain Integration
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The construction industry plays a vital role in Pakistan's economy, yet it continues to face persistent challenges in claim administration that hinder project performance, transparency, and trust among stakeholders. This study addresses these challenges by identifying the principal shortcomings of conventional claim management systems and developing a blockchain-based claims management application to improve security, traceability, and procedural efficiency. A three-stage research design was adopted. First, a systematic literature review was conducted to identify deficiencies in traditional claim management practices. This was followed by semistructured interviews with fifteen contract specialists involved in extension of time (EOT) claims to validate and refine the identified issues. Second, a decentralized application (DApp) was developed using React.js front-end and Solidity-based smart contracts and deployed on the Polygon test network to enable faster and more cost-effective transactions. Third, the developed system was evaluated through expert review involving 32 participants drawn from contracting, consulting, client organizations, and academia, followed by statistical analysis. The findings indicate that the proposed blockchain-based claims management system (B-CMS) improves data integrity, transparency, traceability, and timeliness in claim administration compared with traditional approaches. However, the system is not intended to replace professional judgment in highly subjective claim situations and is not suitable for capturing oral instructions or unstructured design and work-pattern changes. Despite these limitations, the study demonstrates the feasibility of B-CMS for construction claim administration in Pakistan and offers insights that may be relevant to comparable project environments internationally.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: A flow shop scheduling problem incorporating a reconfigurable material handling Robot: A constraint programming approach
Abstract: A reconfigurable manufacturing system (RMS) is a new paradigm for the manufacturing environment to respond to unpredictable market change and frequent new product introduction. Finally, comprehensive computational experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of both models, followed by a sensitivity analysis on three key performance indicators to further assess the CP model and extract the managerial insights. Results show that the CP model has better performance than the MILP model for solving large-scale problem instances and achieves a high-quality solution in a reasonable time. Title: Lifecycle costs of safety instrumented systems in process industries: a systematic literature review
Abstract: A safety instrumented system (SIS) is an automated system designed to detect and mitigate potential risk of hazardous conditions in industrial processes by taking actions to prevent or mitigate incidents. It is essential because it helps protect people, equipment, and the environment by reducing the risk of accidents in hazardous operations, such as in chemical plants, oil refineries, or power stations. While the primary objective of SIS design is safety, economic considerations, particularly lifecycle cost, play a pivotal role in decision-making during the design phase. Although research efforts exist to incorporate lifecycle cost with safety, the literature is fragmented and lacks a comprehensive lifecycle cost framework. Therefore, a systematic literature review is conducted to uncover safety instrumented systems’ lifecycle cost elements and the decision variables that impact them. The review results lead to a comprehensive and structured cost calculation framework to assess SIS designed to protect a process unit economically. Finally, this study provides perspectives on potential research directions relevant to SIS lifecycle cost, including the impact of systematic failures, cybersecurity integration, the relative weighting of different cost elements, inclusion of risk costs, and various SIS application types. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Nuclear ship Mutsu and the 1974 radiation leak Incident: Technical background and management lessons
Abstract: During its experimental voyage in September 1974, Japan’s first nuclear-powered ship, Mutsu, experienced abnormal radiation during a low-power reactor test conducted approximately 800 km east of Cape Shiriya in Aomori Prefecture. The immediate technical mechanism involved fast-neutron streaming and secondary gamma-ray generation caused by an inadequate shielding configuration. Although the event did not involve major fuel damage or a large release of radioactive material, it developed into a serious operational and political problem, leading to resistance to the ship’s return and to a government investigation. This paper reconstructs the incident and reviews the technical and organizational conditions that shaped its occurrence and subsequent handling. Drawing on official reports, technical records, and prior studies, it examines how inadequate project integration, limited design review, contractual separation, and communication failures complicated what began as a shielding-design problem. Using action system theory of management as a heuristic framework, we organize key task-level findings and relate them to recurrent patterns in major public technology projects. The case indicates that, in prototype nuclear systems, technical adequacy alone is insufficient: integrated review, clear responsibility, and effective communication are also essential to safe development and testing. Title: Using reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a wine tasting service in Italy: Findings from a life cycle assessment application experience
Abstract: Wine tourism, including winery visits, tastings, and cultural events, boosts sustainable development but generates environmental impacts ranging from food and wine production to tasting services. This study applies Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), focused on Carbon Footprint (CF), to compare the use of reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a tasting service in an Apulian winery. A cradle-to-grave analysis reveals that, in baseline scenario, reusable plates showed a slightly higher CF than single-use plates (0.0668 vs. 0.0635 kgCO₂eq/person served, respectively). Based on the results obtained, process optimisation solutions were identified: it was found that using photovoltaic-powered energy-efficient dishwasher may reduce the CF of reusable plates by 67%, reducing the impact to 0.0179 kgCO₂eq/person served in the best-performing scenario. Five service configurations were then tested over a total of 2500 customers served in six months, assuming a constant optimal dishwasher loading efficiency (i.e., operating exclusively at full capacity). Whilst the absolute reuse rate of the plate stock inherently scales with customer volume (averaging approximately 73 uses per plate in the baseline period), the results showed that, without technological improvements, the lowest-impact option was to serve 500 people with reusable plates and 2000 with disposable plates. Overall, this study extends the application of Life Cycle Assessment from conventional production systems to experiential tourism services. The findings demonstrate that the environmental performance of tableware is not solely dictated by intrinsic material properties, but is fundamentally driven by the systemic operational configuration, including dishwashing efficiency, service volumes, and the carbon intensity of the electricity mix. Consequently, this study provides a novel, scalable methodological framework to support wineries and tourism operators in designing scientifically grounded, lower-impact tasting services. © 2026

Title: Cross-Boundary Practices within the Construction Industry: The Case of the Quantity Surveyors
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The evolving dynamics of the construction industry have sharpened the need for quantity surveyors (QSs) to reinterpret their role, expanding beyond traditional commercial management practices to encompass broader strategic functions such as value optimization and interdisciplinary collaboration. At the same time, professional overlaps and cross-boundary practices have become an increasing challenge to the quantity surveying profession, leading to potential conflicts and quality compromises in construction projects. However, there is markedly less research on the negative effects of cross-boundary practices for the quantity surveying profession, particularly regarding professional identity and long-term industry implications. Therefore, this study aims to recognize the challenges posed to the quantity surveying profession by cross-boundary practices and to examine the underlying reasons for these challenges. A comprehensive literature review and 25 semistructured interviews were conducted with two samples: QS professionals and non-QS professionals, to collect data. The content analysis method was used to analyze the gathered data. The core quantity surveying functions, such as taking off quantities, preparing bills of quantities, and contract administration, are increasingly performed by non-QS professionals in the construction industry. Even if there are positive effects, including knowledge transfer and reducing the scarcity of QSs through cross-boundary practices, the negative consequences, such as lowering project quality and harming the professional image of QSs, were found to be more significant. By empirically investigating the causes and effects of cross-boundary practices in quantity surveying, this study addresses an overlooked vulnerability in the construction industry and fills a critical gap in the literature on professional role integrity and industry standards.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: River tourism based on community participation and regional linkages for sustainable livelihoods: The case of Can Tho City, Vietnam
Abstract: This study examines the role of community-based river tourism and regional linkages in supporting sustainable livelihoods in Can Tho City, Vietnam. A convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, combining surveys of 385 tourists, 47 local households, and 18 tourism officials and community representatives with 36 semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), cluster analysis, and multiple regression, while qualitative data were integrated through thematic coding, triangulation, and SWOT analysis. The findings indicate that community-based river tourism contributes to livelihood diversification, income generation, skill development, and social capital formation. Participating households reported relatively high livelihood stability (mean = 3.87) and moderate government support (mean = 3.59), whereas regional linkage participation remained low (mean = 1.79). EFA results revealed a common factor linking government support, regional cooperation, and livelihood outcomes, with factor loadings ranging from -0.64 to -0.51. For tourism officials and community representatives, EFA identified two governance dimensions—regional coordination and community-enterprise synergy—which explained 84.83 of the total variance. Tourists reported high overall satisfaction (mean = 4.35), strong community interaction (mean = 4.61), positive perceptions of cultural preservation (mean = 3.71), and willingness to pay for tourism services (mean = 3.98). Regression analysis showed that cultural preservation perception was the only statistically significant predictor of tourist satisfaction ( β = 0.146, p = 0.004 ). Open-ended responses highlighted key development priorities, including reducing crowding ( 29.6 ), increasing the availability of tour guides ( 26.8 ), enhancing cultural activities ( 23.9 ), and extending tour duration ( 19.7 ). Overall, sustainable livelihood outcomes depend not only on community participation but also on effective governance, cultural preservation, and stronger regional integration. The findings provide empirical evidence and practical implications for sustainable tourism planning in riverine destinations of the Mekong Delta. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Enhanced degradation of bamboo shoot shells via a two-step process: Sodium chlorite pretreatment and xylanase hydrolysis for xylooligosaccharides production
Abstract: To improve the high-value utilization of bamboo shoot shells (BSS), a two-step strategy combining sodium chlorite pretreatment and hydrolysis with a thermostable xylanase from Thermomyces lanuginosus Q231 was developed to produce xylooligosaccharides (XOS). The xylanase exhibited an optimum pH of 6.0 and an optimum temperature of 70°C, while maintaining good catalytic performance at 50–65°C. The effects of sodium chlorite concentration (1%–8%, w/v) on the chemical composition, structural characteristics, and enzymatic hydrolysis performance of BSS were investigated. The results showed that sodium chlorite selectively removed lignin in a concentration-dependent manner, thereby increasing hemicellulose exposure and xylanase accessibility while largely preserving the cellulose crystalline structure. The optimal pretreatment concentration was 6% (w/v), at which the XOS yield reached 22.30%. HPLC analysis showed that xylotetraose (X4) and xylopentaose (X5) were the major components, and the xylose/XOS ratio remained at a low level of 0.06 after 2 h of enzymatic hydrolysis, indicating high product selectivity. Under the optimized conditions, 50.50 g of XOS was obtained from 1 kg of pretreated BSS. These results suggest that the proposed process has strong potential for the valorization of BSS and offer valuable insights for further research on enzymatic XOS production from lignocellulosic residues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Toward a relational typology: Mapping social entrepreneur-resident interactions in community-led tourism social entrepreneurship
Abstract: Research on tourism social entrepreneurship has focused on exogenous models while overlooking host communities' agency. The aim of this study was to examine interactions between social entrepreneurs and residents in the context of community-led tourism social entrepreneurship. The exploratory qualitative study design involved three fieldwork phases. We used two dimensions—the initiator's primary motivation and the embeddedness forms in the responder's actions—to identify four relationship types: traditional bonding ties, instrumental ties, patron–client ties, and value-congruent alliances. The social action and embeddedness theories guided our examination of relational formation. Findings further reveal a model of power shift and relationship dynamics. This model suggests that a power shift involves three principal stages centered around dependence. Title: Resilience enhancement of multi-carrier microgrids under extreme weather: A distributionally robust operational strategy with actuarial risk
Abstract: Extreme weather can simultaneously perturb energy supply, demand, and infrastructure availability in multi-carrier microgrids (MCMGs), while physical service loss and its monetary consequence may differ across load classes. This paper develops a two-stage data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) framework that separates physical service adequacy, actuarial valuation, tail-risk preference, and meteorological distributional ambiguity. Regional vulnerability is represented by an externally calibrated actuarial spatial vulnerability factor (ASVF), and a two-tail mean–GlueVaR functional characterizes multi-level upper-tail monetary exposure. The Wasserstein radius is calibrated exclusively from meteorological training data, with validation and holdout samples kept separate. For a fixed finite candidate support, the model admits an exact mixed-integer linear programming reformulation and a finite-candidate column-and-constraint generation (CCG) scheme with an explicit no-violation termination certificate. In the industrial-park case study, Glue-ASVF-WDRO yields zero held-out critical-service expected energy not supplied (EENS) and 21.339 kWh of general-service EENS, whereas risk-neutral WDRO gives nearly identical total EENS but 20.571 kWh of critical-service EENS. Matched-risk conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) and two-tail GlueVaR produce the same reported held-out outcomes, and the CCG and monolithic formulations attain the same objective value to numerical precision. Sensitivity analyses show stable held-out service outcomes across most tested perturbations, whereas stronger external distribution shifts cause marked deterioration. The results underscore the importance of separating physical service adequacy from actuarial valuation when evaluating resilient MCMG operation under extreme-weather uncertainty. Copyright © 2026. Title: Escaping the AI cage: construction workers’ perceived risk with AI gives rise to unsafe behaviors
Abstract: Reducing unsafe behavior among construction workers remains a central concern in construction management. While artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly adopted to replace or monitor workers, the negative perceptions workers hold toward the promotion of such technologies have largely been overlooked. This study introduces the concept of perceived risk with AI, defined as workers’ subjective perception of the potential negative consequences associated with AI adoption. Drawing on self-determination theory, which emphasizes individuals’ core psychological needs, we propose an inside-out theoretical model. This model explains how construction workers’ perceived risk with AI triggers unsafe behavior through two internal psychological pathways: emotional exhaustion and organizational identification. We further identify AI failure as a critical boundary condition that amplifies these effects. Data were collected from 343 frontline workers at 3 smart construction sites where AI actively interacts with human labor. Results indicate that perceived risk with AI increases unsafe behavior, and this relationship is mediated by both heightened emotional exhaustion and weakened organizational identification. Notably, these effects are significantly amplified when AI malfunctions occur. Our findings not only extend the application scope of self-determination theory but also contribute to the knowledge base on workers’ unsafe behavior in the context of human-AI coexistence. Practically, the study offers actionable insights for managers to mitigate the unintended side effects of AI implementation on worker safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The psychology of AI-mediated communication across languages
Abstract: Communication across languages is increasingly mediated by artificial intelligence (AI). This creates opportunities for people with different language backgrounds to communicate in their respective native languages. AI-mediated communication can therefore reduce cognitive effort, disfluency, and social stigma associated with speaking a non-native language. At the same time, non-native language use influences cognitive, emotional, and social processes that go beyond the accurate transmission of meaning. By affecting these processes and introducing new cues, AI-mediated communication could also have unintended effects on communication effectiveness and social evaluations between interlocutors. Title: Contextualizing negotiation research: The unique dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations
Abstract: Effective buyer–supplier negotiations are important for organizations to attain their goals and for wider society to have a reliable supply of goods and services. These negotiations also have distinctive characteristics that differentiate them from other negotiation settings, such as personal buyer–seller negotiations, which have attracted much of the attention in the negotiation literature. Given the differences between professional buyer–supplier and personal buyer–seller negotiations, some findings from personal negotiations may have limited applicability in supply chain settings, while others hold across contexts. These findings have important implications for both negotiation research and education, calling for careful contextualization based on the type of negotiation. By reviewing recent studies in the supply chain management literature, this article highlights several common dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations and how they affect negotiation outcomes. These dynamics are broadly categorized into the non-exhaustive themes of power in ongoing buyer–supplier relationships, other relational factors (supply network complexity, cross-cultural relations, and AI adoption), and negotiation strategies in buyer–supplier relationships (distributive, integrative, and mixed strategies), providing scholars with an overview of selected recent research on buyer–supplier negotiations. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: LLMs’ reshaping of people, processes, products, and society in software development: a qualitative exploration with early adopters
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping software development, but their impact across the full software development lifecycle is underexplored. Existing work tends to focus on isolated activities such as code generation or testing, leaving open questions about how LLMs affect developers, processes, products, and the broader software ecosystem. We address this gap through semi-structured interviews with sixteen early-adopter software professionals who integrated LLM-based tools into their day-to-day work in early to mid-2023. We treat these interviews as early empirical evidence and compare participants’ accounts with recent work on LLMs in software engineering, noting which early patterns persist or shift. Using thematic analysis, we organize our findings around four dimensions: people, process, product, and society. Developers reported substantial productivity gains from reducing mundane tasks, streamlining search, and accelerating debugging, but also described a productivity-quality paradox: they frequently discarded generated code and shifted effort from writing code to critically evaluating and integrating it. LLM use was highly phase-dependent, with strong uptake in implementation and debugging but limited influence on requirements gathering and collaborative work. Participants developed new competencies to use LLMs effectively, including prompt engineering strategies, multi-layered verification, and security-conscious integration to protect proprietary data. They also anticipated changes in hiring expectations, team practices, and computing education, while emphasizing that human judgment and foundational software engineering skills remain essential. Our findings, consistent with evidence from large-scale studies, offer actionable implications for developers, organizations, educators, and tool designers seeking to integrate LLMs responsibly into professional software practice. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Beyond circularity: Topological and temporal limits of the circular economy
Abstract: The circular economy has established itself as a dominant sustainability paradigm, yet the formal properties of its foundational metaphor, the circle, remain unexamined. This paper identifies two analytically distinct constraints embedded in the dominant circular imaginary. The first is topological: when the operative metaphor functions as a single closed loop, it reproduces the cycle graph, a one-dimensional structure with zero redundancy and minimal resilience. The second is temporal: the assessment apparatus associated with circularity operates within quantitative, sequential time (chronos) and renders qualitative, heterogeneous temporalities (kairos) structurally invisible. The claim defended here is specific. Sustainability paradigms generally pose time as a problem left open; the circular economy's founding metaphor figures time as resolved (return, cycle, regeneration) while its apparatus operationalizes only chronos. This blindness is not general ignorance but performative contradiction. Empirical evidence from three continents (African solar projects, Mexican circular assessment, Peruvian extraction) substantiates the diagnosis. We propose a polyrhythmic completion structured as a wheel, with Doughnut Economics as the rim, regeneration as the hub, and ArtefactKairos (institutional devices for temporal composition) as the spokes, operationalized through the Temporal Composition Diagnostic (TCD), a four-step governance protocol. Title: The Max–Min Kano framework: A context-sensitive method for evaluating office design features
Abstract: Product and building-related features are sometimes perceived differently across studies because they are experienced in different environmental contexts. The proposed Max–Min Kano methodology evaluates office design features under two contrasting contexts: a minimal environment with few positively appraised attributes and a maximal environment with many. Office-relevant attributes were identified through participatory elicitation and then evaluated using a Kano questionnaire (N = 32). Perceptual robustness was defined as retention of a Kano classification across the two contexts, while participant-level bootstrapping assessed sampling stability. View-related variables, window size, biophilic views, fewer façade obstructions, and proximity to windows were stable across contexts. They were Attractive, meaning they added satisfaction even when not strictly expected. In contrast, privacy provided by partitions emerged as a Must-be quality, while the presence of windows and ceiling height showed a One-dimensional relationship with satisfaction in both contexts. Other attributes, such as the seated-desk view, density, partition height, focal points, color, and materiality, were more sensitive to the baseline context. Adaptation-Level Theory, Stress Recovery theory, Attention Restoration theory, and Prospect–Refuge theory help explain these results. Overall, the Max-Min Kano approach helps identify features that remain perceptually robust across contexts, making it useful for prioritizing design features in real-world settings. The study shows that Kano categories are context-expressive rather than being intrinsic properties of features. For this reason, baseline context should be reported when evaluating user preferences across different spatial conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu J.; Tang W.; Hsu F.-C.; Goh K.B.
Title: When stigmatized workers become consumers
Abstract: Existing research on occupational stigma has focused primarily on workplace consequences, with less attention to how stigmatized service workers respond to service failures as consumers. Guided by cognitive appraisal theory, this sequential mixed-methods study integrates 20 interviews with a survey of 429 frontline workers in China. Qualitative findings show that perceived occupational stigma heightens sensitivity to disrespect and identity threat, whereas perceived work dirtiness shapes whether failures are attributed to situational constraints or preventable neglect. Quantitative results indicate that both constructs are positively associated with customer aggression and tolerance. Aggression may function as confrontational problem-focused coping, whereas tolerance reflects emotion-focused coping, and both are positively related to service recovery satisfaction. Title: Educational legacies of christian missions: Evidence from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Abstract: This paper investigates the educational legacies of Christian missions established before independence, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, focusing on contemporary disparities in educational content, quality, access, and outcomes. Using georeferenced data from over 20,000 schools and two million students participating in the Examen National d’État (Exetat) between 2016 and 2019, as well as primary data from a phone survey of 624 school directors, we explore how proximity to Catholic and Protestant missions during the colonial period influences educational opportunities today. We find that schools near historical Christian missions offer a broader and higher-quality curriculum, with increased access to study tracks outside the basic Pedagogy section. Students attending these schools are more likely to pass the Exetat and achieve grades qualifying for university admission, although the magnitude of the effect is modest. Observable school-environment and quality characteristics attenuate the Catholic missionary-proximity coefficient by about half, while demand-side patterns point to additional differences in student composition. Our findings reveal that the strong partnership between missions and the colonial state entrenched spatial inequalities in educational access and quality, inequalities that persist to this day. © 2026

Authors: Ming Y.; Xu M.; Li L.; Huang F.; Lin K.; Yang F.
Title: BiCrossNet-DDI: Drug-drug interaction prediction based on bidirectional cross-view attention networks
Abstract: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction plays a crucial role in drug safety assessment and clinical polypharmacy management. Existing approaches predominantly rely on a single graph structure or adopt coarse-grained multi-view fusion strategies, making it difficult to simultaneously capture the multi-scale topological characteristics of drug relationships and fully exploit complementary information across different views, thereby limiting representation capacity and predictive performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a DDI prediction framework based on a bidirectional cross-view attention network, which achieves more comprehensive semantic modeling of drug interactions and robust prediction through multi-scale structural modeling and cross-view interaction alignment. Specifically, the proposed method performs consistent encoding over multi-scale diffusion views and similarity views, and further introduces a bidirectional cross-view attention module as the core component. Concretely, the original view is used as the query to selectively aggregate high-order structural information from the diffusion view, while the diffusion view is simultaneously employed as the query to reversely align interaction evidence from the original view, enabling bidirectional completion and collaborative enhancement between views. Residual connections are incorporated within network layers to preserve critical information and stabilize training, and unified drug embeddings are finally obtained for DDI prediction. Experiments on the ZhangDDI dataset demonstrate that our model achieves an absolute improvement of 3.17% in F1 compared with the strongest baseline method. Title: When passion breeds silence: How coworkers’ work passion elicits envy and employee silence in hospitality workplaces
Abstract: While work passion is well-studied as an intrapersonal motivational construct, its interpersonal consequences for coworkers remain underexplored. Drawing primarily on the Social Functional Theory of Emotions, we examine how employees' observed work passion functions as a social signal that elicits coworker envy and, in turn, shapes silence behaviors. Across four studies (three experiments and a multi-source dyadic field study with hotel employees), we find a robust asymmetric pattern: harmonious passion primarily elicits benign envy, which is associated with prosocial silence, whereas obsessive passion primarily elicits malicious envy, which is associated with deviant silence. Cross-path effects were weaker and less consistent across studies. An exploratory field-study finding suggests that obsessive passion may occasionally relate to benign envy, although this association did not emerge in the experiments and warrants replication. Title: Environmental Mandated Delay: A Source-Based Classification Framework for Compliance-Driven Time Impacts in Construction Contracts
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: This article examines whether prevailing delay classifications in construction contracts adequately address time risk arising from mandatory environmental compliance obligations. It identifies a structural doctrinal gap in existing categories and proposes a distinct classification framework, environmental mandated delay (EMD), supported by a five-element cumulative test. A normative-comparative doctrinal methodology is employed, comprising (1) systematic analysis of delay provisions in major standard form construction contracts [the Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs-Conseils (FIDIC) forms, the New Engineering Contract (NEC), and the Joint Contracts Tribunal (JCT) forms]; (2) comparative review of environmental regulatory frameworks in four jurisdictions (the UK, Australia, Indonesia, and the UAE); (3) a systematic review of published arbitral awards rendered under the auspices of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) and judicial decisions demonstrating recurring classification ambiguity; and (4) application of the proposed framework to documented infrastructure project contexts. None of the major standard form contracts articulates a delay category grounded in mandatory public law compliance. A structured content analysis of seven publicly available ICSID awards (2014-2022) confirms that compliance-based temporal disruption is recurrent across infrastructure disputes but no tribunal applied a structured delay classification framework in any case. Analysis of published arbitral decisions further identifies five recurring patterns that confirm the structural nature of the gap. EMD directly addresses each pattern by grounding entitlement in the public law source of the delaying obligation. The framework offers a structured analytical tool for extension-of-time (EOT) assessment, aligning delay classification with critical path-based scheduling analysis and improving consistency in contract administration and dispute resolution. The article makes three original contributions: (1) identification of a structural doctrinal gap supported by empirical arbitral evidence; (2) development of a source-based approach reorienting delay analysis from event- and actor-based models toward public law obligations; and (3) provision of an operational test applicable in engineering practice, enhancing predictability in the treatment of compliance-driven delay in climate-transition infrastructure projects.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Mechanism study on the inhibition of iron precipitation behavior by microstructure transformation of slag during co-gasification of biomass and coal
Abstract: The wider application of high-iron coal in entrained-flow gasifiers is limited by the precipitation of iron-bearing minerals. The challenge can be addressed by co-gasification with silicon-rich biomass to adjust the slag silicate network structure. In this study, silicon-rich biomass (rice husk, RH) was co-gasified with high-iron coal to investigate the influence on the silicate network structure of the slag and the inhibition of iron-bearing minerals precipitation. The results showed that increasing RH content suppressed the precipitation of iron-bearing minerals by increasing the silicon content in the slag. As RH increased, the R (R = (Q4 + Q3)/(Q2 + Q1 + Q0), where R represents the degree of polymerization of the silicate network structure) increased, indicating that SiO2 promoted the formation of bridging oxygen (BO) bonds and enhanced the polymerization degree of the slag network structure. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the bond lengths of atomic pairs such as Si-O and Al-O gradually shortened, increasing interatomic forces and suppressing iron precipitation. In addition, RH addition increased the ash fusion temperatures and viscosity, reduced the slag crystallization tendency, and shifted the slag type to a glassy state, which facilitated smooth slag tapping. This study provides a theoretical basis for the co-gasification of silicon-rich biomass and high-iron coal in entrained-flow gasifiers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Consumers and local short food supply chains: Critical purchasing factors

Abstract: Short food supply chains (SFSCs) are considered an effective way to promote greater sustainability in agri-food production. In this regard, there is increasing interest from consumers in short supply chain initiatives, as well as from academia and society in general. Despite their importance, limited research on consumers and SFSCs is available in emerging countries. This study, conducted in Colombia, aimed to identify factors influencing consumers' food purchases through local SFSCs (L-SFSCs). For this purpose, a quantitative analysis was performed based on a logistic regression model, comparing frequent L-SFSCs consumers with a control group of non-consumers. It was found that socio-economic characteristics of the consumers, such as age range, level of education and income level, are factors that determine the purchase of food through L-SFSCs. Also, geographical proximity had a significant effect on the purchase of food through L-SFSCs.
