Title: Bidding and market dynamics in the Brazilian structural demand response program
Abstract: This paper studies the Structural demand response Program (SP) in Brazil from a consumer's perspective. We begin by formalizing the SP's operational and financial mechanisms, and then develop a strategic bidding methodology that follows a two-stage decision-making process, formulated as a nonconvex bilevel optimization model. In the first stage, consumers determine optimal bids that balance program revenues with production-related opportunity costs, while the second stage models the all-or-nothing market-clearing process as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming problem. To address computational challenges posed by the strategic bidding model, the nonconvexities are linearized via binary relations, and the bilevel model is reformulated as an equivalent single-level problem solved via a tailored Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm. Empirical evidence from a case study based on data from the Brazilian power system and market environment suggests that the SP's design incentivizes energy-intensive consumers with flexible demand profiles. In contrast, baseline constraints hinder broader participation by price-responsive consumers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Operational constraints in professional kitchens: A theory of constraints perspective on food waste reduction
Abstract: Professional kitchens, where core foodservice operations occur, generate up to two-thirds of total food waste. Addressing this gap, this study applies the Theory of Constraints (TOC) and qualitative triangulation through structured observations and in-depth interviews with kitchen staff to identify and analyze waste reduction constraints across kitchen workflows. Title: The dark side of AI customer service: How service failures damage consumer-brand relationships
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) customer service is increasingly used as a frontline interface, yet its failures may create relational damage that extends beyond a single service encounter. Drawing on service failure theory and consumer-brand relationship literature, this research examines how AI service failures are formed and how they influence negative consumer-brand relationships. Study 1 collected 3208 online complaint records from a major Chinese consumer complaint platform. After data cleaning, 2824 valid complaints were analyzed using Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modeling, which identified ten complaint topics and further synthesized them into five AI service failure dimensions: functional failure, informational failure, systemic failure, interactional failure, and service recovery failure. Study 2 used survey data from 965 Chinese consumers and applied PLS-SEM, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), fsQCA, and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). The results show that all five failure dimensions positively influence negative consumer-brand relationships. Informational failure and systemic failure emerge as particularly influential across linear, predictive, and configurational analyses. The findings advance AI service failure research by developing a data-driven typology of failures and demonstrating that AI-mediated service breakdowns are not merely technical problems but relational threats that undermine consumer trust, satisfaction, and engagement with brands. However, because this research focuses on Chinese consumers and complaint data from a single national platform, future studies should examine whether the proposed failure typology and relational effects can be generalized across different countries, cultures, platforms, and regulatory environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Lost in the narrative: How embedded content reduces sales on short video commerce platforms

Abstract: Embedded content on short video commerce platforms, which integrates product-focused content with creators' self-focused content, has been widely adopted as a strategy to enhance viewer engagement and drive product sales. Despite its prevalent application, the effect of embedded content on product sales remains unclear. While self-focused content may reduce advertising avoidance, it risks distracting attention from the product, thereby making its effect on subsequent product sales unclear. To explore the sales effect of embedded content and its underlying mechanisms, we employ a mixed-methods approach, combining an observational study with a randomized experiment. Our empirical analysis reveals that a higher ratio of self-focused content decreases product sales. Heterogeneity analyses further uncover several measures to mitigate the negative impact: optimizing commercial embedment timing, increasing creator positive facial expressions, and enhancing product visual salience. Finally, we conduct a randomized experiment to validate the dual-path mechanism, which shows that self-focused content indeed reduces ad avoidance but also reduces ad attention, thereby affecting viewers’ purchase intentions through two opposing pathways. Title: Consumer complaints as regulatory signals: Evidence from water services in Metropolitan Lima
Abstract: In regulated monopoly services, consumers lack effective exit options, making complaint systems a central mechanism for expressing dissatisfaction and generating regulatory information about service performance. However, complaint rates are not direct or unbiased indicators of service failures, as the decision to complain involves informational, procedural, and behavioral costs, reflecting both service problems and heterogeneous access barriers. Because administrative data record filed complaints rather than adjudicated outcomes, complaint rates are interpreted as noisy signals of perceived billing anomalies rather than direct measures of confirmed service failures, firm misconduct, or regulatory noncompliance. This paper reinterprets billing-related complaints as endogenous regulatory signals in essential public services. We develop a microeconomic framework in which households decide whether to complain when facing an atypical bill under uncertainty about its origin—whether it reflects a firm billing error or household-specific factors. The model’s predictions are tested using sector-month administrative data from Sedapal, the public water utility serving Metropolitan Lima (Peru), covering January 2022–June 2023. We estimate a dynamic panel model (System GMM) to identify persistence in complaint behavior and its response to unanticipated tariff shocks. We find strong persistence in complaint rates and a significant response to unexpected tariff increases. These patterns suggest structural frictions in service provision or communication and a critical role for tariff transparency. Overall, the results imply that regulators should strengthen tariff communication and incorporate complaint data into monitoring systems as screening and triage indicators, rather than as mechanical evidence of confirmed billing errors or firm misconduct. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Audiovisual aesthetic matching enhances food evaluation by amplifying pleasure and perceived tastiness
Abstract: Aesthetic experiences can shape the evaluations of consumers, including in the case of food. Title: Paying for the future? Cross-season pre-sale product launch strategy in hotels
Abstract: Traditional hotels face persistent seasonal demand imbalance, with weak off-peak demand and constrained peak-season capacity. Title: Driving impact? How imperfect displacement shapes heterogeneous rebound in carsharing
Abstract: Green technologies, products, and services, such as carsharing, are commonly promoted as pathways to lower environmental impacts by increasing efficiency. Yet rebound effects, behavioral and economic responses to improved efficiency, may erode these environmental impact reductions. Many rebound studies assume perfect displacement, where a new technology or mode of service provision fully replaces an existing service on a one-to-one basis. While analytically convenient, this assumption overlooks real-world complexity and consumer heterogeneity. Using survey data from nearly 4500 Belgian carsharing users, we compare rebound estimates under perfect displacement with those based on reported shifts in mobility. Under the perfect displacement assumption, we find a 53% rebound effect. When accounting for imperfect displacement, however, rebound effects vary widely across users. While median effects remain positive (20%–46%), at the individual level rebound effects range from substantial net benefits to strong rebound (5th–95th percentile: −331% to 147%). A cluster analysis further reveals distinct user groups with systematically different impacts, underscoring that displacement patterns vary not only in scale but also in direction. These findings suggest that carsharing's environmental impact is highly user-dependent, and that relying on a single aggregate estimate may mask critical behavioral variations. Title: Effects of China's Community Gridding on Coproduced Reporting of Rainstorm-Induced Emergencies: A Community-Wide Analysis
Abstract: Presently, the involvement of citizens in emergency management is inevitable and indispensable, but how to facilitate the participation of citizens remains unclear. Utilizing panel data from 174 communities in China between 2013 and 2023, this study investigated the effects of the community gridding policy (an important policy for facilitating citizen participation in public services in China) on citizens' coproduced reporting of rainstorm-induced emergencies (e.g., small-scale debris flow, water inundation, and trapped citizens) by integrating propensity score matching (PSM) and difference-in-differences (DID) methods. Statistical results showed that the community gridding significantly enhanced both citizens' reporting engagement (represented by the number of citizen reports) and reporting quality (represented by the ratio of the reports that have been accepted by communities to the total received reports). Mediating effect analysis showed that community gridding policy enhanced citizen reporting by increasing the capability of citizen training, reporting rule completeness, and technological maturity. In addition, the effects of community gridding on enhancing citizen reporting strengthened with the increase of the community scale. Furthermore, high risk perception increased the impact of community gridding on citizen reporting. The findings contribute to both the literature on and practice of emergency service coproduction and rainstorm disaster risk reduction. Moreover, those findings provide guidance of improving citizen participation for the jurisdictions that have similar rainstorm risk situations as China. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Wei S.; Hu Z.; Zhang D.; Liu X.
Title: Too personal to be accepted? How personalization visibility drives perceived surveillance and advertising intrusiveness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: A central challenge in digital advertising is that firms seek to increase relevance through personalization, yet visibly signaling the use of personal data may provoke consumer discomfort and resistance. Guided by privacy calculus theory and communication privacy management theory, this research develops and tests a model in which personalization visibility shapes perceived intrusiveness through perceived surveillance, with data sensitivity and prior brand trust as boundary conditions. Across five studies, including four controlled online experiments and one real-world field experiment using personalized watch advertisements, we examine how explicit versus implicit personalization cues affect consumers’ privacy-related responses. Study 1 shows that explicit personalized visuals, relative to implicit personalized visuals, increase perceived intrusiveness. Study 2 validates this main effect in a live platform-based advertising environment, showing that explicit personalized visuals increase self-reported intrusiveness and produce directionally consistent behavioral ad-dismissal responses under naturally occurring exposure conditions. Study 3 replicates the effect and demonstrates that perceived surveillance partially mediates it, whereas perceived ad relevance does not account for the effect. Study 4 shows that the positive effect of explicit personalization visibility on perceived intrusiveness is stronger when the advertisement is based on sensitive rather than general consumer data. Study 5 further demonstrates that prior brand trust weakens both the direct effect of explicit personalized visuals on perceived intrusiveness and the indirect effect through perceived surveillance. These findings contribute to consumer behavior theory by identifying personalization visibility as a distinct antecedent of advertising intrusiveness and by clarifying the surveillance-based process through which visible targeting cues trigger privacy-related reactions. By combining controlled experimental evidence with field-based validation, the research also strengthens the ecological validity of the personalization visibility account. Managerially, the results suggest that firms should avoid overly conspicuous personalization cues, especially when sensitive data are involved or brand trust is weak. © 2026

Authors: Hoang Q.
Title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
Abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. The regression model yielded an adjusted R2 of.862, indicating that the independent variables account for 86.2% of the variance in language choice. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the Chơ Ro language remains a functional medium in domestic and communal domains, supported by Intergenerational Transmission Strength (ITS) (β = 0.171) and Institutional Support (IS) (β = 0.166). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. By documenting the resilience of a small-scale minority, the study contributes to a comparative theory of bilingualism in urbanizing contexts, emphasizing that internal conviction and communal structures are necessary to mitigate linguistic attrition in high-density economic zones. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Luo Y.; Wei Y.; Cheng Y.
Title: Maintenance optimization in dynamic environment considering environment-induced maintenance delay
Abstract: Most maintenance optimization studies for production systems assume stationary environmental states. In practice, however, the operating environments vary over time, changing both degradation dynamics and production reward of the system. Moreover, under certain harsh environmental states, maintenance actions cannot be executed and must be postponed. These factors impact the production reward, degradation penalty, and maintenance cost in a coupled manner, posing challenges for making optimal maintenance decisions. In this paper, we develop a maintenance optimization framework for minimizing the operational cost of a production system operating in dynamic environments with environment-induced maintenance delay. The optimization problem is formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP) over an infinite horizon, including the quantification of the threefold impact of the environment on maintenance. We establish key structural properties and prove that the optimal maintenance policy has a control limit structure. Based on these properties, we develop an improved value iteration algorithm, exploiting the monotone threshold characterization of the optimal policy and avoiding redundant action comparisons, to obtain the optimal solution efficiently. A numerical study of offshore wind turbines illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework and algorithm. Managerial insights are provided through sensitivity analysis. Copyright © 2026. Title: Mechanistic interpretability of Mamba's selective gate in financial markets: A leakage-controlled study
Abstract: Selectively gated state-space models (SSMs), notably Mamba, are increasingly used for financial time series, yet how they internally represent market regimes (bull, bear, sideways) remains opaque. This paper applies Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) to a six-layer Mamba trained on approximately twenty-one years of daily data for a point-in-time set of S&P 500 constituents plus macroeconomic and Fama-French factors, decomposing per-layer hidden states with Top-K Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs). Our central contribution is methodological and cautionary. A prior, uncontrolled configuration recovered market regimes from SAE features at F1 = 1.00. Under a controlled protocol that (i) removes the three input features that overlap the HMM label definition, (ii) disables the auxiliary regime-classification head, (iii) uses a point-in-time constituent universe, and (iv) evaluates against labels disjoint from the inputs, the same regime label is recovered at only F1 = 0.398, indistinguishable from a logistic baseline on raw inputs (0.435) and from an SAE trained on a randomly initialized, untrained Mamba (0.364). A 2 × 2 attribution grid shows the near-perfect result is an interaction of auxiliary supervision and label-defining inputs: neither factor alone exceeds F1 ∼ 0.40. Effect sizes with block-bootstrap inference show the residual selective-gate (Delta t) regime effect is statistically detectable but economically negligible and uniform across layers rather than layer-specialized; the apparent polysemanticity gradient disappears under continuous, theory-grounded measures. We contribute a reproducible leakage-control protocol for interpretability evaluation of financial SSMs, a quantified demonstration that previously reported regime structure is a label-contamination artifact, and a modest economically grounded feature subset that genuinely survives the controls. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang S.; Sun W.; Wu T.; Guo X.
Title: Discount display in tiered pricing: Nudging subscriptions in online healthcare services
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Discounts are increasingly embedded within tiered pricing to encourage larger purchases or longer service commitments. However, such discounts are often implicit and embedded across the price options, heightening consumers’ cognitive burden of cross-tier comparisons. How platforms display these discounts and whether salient discount display in tiered pricing can drive consumer demand remain largely unclear. Drawing on nudge theory, we conceptualize discount display as a digital salience nudge and examine its effect on consumer subscription demand in online healthcare settings. We leverage a quasi-natural experiment on a leading Chinese online healthcare platform, which redesigned its subscription interface to render implicit savings across tiers salient to patients. Using an intensity-based difference-in-differences approach, we find that discount display significantly increases patient subscriptions. Further analyses suggest that this effect is unlikely to stem from physician-side price reductions or concurrent platform-side changes and is instead consistent with the informational effect of discount display. Moderation results further show that the promotional effect of discount display strengthens for physicians treating a higher share of chronic conditions and becomes statistically insignificant in predominantly episodic care. This study contributes to discount promotion literature by offering robust empirical evidence on the positive effect of salient discount display in tiered pricing contexts and provides managerial implications for interface design and promotion management in digital retailing markets. © 2026

Title: Rule-based BloodCell interpretable and actionable hematological classification using ConvNeXt-Tiny
Abstract: The automated identification and classification of peripheral blood cells is critical for diagnosing a range of hematological disorders, from systemic infections to leukemia. Such classification supports diagnosis by providing differential cell counts and by detecting abnormal cell morphology, rather than diagnosing a disease directly. Traditional manual microscopy is labor-intensive and prone to subjective error, while existing deep learning “black-box” models often lack the transparency required for clinical adoption. This study proposes an interpretable, research-oriented decision-support framework leveraging the ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture, optimized with tuned hyperparameters and an input resolution of 64 × 64 pixels to enable rapid, lightweight training. The model was trained on a dataset of 17,107 images, using 13,685 for training and 3,422 for testing across eight classes: Basophils, Eosinophils, Erythroblasts, Immature Granulocytes (IG), Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Neutrophils, and Platelets. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.98 and a weighted F1-score of 0.98. Reliability was assessed with a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.974 and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.974, indicating strong agreement with the expert-labeled ground truth. A key contribution is the integration of Explainable AI (XAI) through LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations), which highlights influential superpixels to spatially validate cellular morphology. These visual explanations are complemented by a rule-based clinical decision-support (expert-system) module that maps the predicted cell class to predefined, non-diagnostic clinical guidance. By combining deep-learning feature extraction with rule-based recommendations drawn from standard hematology references, the framework provides a transparent and lightweight research prototype intended to assist, rather than replace, expert hematological assessment. Compared with existing approaches (Table 6), it addresses all eight clinically relevant classes with competitive accuracy and reliability while adding region-level LIME interpretability and a rule-based decision-support layer that most prior systems lack. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Uncovering heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on stock returns using causal forest double machine learning
Abstract: Global uncertainty has become an important source of financial market instability, yet its effects are inherently heterogeneous and difficult to identify using conventional econometric models. Existing empirical studies primarily rely on linear and average-effect estimators, which may conceal substantial heterogeneity across economic conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable causal machine learning framework that integrates Causal Forest Double Machine Learning (CF-DML) with SHAP explanations to estimate and interpret heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on industry-level stock returns. Using a balanced panel of six major industries listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange from 2011 to 2022, global uncertainty is measured by the World Uncertainty Index (WUI), while macroeconomic and financial variables are incorporated as lagged covariates. The CF-DML framework enables robust causal inference under high-dimensional confounding and nonlinear relationships, whereas SHAP values identify the main drivers of treatment-effect heterogeneity. The results show that the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) of global uncertainty is statistically insignificant, yet substantial heterogeneity exists across observations. Differences across industries are relatively modest, indicating that global uncertainty is transmitted primarily through time-varying macro-financial conditions rather than fixed sectoral characteristics. SHAP analysis identifies exchange-rate volatility, inflation, and market valuation as the dominant factors explaining heterogeneous responses. The study contributes to the literature by combining causal inference, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified framework for financial analysis. The findings suggest that global uncertainty should be viewed as a state-dependent macro-financial phenomenon, providing practical insights for portfolio risk management, macro-financial surveillance, and the design of policies aimed at enhancing financial resilience in emerging economies characterized by persistent inflation and exchange-rate volatility. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
Abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. Second, we explore how ambitious and flexible first offers should be. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Lee S.; Choi N.
Title: Club research: A review and research agenda
Abstract: Private clubs constitute a distinctive hospitality context defined by membership-based governance, shared authority, and long-term relational exchange, yet existing scholarship remains theoretically fragmented. This study systematically reviews 67 SSCI-indexed journal articles published through 2025 to examine the thematic evolution, theoretical foundations, and methodological patterns of club research. Using multi-layered bibliometric and content-based analyses, the review shows that research has expanded from managerial competency and member satisfaction toward innovation, governance, and digital engagement, but remains divided between consumer-experience and organization-centric management perspectives. This fragmentation under-theorizes clubs as hybrid governance-service institutions, especially at the member–management interface where authority, legitimacy, accountability, and value co-creation intersect. Methodological reliance on cross-sectional quantitative designs, U.S.-centric samples, and single-stakeholder perspectives further constrains cumulative theory building. Grounded in an institutional governance lens, the review advances a hybrid governance perspective and proposes future research on member–management dynamics, multi-role members, and access-sensitive, multi-stakeholder methods suited to private club settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: BaCu₃ScSe₄ and BaCu₃YSe₄ quaternary selenides: a first-principles exploration of mechanical, optical, and energy-conversion properties
Abstract: An emerging platform for energy-conversion and optoelectronic devices is quaternary chalcogenides. Here, using FP-APW + lo density-functional theory in conjunction with TB-mBJ band calculations, we conducted a thorough first-principles evaluation of BaCu₃ScSe₄ and BaCu₃YSe₄. Around Ba and the trivalent cations, DOS and charge-density maps reveal a mixed ionic nature with dominating Cu-Se covalency. Optical spectra derived from complex dielectric function yield prominent optical response. Photocatalytic water splitting potential of compounds shows efficient water splitting. BaCu₃ScSe₄ exhibits higher electrical and thermal conductivities temperature-dependent transport, while BaCu₃YSe₄ yields a higher Seebeck coefficient and figure of merit. The results show that BaCu₃ScSe₄ is a mechanically robust candidate and that BaCu₃YSe₄ is an attractive p-type high-temperature thermoelectric with a notable visible-light response. Title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
Abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Affective and normative commitment reduced abandonment odds, whereas need-based commitment increased them. Generation did, however, structure post-exit destinations: among Twitter/X leavers, digital natives were more likely to name Instagram and TikTok, and older cohorts were more likely to name Facebook. Title: Heterogeneous edge AI orchestration: A systematic review, taxonomy and future directions
Abstract: The confluence of Machine Learning (ML), Edge, and containerization has resulted in the emergence of Edge AI, which enhances reliability, fault tolerance, data security and privacy, inference time and accuracy. On one hand, accelerated hardware and advanced interconnects have reduced training times and improved accuracy. Leveraging this, the orchestration engines automate workload management but often struggle with limited features and sub-optimal policies. Edge offers a myriad of interconnected devices employing hardware and orchestration engines, but these devices are inherently distributed and resource-constrained, which adversely impacts Edge AI adoption. Moreover, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Edge orchestration to optimize resource provisioning, scheduling, and management without compromising the quality of service has been the driving motivation. However, integrating these components to enable Edge AI poses substantial challenges encompassing the hardware, interconnects, orchestration engines, computational, application, and workload heterogeneities. Additionally, training data scarcity, constrained and heterogeneous resources, control plane management overhead, delayed data traversal, and other factors exacerbate Edge AI orchestration challenges. Considering these challenges and opportunities, this paper establishes a top-to-bottom architectural view to investigate cross-layer Edge AI orchestration progress across three layers. At the bottom layer, NVLink, Compute Express Link, and other heterogeneous interconnects that manage the underlying hardware are discussed and compared in terms of offered bandwidth, latency, topology, and other features. In the middle layer, heterogeneous container orchestration engines and their high/low-level runtimes are contrasted for Edge AI. For the top layer, a systematic review of research works empowering heterogeneous Edge AI orchestration which proposed heuristic, meta-heuristic, optimization, and AI/ML solutions for container migration, autoscaling, ML/DL model-switching, resource forecasting, and scheduling is conducted. Furthermore, this article investigates the employment and position of Generative AI in Edge computing. Subsequently, taxonomies of optimization models, ML/DL models, orchestration engines, runtimes, and orchestration objectives are provided. Finally, the identified research gaps and possible future directions conclude this article. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Talking to the screen: Influencer nonverbal cues and observed platform engagement in Douyin travel short-form videos

Abstract: Short-form travel videos have become important digital service touchpoints, yet little is known about how influencers' auditory and visual nonverbal cues jointly relate to cumulative observed likes. Title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
Abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. Title: Comparison of staff-deployed and patient-directed electronic meal ordering systems: Patient experiences and food intake in an Australian acute care hospital
Abstract: Hospital foodservice plays a critical role in patient satisfaction, nutritional intake, and recovery; however, evidence comparing electronic meal ordering systems (eMOSs) remains limited. This study assessed differences in patient satisfaction, self-reported food intake, and reasons for incomplete meal consumption between staff-deployed and patient-directed eMOSs in an Australian acute care hospital. A survey comprising quantitative items and optional free-text comments was distributed via lunch trays across the same participating wards during the staff-deployed eMOS period and repeated following implementation of the patient-directed eMOS. Fifty-one and sixty-one patients completed the survey during the respective study periods. No significant differences in patient satisfaction across foodservice domains or self-reported food intake were observed between systems. Across both groups, food quality was rated lowest, while the dining environment received the highest ratings. Incomplete meal consumption was primarily attributed to dissatisfaction with food quality, including unappealing presentation, disliked taste, and unsuitable food types, as well as reduced appetite and illness-related factors. Thematic analysis identified food quality (flavour, temperature, presentation, and menu variety), and the meal ordering process as central to patient experience. While overall satisfaction did not differ between systems, the nature of negative experiences varied: the staff-deployed eMOS was limited by staffing capacity, whereas the patient-directed eMOS was constrained by usability challenges with television-based interfaces. These findings indicate that eMOS implementation alone is unlikely to improve patient outcomes. Title: The role of masculinity in understanding gender gaps in negotiation
Abstract: We review empirical research on masculinity processes in negotiations. Studies to date are typically based on the precarious manhood thesis, which suggests that men seek to demonstrate their manhood to others, or on evolutionary psychology, which suggests that men are susceptible to evolutionary pressures to compete for mates. The current empirical literature on masculinity and negotiation suggests that men negotiate assertively, or even unethically, when they perceive their manhood to be threatened. Moreover, research repeatedly has shown that men's negotiation behavior is influenced by counterpart attributes, particularly the gender of the counterpart. Authors: Li D.; Zhu X.; Han Y.; Zhao X.; Chai X.; Xia C.; Huang P.; Xue J.
Title: UDA2L: Unsupervised deformation-aware adaptive learning for medical image registration
Abstract: Medical image registration plays a key role in diagnosis, therapeutic strategy design, and longitudinal studies. However, the existing methods are prone to misregistration when encountering complex anatomical changes, making it difficult to effectively maintain the topological consistency of anatomical structures. To address these problems, we propose an unsupervised deformation-aware adaptive learning method (UDA2L) for medical image registration, in which deformation information is explicitly used to guide high-risk region perception, hierarchical feature interaction, and consistency regularization. Specifically, an adaptive High-risk Deformation Area-Aware Mechanism (HDA2M) introduces deformation-field gradient information into the attention modeling process, enabling the network to emphasize regions with unstable or large local deformations. A Triple-view Hierarchical Feature Integration (THFI) module jointly integrates fixed-image features, moving-image features, and deformation-field representations through a coarse-to-fine pyramid structure, thereby strengthening deformation-appearance coupling and capturing both fine-grained anatomical details and global contextual information. Moreover, Cross-Cycle Consistency (C3) learning imposes bidirectional deformation consistency and residual-level reconstruction constraints to improve local alignment accuracy and enhance the topological stability of the learned deformation field. Experimental results on multiple 3D brain MRI image datasets (including three single-modality and one cross-modality) show that UDA2L achieves relatively ideal performance and efficiency in the image registration task, demonstrating its application prospects in this field. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Fracture mechanical properties and mechanism analysis of structural fiber recycled coarse aggregate concrete
Abstract: To investigate the influence of structural fibers (STF) on the fracture mechanical properties of recycled concrete, three-point bending tests were conducted to study the effects of STF type, STF content, and recycled aggregates (RA) substitution rate on the fracture failure mode, load displacement curve, load CMOD (crack mouth opening displacement) curve, residual bending strength, fracture energy, and fracture toughness of concrete. Finally, a bilinear softening constitutive curve for structural fiber-reinforced recycled concrete (STFRRC) was established based on the double-K fracture model. The results indicate that STF can change the failure mode of concrete and significantly improve its fracture performance; The fracture performance (residual bending strength, fracture energy, and fracture toughness) of STFRRC is positively correlated with STF content and negatively correlated with RA substitution rate. Among the STF types, ESF (End-hooked steel fiber) has the greatest effect on the fracture performance of STFRRC, followed by CSF (Corrugated steel fiber) and, finally, SCSF (Shear corrugated steel fiber). Compared with the non-fiber specimens, STFRRC exhibited improved fracture performance and post-cracking toughness. The bilinear σ−w relationship provides a model-derived representation of the post-cracking tensile softening behavior of STFRRC based on the measured ft, Gf, and CTODc, rather than an independently validated constitutive response. Title: Bridging game-theoretic modeling and Artificial Intelligence for fast policy recommendations in multi-channel retail
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Emerging-market milk retail is increasingly split across General Trade, Modern Trade, and E-commerce, where pricing and advertising are strategically interdependent through cross-channel substitution, advertising spillovers, and trust-sensitive demand. Yet decision support is challenging: game-theoretic models capture these interactions but are costly to solve repeatedly, while standard machine learning approaches typically require rich quantitative data, often unavailable in fragmented markets where key drivers (e.g., “low trust”) are qualitative. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a hybrid simulation–surrogate decision-support framework that operationalizes omnichannel theory into rapid decision support. First, a tri-channel game-theoretic simulator incorporating trust, advertising spillovers, and cost heterogeneity generates constrained solver benchmark pricing and advertising decisions. Second, to reduce repeated equilibrium-solving costs during scenario evaluation, a lightweight policy network is trained to approximate this structural mapping, providing feasible scenario-based recommendations at low computational cost. A rule-based natural-language descriptor layer operationalizes qualitative managerial inputs by mapping predefined cues into parameterized intervals. Across 10,000 simulated market states, the trained surrogate policy closely approximates the solver-generated benchmark decisions, with evaluation on the held-out test set yielding a mean profit ratio of 1.001, a trimmed profit ratio of 0.999, and mean economic regret of 0.40%. Authors: Nguyen M.; Zhang Y.; Cao T.T.
Title: The right endorser for the right stay: How human and AI endorsers shape accommodation booking
Abstract: This research examines how endorser presence and endorser type influence consumers’ accommodation booking intention. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory, it shows that endorsers shape booking intention by activating embodied mental simulation. It further examines two hospitality-specific factors, booking purpose and service mode, that influence when human and AI-generated endorsers are more effective. Across five experimental studies, we demonstrate that endorser presence increases booking intention via embodied mental simulation. Human endorsers generally produce stronger embodied mental simulation and booking intention than AI-generated endorsers. However, this pattern reverses in high-privacy booking and self-service environments, where AI-generated endorsers are better aligned with the accommodation experiences consumers are imagining. This research extends Embodied Cognition Theory by showing that the effectiveness of embodied cues depends on the match between endorser type and the accommodation experience consumers mentally construct. It also offer practical guidance for hospitality marketers seeking to align endorser strategies with different booking contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Why and when customer-related social stressors impair service performance: A conservation of resources perspective
Abstract: Building on the conservation of resources theory, we investigate how customer-related social stressors impact service performance among hospitality employees. To explore this, we gathered data from 350 supervisor-employee pairs across twelve hotels in China through a three-wave survey. The results show that customer-related social stressors detrimentally affect work engagement, which in turn reduces service performance. Furthermore, job social support and employees’ social skills emerge as two key moderators, buffering both the direct impact of customer-related social stressors on work engagement and the indirect effect on service performance via work engagement. These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the interactions among customer-related social stressors, work engagement, and service performance, offering significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Digital service nudges and consumer adoption of reusable packaging in online retailing: From convenience to circular responsibility
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online retailers increasingly offer reusable express packaging, but adoption remains difficult because sustainable options can conflict with the convenience expectations that define online retailing. This article examines reusable packaging adoption as a circular retail service conversion problem. Across three studies with adult online shoppers, we test how digital service nudges and responsibility framing influence adoption through perceived service friction, perceived environmental efficacy, and sustainable service trust, and how these effects depend on return convenience. Study 1 uses a quota-based, post-stratification-weighted survey to show that decision-relevant service nudges reduce perceived service friction and increase adoption intention, while responsibility framing increases perceived environmental efficacy and sustainable service trust. Study 2 uses a discrete choice experiment to estimate trade-offs among nudge timing, return convenience, deposit/refund rules, delivery delay, environmental benefit visibility, and responsibility framing. Study 3 uses an incentivized simulated checkout task to test behaviorally consequential reusable-packaging choice at the decision point. The results show that return convenience and deposit clarity are stronger adoption drivers than generic environmental claims, and that consumers penalize delivery delay more strongly than they reward verified environmental-benefit information. Decision-point nudges increase reusable-packaging checkout choice more than post-checkout reminders, especially when return convenience is high. The findings contribute to retail service convenience, digital nudging, and circular retailing research by showing that sustainable retail adoption depends on service-touchpoint design, not only on environmental attitudes. We position the model as a middle-range service-conversion framework grounded in service convenience, limited-attention decision-making, and sustainable-consumption efficacy and trust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Technology and the psychology of experience: A temporal framework

Authors: Huang Z.; Guo Y.; Tong L.; Zhao M.
Title: Resilience asymmetry in city networks: State and private firm linkages across China's four mega-city regions
Abstract: In an increasingly uncertain global environment, the resilience of city networks has become a key indicator of regional stability and adaptability. This paper examines four mega-city regions in China by constructing two ownership-segmented city networks based on state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and privately owned enterprises (POEs). Comparative analysis of their structures and resilience performance reveals systematic “resilience asymmetry” associated with ownership logics. Both networks display a basic center–periphery pattern, but with distinct configurations and shock responses: SOE-based networks form highly centralized, radiating structures with strong resource integration, exhibiting a “weaker resistance—faster recovery” trajectory; POE-based networks exhibit multi-centered, proximity-based structures with greater initial resistance but slower recovery, showing a “stronger resistance—slower recovery” trajectory. These findings highlight that ownership-driven network structures each possess unique resilience advantages. The paper contributes by advancing the concept of resilience asymmetry and suggesting that future governance should foster more compound and adaptive network configurations. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Does retirement reduce household carbon emissions in China? Evidence from fuzzy regression discontinuity design
Abstract: This study examines the causal effect of household-head retirement on household carbon emissions (HCEs) in China. Combining multi-wave data from the China Family Panel Studies with household carbon accounting, we construct household-level total carbon emissions (TCEs), distinguishing between direct carbon emissions (DCEs) from household energy use and indirect carbon emissions (ICEs) embodied in the goods and services purchased by households. We estimate the local causal effect of retirement using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on China's statutory retirement age of 60 for urban male household heads. The results show that retirement significantly reduces TCEs by approximately 7.4–9.0 tCO₂ per household. This reduction is driven primarily by lower ICEs, while the estimated effect on DCEs is statistically insignificant. Point estimates are larger for households headed by individuals without tertiary education and for low-asset households, but formal bootstrap tests do not reject equality across education or asset groups. The mechanism results suggest that the decline in ICEs is mainly associated with a contraction in overall household consumption, particularly reductions in non-subsistence and work-related expenditure, with limited evidence of a broad shift in consumption composition. Disaggregated results further show that the emission reductions are concentrated in clothing, household facilities and services, and transportation and communication. These findings provide local causal evidence that retirement reshapes HCEs mainly through reductions in consumption-based indirect emissions rather than through changes in direct household energy use, highlighting the importance of life-course transitions for understanding demand-side emission dynamics in aging societies. © 2026

Title: An empirical study on the capability of LLMs in decomposing bug reports
Abstract: Bug reports are essential to the software development life cycle. They help developers track and resolve issues, but are often difficult to process due to their complexity, which can delay resolution and affect software quality. This study investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can assist developers in automatically decomposing complex bug reports into smaller, self-contained units, making them easier to understand and address. We first conducted an empirical study using 127 resolved privacy-related bug reports collected from Apache Jira. We evaluated ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V1 using zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Under zero-shot prompting, the models correctly decomposed only 10 and 11 reports, respectively. Few-shot prompting increased their true decomposition rates by 140% (10 vs. 24) and 163.64% (11 vs. 29), respectively, although the overall accuracy remained limited. To examine whether the findings generalize beyond privacy-related reports and to expand the dataset size, we further analyzed 127 security-related bug reports using GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. We compared zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and persona prompting. Few-shot prompting achieved the best performance for both models, correctly decomposing 89 reports with GPT-5.5 and 51 reports with DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Across the experiments, we identify a concrete failure taxonomy for LLM-based bug report decomposition, including over-decomposition, over-analysis, incorrect interpretation of solutions, lacking key information, and empty output. Over-decomposition is the most common failure mode, suggesting that LLMs often struggle to distinguish independent bug units from supporting information such as logs, code snippets, background context, and proposed fixes. Title: Artificial intelligence in ports: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Ports, as a key component of transportation, have increasingly relied on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Despite the rapid growth of AI-related research in ports, a structured and integrated understanding of how major AI fields contribute to port operations remains lacking. In this paper, to analyze the knowledge structure, research trends, and emerging topics in port-related AI applications, we conduct a quantitative bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer on 588 articles retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus covering 1997 through July 2026. Based on this schema, we develop a systematic mapping that aligns six major AI fields with port sectors and operational layers, clarifying their functional roles. These contributions are synthesized into a new three-tier hierarchical model—operational, predictive, and strategic/resilience levels—providing an integrated basis for future research and decision-making in port management and maritime policy. The findings indicate a transition from classical AI algorithms toward advanced algorithmic approaches and specialized applications, alongside a growing convergence of technical and managerial perspectives in the development of port intelligence. Title: AI companions as hyper-attachment and caregiving targets
Abstract: How should we make sense of people's interactions with AI companions—conversational systems built for ongoing, emotionally meaningful relationships? Title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. User-generated content significantly strengthens this relationship, with the largest effect among consumers holding moderate brand-image perceptions. Brand ambassadors moderate the relationship but show a bounded pattern, with diminishing influence once brand image is already strong. Testimonials exert a dual effect: they amplify the brand image-repurchase link when perceived as credible, but, when seen as commercially motivated, they independently trigger skepticism and weaken repurchase intention. Title: Knowledge domains in particulate multiphase flow in porous media based on bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Particulate multiphase flow in porous media underpins research in energy exploitation, environmental protection, and geological engineering. Deep insights into such flow systems are critical for revealing subsurface fluid migration mechanisms, improving resource recovery efficiency, and assessing geological-engineering safety. However, a systematic bibliometric delineation of its knowledge structure and evolutionary trajectories remains lacking, particularly at the intersection of solid particulate phases, multiphase fluids, porous structures and particle-related transport. This study retrieved 936 records from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015–July 2026) using combined search terms covering particulate, multiphase, porous-media and transport concepts. After manual screening for eligibility, 912 publications were retained and analyzed via VOSviewer, CiteSpace, Bibliometrix and SCImago Graphica, mapping publication trends, collaboration networks, citation impacts and thematic evolution. Annual output increased from 35 publications in 2015 to 88 in 2025, with a compound annual growth rate of 9.7%. China ranked first with 239 publications (26.2%) and a total collaboration link strength of 83, followed by the United States with 150 publications and a comparable link strength of 82. Six core keyword clusters were identified: multiphase flow, mass transfer, porous media, particle hydrodynamics, lattice Boltzmann method, and discrete element method. Chemical Engineering Science was the most productive journal, Powder Technology had the highest average citations per article (33.6), and the top-cited lattice Boltzmann method review received 889 citations. These findings clarify the domain's intellectual boundaries and indicate that experimentally validated, cross-scale particle–fluid–pore interactions remain the central research priority. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Traditional or New Media: Impact of Risk Perception and Government Trust on Media Trust in Various Risk Scenarios in China
Abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of public risk perception on media trust in different risk scenarios, examining the role of government trust therein. Risk scenarios include known and unknown risks. Media types are categorized as traditional and new. Based on data from 1,925 survey responses collected in China, the study employs multiple linear regression models and moderation analysis. The findings suggest a significant positive predictive relationship between risk perception and public media trust. However, this positive effect substantially diminishes under conditions of heightened risk uncertainty. Irrespective of risk uncertainty, the influence of risk perception on trust in traditional media consistently surpasses its impact on trust in new media. Furthermore, government trust emerges as a pivotal factor affecting public trust in media. Nevertheless, in contexts characterized by elevated risk ambiguity, the beneficial effects of government trust on media trust experience a marked reduction. Similarly, government trust exerts a more robust positive influence on trust in traditional media compared to its impact on trust in new media. Lastly, government trust serves as a moderator in the relationship between risk perception and media trust, with the nature of this moderation varying according to different media types and risk scenarios. These findings broaden the research scope on public trust in the media and provide valuable insights for entities involved in public risk management.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: AI and negotiation: The silicon–carbon communication orientation (SILCCO) framework for understanding technology-mediated negotiation
Abstract: Technology is reshaping negotiation as communication has moved to digital channels, and counterparts are increasingly AI agents. Both changes challenge a persistent underlying assumption in negotiation research that emotions are readily and reliably transmitted between negotiators and in turn shape outcomes. Recent findings suggest neither change affects everyone equally, as digital exchanges and AI expressions can feel rich and authentic to some negotiators, yet hollow and artificial to others. To capture this individual belief, we propose the Silicon–Carbon Communication Orientation (SILCCO) framework. SILCCO comprises two dimensions, channel and sender, that together capture general individual differences in the perceived capacity of technology-mediated communication to convey emotional signals and foster emotional connection. We introduce a six-item scale to measure SILCCO and discuss its potential influence on technology-mediated negotiation outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Dal Molin M.; Landoni M.
Title: The public funding of the New Space Economy. Confronting public procurement and public-private partnership
Abstract: This paper confronts public funding mechanisms in the New Space Economy (NSE). NSE refers to the rise of private actors’ activities in space; however, public funding remains crucial. Addressing this issue, this paper critically compares Public Procurement - an order from the public sector - and public-private partnership (PPP) - i.e., a long-term agreement between public and private actors for the provision of public services or goods - with the final aim of highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and applicability in the NSE. We compare both models to underline differences and benefits, and contend that public procurement is advantageous for both public and private actors. Governments retain public control over space programmes on the one side, while private firms reduce risks on the other. Our results inform public decision-makers with a critical discussion on the advantages and disadvantages of the two models in the context of the NSE. The paper concludes that the supposed privatization of space is far from happening and that private actors would not have entered the space economy without public procurement. © 2026 IAA. Title: Calibrated penalty based variable selection for partially linear single-index varying coefficient spatial autoregressive models

Abstract: In this paper, we consider the variable selection for a class of partially linear single-index varying coefficient spatial autoregressive models. Title: Perceptions of expertise and its development among critical care trainees and staff physicians: A qualitative interview study
Abstract: Background In highly specialized fields such as critical care medicine (CCM), understanding how expertise is defined and developed is essential for both clinical practice and education. While expertise has been widely studied, its characteristics and developmental trajectory among critical care physicians remain incompletely understood. Methods The qualitative interview study involved purposively sampled CCM trainees and experienced staff physicians. Two systems-design researchers interviewed, recorded and transcribed the interviews verbatim. One researcher inductively coded all transcripts, while another researcher reviewed the codes and representative quotations. A CCM physician contributed to theme development, and interpretations were refined through team discussion. Results 36 participants were interviewed (18 trainees and 18 staff physicians). Expertise in CCM was described as multifaceted, encompassing knowledge, experience, technical and non-technical skills, communication, performance, and personal attributes. Mental model development emerged as a central indicator of progression toward expertise. Trainees and staff physicians largely shared similar views; however, trainees emphasized confidence in decision-making and the role of experts as mentors and leaders. Discussion Expertise in CCM extends beyond technical competence to include cognitive and interpersonal dimensions. The importance of mental models and decision-making under uncertainty highlights the role of experiential learning and reflective practice. Differences in perception between trainees and staff physicians suggest that confidence and teaching ability may serve as key markers of expertise from a learner perspective. Conclusion Expertise in CCM is complex and evolving, shaped by experience, reflection, and cognitive development. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing ICU training strategies and supporting clinicians' progression toward expert performance in high-stakes environments. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Dual replacement strategies for systems with dependent failures under lemon laws
Abstract: Lemon laws mandate vehicle replacement or refund when repair attempts or downtime exceed statutory thresholds. While providing essential consumer protection, these regulations also create substantial warranty cost challenges for manufacturers, particularly in modern vehicles where component failures often exhibit positive dependence. This paper develops a comprehensive maintenance optimization framework for systems with dependent failures under lemon laws by integrating the Multivariate Poisson Generalized Gamma Process (MPGGP) into statutory maintenance analysis. Within this framework, two representative manufacturer replacement strategies, namely Replacement First and Replacement Last, are systematically evaluated. Closed-form expressions for the long-run expected cost rate are derived, and an efficient hierarchical coordinate descent algorithm is developed to determine the optimal maintenance decisions. Based on the analytical model and numerical optimization, we establish a policy selection phase diagram that characterizes the relative economic performance of the two replacement strategies under varying replacement costs and dependence levels. The results show that the proactive replacement strategy is generally more cost-effective under moderate replacement costs and stronger failure dependence, whereas the conservative strategy becomes economically competitive as replacement costs increase substantially. These findings provide quantitative insights into maintenance optimization under dependent failures and practical decision support for manufacturers operating under lemon law regulations. Authors: Xie Y.; Li W.; Li J.
Title: Matching-game-based beam scheduling for spectrum sharing in massive LEO constellations
Abstract: This paper develops an on-board, knowledge-driven decision system for autonomous beam management in massive LEO constellations, in which a bounded local knowledge base and a provably objective-aligned inference rule replace the ground-side optimization loop that current constellations depend on. Massive low-Earth-orbit (LEO) constellations have made orbital spectrum a principal bottleneck on the capacity and service quality of next-generation satellite networks. Letting LEO satellites reuse the pre-assigned geostationary-orbit (GEO) downlink spectrum relieves this scarcity but introduces co-channel interference that must be suppressed. Since a ground user is visible to several LEO satellites and its choice of serving satellite reshapes the beam-pointing geometry, interference can be regulated through beam matching alone once beam power and channel are fixed. On this basis, a spatial-adaptive matching learning (SAML) method is proposed. The user–satellite association is cast as a many-to-one matching game whose exact potential function guarantees that distributed local matching converges to a stable association equivalent to a Nash equilibrium. A quasi-static slot upper bound is then derived in closed form from a joint visibility–Doppler criterion and coupled with the beam-relay overlap window, fixing the hard time budget for service continuity. SAML itself uses only O(1) local interaction and O(N) per-slot computation; its asymptotic optimality is proved by Gibbs-measure concentration and refined by a finite-temperature convergence-rate bound tied to the single-slot budget. Simulations show that SAML attains satisfaction within a few percent of a full-information best-response reference, itself a heuristic rather than the exact optimum, sustains stable link-establishment time across relayed slots, meets an end-to-end on-board time budget within the relay overlap window, and allocates resources more fairly than throughput-oriented baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Educational strategies grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour for sustainable food safety culture evolvement
Abstract: Food safety (FS) culture is a behavioural phenomenon that shapes the food safety and hygiene behaviour of people across all organisational levels, contributing to the prevention of foodborne diseases. Although interventions can strengthen FS-culture, evidence on how to systematically develop it remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) in improving food handlers’ behavioural intentions and strengthening the prevailing FS-culture within a Brazilian military food service. A quasi-experimental study was conducted between 2022 and 2025 with 137 food handlers and seven quality managers. Data collection occurred at three time points (t = 0 in 2023, t = 1 in 2024, t = 2 in 2025). FS-culture was evaluated using a mixed-methods approach, while TPB constructs (i.e., subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, attitude, and intention) were measured through a validated questionnaire. Educational interventions were designed to address the lowest-scoring FS-culture element and the TPB constructs most strongly associated with behavioural intentions. FS-culture changed from active (score 2) at t = 0 to active–proactive (score 2-3) at t = 1, with significant improvements in knowledge and communication elements. At t = 2, FS-culture remained at an active-proactive level. Perceived behavioural control was the strongest predictor of intention at baseline (β = 0.27, p = 0.004). Interventions were associated with an increase in attitude scores between t = 0 and t = 1 (p = 0.002) and t = 1 and t = 2 (p = 0.009). These findings support the effectiveness of TPB-based educational interventions in strengthening FS-culture in food services. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Fang C.; Guo F.; Yu M.; Belpaeme T.
Title: Show me your care: The impact of multimodal attentive behaviours for robots on user experience in a healthcare context
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: While robot attentive behaviours hold significant potential for improving user experience in healthcare contexts, how multimodal cues are jointly interpreted by users remains poorly understood. This study examines how multimodal attentive behaviours shape user experience in a simulated ward-round interaction with a Pepper robot acting as a healthcare assistant. A 2 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment manipulated attentive behaviours across auditory, visual, and tactile modalities, including voice pitch (low vs high), lean forward (with vs without), and robot-initiated touch (with vs without). Subjective perceptions (questionnaires), visual attention (eye-tracking), and neural activity (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, fNIRS) were measured. Results showed that a high-pitched voice, a forward-leaning posture, and robot-initiated touch positively influence users’ perceptions. Robot-initiated touch attracted visual attention and was associated with increased neural activity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Significant interactions revealed a cross-modal compensatory mechanism, whereby the absence of cues in one modality increased sensitivity to cues in another. Both visual and tactile cues independently improved user perceptions compared to the auditory-only condition, while combining visual and tactile modalities yielded diminishing incremental benefits. These findings provide converging subjective, behavioural, and neurophysiological evidence that multimodal attentive behaviours can shape users’ experience through cross-modal compensatory mechanisms rather than linearly additive effects. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Women Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability in Africa: The Critical Roles of Electronic Government Services
Abstract: Recent literature acknowledges the significance of women’s empowerment in the global agenda for environmental sustainability. While the role of information and communication technology has been acknowledged, only a few studies have examined the relevance and peculiarities of electronic government (e-government) in combating environmental degradation in developing economies. In addition, the role of e-government in the women empowerment-environmental sustainability nexus has not been explored. This study examines the role of electronic government (e-government) in the relationship between women’s empowerment and a sustainable environment across a panel of 31 African countries from 2003 to 2022. Environmental sustainability is proxied by ecological footprint, while women’s empowerment is proxied by women’s political empowerment and the female labour participation rate. The results, based on the system generalised method of moments, pooled ordinary least squares based on Driscoll and Kraay, and panel quantile regression via moments, show that women’s empowerment reduces ecological footprints, while e-government strengthens and complements women’s empowerment to sustain environmental quality in Africa. This result underscores the significance of women’s empowerment in protecting the environment. Hence, policies to enhance the empowerment and participation of women in all spheres of life should be vigorously pursued in the region, while e-government applications serve as an important policy instrument to transition to a safer and more conducive environment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Integrated scheduling of single-track channels, tugboats, continuous berths and quay cranes via learning-driven multi-objective artificial bee colony algorithms
Abstract: Container terminals, pivotal hubs for modern maritime logistics, underpin economic development and environmental protection. The diversity of resources in port operations makes holistic optimization a vital research focus for both scholars and practitioners. This work proposes a multi-objective integrated scheduling problem of a single-track channel, tugboats, continuous berths and quay cranes in consideration of economic and environmental sustainability. Firstly, a mixed integer programming model is formulated to minimize total dwelling time of vessels and energy consumption of quay cranes. Secondly, an artificial bee colony algorithm with a deep Q-network is developed. Therein, problem-specific encoding and decoding strategies are incorporated, and the deep Q-network is used to intelligently select effective crossover methods. Furthermore, a learning-based local refinement strategy with adaptive neighborhood selection methods is designed. Title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
Abstract: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. The co-citation analysis shows that robo-advisor research sits at the crossroads of finance, marketing, and information systems, built on foundational work like TAM, UTAUT, SEM, and Markowitz’s portfolio theory; the co-authorship network reveals a diverse field dominated by small, internally cohesive teams, with limited cross-border collaboration, despite the citations that show substantial convergence. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. The keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis differentiates well-known themes from accelerating ones. AI, trust, LLMs, UTAUT, perceived risk and value, anthropomorphism, GenAI, and DeFi remain robust across temporal specifications. The study concludes by providing actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers with a call for future research by converting the findings into four research programs: adaptive and personalized investment intelligence, human–AI collaborative advisory, responsible and autonomous financial AI, and programmable and expanded investment ecosystems to ensure responsible and inclusive development of robo-advisory systems across diverse financial ecosystems. © 2026 The Author(s).
