Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of biomass energy carbon reduction in China
Abstract: This study assesses the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and future potential of biomass energy carbon reduction (BCR) in China using data for 31 mainland provincial-level units and a balanced 30-province analytical sample from 2012 to 2022, with projections to 2030. BCR is defined as the theoretical CO2 reduction from replacing coal-fired electricity with energy recovered from agricultural residues, forestry and orchard waste, livestock manure, sewage-derived organic matter, and municipal solid waste; it is not a project-level life-cycle estimate. Biomass-resource accounting was integrated with Moran's I, standard deviational ellipses, fixed-effects STIRPAT, spatial dynamic panel models, Random Forest with PDP/SHAP, and province-specific GA-LSTM forecasting. Results show significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.143–0.193, p < 0.05) and a northeast-to-southwest centroid shift. Population scale and energy consumption structure show significant positive linear associations (coefficients 0.66 and 1.05, p < 0.01), whereas environmental regulation and industrial structure show negative associations. Random Forest achieved R2 = 0.844, RMSE = 13.98 Mt CO2, and MAE = 6.43 Mt CO2; population scale (38.25%) and environmental regulation (30.59%) were the leading predictors, with nonlinear and threshold-like responses. Spatial dynamic estimates confirm path dependence (0.103) and cross-provincial spillovers. GA-LSTM projects aggregate BCR to increase from 1.854 Gt CO2 in 2023 to 2.092 Gt CO2 in 2030, led by Heilongjiang, Henan, and Shandong. Title: Data-driven decision-making in retail: Impacts on firm performance and consumer outcomes

Abstract: Concept: Big data and advanced analytics have radically transformed the retail industry's strategic landscape. In response, companies have adopted data-driven decision-making (DDDM) models as a competitive weapon to address these challenges. Objective: This study examines the multidimensional relationship between the intensity of DDDM adoption and two outcomes: firm performance and consumer welfare. It also investigates how firm size and retail subsector moderates these relationships. Tools: Using a mixed-methods design, we surveyed 386 retail firms across six subsectors and surveyed retail executives regarding application domain barriers in the United States. Quantitative methods included multiple regression, one-way ANOVA, and hierarchical moderated regression, supplemented by surveys from 1200 consumers measuring privacy percept (β = 0.61, p < 0.001, R2 = 0.492). However, 61.3% of consumers express concern about excessive data collection, while 53.6% acknowledge that personalized offers enhance their shopping experience, revealing a 7.7 percentage point privacy paradox accompanied by a notable trust deficit (only 31.6% consumer trust). Application: These findings provide retail managers with ROI estimates (ranging from 2.4× to 3.2×) for analytics investments across application domains while identifying key infrastructure bottlenecks (52% legacy system friction). Title: Personality traits add incremental value beyond food choice motives in predicting food-group consumption
Abstract: Background: Big Five personality traits and food choice motives are well-established correlates of dietary behavior, but they are rarely examined together. If motives are the mechanism through which traits operate, trait effects should largely disappear once motives are controlled; if traits also act through channels people do not report as reasons, dispositional variance should survive. This study tested these competing accounts. Methods: In a Brazilian adult sample (N = 449), participants completed the NEO-FFI-R, the Food Choice Questionnaire (FCQ), and single-item weekly frequency measures for six food groups (meat, fish, dairy, eggs, vegetables, and fruits). We estimated Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control and hierarchical regressions entering sociodemographics, then food choice motives, then Big Five traits. Results: Openness to experience and conscientiousness were the most consistent trait correlates, in the direction reported meta-analytically. Food choice motives accounted for most of the explained variance, yet personality contributed small but reliable increments for five of the six groups: meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and vegetables (ΔR2 = 0.025–0.038). This incremental explained variance was driven mainly by openness, extraversion, and conscientiousness, with no reliable increment for fruit consumption. Conclusions: By controlling proximal motives, the findings indicate that broad dispositions are not fully reducible to the reasons people give for their food choices. The single exception, fruit, was also the group most tightly governed by explicit motives, suggesting that the division of explanatory work between traits and motives is food-specific. Title: Artificial intelligence-based employee selection in tourism and hospitality: Justice, inclusion, and gender differences in resume screening and interviews
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in human resource management, its role in tourism and hospitality hiring remains underexplored. This study investigates job applicants’ perceptions of AI in employee selection, focusing on resume screening and interviews. Drawing on fairness heuristic theory and social role theory, we examine how AI affects perceived justice, inclusion, and organizational attractiveness. Four scenario-based experiments and one qualitative study were conducted with job applicants comparing AI-based and human-based selection methods. Results show that human recruiters are generally perceived as more just and inclusive, enhancing organizational attractiveness. However, gender moderates these effects: females favor AI-based resume screening, whereas males are more receptive to AI-based interviews. Authors: Zhang C.; Hu J.; Bi Z.; Wang Y.
Title: Designing the waiting experience: How order tracking shapes consumer engagement and loyalty
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The post-purchase waiting period is an important yet underexamined stage of the digital customer journey. Consumers increasingly interact with order tracking systems during this phase, yet research has treated tracking primarily as a logistics tool rather than an experiential touchpoint. This study examines how tracking experience design shapes consumer engagement and loyalty through two psychological mechanisms: perceived control and anticipation. Drawing on perceived control theory and anticipatory utility theory, we develop a framework proposing that richer tracking interfaces enhance consumers' sense of predictability and forward-looking excitement, which in turn strengthen post-purchase engagement and loyalty. We test this framework using a three-study design combining scale validation (N = 240), a between-subjects experiment (N = 180), and structural equation modeling with a large field sample (N = 920) of online shoppers. Across all studies, richer tracking experiences consistently increase perceived control and anticipation, both of which stimulate engagement during the waiting period and contribute to customer loyalty. Engagement further mediates the effects of perceived control and anticipation on loyalty. These findings extend customer experience research, contribute to the psychology of waiting literature, and provide actionable guidance for retailers designing post-purchase interfaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zeng B.; Wider W.; Wu C.; Yang C.; Jiang L.; Tee M.; Wu H.
Title: Identifying and prioritizing key factors influencing electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure planning in China: A Delphi study
Abstract: The rapid expansion of China's new energy vehicle market has intensified demand for a coordinated, equitable fast-charging infrastructure system. Despite substantial growth, regional disparities, technical incompatibilities, and fragmented governance arrangements continue to constrain the efficiency and long-term sustainability of network deployment. This study systematically identifies and prioritizes the key determinants shaping the planning of fast-charging infrastructure in China. A two-round Delphi process was conducted with 30 experts drawn from government, industry, and academia to establish consensus on critical influencing factors. Anchored in diffusion of innovation and institutional theory, the analysis integrates technological, economic, spatial, social, environmental, and governance dimensions into a coherent evaluative framework. Six principal factors emerged: governance and institutional coordination; economic and financial viability; technological integration and standardization; social equity and user-oriented considerations; spatial and urban planning; and environmental sustainability. Governance and institutional coordination ranked highest in importance, with strong consensus among participants (Kendall's W = 0.696, p < 0.001). The findings underscore the central role of policy coherence, sustainable financial models, and interoperability in accelerating the diffusion of infrastructure and reducing regional inequality. The study advances a theoretically informed prioritization framework to support strategic infrastructure planning in rapidly electrifying economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Multi-cue judgments of food healthfulness: Evidence for distinct consumer decision strategies
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Consumers frequently evaluate the healthfulness of packaged foods based on multiple on-pack cues presented simultaneously. While prior research has extensively examined individual signals such as nutrition labels or claims, less is known about how consumers integrate competing information and whether they rely on consistent or heterogeneous decision strategies. This study addresses this gap by investigating how different types of product-related cues jointly shape perceived healthfulness and by identifying distinct patterns of cue weighting across consumers. Using a mixed-methods design, we first conducted focus groups to explore how consumers conceptualize healthfulness in real-world evaluation contexts. Building on these insights, a full-profile conjoint experiment with a UK sample recruited by quota sampling on age and gender quantified trade-offs among four on-pack cues: ingredient composition, health-related claims, calorie information, and vitamin tables. At the aggregate level, ingredient-related information exerted the strongest influence, followed by claims and vitamin information, while calorie information played a more limited role. However, segmentation based on individual-level importance weights revealed three distinct health inference strategies: consumers primarily guided by ingredient simplicity, those anchored in energy-related information, and those relying on claim-based cues validated by nutrition tables. Accounting for these strategies substantially improved explanatory power, indicating that heterogeneity in healthfulness judgments is systematic rather than random. The findings contribute to research on consumer information processing by demonstrating that perceived healthfulness reflects distinct, strategy-based patterns of cue weighting rather than uniform cue effects and suggest the need for more nuanced approaches to food labeling and retail communication. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation influences safety behaviour: A moderated serial mediation of psychological safety climate, employee resilience, and ethical leadership
Abstract: Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study examines the psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation is associated with employees’ safety behaviour in Ghana’s mining sector. Specifically, the study investigates the mediating roles of psychological safety climate and employee resilience, as well as the moderating role of ethical leadership. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 418 employees across ten mining sites. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings indicate that digital transformation is positively associated with psychological safety climate and employee resilience, which in turn relate to both safety compliance and safety participation. Psychological safety climate emerged as a stronger predictor of compliance, whereas employee resilience played a more critical role in fostering participatory safety behaviours. Furthermore, the results support a serial mediation pathway, demonstrating that digital transformation indirectly influences safety behavior through the sequential effects of psychological safety climate and resilience. Ethical leadership was found to moderate these relationships, strengthening the positive associations between digital transformation on psychological resources and behavioural outcomes. The study contributes to literature by extending conservation of resources theory to explain how technological, contextual, and personal resources interact in relation to safety behavior in high-risk work environments. Practically, the findings highlight the importance of integrating digital technologies with supportive psychological climates, resilience-building strategies, and ethical leadership practices to promote sustainable safety outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wen C.; Long Y.
Title: Modular microgrids and their deployment: Aligning technological interoperability with integrators’ customization
Abstract: Modularity is recognized as a strategic instrument for advancing microgrid deployment and development. However, this potential is often constrained by a complex interplay of factors, including fragmented standards and site-specific requirements. In addressing these challenges, practitioners have taken different positions or priorities, which may lead to different paths and outcomes in microgrid deployment. This study employs Q methodology to explore practitioners’ subjective perspectives on this issue, aiming to reconcile the inherent tension between standardization and customization in leveraging modular microgrids. Drawing on insights from 17 Chinese experts with extensive experience in microgrid deployment, four distinct viewpoints were identified: (1) prioritizing the establishment of interoperability, (2) demand-oriented customization, (3) techno-economic optimization, and (4) industrial synergies. The findings suggest that aligning interoperability with customization can facilitate the deployment of modular microgrids. The proposed framework provides practitioners with a strategic tool to optimize negotiations and mitigate microgrid deployment risks, while offering policymakers a basis for formulating policy guidance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Feng J.; Li Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Payroll taxes, firm dynamism, and aggregate productivity
Abstract: This study examines the impact of payroll-tax enforcement on firm dynamism and its implications for aggregate productivity. We exploit China's Social Security Collection Agency Reform, which transferred responsibility for collecting social-insurance contributions from local social-insurance agencies to tax authorities, thereby strengthening enforcement. We show that the reform increased firms’ social-insurance contributions, shifted workers toward informal employment without reducing overall nonagricultural employment, and reduced new firm entry while weakening incumbent firms’ profitability and investment. Overall, the reform reduced measured aggregate productivity in China's registered, above-scale industrial sector by 3.3 percent, with entry into the above-scale industrial sector accounting for about 45 percent of the estimated decline. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: “It's all just code”: How is responsibility embedded (or not) in the work of a team of software engineers?
Abstract: Recent research has documented how software can sometimes contribute to harm and inequality, affecting individuals, societies, and the environment. We argue that human values embedded in software, consciously or unconsciously during design and development, play a significant role in producing these outcomes. In other words, to understand responsibility in software engineering, it is crucial to understand how Software Engineers (SEs) incorporate responsibility into their practices, and if or how they reflect on the potential impact of their work. The research reported here probes this assertion by focusing on a team of research SEs involved in developing a commercial source code clone detection tool. Through reflexive thematic analysis of in-depth interviews, with meta-reflections from the SEs Principal Investigator, we offer a detailed account of the practices and artefacts referenced when these professionals reflect on responsibility in their work. Our analysis suggests that the team does not consider responsibility as a singular, unified concept. Instead, reflections on potential negative software impacts and mitigation strategies vary depending on whether they relate to the institutional/organisational context, the specific task, or the intended use. Overall, these SEs tend to perceive software as neutral or inherently beneficial, which, in turn, feeds into a lack of practice of engaging in speculation about the broader implications of the technologies they work with. To address these gaps, we propose a paradigm shift toward an infrastructural view of responsibility - interdisciplinary, sociotechnical, and situated – embedded within the diverse practices and organisational cultures of SE teams operating in different contexts. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Staff interactions and individual influences on complaint behaviour in restaurants
Abstract: This study examines the influence of early staff interactions and individual characteristics on customer complaint behaviour during restaurant dining. A two-stage mixed-methods design was employed: Study 1 surveyed 790 diners, measuring sociodemographic and personality variables alongside self-reported propensity to complain. Study 2 applied these findings in a longitudinal design tracking 98 customers across 994 restaurant visits over one year, capturing individual and situational factors, including staff interactions. Drawing on voice/exit theory and cognitive appraisal frameworks, findings identify redress orientation as a consistent predictor of complaint propensity, whilst empathy reduces both the likelihood of perceived dissatisfaction and willingness to raise issues verbally. Authors: Mislin A.
Author full names: Mislin, Alexandra (14063745600)
Title: Hidden dissatisfaction after agreement: Post-negotiation perceptual alignment
Abstract: Negotiations continue to have consequences after an agreement or impasse. When parties reach a deal, value is often created only later, as they implement commitments, adapt to uncertainty, or decide whether to negotiate again. This review introduces post-negotiation perceptual alignment, how accurately a negotiator understands the counterpart's post-negotiation experience. Integrating research on subjective value, interpersonal perception, and post-agreement outcomes, I distinguish four states: recognized satisfaction, recognized dissatisfaction, overestimated dissatisfaction, and hidden dissatisfaction. Hidden dissatisfaction is consequential because it creates a false sense of success where one party treats agreement as evidence that the negotiation went well while the counterpart carries forward negative appraisals that remain unrecognized and unaddressed. Recent research suggests tactics that appear successful at agreement can impose unrecognized social and relational costs. I review why misalignment arises, emphasizing how negotiators’ imperfect inferences about counterparts’ experiences can combine with social pressures that discourage dissatisfied parties from speaking up. I conclude by outlining directions for measuring alignment and testing how negotiators can recognize and respond to dissatisfaction after negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chen Q.; Qian X.; Shao E.; Tan Y.; Xia L.; Zhang H.; Xiao H.; Deng S.
Title: ASCA-SHAP dual screening of PMI-related corneal ATR-FTIR spectral bands under temperature-dependent variation
Abstract: The estimation of postmortem interval (PMI) is a long-standing scientific challenge in forensic pathology, and its accuracy is susceptible to environmental conditions. Environmental temperature can affect processes such as corneal tissue dehydration, water migration, and degradation of biological macromolecules, altering the spectral evolution characteristics of the cornea after death. Therefore, the relationship between PMI and spectral features may change with temperature conditions. This study collected attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) spectra of 144 rat corneal homogenate samples under three controlled temperature conditions (4°C, 20°C, and 30°C) and six PMI time points (0, 6, 12, 24, 36, and 48 h). Firstly, partial least squares regression (PLSR) models were established for different temperature groups and combined data to compare the modellability of the PMI-spectral relationship under different temperature conditions; subsequently, variance-synchronized component analysis (ANOVA-simultaneous component analysis, ASCA) was used to decompose spectral variations into PMI, temperature, and PMI × temperature interaction effects, and dual screening was conducted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and other equivalent contribution analyses based on PLSR linear coefficients. The results showed that the single-temperature model was superior model performance to the combined, suggesting that temperature affects the relationship between PMI and spectra. The ASCA results indicated that PMI, temperature, and PMI × temperature interaction effects explained 27.38%, 5.94%, and 21.57% of the total spectral variation, respectively. The higher interaction effect suggests that temperature does not merely introduce constant background differences but also alters the spectral evolution trajectory related to PMI. Based on this, this study constructed a dual-screening strategy integrating ASCA effect decomposition and SHAP contribution analysis to identify interpretable PMI-related spectral bands under temperature-dependent variations. Through this screening framework, 56 wave numbers were identified and merged into 9 consecutive candidate spectral bands. These spectral bands are mainly related to protein, amide region, carbonyl group and fingerprint region molecular changes, suggesting that they may reflect the molecular degradation process of the cornea after death. The above spectral bands exhibit strong PMI-related effects, relatively low temperature main effects, and relatively consistent cross-temperature change trends under the current controlled conditions. However, they should not be interpreted as completely independent biomarkers that are completely unaffected by temperature. The proposed ASCA–SHAP dual screening framework in this study can provide candidate spectral features for cross-temperature and interpretable corneal PMI models. Copyright © 2026. Title: Corporate social responsibility and socio-economic impacts in the mining sector: A bibliometric review of local community empowerment and sustainable development
Abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the scholarly literature on corporate social responsibility (CSR) and its socio-economic implications in the mining sector, with a focus on local community empowerment and sustainable development outcomes. Using the Scopus database, a systematic search yielded 217 documents published between 2015 and 2025, which were then refined into 182 articles and reviews through structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study covers three main dimensions: (1) the evolution of mining-related CSR publication trends over the period 2015–2025; (2) the identification of dominant countries, institutions, and authors along with evolving collaboration patterns; and (3) thematic clusters that shape the intellectual architecture of the field, specifically how these clusters reflect the tension between corporate interests and stakeholder rights as theorized by Stakeholder Theory. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer and the Bibliometrix package in R to map publication trends, author productivity, international collaboration networks, and thematic keyword clusters. The findings show a progressive growth in publications, reaching a peak of 37 documents in 2023, reflecting increasing academic and regulatory attention to corporate accountability in the extractive industries. Five thematic clusters were identified: CSR and indigenous peoples, economic sustainability and the resource curse, artisanal mining and local livelihoods, coal mining and occupational health, and a methodological cluster related to data mining in computer science. The United States and Australia lead in publication volume, while Ghana records the highest citation-per-document ratio. Indonesia, while present in the corpus, exhibits limited citation visibility, indicating significant room for increased global research engagement. The study identified critical gaps, including a dearth of longitudinal CSR assessments, limited multinational accountability research, and underrepresentation of Southeast Asian perspectives as urgent research priorities for advancing equitable mining governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: AI and negotiation: Facilitating learning or Fostering dependency?
Abstract: AI is being used in negotiation teaching and training both to promote learning and to facilitate planning for and executing a negotiation. This is a review of current empirical research on the relationships between AI negotiation interventions and learning and dependency. It categorizes AI negotiation interventions by practice, coaching, and feedback. It evaluates their effects on learning with respect to knowledge, satisfaction, behavior, and outcomes. Socratic coaching and post negotiation feedback and reflection appear to facilitate learning. However, interactive explicit AI coaching during planning or negotiation may risk dependency. Rather than dependency due to laziness, motivated students may defer to AI expertise. Alternatively, they may be overloaded by dynamic AI advice. The review concludes that there are many opportunities for future research on the question of if, why, and how AI can facilitate negotiators’ learning versus dependency. Research that looks broadly at learning, that compares separate versus packages of AI interventions, and that identifies mechanisms behind learning versus dependency is especially needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Reliability assessment modeling of multi-component series systems considering phase-type shocks and multiple degradation pathways
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In order to solve the reliability evaluation problem of multi-component series systems affected by multiple impact sources, this paper proposes a unified modeling framework. Traditional approaches typically assume mutual independence among degradation paths and between degradation and shock processes, which may lead to errors. The proposed framework is capable of joint modeling (1) the dynamic impact of each shock source on multiple components, and (2) the strong statistical dependence among multiple degradation paths within each component. Specifically, vine copulas are employed to flexibly capture high-dimensional dependencies among degradation processes without restrictive parametric assumptions, while phase-type distributions are used to represent cumulative damage from mixed-type shocks in a tractable and general manner. Under this framework, an analytical reliability function for the system is derived and its effectiveness is validated through a case study on MEMS oscillators and sensitivity analyses. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Exploring livelihood assets among inland fishing communities: Evidence from the Sungai Pahang, Malaysia
Abstract: The Inland fishing community consisted of Inland fishermen and cage fish farmers. They are among the vulnerable rural groups that require economic assistance. Their dependence on natural resources results in unstable income and increased vulnerability. The vulnerability affects their well-being and livelihoods. Therefore, this study helps by addressing livelihood assets that help minimise vulnerability among the inland fishing community. This paper aims to identify and explore the livelihood assets of inland fishermen and cage fish farmers along the Sungai Pahang. The study employs the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) to identify five livelihood assets: human, natural, financial, physical, and social assets. A survey was conducted among 521 respondents, including 261 inland fishermen and 260 cage fish farmers, using a structured questionnaire. The study was conducted in five districts along the Sungai Pahang Jerantut, Temerloh, Bera, Maran, and Pekan. The data was then analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the main dimensions of the five livelihood assets within the inland fishing community groups. The data were also checked with reliability coefficients (Cronbach’s alpha). The findings show that inland fishermen depend heavily on financial assets 79.53% variance and physical assets 76.48% variance, highlighting the importance of access to credit and fishing gear for their livelihoods. In contrast, cage fish farmers mainly rely on social assets, accounting for 77.96% of the variance, and human assets, accounting for 69.67 of % variance. This reflects the cage fish farmers' reliance on relevant government institutions for support, training & skills, health, and experience to sustain cage fish production. Although both community groups share the same river ecosystem, their needs is differ, highlighting the diverse in main livelihood assets within riverine communities. However, both communities identify natural assets as a weak livelihood dimension, reflecting their shared vulnerability. Policy interventions in Malaysia should therefore prioritise river conservation, stricter pollution control, sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and community-based environmental awareness programmes. Relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment Malaysia, should collaborate with inland fishing communities to implement integrated, participatory environmental management strategies that enhance livelihood resilience and ensure the long-term sustainability of the Sungai Pahang ecosystem. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Quantifying the prestige of scientific awards: A network-bibliometric framework
Abstract: Scientific awards play a central role in recognizing excellence and shaping research trajectories, funding priorities, and disciplinary visibility. Yet despite their importance, scalable and reproducible quantitative frameworks for assessing award prestige remain limited, with prior efforts relying largely on small-scale or perception-based evaluations. This study introduces a data-driven framework for quantifying the prestige of scientific awards by integrating network centrality measures derived from inter-award linkages with bibliometric indicators of prize-winners’ research profiles. Using a dataset of 1352 research-related award records across seven disciplines, we treat award prestige as a latent construct approximated by two external reference dimensions: public attention (crowd-sourced engagement) and professional reputation (expert survey responses). Across three complementary modeling approaches and repeated cross-validation, the framework recovers rankings that are broadly consistent with conventional perceptions of scientific prestige, with awards such as the Nobel Prize, Abel Prize, and Turing Award consistently appearing near the top across external reference dimensions. Among the examined features, network prominence, as measured by eigenvector centrality, emerges as the most consistently important signal, followed by recent bibliometric activity and authorship leadership. The proposed framework offers a scalable and transparent approach to quantifying scientific recognition, providing empirical insights into the structure of academic prestige and informing future evaluations of emerging or underrecognized awards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: When do sustainability-related fashion reviews become helpful? The credibility role of verified purchase in online retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online reviews are an important source of information in digital retailing, yet not all reviews are equally useful to consumers. This study examines whether sustainability-related content is associated with online review helpfulness and whether verified purchase status conditions this relationship. Using 1,680,956 Amazon Fashion reviews, sustainability-related content is identified through a two-stage procedure combining a keyword pre-filter with large language model–assisted semantic classification and is integrated with review-, product-, and reviewer-level information. A formal linear-combination test shows that the combined sustainability effect among verified reviews is positive (β,=0.195p=0.023), corresponding to approximately 21.5% more expected helpful votes. Title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
Abstract: Algorithmic management is increasingly embedded in hotel operations, raising questions about how employees interpret managerial authority and voice concerns. Drawing on organisational justice and trust perspectives, this study examines relationships among perceived algorithmic control, perceived algorithmic fairness, and employee voice intention. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design combined structural equation modelling with semi-structured interviews. Perceived algorithmic control was negatively associated with procedural justice, interactional justice, and voice intention, whereas perceived algorithmic fairness was positively associated with trust in the employer and voice intention. Title: From hostile feedback to withdrawal: Emotional exhaustion as a barrier to social media misinformation correction
Abstract: User-driven misinformation correction is essential for sustaining the integrity of democratic discourse on social media, yet the emotional costs that discourage engagement remain understudied. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how the emotional tone of other users' feedback affects correctors' emotional exhaustion and subsequent willingness to engage in future corrections in a social media environment. In a cross-national experiment (N = 2001) across Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, and Poland, utilizing a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design, participants corrected misinformation and received feedback varying in valence and arousal. Results show that angry, high-arousal feedback uniquely depletes emotional resources, producing higher exhaustion than civil disapproval or positive feedback. This indicates that critical feedback does not inherently exhaust correctors, but it is the hostile tone, not the negativity itself, that drives depletion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, predicts avoidance of future corrective engagement. Title: Generative AI as a social partner for young adults: Dual pathways to resilience and AI dependence
Abstract: This study examines LLM-based AI chatbots as social interaction partners. It identifies young adults’ support-seeking motivations and models their associations with two interaction processes (Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity) and two psychological outcomes (Resilience and AI Dependence). In Study 1, we developed the Motivation Scale for Generative AI (MS-GAI) through theory-driven item generation and interviews and validated it with a survey of Korean young adults (N = 300). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported an eight-factor, 40-item structure grounded in four social-support domains and supplemented by context-specific motivations. In Study 2, structural equation modeling showed that Emotional Support and Self-Enhancement were positively associated with both Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity. Objective Advice Seeking was positively associated with Perceived Authenticity, whereas Learning Assistance, Daily Problem-Solving, and Entertainment/Mood Diversion were positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Perceived Authenticity was also positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Both interaction processes were positively related to self-reported Resilience and AI Dependence, with Interaction Intensity showing the stronger association with AI Dependence. These findings identify distinct but overlapping interaction pathways through which support-seeking motivations are associated with adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. The study extends understanding of social support in human–AI interaction by providing a validated motivation measure and showing how shared interaction processes relate to both short-term perceived recovery and dependence. The findings are consistent with the Paradoxes of Technology perspective and highlight the need for emotionally supportive yet balanced design and policy safeguards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Halo or horn? The role of prior attitudes in shaping consumer responses to high-protein food labels
Abstract: Front-of-pack nutrition claims can shape consumers' perceptions of food products by triggering inferences about their overall healthfulness. Among these claims, “high-protein” labels have rapidly expanded across food categories, yet their influence on consumers' nutritional judgments remains underexplored. The present study investigated whether a high-protein label induces a health halo effect and examined the role of product characteristics and individual differences in shaping these perceptions. In an online experiment (N = 218), participants evaluated five food products presented either with or without a high-protein label. For each product, participants rated perceived calories, healthiness, sugar content, additives, level of processing, and purchase intention. Individual differences in drive for muscularity and attitudes toward protein products were also measured. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that the high-protein label did not produce a generalized positive halo effect: it did not significantly affect perceived healthiness, caloric content, sugar content, or purchase intention. However, products labeled as high protein were perceived as containing more additives and as being more industrially processed, consistent with a horn effect. The influence of the label on calorie and sugar estimations was moderated by the caloric content of the product, with effects emerging primarily for high-calorie products. Attitudes toward protein products moderated the label's effect across nutritional judgments, whereas drive for muscularity did not moderate labeling effects. These findings highlight the central role of individual predispositions in shaping responses to nutrition claims and suggest that high-protein labels may generate complex and sometimes contradictory perceptual biases, with implications for dietary behavior and public health. © 2026 The Authors

Title: From Scrum to DevOps education: A review of Agile and Lean software development methods and teaching approaches
Abstract: Context: Teaching agile and lean concepts is vital for software engineering students, as the software industry increasingly adopts methods such as Scrum, Extreme Programming, Kanban, and DevOps, equipping students with essential skills for real-world software development. However, despite the importance of software process education, a gap remains in understanding the most effective pedagogical strategies for teaching these methods. Objective: This study aims to address the gap in understanding by identifying the most widely taught software development methods and effective pedagogical strategies for teaching them in higher education. Method: This study addresses the existing gap through a literature survey of 50 primary studies. Results: The literature survey analyzed diverse teaching approaches and learning environments, while the experience report provided insights into how these approaches perform in practice. Combining traditional teaching methods, such as project-based learning and lectures, with innovative approaches like gamification, role-playing, simulations, and industry visits enhances both student engagement and skill development. Title: Picard approximation and stability analysis of generalized ϱ-Caputo stochastic fractional differential equations with application to a Black–Scholes-type model

Title: Do narcissistic personality traits and immature defense mechanisms hinder communication and cooperation in pilots?
Abstract: This study examines the safety operation behaviors of pilots within the framework of communication and cooperation, compares how these behaviors are affected by narcissistic personality traits, and compares the results for the correct evaluation and management of immature ego defense mechanisms, which are thought to be a factor triggering this relationship. The data were collected from 150 pilot participants working at airlines in Turkey using a survey data collection tool. It was observed that the participants frequently used the defense mechanisms of rationalization, isolation, and acting out. This result shows that pilots continue to exhibit the same behavior by providing acceptable reasons rather than trying to eliminate negative situations by discussing them realistically. It was also observed that they tend to focus only on the objective aspects of events and avoid discussing the parts that negatively affect them psychologically. In addition, it was found that narcissistic personality traits negatively affect the communication and cooperation behaviors of pilots, and immature ego defense mechanisms are a precursor that strengthens the narcissistic personality. It is thought that examining narcissistic personality traits within the framework of immature ego defense mechanisms and managing these mechanisms effectively will contribute greatly to aviation psychology research to prevent risks related to the human factor, which airline companies and authorities view as an important risk within safety management systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Pathways to plant-based meal consumption: A two-wave test of the health action process approach (HAPA)
Abstract: Despite well-documented health and environmental benefits, increasing plant-based meal consumption remains challenging in meat-centric societies, reflecting complex socio-cognitive processes in translating intention into action. Grounded in the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA), this study examined plant-based meal consumption among young adults from the USA, Portugal, and the Netherlands who had not fully adopted a plant-based diet (N = 266). Using two waves one week apart, we estimated three structural models of plant-based meal consumption, controlling for prior behavior and common method variance. Findings were broadly consistent with HAPA. Action self-efficacy was most strongly associated with intention, which in turn was associated with action planning. Coping planning and self-monitoring pathways were not supported. While past behavior remained most strongly associated with plant-based meal consumption, the parsimonious model reaffirmed action planning as the key intention-behavior mediator. The findings highlight this volitional process in translating motivation into action and suggest interventions may benefit from strengthening efficacy beliefs and concrete planning strategies to support plant-based dietary change. © 2026

Title: Digital transformation policy and production efficiency in state-owned electric power enterprises: Evidence from China
Abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly used to modernize public utilities, but its efficiency effects remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effect of China's 2020 digital transformation policy for state-owned enterprises on the production efficiency of listed electric enterprises. Treating the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a super-efficiency data envelopment analysis model to measure production efficiency and a difference-in-differences model to examine the policy effect. The results show that the policy significantly improves the production efficiency of state-owned electric enterprises relative to non-state-owned enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects among utilities in eastern China, labor-intensive firms, and large firms. Mechanism analysis further shows that increased R&D investment is an important channel through which the policy generates efficiency gains, while managerial equity incentives strengthen policy effectiveness. The findings provide policy implications for utility digitalization, differentiated policy support, innovation incentives, and governance reform. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Together or apart? Migration, education access, and intergenerational mobility in China
Abstract: This paper studies how hukou-based education wedges and child-arrangement costs jointly shape welfare and intergenerational educational mobility in China. I develop a quantitative spatial model with overlapping generations in which households sequentially choose education, migration, and child arrangement, and estimate it using census and household-survey data. Under a common financing rule, two child-targeted policies raise the co-migration rate to a similar extent but differ sharply in welfare and mobility. Subsidizing co-migrating families in high-cost destinations generates 1.4 times as much welfare per unit of government revenue as removing migrant children's education-access wedges. These gains concentrate on recipients. Removing the education-access wedges delivers over four times the mobility gain per unit of revenue, and the resulting human capital generates growing welfare gains across generations. A broader reform that equalizes public-service access for all migrants is the most welfare-efficient but does not raise mobility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
Abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. Using the DeepSeek R1 671B model with few-shot learning, we classified 225,515 social media comments from Douyin into five theory-driven categories and an “Other” category, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.67% against stratified human reference labels (Cohen’s kappa = 0.828). We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. By integrating theory-driven LLM classification with spatial analysis, the proposed framework connects computational linguistics and spatial social computing, providing a replicable approach for examining regional heterogeneity in digital crisis discourse. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Transformative leadership models and styles to improve the quality and development of Muhammadiyah school education in Blora Indonesia
Abstract: This study aims to investigate models and leadership styles that are effective in improving the quality of education in Muhammadiyah Schools in Blora, Indonesia. The research method used is a case study with a focus on qualitative data analysis, including interviews, observations, and analysis of related documents. This research identifies various leadership models that have been applied in Muhammadiyah Schools, including transformational, transactional, and participatory leadership. In addition, this study explores stakeholder preferences and perceptions of the most effective leadership styles in the context of Islamic education in the Muhammadiyah school environment in Blora. The implementation of transactional and participatory strategies has also proven important in day-to-day management and consensus-based decision-making. The novelty of this study lies in the identification of a combination of transformational and participatory leadership as an optimal leadership model in the context of Islamic education. This research also adds a new perspective on stakeholder preferences in the implementation of leadership styles in Muhammadiyah schools. The implication of this study is the need for educational leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools to consider the application of a combination of flexible and innovative leadership models, in order to achieve continuous improvement in the quality of Islamic education. Title: Bibliometric study of environmental education: Scientific architecture and the transition toward micro-educational and behavioral approaches
Abstract: Although scientific production in environmental education has grown steadily, fragmented approaches and limited interdisciplinary integration persist. Moreover, the transition from macronormative frameworks to microeducational approaches oriented toward behavioral change remains insufficiently characterized. The objective of this study was to comprehensively analyze the scientific architecture of environmental education, identifying its structural evolution, key actors, predominant sources, funding dynamics, thematic trends, and scientific production cycle, with particular attention to the shift toward microeducational and behavioral approaches. The study followed a rigorous and consolidated four-stage bibliometric method. A total of 4,952 documents indexed in Scopus were analyzed using the Bibliometrix software, examining six main indicators: (1) authors, (2) sponsors, (3) thematic evolution and conceptual structure, (4) sources, (5) documents, and (6) scientific production. The findings reveal sustained expansion in environmental education, with a productivity peak in 2025 and a projected stabilization toward 2032, confirming its advanced consolidation phase. An editorial structure concentrated in historical core journals—Environmental Education Research and Journal of Environmental Education—was identified, alongside growing interdisciplinary expansion toward sustainability, higher education, and technological innovation. Scientific leadership is concentrated in the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom, although emerging economies such as Brazil and China are gaining prominence. Thematically, macrostructural cores linked to sustainability and sustainable development persist; however, microeducational approaches such as pro-environmental behavior, outdoor environmental education, and environmental knowledge are emerging more strongly, indicating a shift toward the analysis of situated learning processes and behavioral change. Bibliometric findings were contrasted with evidence from other bibliometric studies and systematic reviews. It is concluded that environmental education has evolved from a paradigm centered on global normative frameworks toward a multidimensional model integrating experience, behavior, technological innovation, and community action. The study provides insights for educational policy and teaching practice. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: How can hotels strategically enhance competitive performance? Investigating the dynamic roles and impacts of service attributes on customer satisfaction and dissatisfaction

Title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
Abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). To address this deficiency, this study, conducted in the Republic of Ireland, adopts a sequential research design in which expert workshops and focus groups were used to develop a nationally representative discrete choice survey (n = 970) to estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for environmental improvements and to enhance the effectiveness, legitimacy, and practical uptake of SEA. Our findings reveal strong public support for planning scenarios that include greater public participation, substantial increases in local green space (10–30%), and acceptance of short procedural delays (1–2 years) in SEA processes to ensure comprehensive environmental assessment. Model estimates indicate that respondents expressed a WTP of approximately €48–€63 per year for a 30% increase in green space, with the lower estimate derived from the multinomial logit (MNL) model and the higher estimate from the random parameters logit (RPL) model. Results also indicate limited public familiarity with SEA instruments and relatively low trust in governmental environmental decision-making. The study presents a methodological framework for integrating ecosystem service valuation and measurable forms of public participation into SEA processes to support more effective and legitimate environmental decision-making. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Inertial bregman proximal iteratively reweighted algorithms for a class of nonconvex nonsmooth regularized problems

Abstract: In this paper, we study a class of nonconvex nonsmooth regularized optimization problems whose objective consists of a continuously differentiable loss function and a structured nonconvex regularizer. To solve this class of problems efficiently, we first propose an inertial Bregman proximal iteratively reweighted algorithm for the case where the loss function has a Lipschitz-continuous gradient. An explicit and verifiable condition for selecting the extrapolation parameters is established. We then extend the proposed framework to the relatively smooth setting, where the loss function is differentiable but not necessarily gradient-Lipschitz continuous. In both settings, we prove that any accumulation point of the generated sequence is a critical point of the problem. Moreover, under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property of suitable Lyapunov functions, the global convergence of the whole sequence is established. Title: Trust patterns in food chain actors in the European region over a six-year period (2019-2024): an exploratory analysis

Title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
Abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. In addition, the study highlights directions for future research, offering valuable insights for policymakers, managers, and scholars seeking to promote work well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Helpfulness and enjoyment in eWOM: A dual-value perspective for hedonic digital products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As the digital economy increasingly pivots toward the experience sector, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) serves not merely as a decision-support tool but as an intrinsic source of entertainment. Yet, the literature remains overwhelmingly anchored to a unidimensional metric: review helpfulness. Challenging this utilitarian bias, this study establishes a dual-value evaluative paradigm that encompasses both diagnostic helpfulness and enjoyment to decode peer evaluations of hedonic digital product reviews. Grounded in processing fluency theory, we investigate how cognitive stimuli (product informativeness) and affective stimuli (emotional richness) synergistically yet distinctly drive these dual dimensions. Leveraging a dataset of 12,823 reviews from Steam, we deploy a rigorous methodological triangulation: extracting deep semantic features via Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and VADER sentiment analysis, estimating causal mechanisms via Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) regressions, and validating predictive robustness using Random Forest algorithms. The empirical findings reveal that review breadth and thematic distribution divergence concurrently enhance both outcomes. Review thematic density exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship across both dimensions. While the negative sentiment rate enhances utilitarian risk-mitigation but severely disrupts hedonic gratification. The study advances eWOM literature by establishing a dual-value evaluative paradigm, providing actionable guidelines for digital platforms to optimize content distribution for review helpfulness and enjoyment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Licochalcone D accelerates cutaneous wound healing with improved perfusion and antioxidant responses
Abstract: Impaired local perfusion, excessive oxidative stress, persistent inflammation, and apoptosis can compromise cutaneous wound healing. Licochalcone D (LCD), a licorice-derived flavonoid, has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its effects on cutaneous repair remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated LCD in a rat full-thickness excisional wound model. Thirty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to vehicle control or LCD treatment at 5, 25, or 50 mg/kg/day by oral gavage. Wound closure, local perfusion, histological repair, oxidative stress, inflammatory mediators, apoptosis-related proteins, antioxidant signaling-related proteins, and selected mitochondrial protein markers were evaluated. LCD accelerated wound closure, enhanced perfusion, increased VEGF expression, reduced inflammatory-cell infiltration, and improved collagen organization. LCD also increased SOD activity, reduced MDA and 4-HNE levels, and decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1 expression increased after LCD treatment, supporting an association with enhanced antioxidant responses. Apoptosis-related proteins shifted toward an anti-apoptotic pattern. LCD treatment was additionally accompanied by changes in PINK1, Parkin, LC3B, SQSTM1/p62, and COX IV expression; however, these single-time-point measurements do not establish altered mitophagic flux or a causal mitochondrial mechanism. Overall, orally administered LCD improved multiple wound-healing-related outcomes, with more pronounced effects in the medium- and high-dose groups. © 2026

Title: Suppressed inquiry: The hidden toll of working with satisfaction-optimized AI
Abstract: LLMs have become thinking companions for hundreds of millions worldwide, and they often do remarkable work. But their satisfaction-optimized design produces suppressed inquiry: the tendency for LLMs to inhibit rather than facilitate users' questioning process. LLMs appear fluent, confident, and seemingly all-knowing, their near-instant and polished output making non-LLM work feel unacceptably tedious and less eloquent. They affirm rather than interrogate users' assumptions, producing output that is deceptively adequate—shallower, less original, and less carefully reasoned than it appears. Seemingly competent systems also reduce vigilance and the monitoring impulse that independent judgment requires. Their responses also confine users within the frame they establish, narrowing what users think to ask. These costs are self-concealing: detecting them requires the very engagement that they suppress. And repeated delegation gradually atrophies users' capacity to reason independently. Three converging pressures make correction difficult: commercial incentives that reward satisfaction over substance, LLMs’ tendency to revert to satisfaction-optimized defaults even when users push back, and a societal drift toward less-effortful engagement. We propose a research agenda to deepen the understanding of suppressed inquiry and how to counter it, to move closer to the remarkable thinking partners LLMs promised to be. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy
Abstract: This research note reconceptualizes tourism intensity as a structural stressor capable of undermining the social capital that sustains urban life. Drawing on a 15-year longitudinal panel data of 42 Italian cities (2009-2023) and employing a dynamic System GMM estimator, our study analyses how varying levels of tourism intensity affect social capital, operationalized through a multi-indicator civic engagement index. The results reveal a non-linear erosion process, where social capital remains stable at low and moderate levels of tourism intensity but declines sharply once cities surpass high-intensity thresholds. Our findings provide a quantifiable basis for understanding overtourism as a threshold-based social phenomenon, extending beyond resident perceptions to the structural weakening of civic cooperation, trust, and engagement. The present study advances theoretical debates by positioning tourism intensity as a civic destabilizer and highlights the need for governance models that protect social capital as a critical urban asset. Without such safeguards, cities risk transitioning from vibrant, participatory communities into socially depleted Non-places. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Political activism and indulgent preferences: Perceived moral contribution and deservingness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Political activism is commonly conceptualized as a form of collective action that promotes individual empowerment, collective efficacy, and societal well-being. However, this research demonstrates that activism focused on the pursuit of a collective goal can also have paradoxical consequences by increasing subsequent indulgent preferences. Drawing on moral licensing theory, when high-effort, in-person activism is grounded in moral conviction, actors may interpret their effortful involvement as a morally meaningful contribution to a collective cause, enhancing a sense of perceived moral contribution, which heightens perceived deservingness and, in turn, indulgence. Across four experimental studies (n = 852) in emerging and developed economies, the results highlight that participants exposed to high-effort, in-person activism scenarios subsequently demonstrated higher levels of indulgence than those in low-effort online actions or the control condition. These effects are moderated by consumer type in emerging markets, with the effect of high-effort activism on indulgence being stronger among bottom-of-the-pyramid (BOP) consumers. Our findings caution advocacy organizations against assuming that effortful civic participation consistently reinforces prosocial behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A rapid on-site visual detection strategy for vanillic acid based on the specific diazo coupling principle
Abstract: The accurate determination of vanillic acid (VA) is essential for quality control and authenticity verification in food and pharmaceutical products. The reliance on instruments hinders on-site VA detection, and existing colorimetric probes, though visually intuitive, remain limited in specificity and signal intensity. In this work, a novel bis-diazonium probe, 1,5-bis(diazonium tetrafluoroborate)naphthalene (NADBF), was designed and synthesized for the rapid and specific colorimetric detection of VA. NADBF features a naphthalene backbone as the π-conjugated chromogenic scaffold, with two diazonium groups introduced to enable diazo coupling with VA. This probe enables direct detection of VA in deep eutectic solvent (DES) extracts without requiring solvent exchange or additional sample processing steps. The method exhibited a linear detection range of 0.75–45 μM, with a detection limit of 0.698 μM and a reaction time within 6 min. It was successfully applied to the determination of VA in corn flour, yielding recoveries of 97.30%–105.90% (RSD < 2.32%). This work provides a new molecular tool for the on-site screening of VA and offers valuable insights for the design of targeted colorimetric probes for phenolic compounds. © 2026

Title: What do feature branches tell us about feature implementation in open-source projects?
Abstract: Although “feature” is a common term across requirements engineering, product-line engineering, and agile methods, its operationalization in practice–especially through feature branches–has received little empirical attention. Feature branches are widely recommended on platforms like GitHub; yet, empirical evidence on how they are actually used is scarce. This study investigates feature-branch development practices in open-source software (OSS) projects. We conducted a large-scale empirical analysis of 27,103 feature branches from 3,388 popular GitHub repositories. Using branch-naming conventions, we identified feature branches and measured their lifespan, commit history, and commit-share distributions among contributors. In addition, we profiled contributors according to their opened issues, opened pull requests, number of followers, and total stars. Our analysis revealed that feature branches in open-source projects are long-lived, with a median lifespan exceeding two years, diverging from the short, agile iterations typically employed in software development. Commit intensity is low and irregular, averaging fewer than two commits per day. Contribution is highly unequal within feature branches: a small share of contributors accounts for most commits, revealing strong dependence on a small subset of developers. These findings have several practical implications. Our findings suggest that monitoring contribution concentration within feature branches– for instance, by computing the share of commits attributable to the top contributor or a Gini coefficient over the branch’s commit history–can help maintainers identify branches where development knowledge is held by very few individuals. Likewise, rolling commit intensity–computable directly from commit timestamps–may serve as an early signal of branch stagnation in OSS projects. Moreover, these findings establish an empirical baseline for future studies, including analyses of proprietary repositories. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Fan G.; Deng Z.; Fang H.
Title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
Abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. This study contributes to the literature on knowledge co-construction, expands the understanding of health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms, and provides practical guidance for platform managers and doctors. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: Bridging the Human-AI preference gap: A persuasion-oriented tripartite framework
Abstract: The remarkable performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems on a wide variety of complex tasks has fueled its rapid adoption in recent years. Yet, many individuals still exhibit a human-AI preference gap, such that they prefer human-generated over AI-generated outputs and follow recommendations made by generative AI (GenAI) less than human advice. We conceptualize the rejection of a superior AI system in favor of an inferior human as a persuasion failure that necessitates psychological rather than technological resolution. Recent research has identified various interventions that compress the human-AI preference gap. We codify these interventions by introducing a persuasion-oriented tripartite framework that delineates three distinct paths by which the preference gap between humans and AI systems may be narrowed: (1) AI-centric interventions, which directly bolster perceptions and evaluations of AI systems; (2) human-centric interventions, which reduce the (often inflated) perceptions and evaluations of humans; and (3) hybrid interventions, which offer an integrated or reformulated alternative that combines human and AI elements. Ultimately, our tripartite framework illustrates how different persuasion tactics fundamentally reshape beliefs and attitudes about both AI and humans, thereby informing system design elements and communication strategies that can bridge the human-AI preference gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Mapping the research landscape of generative artificial intelligence in education with implications for teacher education: A bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models, has significantly transformed educational research and practice, resulting in a rapidly expanding yet fragmented body of literature. This study aims to systematically map the research landscape of GenAI in education and examine its implications for teacher education through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Using the Scopus database, 16,250 documents published from 2021 to 2025 were analyzed through performance analysis and science mapping techniques, including keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship network analysis, and citation analysis to capture the structural and intellectual development of the field. The findings reveal a sharp increase in publication output beginning in 2023, indicating a transition from an emergent to a high-growth phase of research development. Research productivity and scholarly influence are concentrated among a limited group of authors, institutions, and countries, particularly the United States and China, reflecting uneven global participation. Collaboration networks exhibit a multi-clustered structure, suggesting active yet fragmented research communities with limited cross-group integration. Citation patterns indicate that a small number of recent publications exert strong influence and serve as foundational references in the field. Thematic analysis further identifies three dominant and interconnected areas: core technological developments, educational applications, and domain-specific implementations, highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of GenAI in education. The field is expanding rapidly but remains structurally fragmented and is still undergoing intellectual consolidation. These findings emphasize the need for more cohesive research efforts, stronger international collaboration, and greater integration across thematic domains. Implications for teacher education include the integration of AI-related competencies into pre-service programs, the adoption of pedagogically grounded and context-sensitive approaches, and the provision of continuous professional development to support teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Author full names: Blanchard, Simon J. (24280915800); Garvey, Aaron M. (56781208100); O'Laughlin, Laura (60905627500)
Title: Hallucinations in organization-backed AI advisors: Evidence about skepticism, verification, and reliance in goal-directed use
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems are increasingly used by organizations to deliver information to consumers, patients, students, employees, and citizens. These systems can hallucinate, producing plausible but inaccurate responses. A central question for AI-advised decisions is therefore not only whether users rely on inaccurate information, but whether they recognize that a response may require verification. To answer this question, we review emerging empirical evidence relevant to hallucination detection in goal-directed interactions, with a focus on organization-backed AI advisors. We distinguish three constructs that existing studies often conflate: whether users are skeptical of information presented, whether they verify it (distinguishing attempted from successful verification), and whether the result of verification affects reliance on the information. Across studies examining product search, medical decision-making, content generation, and chatbot-assisted tasks, several patterns emerge. Nearly all studies measure reliance, while variables such as user skepticism and verification of the information are more often targeted by an intervention than measured directly. The cues used to prompt scrutiny of the AI response are predominantly related to the AI output, such as source citations. Whereas general warnings about the risk of hallucinations are among the most deployable interventions for organizations, they show the weakest and most mixed effects in the studies reviewed. More targeted cues about where AI systems tend to fail appear promising, however evidence remains limited. Although the existing literature posits that users may be more likely to scrutinize responses related to particular areas of content, no studies varied the content category, leaving this question open for further research. In future research, measuring skepticism and verification separately from reliance may clarify what current evidence shows, what it only implies, and which questions require further exploration. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Techno-economic study and sensitivity analysis- benefits of complex petrochemical waste refining
Abstract: For the petrochemical industry to maintain resource sustainability, complex waste must be treated effectively. In the previous work, the Aspen Hysys V12.0 modeling tool was used to analyze the regeneration of water, aromatics (BTX), and glycols (MEG, DEG, and TEG) from petrochemical effluent and the operating parameters were validated with experimental study. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of an integrated petrochemical wastewater treatment system with resource recovery. The process enables recovery of water (7.8 MM kg/year), aromatics such as benzene and toluene (468,000 kg/year each), and glycols (over 16.5 MM kg/year). The total capital investment is estimated at $42.4 MM, with annual operating costs of $8.46 MM and revenue of $18 MM. The system achieves a net present value (NPV) of $31.8 MM, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 19.9%, and a payback period of 4.87 years. Sensitivity analysis identified product price and electricity cost as key economic drivers. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) showed a 95% probability of positive NPV, indicating robust performance under uncertainty. The carbon footprint is estimated at 11,970 tons CO2/year (0.12 kg CO2/kg treated), representing an 87% reduction compared to conventional systems. Carbon pricing further enhances economic viability. The novelty of this work lies in integrating techno-economic analysis, uncertainty quantification, carbon footprint evaluation, and circular economy principles into a unified framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed system is a sustainable and economically viable solution for petrochemical wastewater management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
