Authors: Li Z.; Zhou H.; Wu Q.
Title: An adaptive-problem structure framework for survival relevance in temporal processing
Abstract: Research on survival-relevant cues and subjective time often groups stimuli into immediate-survival, reproductive, and social categories. These labels do not explain why cues within one category recruit different temporal processes across contexts and perceivers. The Adaptive-Problem Structure (APS) Framework characterizes the adaptive problem indicated by a cue through two separable appraisals: ecological urgency, the time sensitivity and cost of delaying a response, and interpretive indeterminacy, the extent to which adaptive meaning and the appropriate response remain unresolved. APS predicts when these appraisals recruit established arousal, attention, information-sampling, and memory processes, how diagnostic context changes those links, and which personality differences strengthen them. Temporal consequences depend on the timing paradigm, interval, and response format. We outline independent ratings, selective within-domain manipulations, process measures, and staged construct validation. Five predictions specify task conditions, personality mappings, comparison baselines, and non-supporting outcomes. APS offers testable constraints on mechanism recruitment and prediction for new stimuli; the framework itself remains to be empirically validated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Large language model-based carbon emission forecasting: A sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework with transformer-long short-term memory networks
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions from coal, oil, natural gas, cement, and total CO2 is critical for formulating effective emission reduction strategies and carbon trading policies. However, existing models are plagued by overemphasis on total CO2 prediction, overreliance on single-task learning that overlooks cross-source correlations, neglect of sentiment information in carbon-related texts, and the absence of domain-adapted large language models (LLMs) for carbon sentiment extraction, which severely impairs their prediction accuracy and generalization ability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a novel sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework for carbon emission forecasting, which integrates an LLM with a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) network. First, a domain-adapted LLM is developed based on DeepSeek-R1 and a multi-level fusion attention mechanism, enabling efficient sentiment feature extraction from carbon emission reports (e.g., policy, transaction, social awareness) with few-shot data. Second, a Transformer-LSTM-based multi-task learning model is designed to synergistically predict emissions from the five aforementioned sources by exploiting shared features and the complementary strengths of parallel computing and long-term dependency capture. Finally, a strengthened blood-sucking leech algorithm with Cauchy chaotic mutation and chaotic mapping is proposed to optimize the hyperparameters of the multi-task model, thus avoiding local optima and enhancing convergence stability. Validated on real-world data from the International Energy Agency, the proposed framework reduces the root mean square error by 11.14 tons compared with benchmark models. Meanwhile, the developed LLM achieves a sentiment classification accuracy 0.145 higher than baseline methods, which fully verifies the effectiveness of integrating sentiment information in carbon emission forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: QualiTact: A semantic model for quality-driven development of AI-based systems based on architectural tactics
Abstract: Systems operating in safety-critical industries increasingly adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI). Satisfaction of system quality attributes in these industries is mandatory and rigorously verified. To influence system quality, a crucial development practice is the use of architectural tactics. However, selecting and balancing these attributes is often based on experience rather than on conscious decisions. This can unexpectedly impact system quality and might be detected too late in the testing phase. For development projects, it is desirable to identify and plan the selection of architectural tactics in a quality-driven manner. This article presents an approach that calculates a tactic's relative influence between 24 linked quality attributes and 150 tactics as part of a semantic model that supports the quality-driven development of AI-based systems. Attribute selection and filtering create recommendations of relevant tactics for a specific design and development task. In an exploratory multi-case study, the suitability of the recommended tactics was analyzed using source code. Results show that the model can compensate missing quality attribute information input and can provide recommendations. Despite an average input of only 39.98% from 30 case-relevant quality attributes for the model, the average recommendation completeness reaches 49.26% for 20.67 known tactics in source code across cases, leading the model to suffer from gaps between the literature and cases. Yet, 28 new design tactics linked to 30 known quality attributes were identified. Our work thus lays the foundation to support quality-driven design and development by recommending architectural tactics based on quality requirements. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The role of citizen science in engaging older adults with age-friendly green spaces
Abstract: This project addresses the global challenges of an ageing population and rapid urbanisation by exploring how citizen science can support the engagement of older adults in shaping age-friendly green spaces. Conducted in the City of Unley, South Australia, the study engaged 30 older residents (aged 60+) as citizen scientists to trial a multi-format audit tool and co-reflect on its use in practice for creating age-friendly environments, generating practical insights for future research and design practice. Integrating audits into participants’ daily routines and everyday life spaces ensured that findings reflected lived experiences. Citizen science was not merely a data collection tool but a sustained dialogue, with regular workshops and informal café sessions supporting motivation, peer learning, and collaborative analysis. Participants reported challenges such as sustaining long-term motivation, but also highlighted opportunities for empowerment, confidence-building, and strengthened community ties. Importantly, many older adults described shifts in how they experienced their environments—becoming more observant, extending their walking habits, and growing more confident in voicing ideas. Several participants continued their civic engagement beyond the project, illustrating the lasting impact of participation. The study contributes methodological insights into designing inclusive citizen science initiatives, offering guidance on recruitment, tool development, and engagement strategies tailored to older populations. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of citizen science not only to generate grounded data but also to empower older adults and co-produce inclusive urban knowledge. Findings provide process-focused insights into age-friendly engagement and illustrate the broader potential of citizen science in shaping equitable, community led public spaces. Overall, this research demonstrates how citizen science can move beyond data collection to become a co-creative process that empowers older adults and informs age-friendly urban transformation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Layered lanthanum hydroxycarbonate turns phosphate pollution into slow-release fertilizer
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: Mismanagement of Phosphorus (P) depletes phosphate finite rock reserves and exacerbates widespread aquatic eutrophication, driving an urgent demand for integrated strategies that simultaneously remove and recover phosphate (PO43−). Herein, we show that rough-surfaced oblate La(OH)CO3 particles capture PO43− with exceptional efficiency, and the spent one can serve as a slow-release P fertilizer, enabling full pollutant-to-resource conversion. The material achieves a maximum adsorption capacity of 211.59 mgP g−1, rapid chemisorption-dominated kinetics, a broad pH window (3–7), and strong selectivity against competing anions and natural organic matters. In fixed-bed column tests, effluent P concentrations stayed below 0.2 mg L−1 discharge threshold for a breakthrough time of 84 h and > 90% P recovery was achieved. When evaluated as a fertilizer in hydroponic cultivation of Pisum sativum, the spent adsorbent produced plant height and biomass that matched or exceeded those from a conventional soluble P source at the optimal dosage. Mechanistic and comparative studies with La(OH)3 and La2(CO3)3 reveal that the superior performance originates from the synergy of electrostatic attraction, surface OH− ligand exchange, interlayer CO32− anion exchange (facilitated by favorable size matching), and inner-sphere complexation, all enabled by the unique layered structure of La(OH)CO3 ([La(OH)]2+ framework layers and interlayer CO32−). This work reports a high-performance La-based adsorbent for efficient P control and establishes a broadly applicable pollutant-to-resource paradigm that bridges environmental remediation with circular nutrient economies. © 2026

Title: Enhanced dissipation and global well-posedness for a three-dimensional flame propagation model with couette flow
Source title: Nonlinear Analysis, Theory, Methods and Applications
Abstract: We study a three-dimensional gravity-induced flame front model under a Couette flow. By exploiting the enhanced dissipation induced by the Couette flow, we prove global-in-time well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in R3 and derive decay estimates for the solution and its spatial derivatives in Lp norms for all p > 1. The analysis is based on a Green’s function approach for the associated variable-coefficient linearized operator. Since an explicit representation of the Green’s function is unavailable, we first establish decay estimates in the spectral domain and then transfer them to physical space. These results show that enhanced dissipation induced by the Couette flow is the key mechanism leading to global existence in the whole space, in the large initial data regime. Copyright © 2026. Title: MOOC Dropout Prediction with Machine Learning Techniques: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) have gained popularity as an accessible form of education, attracting a diverse and widespread student base. Despite their potential, MOOCs face a significant challenge: high dropout rates, which undermine their effectiveness and impact. The increasing interest in addressing this problem led to numerous studies developing new models to predict dropouts early and automatically, many of which use Machine Learning (ML) approaches. This research performs a quantitative synthesis of the performance of ML techniques for early dropout prediction in MOOCs. Following PRISMA guidelines, we perform a systematic review and meta-analysis. To analyze the overall performance, we use a random-effects model for a meta-analysis of proportions, analyzing two metrics: sensitivity and specificity. We have also studied the relationship between some of the studies’ characteristics and the performance obtained by means of subgroup analysis. The results indicate that ML systems are capable of accurately detecting a significant percentage of potential dropouts. However, the performance of these systems varies depending on the dataset and the definition of dropout used in each study. Despite the promising findings, the high heterogeneity observed across studies suggests that these results should be interpreted with caution. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Climate-Informed Nonstationary Multihazard Design Load Characterization for Performance-Based Evaluation of Coastal Structures
Abstract: Current structural design guidelines face increasing challenges from interacting natural hazards in coastal regions. Climate-driven shifts in hazard intensity, frequency, and interaction add further complexity. Traditional multihazard design approaches often neglect hazard nonstationarity or treat hazards independently, resulting in inaccurate structural demands. This paper presents a probabilistic framework for simulating future multihazard scenarios under changing climate conditions. The nonstationary trends in hazard intensities and frequencies are characterized by probability distributions and regression models with time- and climate-informed parameters, respectively. Interhazard dependence is captured using multivariate copulas on the detrended hazard intensities. The framework supports two approaches: historical data-driven (suitable for regions with sufficient observations) and hybrid simulation-based (leveraging physics-based models to supplement limited observations). The framework's application is demonstrated on coastal wind and flood hazards for San Francisco (historical data-driven) and Miami (hybrid simulation-based), producing joint hazard curves (wind speed versus water level at a target return period) under multiple shared socioeconomic pathway scenarios through 2100. The resulting joint hazard curves provide a risk-consistent basis to select wind-flood intensity pairs for adaptive performance-based evaluation of coastal structures under future climate conditions. At the 100-year return period, ASCE 7 wind speeds are lower by about 21% and 17% in 2050 and 2100 for San Francisco, respectively, and by 6% and 9% for Miami, reinforcing the need to assess structural performance over the full joint hazard curve to capture compound loading scenarios and preserve reliability under nonstationary conditions.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Ding S.; Pan X.; Zhou Z.; Deng H.; Tan J.; Sun L.
Title: A probabilistic model for situation awareness reliability assessment in uncertain environments
Abstract: Human error remains a major contributor to accidents in safety-critical systems, partly because operators may fail to establish effective situation awareness (SA) within critical time windows. Existing approaches to situation awareness reliability (SAR) often use SAGAT scores directly as reliability measures, conflating observed single-trial performance with the probability of successful SA formation under repeated conditions. They also lack a unified probabilistic framework integrating individual cognitive ability, task uncertainty, and available time. To address these limitations, this study applies the stress-strength interference principle from reliability engineering and models SA formation as a stochastic competition between cognitive strength and cognitive demand. A closed-form SAR expression with interpretable parameters is derived, forming the SAR-SSI model. The model was evaluated in a controlled experiment involving 29 participants and 1740 trials. Trial-level AUCs were 0.8032 for the full-sample fit and 0.8011 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, indicating similar discrimination for held-out participants within the same experimental paradigm. Higher values of the task-related indicator C and longer available time were associated with higher SAR, whereas greater task uncertainty was associated with lower SAR and attenuated these relationships. The SAR-SSI model provides an interpretable probability-based tool for comparing how alternative information-presentation and task configurations may affect the likelihood of successful SA formation in controlled dynamic tasks. Authors: Xu X.; Yao G.; Fan L.
Author full names: Xu, Xiangyang (56468234400); Yao, Guojian (60782409500); Fan, Linfang (58772912000)
Title: Thermo-mechanical mechanism of asperity-induced micropitting in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts
Abstract: This study develops an asperity-resolving, mechanism-oriented thermo-mechanical framework for investigating micropitting initiation in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts, using differential planetary gears as a representative high-power-density application. The framework sequentially maps transient gear-scale loading and sliding conditions onto a local representative volume element and iteratively couples thermal mixed elastohydrodynamic lubrication with mechanism-based strain-gradient plasticity. Micromorphic regularization is introduced to regularize highly localized plastic deformation under severe asperity contact. For the baseline operating condition, the coupled solution predicts a peak asperity pressure of 1.58 GPa and a localized flash temperature approaching 300 °C. Constitutive decomposition of the converged state indicates a crossover between near-surface thermal softening and subsurface geometrically necessary dislocation-mediated strengthening at approximately 1.62 μm. The associated fatigue-driving field is concentrated within a 0.63–2.30 μm subsurface band and reaches a maximum 34.6% above its surface value. Comparison with published experimental observations provides mechanism-level corroboration of the predicted damage-depth scale and preferential subsurface localization. The framework does not directly predict component-level fatigue life; rather, it provides topography-resolved, temperature- and size-dependent initiation fields that can serve as physically enriched local inputs to future macroscopic fatigue assessments. Explicit crack propagation, progressive material removal, and damage feedback remain outside the present scope. These findings clarify how frictional heat accumulation, high-frequency micro-slip, and strain-gradient strengthening jointly govern the early localization of micropitting damage in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang P.; Yang Z.; Chen R.
Title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. These findings extend sustainable-consumption research by identifying population composition as a social-environmental condition relevant to men's green product evaluations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Gao H.; Wang X.; Liu Z.; Lv Y.; Zhai Y.; Song K.; Zhang X.; Ji W.; Wang Q.
Title: A knowledge graph–enhanced retrieval-augmented framework for automated SysML model generation in MBSE
Abstract: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) has become an important approach for modelling complex systems. However, transforming natural-language requirements into formal Systems Modeling Language (SysML) models remains difficult because of the complexity, multi-domain coupling, and knowledge-intensive nature of system design. To address this problem, this study proposes a knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation (KG-RAG) method for automatic SysML model generation. First, a domain-oriented SysML knowledge graph (KG) is constructed on the basis of the SysML metamodel and domain-specific knowledge. Second, a retrieval-augmented prompting strategy is developed to guide a large language model (LLM) in generating structured SysML artefacts under explicit syntactic and semantic constraints. Third, an automated transformation mechanism is established to convert the generated structured artefacts into tool-native editable SysML models. The proposed method is validated through a fixed-wing aircraft flight control system case study. The results show that the method can automatically generate eight types of SysML diagrams, including requirement, block definition, internal block, use case, activity, state machine, sequence, and parametric diagrams. Quantitatively, the automatically generated models achieve an average element-level model coverage rate of 90.42 ± 1.46%. These results indicate that the proposed method can reduce repetitive manual modelling effort and improve modelling efficiency, demonstrating its potential to support practical MBSE-based system design. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Digitalising waqf for sustainable development growth: Investigating user intentions through technology readiness and ethical commitment
Abstract: The digitalisation of cash waqf represents a promising avenue within Islamic social finance, offering substantial potential to enhance the welfare and socio-economic development of Muslim communities. Through digital platforms, cash waqf can be collected, managed and distributed more efficiently, transparently and widely compared to traditional methods. Despite these advantages, the level of public participation and contributions to digital cash waqf platforms remains significantly below expectations. This gap highlights the need to better understand the factors that influence individuals’ willingness to adopt digital channels for charitable giving. This study aims to explore the determinants that influence individuals’ intentions to contribute to cash waqf via digital platforms by employing the Technology Readiness framework. Specifically, the study examines the roles of optimism, innovativeness, insecurity, discomfort, and moral obligation in shaping users’ behavioural intentions toward online waqf contributions. Data were collected through an online survey involving 211 Muslim respondents in Malaysia who have experience with digital financial services. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that optimism, insecurity, and moral obligation have a positive and significant influence on individuals’ intentions to donate cash waqf through digital platforms. In contrast, discomfort demonstrates a significant negative effect, indicating that feelings of technological anxiety and lack of confidence in using digital systems may discourage adoption. Given the limited empirical research on digital cash waqf, this study contributes valuable insights into the psychological and behavioural factors influencing online donation behaviour. The findings provide practical implications for waqf institutions and policymakers to design strategies that reduce technological barriers while strengthening moral and religious motivations, thereby encouraging wider adoption of digital cash waqf platforms, particularly in developing countries with similar socio-economic environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation model to explain how emotional attachment, shaped by experiential and symbolic brand stimuli, is associated with consumer-based brand equity (CBBE) in the luxury fashion context, and the role of consumers’ social environment, drawing on Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Data were collected from 544 luxury fashion consumers and were analysed using Hayes' PROCESS Model 15. Both brand experience and brand mystery were positively associated with brand attachment. Brand attachment was also positively associated with CBBE and significantly mediated the indirect associations between experiential and symbolic brand resources and CBBE. Furthermore, subjective norm moderately weakens the positive relationship between brand attachment and CBBE, indicating that while subjective norm weakens the relationship between emotional attachment and consumers' evaluations of luxury fashion brands, it does not replace it. This study advances luxury branding research by showing how an identity-based relational mechanism is associated with broader CBBE, with experiential encounters and symbolic meanings relating to brand equity through emotional attachment. By integrating Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour within a unified framework, the study shows that experiential and symbolic brand resources are associated with luxury brand equity through complementary relational pathways. © 2026

Authors: Zhang P.; Bao A.; Lu M.; Xu K.; Li M.; Guo K.
Title: FedVRU: Variational representation decomposition with uncertainty-aware refinement
Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training. However, data heterogeneity across clients degrades the performance of a single global model. Existing Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) methods partially mitigate this issue via client-specific modeling. However, most rely on deterministic point estimation, ignoring the implicit uncertainty within personalized features and leaving the joint representation space vulnerable to local noise. We propose FedVRU, a unified framework for Federated Variational Representation Decomposition with Uncertainty-aware Refinement. Specifically, FedVRU models client-specific representations probabilistically through variational learning to characterize feature uncertainty. An Uncertainty-Aware Gating (UAG) mechanism then adaptively regulates personalized features according to the estimated uncertainty. Concurrently, a Multi-Contrastive Distillation (MCD) objective promotes temporal consistency of global representations and separation between global and personalized representations. Extensive experiments on multiple heterogeneous benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of FedVRU across diverse federated settings without additional communication overhead. Title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was -1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately -6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of -6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects. © 2026 The author(s). Authors: Feng Z.; Niu Y.; Zou H.
Title: Measurement scale for push and pull factors of Chinese pedestrian streets
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The concepts of push and pull theory have been proposed and extensively discussed in various studies, particularly in tourism research. However, push and pull theory in the field of pedestrian street is not addressed in the existing research. This study takes the perspective of pedestrian-street consumers, follows a systematic scale-development procedure, and uses samples from eight Chinese cities to develop and test a scale measuring perceived push and pull factors. The scale is composed of 11 dimensions for each of the push and pull domains. This study then examines the nomological validity by testing the associations between push and pull factors and revisit intention and recommendation intention. The results of the study support the nomological validity of the proposed relationships. This study does not propose push and pull as new constructs. Instead, it organizes and validates their context-specific manifestations within Chinese pedestrian streets and provides a culturally grounded measurement instrument for subsequent retail and consumer research. The evidence supports its initial applicability across the Chinese cities examined, while its cross-national applicability remains to be established. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Meaning in the age of AI: Experiencing less, needing more
Abstract: What does it mean to be human when artificial intelligence (AI) can simulate human thought and creative labor with increasing fidelity? Unlike AI, humans experience meaning in life. Yet AI may create a paradox for meaningfulness. AI may reduce people's ability to experience meaning by disrupting selfhood (loss of effort and self-efficacy), social relationships (reduced mattering and connection), and culture (erosion of value and stability). At the same time, it may heighten people's need for meaning by challenging human exceptionalism and increasing the need for coherence amidst upheaval. This paradox—experiencing less while needing more—is what we term the AI Meaning Gap. Yet meaninglessness is not inevitable. If developed and used intentionally, AI could become a tool for reflection, understanding, and self-growth, thereby enhancing meaning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fu S.; Liu Z.; Niu Z.
Title: Product visual form and customer satisfaction: Multimodal evidence on affective value and functional diagnosis
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Product visual form conveys important aesthetic, quality, and use-related cues for functionally complex products. However, multimodal evidence from real-world retail settings remains limited regarding how product visual form relates to consumer evaluations in online reviews and satisfaction. Using data from 200 smart standing desks, 41951 valid reviews, and 200 product images, this study combined engineering-attribute encoding, CLIP image embeddings, and CLIP-text concept scores to construct a multilayer representation of product visual form. A large language model was used to extract affective and functional evaluations from the reviews, and the platform favorable rate served as a product-level proxy for satisfaction. Product-level path analysis showed that PC3 (Non-standard premium form) was positively associated with affective evaluation, and affective evaluation was positively associated with satisfaction. Together, these coefficients yielded a significant positive indirect association (indirect association = 0.075, 95% BCa CI [0.021, 0.156], FDR-Adj. p = 0.014). Functional evaluation, by contrast, was negatively associated with satisfaction (β = −0.254, p < 0.01). Further decomposition showed that this negative association was more closely related to functional-mention coverage than to overall polarity of functional evaluations. Noise control and Workspace size adequacy were the principal negative sources. These findings indicate that affective and functional evaluations relate to satisfaction in distinct ways. For online retailers and e-commerce platforms, combining analysis of product visual form with online-review monitoring can help identify design value, detect quality risks, and prioritize service recovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Experimental and simulation studies on plasma gasification of medical waste for the co-production of ammonia and urea
Abstract: This study explores the novel integration of plasma gasification and urea synthesis using medical waste as a feedstock, a research area largely unexplored compared to conventional plasma gasification applications. This investigation is designed to evaluate the technical and economic viability of producing hydrogen-rich syngas followed by the synthesis of ammonia and urea via advanced process simulation and experimental validation. Medical waste gasification occurs under a CO2 environment to increase syngas quality when using medical waste such as syringes, gloves, surgical masks, and drip sets. Although, the maximum value of lower heating value (LHV) (12.4  MJ/m3) was achieved by utilizing plasma at 1.25  kW, the highest energy efficiency of 53.8 % was obtained at 1.00 kW due to lower energy input. Residue content decreased from 19 wt% (0.75  kW), 14 wt% (1.0  kW), and 11 wt% (1.25  kW). A sensitivity analysis of the simulation indicates that increasing feed rates and plasma power improve syngas quality: CO reaches a maximum of 69 vol% and H2 rises to 31.1 vol%. Ammonia and urea units show N2 and CO2 conversion efficiencies of 87.6 % and 81.56 %, respectively, with maximum urea production of 2853  kg/h. Techno-economic analysis shows that a CAPEX of $32.9 million and OPEX of $4.49 million/year result in a competitive urea cost of $0.49/kg and annual revenue of $6.7 million. The cost analysis showed that a strong positive cash flow and net earnings in a period of 10 years confirm the long-term economic viability and sustainability of this waste utilization for fertilizer production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Auditing TikTok’s recommendations: Understanding the prevalence of misinformation on the platform
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Short video platforms have rapidly increased in popularity, bringing forth a concerning trend: widespread dissemination of misinformation partially owing to the persuasive nature of the rich media these platforms support. However, little research has systematically investigated the role of algorithmic recommendations in this phenomenon. Our study addresses this gap by auditing the recommendation algorithm of TikTok, the leading short video platform, through four experiments. We explore the prevalence of misinformation in TikTok’s auto-complete suggestions, search results, and For You Page (FYP) recommendations. Our audits yielded a novel dataset comprising 8535 auto-complete suggestions, 1606 search queries, and 2893 videos labelled by stance (promoting misinformation, neutral in nature, or debunking misinformation). Our analysis reveals that TikTok’s algorithm exhibits sensitivity to user behaviours, often in unexpected ways. We find the algorithm recommends substantially more misinformation to newly created accounts lacking search histories, potentially shaping the tone of the content these accounts engage with. We also find that watching and engaging with videos (e.g., liking and favouriting) dynamically influence misinformation prevalent on the platform, potentially reinforcing existing beliefs and contributing to echo-chambers. Further, we emphasise how engaging with misinformation on one topic serves as a gateway, prompting the algorithm to recommend misinformation spanning both related and unrelated topics. Our work stands as the first large-scale, systematic, and empirical assessment of misinformation in TikTok’s recommendations, contributing valuable insights on the dynamics of misinformation dissemination on TikTok and also underscoring the pressing need for responsible auditing practices across digital platforms. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Fu Y.; Meißner M.
Title: Personalizing AI voice agents: How voice agents with similar voices shape trust, self-congruency, and behavior
Abstract: As voice agents become embedded in products as well as service interactions, firms increasingly seek personalization strategies that strengthen consumers' acceptance and engagement. This research examines whether voice agents that sound more similar to users' own voices elicit more favorable behavioral responses. Moreover, we investigate through which psychological mechanisms these effects occur. Across two experiments, we manipulate voice similarity using (1) pretested similar versus dissimilar AI voices and (2) individualized voice cloning that replicates users' voices. Results consistently show that higher voice similarity increases purchase intention, use intention, and willingness to disclose personal information. Mediation analyses indicate that voice similarity operates via two parallel mechanisms: self-congruency and trust. Our research advances research on voice agent-consumer relationships and demonstrates that increasing voice similarity is a robust personalization strategy that enhances consumers’ behavioral responses. © 2026 The Authors

Title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. Drawing on affordance theory and uses and gratifications reasoning, this research examines whether screenshotable ad design increases preservation-oriented engagement by making ads seem useful for later use. The process was stronger when consumers anticipated a future rather than immediate need, such that perceived future utility translated more strongly into ad saving and liking under future-need conditions. Title: Threats to food security in rice farming: A scientific mapping of climate change impacts
Abstract: Climate change is severely disrupting many aspects of human life worldwide, particularly rice farming, as it feeds many people worldwide. In the absence of stable rice production, food security will is threatened for the global population. This paper examines how climate change is related to rice farming and what it means for overall food security. I used bibliometric analysis to examine the literature on this topic from 1998 to 2024, a 26-year period. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database using specific keywords, yielding 549 matching documents. Using VOSviewer helped visualize connections and identify trends in the research. Researchers have consistently focused on climate change, rice farming, and food security over time, but have not yet mapped the interrelationships between these variables. The findings suggest a reciprocal relationship. Agriculture produces greenhouse gases that exacerbate climate change, but climate change subsequently reverses itself and harms agricultural productivity. It is particularly difficult for rice to respond to changing temperatures, unusual rainfall patterns, and recurring extreme weather events. As a result, when crop yields decline, the availability of rice as a staple food decreases, directly impacting food security. These findings directly relate to Sustainable Development Goal 2, which aims to end hunger, making it urgent to find better ways to adapt agriculture to climate change and make it more sustainable. This necessary adaptation in rice farming aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 13, Climate Action. Therefore, this Action requires support from the government and the agricultural sector workforce to achieve food security and sustainable rice farming. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: When plateware shape matters: The congruence effects between food pungency and plateware shape on food preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although considerable attention has been paid to enhancing the visual appeal of food, less is known about how plateware design should align with the sensory characteristics of food. Across four online experiments with Chinese participants, we obtained 754 valid responses covering all seven major geographic regions of China. Title: Allocation of foreign aid in emerging economies: Investment in new vs maintenance of old infrastructure
Abstract: This paper analyzes the growth and welfare effects of allocating public resources — both domestic tax revenues and foreign aid — between investment in new public capital and the maintenance of existing public capital in emerging economies. We show that moderate increases in maintenance enhance growth and welfare by improving capital efficiency and longevity, while excessive maintenance crowds out consumption and productive investment and has adverse effects. Title: Corporate environmental credit rating and social stability: Evidence from capital-labor conflicts in China's polluting industries
Abstract: Mitigating capital-labor conflicts is essential for maintaining social stability. Using China's Enterprise Environmental Credit Evaluation System (EECES) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the impact of corporate environmental credit rating on capital-labor conflicts. The results indicate that EECES reduces capital-labor conflicts in polluting industries by approximately 17.63%, although its effect weakens over time. Channel tests show that EECES mitigates capital-labor conflicts by reducing workers' pollution exposure risk, improving corporate environmental information transparency, and enhancing social trust in corporations. Moreover, in cities with weaker social governance capacity, EECES exerts a stronger restraining effect on capital-labor conflicts, suggesting that it effectively compensates for deficiencies in social governance. Further analysis reveals that although EECES reduces industrial output, it significantly promotes economic transformation. Overall, these findings highlight EECES as an effective policy tool for safeguarding social stability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: A structure and splitting approximation based preconditioning method for solving space-time fractional advection-diffusion equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper focuses on the fast numerical solution of initial-boundary value problems for space-time fractional advection-diffusion equations. The forward difference formula and Grünwald formula are used to discretize the equations, resulting in a structured linear system. To accelerate the convergence of the GMRES method for solving this system, an approximate inverse preconditioner is constructed and applied. The proposed preconditioning method is first based on the splitting approximation of the coefficient matrix. Then the inverse is approximated row by row and the involved Toeplitz matrix is approximated by the τ matrix. Title: Clause-level structural alignment between ASME Section III and Czech NTD A.S.I. Section III: Domain- and component-resolved assessment
Abstract: Comparative studies of nuclear pressure-boundary component design codes have focused mainly on selected provisions and governing equations, but domain- and component-resolved clause-level quantification between ASME Section III and NTD A.S.I. Authors: Pik E.
Title: Degradation of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast integrity: Temporal clustering and anomaly persistence
Abstract: As safety systems like the Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X) increasingly depend on Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B), the structural reliability of these data streams is critical. Traditional monitors assume independent, stochastic failures. This study challenges that assumption by building a global baseline of longitudinal degradation from 229.0 billion state vectors. The framework integrates multiscale permutation testing with day-resolution, exposure-adjusted survival analysis. Significant temporal clustering appears in 98.9% of the high-utilization commercial cohort (≥20 flight-hours/month; N=30,716) and in 67.2% of the sparser remainder under the uniform null; 81.3% of sparse-cohort detections survive a stricter block-preserving null. Clustering peaks at a 3-second characteristic scale, and the mean sustained duration of 28.83 s exceeds the 5-second fault tolerance of decentralized fusion trackers. Across the fleet, 58.4% of aircraft record clustered anomalies on two or more distinct observation days, and 55.5% across two or more calendar months. With follow-up censored at the first >30-day observation gap, 56.0% of aircraft experience a first clustered anomaly, with a median of 9 observed days. A recurrent-event hazard model links recurrence to recent utilization (hazard ratio 1.19 per standard deviation) and, more strongly, to network observability coverage (hazard ratio 1.52). The negative time-to-first exposure coefficient is largely an artifact of onset timing. These results shift integrity monitoring from point-in-time anomaly detection to predictive system health management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Tailoring zeolite-based catalysts for mild, methane-selective VOC combustion in stack emission monitoring systems
Abstract: Accurate methane quantification in industrial emissions is frequently hindered by the presence of non-methane hydrocarbons and volatile organic compounds, which can interfere with conventional analytical methods. Commercial oxidation catalysts can remove these compounds, but their relatively high operating temperatures increase energy consumption and may also promote undesired methane oxidation. Here, we report a catalytic gas-conditioning strategy based on Cu- and Co-containing MFI, BEA, and FAU zeolites for the preferential oxidation of interfering hydrocarbons while preserving methane. Catalysts prepared from cobalt acetate showed superior performance, with activity increasing sharply above ~5 wt% Co. Structural characterization revealed that cobalt is initially present as highly dispersed Co2⁺ species that transform into mixed-valence cobalt oxides during reaction. Although cobalt migration and sintering occur under reaction conditions, the zeolite frameworks remain structurally stable and maintain high CO₂ selectivities (>90%). Compared with the commercial Carulite® catalyst, Co/MFI displayed superior atom efficiency and enhanced ethane-over-methane selectivity, attributed to the confinement of isolated cobalt species within the zeolite pore network. The combination of molecular confinement and highly dispersed metal sites was identified as the key factor governing low-temperature activity and methane selectivity. By integrating heterogeneous catalysis with energy-efficient, solvent-free gas-phase operation and real-time emission monitoring, this approach supports the green chemistry principles of pollution prevention, catalysis, energy efficiency, and real-time analysis. Title: Integrated cognitive processing model of phishing detection: Mood state as moderating factor in the mindful cognition mediated detection process
Abstract: Previous studies have shown that security awareness alone is not consistently associated with phishing detection accuracy, yet the processes through which awareness is associated with detection remain underexplored. Positive mood is negatively associated with detection accuracy, and the estimated beneficial indirect associations involving domain mindfulness and cognitive processing are weaker at higher levels of positive mood. Title: Quantifying the safe operating space of Chinese provinces through a dual-dimension water planetary boundary and trade framework
Abstract: Quantifying human water use relative to planetary boundaries is critical for limiting hydrological degradation. Here, we integrated a dual-dimension framework for blue- and grey-water planetary boundaries with virtual water trade analysis to assess water-related pressures across 30 Chinese provinces from 2002 to 2017. Grey water footprints dominated changes in boundary transgression, reaching a maximum in 2012 and declining by 49% by 2017 following the implementation of stringent national pollution control policies. This massive biophysical relief increased the number of provinces operating within the regional safe space from 10 in 2012 to 17 in 2017. Notably, no province transgressed the blue-water boundary alone, indicating that assessments excluding grey water may overlook the principal source of water-related boundary exceedance. Cumulative stress revealed hidden biophysical risks where aggregate pressure exceeds the regional boundary despite individual components remaining compliant. Highly stressed exporting regions such as Hebei support consumption in wealthier importing regions, including Beijing. The import dependence index and the export contribution index demonstrated that provinces with high export contribution remain in transgression, while provinces with high import dependence improved but rarely entered the absolute safe operating space. Title: Mapping the evolution of communication research in aquatic conservation: A systematic literature review of emerging patterns and research opportunities (2015–2025)
Abstract: This review examines the development of communication research in aquatic conservation through a systematic literature review. Although communication is increasingly recognized as crucial for environmental governance, promoting aquatic conservation remains underexplored and often treated instrumentally. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this review analyzed eleven articles (n = 11) published between 2015 and 2025, drawn from Scopus and Web of Science databases. Findings indicate that existing studies are predominantly presented in the Global North and tend to emphasize media representation, message framing, and individual behavioral change. These patterns suggest that communication is often conceptualized as a tool for disseminating information rather than as a broader social process. Most of the research described is qualitative, further strengthening the exploratory nature of the evidence. This review identifies limited engagement with systemic perspectives in understanding how communication shapes environmental responses. To address this, this study introduces Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory as an analytical lens for reinterpreting communication in aquatic conservation. From this perspective, communication is understood as a process of systemic resonance in which environmental issues are selectively interpreted across different social systems. This study contributes to the field by providing an exploratory synthesis of existing research and highlighting the need for more methodologically robust, geographically diverse, and theoretically grounded studies. Title: ORBIT-FL: Scene-aware and budget-adaptive federated continual learning for multi-UAV environmental monitoring
Abstract: Multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems are increasingly critical for large-scale environmental monitoring, offering agile data acquisition through distributed sensing. However, applying state-of-the-art deep learning to these systems is hindered by the impracticability of centralized data transmission due to privacy concerns and communication limitations. While Federated Learning (FL) presents a promising decentralized alternative, standard FL approaches are inadequate for the unique challenges of real-world UAV deployments. These challenges include highly heterogeneous non-IID data distributions with few-shot labels, the need for continual adaptation to evolving sensing tasks without catastrophic forgetting, and strict, disparate onboard resource constraints. To address these issues in a unified manner, this paper proposes ORBIT-FL, an orbit/scene-aware, retrieval-augmented, and budget-adaptive FL framework. ORBIT-FL departs from single-model convergence, instead maintaining a composable model universe. It tackles non-IID and few-shot scenarios via a scene-conditioned hyper-adapter that generates lightweight, personalized parameters based on privacy-preserving context tokens. To support evolving missions, it introduces a retrieval-augmented federated continual learning mechanism using a time-indexed memory graph of semantic prototypes. Furthermore, ORBIT-FL incorporates budget-conditioned training and anytime inference routing to dynamically adapt to the heterogeneous compute and energy constraints of different UAV platforms. This framework enables robust, privacy-preserving environmental awareness across diverse and dynamic UAV fleets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Factors associated with casualty injury severity in e-scooter crashes: A machine-learning approach with SHAP explainability
Abstract: The rapid adoption of electric scooters (e-scooters) as a micro-mobility mode has been accompanied by rising crash-related injuries, yet the factors associated with severe outcomes remain poorly understood. Because the released dataset is organised at the casualty level, the outcome analysed here is the injury severity of an individual casualty involved in an e-scooter crash, classified as slight versus serious/fatal ; the unit of analysis is the casualty record, not the collision. Using 5166 police-reported casualty records from Great Britain between January 2020 and November 2024, we examine 25 crash-scene, rider, casualty, and environmental features. Five supervised classifiers are compared via randomised hyperparameter search with stratified five-fold cross-validation, with all oversampling confined to the training folds; an integer-encoded SMOTE specification is held fixed as a common reference for comparison rather than as a preferred model. The three gradient-boosted tree models have similar aggregate performance: LightGBM attains a weighted F1 of 0.660 (AUC-ROC 0.624), while paired McNemar tests and bootstrap intervals show that LightGBM, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting each outperform the fitted Logistic Regression baseline; the LightGBM–Random Forest comparison is not robust across the two inferential checks. Cost-sensitive learning raises serious-class recall to 0.536, and a native-categorical CatBoost pipeline raises it to 0.559. Although weighted F1 remains between 0.653 and 0.661 across the four encoding pipelines, minority-class detection and SHAP rankings are encoding-sensitive. SHAP identifies number of vehicles, latitude, casualty sex, time-of-day band, and rider age as the leading predictors in the common reference model, although encoding sensitivity shows that only NumVehicles and DayTime occur in every encoding-specific top five, and the cost-sensitive ranking agrees only moderately with the SMOTE model (ρ=0.6662). Casualties recorded in single-vehicle incident configurations had higher descriptive serious/fatal injury rates than those recorded in two-vehicle configurations (38.6% versus 26.6%), and a refit restricted to the driver/rider-casualty subset used as a proxy for e-scooter riders — in which NumVehicles remains the top predictor with a stronger single-vehicle effect — indicates the pattern persists within that subset rather than arising solely from mixing riders with pedestrians. A fall or head-impact mechanism is plausible but unmeasured: helmet use, fall occurrence, and head impact are absent from the data, and the subset used to test the pattern is defined by a driver/rider role code that proxies for, rather than verifies, e-scooter rider status. Records involving older riders had higher serious/fatal injury rates (28.8% below age 50 versus 42.7% at or above 50), without establishing age 50 as a policy threshold. DayTime band 0 had the highest observed serious/fatal rate, but the four-band rates are not strictly monotonic and their clock-time meanings are undocumented. Discrimination is moderate and the predicted probabilities are poorly calibrated (Brier 0.219 against a 0.208 prevalence baseline), so these results support cautious, locally evaluated hypotheses rather than causal, operational, or universally transferable prescriptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mobile internet connectivity and climate change literacy in Africa
Abstract: Addressing climate change requires individual behavioral shifts and a deep understanding of its impacts, yet the role of information and communication technologies (ICT), a powerful driver of social movements and cultural shifts, in shaping climate change literacy remains underexplored. Title: Trends and directions in military professionalism research: A scopus-based bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The current bibliometric analysis examines the evolution of research related to professionalism in the military based on the Scopus database. Author contributions, country-based production, institutional engagement, and co-occurrence analysis were reported. The biblioshiny in the R language was used to examine the data, and the Garza-Reyes was utilised to ensure the validity and reliability of the data. In this case, a total of 35 relevant publications were selected to be reported in the bibliometric analysis. Based on the finding, the USA is the most contributing country and has a steady increase in the number of publications, which peaked in 2023. However, even though the USA was indicated as the country with the most publications in this research theme, the United Kingdom was found to have the most impactful and influential publication, with a total cited score of 49. In terms of the most contributive affiliation, Uniformed Services University from the USA was dominant and followed by two universities from the Netherlands namely, VU University Medical Centre and the Netherlands Defence Academy. For the most contributive authors, Cole Rebekah and Rudinsky Sherri L were identified as the most productive authors. In this case, the author production over time analysis indicates Cole Rebekah, and Rudinsky Sherri L, are the most productive and influential authors in this research theme. In the thematic map analysis, the concepts of 'human', 'military personnel', and 'humans' emerge as well-developed and central, indicating that discussions around military professionalism are strongly anchored in the human dimension of service members. It was emphasised in the co-occurrence analysis that highlights the centrality of military personnel, humans, and humans, which appear as the most frequent and interconnected terms, indicating that research on military professionalism is predominantly framed around the human dimension and the role of personnel. Finally, the current research reveals three major military professional research directions through Multiple Correspondence Analysis namely, (1) education and social identity, (2) healthcare personnel and military health, and (3) professionalism and ethics, with demographic factors serving as a transversal element across clusters. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: A meta integral reinforcement learning-based cooperative guidance evasion scheme against noncooperative spacecraft
Abstract: The increasing congestion of space orbits has led to a growing number of close-proximity encounters between operational satellites and noncooperative spacecraft. To achieve online autonomous evasion from noncooperative spacecraft, this paper proposes a Meta Integral Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MI-MARL)-based cooperative guidance scheme. Firstly, the multi-agent orbital encounter is formulated as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP), where the interaction among spacecraft is modeled as an orbital pursuit-evasion process under incomplete information. Then, a meta multi-actor-critic architecture incorporating a convolutional recurrent inference network is developed to infer high-dimensional spatiotemporal features directly from stacked angle-only observations of noncooperative spacecraft. The proposed meta-network architecture enhances situational awareness and enables online policy retraining within a Dec-POMDP. Furthermore, by theoretical analysis in the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs framework, we formulate the rational decision-making and Nash equilibrium stability conditions of a perfect Bayes-Nash equilibrium, thereby guaranteeing the convergence and optimality of the MI-MARL. Finally, numerical simulations and computational efficiency evaluations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, superior performance, and real-time onboard feasibility of the proposed method in highly dynamic close-proximity encounter scenarios. © 2026 IAA. Title: Factors affecting public transport adoption in Riyadh- case study
Abstract: Riyadh's greenhouse gas emissions and urban climate risks are likely heightened by accelerated urbanization and profound dependence on private cars. Despite the government's investment in public transportation, societal resistance to giving up private cars and using public transit persists due to cultural and traditional factors. Within the Gulf context, this study is the first to investigate the unique socio-cultural and urban context of Riyadh to understand university students' mobility behavior, identify four factors that significantly are associated with their travel choices, and quantitatively rank the relative influence of these factors. Surveys (n = 710) were used to assess four key factors, analyzed via multiple regression, chi-square, and t-tests. Results indicate that, in descending order of influence, psychological factors (explaining 23% of the variance) have the most significant association with students' willingness to switch to public transport in Riyadh, followed by trip characteristics (13%), urban factors (12%), and socioeconomic and demographic factors (12%). The result suggests that, alongside infrastructure improvements, coordinated strategies are required to change social norms, enhance environmental awareness, and create culturally responsive incentives. The findings support the implementation of place-based policies for sustainable mobility. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Design, dynamic analysis, and optimization of a hybrid nuclear-storage power system for mobile applications
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of heat pipe-cooled reactor (HPR) technology, the integration of mobile nuclear power with energy storage offers a promising solution for energy supply in remote and off-grid scenarios. However, existing research predominantly focuses on stationary systems, lacking comprehensive investigation into the dynamic coupling of HPRs and hybrid storage in mobile environments. To address this gap, this paper proposes a novel hybrid nuclear-storage power system (HNSPS) integrating an HPR with a lithium-ion battery and supercapacitor for mobile applications. A high-fidelity system model is developed in MATLAB/Simulink, incorporating a nuclear power generation system, hybrid energy storage, and control models. A fully active parallel topology is employed for the storage subsystem, utilizing lithium-ion batteries for baseload and supercapacitors for transient power fluctuation mitigation. Simulation results demonstrate robust synergistic operation, characterized by excellent dynamic response and energy management performance. Parameter optimization indicates that the lithium battery rated voltage (determined by series configuration) should balance cycle life and manufacturing cost, while its response time should be extended for high-frequency operation and shortened for high-power-demand scenarios. For the supercapacitor, an initial voltage of 100–200 V and a series number of approximately 200 are recommended to balance transient power capability, safety, and cost. This work validates the feasibility and reliability of the proposed HNSPS for mobile scenarios, providing a theoretical reference for the deployment of mobile nuclear energy applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Hungry for change: Inclusive dining for travelers with dietary restrictions
Abstract: Dining is central to tourism experiences, yet for travelers with dietary restrictions, it can become a source of exclusion rather than enjoyment. Guided by stigma theory, this study examines how dietary restrictions function as a form of concealable stigma in tourism dining contexts. Using a sequential exploratory mixed-methods design, the study combines Critical Incident Technique interviews with 32 individuals and text mining of 3,165 traveler Yelp reviews. Findings reveal that stigma manifests through internal (self-burden, anticipatory anxiety) and external (public, structural, associative) forms producing psychological and behavioral consequences that constrain participation in dining experiences. Individuals employ a range of voluntary and involuntary coping responses to navigate such challenges. Building on these findings, the study proposes a mutual reinforcement model in which internal and external stigma recursively sustain one another across repeated dining encounters, highlighting the anticipatory and cumulative nature of dietary stigma in tourism and offering theoretical and practical insights. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu R.; He X.; Lv L.
Title: Recommend or not? Investigating the effectiveness of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online charitable platforms are important channels through which the public participates in micro-donations, and these platforms have increasingly leveraged algorithmic recommendation technologies to deliver personalized charitable advertisements to potential donors. Nonetheless, whether personalized algorithmic recommendations enhance or undermine consumers’ micro-donation intentions remains unclear. Drawing on moral identity theory, our research addresses this gap through five online scenario-based experiments. The results show that consumers exhibit lower micro-donation intentions when exposed to micro-donation advertisements with personalized algorithmic recommendations, and that this negative effect is driven primarily by perceived identity value threat. Furthermore, we find that the negative effect of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising is attenuated in the presence of legitimization cues or among consumers with low scores on the moral identity scale. Our findings not only extend the literature on the antecedents of micro-donations and the economic consequences of algorithmic personalization in the charitable advertising context, but also offer actionable guidance for charitable platforms seeking to optimize their algorithmic recommendation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Perceptions of biodiversity benefits of regional food: A Q-method study from a German biosphere reserve
Abstract: Increasing consumer demand for food produced using biodiversity-friendly practices may create market incentives that support biodiversity conservation. However, there is limited understanding of consumer perspectives regarding the perceived biodiversity aspects of such products. This study represents an empirical approach to investigate how consumers perceive biodiversity-related attributes of regional products and how these perceptions influence purchase motivation in the context of the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve. Regional product criteria related to biodiversity protection and prevalence within the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve were assessed through a literature review. The Q-method was applied to determine their influence on consumer purchase motivation. Key findings include the determination of three prevalent consumer perspectives consisting of Traditional Regionalists valuing local community support and cultural identity, Environmental Pragmatists appreciating criteria with direct environmental protection benefits and Quality Seekers being motivated by concerns of food safety and transparency in the food industry. The regional product criteria were revisited regarding their importance for the individual consumer perspectives, providing insights into how each group relates to criteria associated with perceived biodiversity benefits. Equal to future research prospects extending on the relevance of demographic and economic variables, these insights suggest potential pathways for adapting and expanding the offering of biodiversity-friendly regional products, in combination with consumer-oriented communication and marketing approaches. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Jia H.; Lin B.
Title: Appliance-level energy assessment and its implications for the environmental impact of household energy conservation: Evidence from urban China
Abstract: Accurate appliance-level energy judgments may help households identify and prioritize meaningful electricity-saving opportunities, with potential implications for the environmental benefits of household conservation. Using survey and experimental data from 2592 residents in Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, this paper assesses how accurately urban households estimate the electricity consumption of 11 common appliances, whether their judgments exhibit patterns consistent with availability-based reasoning, and whether a randomized heat-related information cue improves relative appliance-energy judgments. The results reveal substantial misalignment between perceived and benchmark electricity use: (1) respondents tend to overestimate the energy use of low-energy, frequently used appliances (e.g., televisions) while underestimating high-energy, infrequently interacted devices (e.g., water heaters); (2) appliance use frequency is positively associated with perceived energy consumption, a pattern consistent with greater cognitive accessibility of frequently used appliances; (3) random assignment to the heat-related cue increases perceived energy use for heat-producing appliances and improves respondents' measured relative correspondence with the benchmark; and (4) further analyses show that higher educational attainment is associated with closer benchmark alignment and that closer alignment is associated with lower reported household electricity expenditures. These findings document systematic deviations in appliance-level energy judgments and show that a targeted information cue can improve such judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Wind farm resilience to tornado strikes: A coupled probabilistic damage and system dynamics framework
Abstract: This study develops a coupled probabilistic damage and system dynamics framework for quantifying wind farm resilience to tornado strikes. The loss of resilience, defined as the time-integrated performance deficit, serves as the primary metric, complemented by four shape descriptors (robustness, redundancy, resourcefulness, rapidity) characterizing system performance under disturbance, with and without adaptation measures. Monte Carlo simulations on template wind farms yield mean losses of 62 ± 15 and 116 ± 18 days for EF1 and EF2 tornadoes. The EF1 rapidity distribution is bimodal, reflecting whether large components must be procured, with implications for spare parts inventory decisions. The framework is extended to model suboptimal turbine performance from undetected damage, coupling a stochastic capacity factor with a detection-time model, and to evaluate repowering of collapsed turbines with higher-capacity units. Comprehensive inspections reduce mean recovery time by one week and halve its variability relative to expedited inspections; repowering at a 1.3 capacity ratio reduces L by 7%. A regional-scale application to the Roscoe Wind Farm uses real turbine coordinates and Texas tornado climatology, yielding return periods near 45 and 57 years for EF1 and EF2 strikes and a 100-year resilience loss of 524 turbine ⋅ days. The resulting quantitative resilience value provides an additional decision-making criterion for inspection prioritization, spare parts logistics, and long-term risk management. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: What drives hybrid cultivated meat acceptance? Evidence from a controlled real-product tasting
Abstract: Despite growing interest in cultivated meat, most consumer-related evidence remains based on hypothetical assessments rather than real product exposure, limiting understanding of actual sensory-driven acceptance. To address this gap, the present study investigated consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated chicken product through a controlled affective sensory evaluation with young Singaporean consumers. Participants (n = 82) evaluated overall liking and sensory liking for appearance, smell, taste, texture, and aftertaste, completed Just-About-Right (JAR) diagnostics and were segmented according to Net Promoter Score (NPS) responses. JAR penalty analysis suggested that deviations from optimal sensory intensity systematically affected overall liking, with excessive intensity perceived in taste, smell, and aftertaste generating the largest penalties. Across sensory dimensions, oral attributes exerted a stronger influence on liking than appearance, with taste emerging as the primary driver of acceptance and texture showing a secondary contribution. Multiple regression analysis confirmed taste liking as the strongest predictor of overall liking, whereas the remaining sensory aspects showed weaker or non-significant effects. NPS segmentation further revealed clear differences in recommendation behaviour across detractors, passives, and promoters, closely mirroring hedonic liking patterns and supporting consistency between sensory evaluation and recommendation-oriented behavioural responses. Overall, this study provides an initial empirical benchmark of consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated meat product under controlled conditions, highlighting the central role of taste quality and sensory balance in shaping hedonic responses and consumer satisfaction. The findings offer a reference point for future research as cultivated meat products potentially enter broader markets. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Kang I.; Wei S.
Title: Persuasive triggers and psychological pathways: Unplanned purchase behavior in live-streaming blind box commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Unplanned purchasing is increasingly embedded in digital experiences in which consumers encounter commercial opportunities without a prior intention to shop. This study examines how such opportunities become valued and actionable in live-streaming blind-box commerce. Using survey data from 231 Chinese consumers with experience purchasing blind boxes through livestreams, we test a process model linking scarcity messages, time pressure, economic benefits, and fear of missing out (FOMO) with perceived value, emotional and cognitive self-efficacy, and unplanned purchase behavior (UPB). All four conditions were positively associated with perceived value, which was positively associated with both forms of self-efficacy; emotional and cognitive self-efficacy were, in turn, positively associated with UPB. Streamer persuasiveness strengthened the relationships between all four antecedent conditions and perceived value. The findings show that an unplanned purchase need not arise simply from impulsive responding. Consumers may encounter an unexpected opportunity, judge it to be worthwhile, and feel capable of acting even when the purchase was not previously planned. The study extends research on livestream commerce by explaining how persuasive conditions relate to value appraisal and perceived capability, providing a process-based account of UPB in an uncertain and interactive retail setting. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of combining persuasive communication with clear and transparent presentation of purchase conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Liu J.; An X.; Xu S.
Title: A framework integrating topological potential and semantic embeddings for identifying scientific research clusters in scholarly collaboration networks
Abstract: Multi-team collaboration is essential for addressing major scientific challenges. Previous methods focus predominantly on individuals or single teams, making it difficult to capture the structure of multi-team collaborative innovation systems. To address this, this study conceptualizes a research cluster as a multi-team system formed through inter-team relationships and related research goals within complex collaborative research environments. We further introduce a four-phase Topological Potential–Semantic Embedding Research Cluster Identification (TPSE-RCI) framework to identify scientific research clusters. First, research teams are detected and a team collaboration network is constructed. Second, team feature vectors are generated via topological potential–enhanced Node2Vec and initial clusters are identified with HDBSCAN. Third, team publications are analyzed using BERTopic with BGE-M3 semantic embeddings to derive hierarchical research goals. Fourth, validity criteria are applied to filter scientific research clusters. Using medical informatics publications as a case study, we detected 4262 research teams from 81,557 publications by 269,598 authors. At the structural level, 702 initial scientific research clusters were identified. At the thematic level, 319 topics were extracted from the team publications and consolidated into 21 secondary and 7 primary research goals. By integrating structural and thematic results, we ultimately identified 239 scientific research clusters. Comparative and ablation analyses indicate that incorporating topological potential improves team representation and structural-clustering quality within this empirical setting. The identified research clusters can provide decision support for practical tasks such as organized research management, major project coordination and optimization, domain expert identification, and research resource allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
