Title: Repairing trust in AI: Attribution, anthropomorphism, and the illusion of difference
Abstract: Trust repair between humans and AI systems is an emerging area of inquiry that builds on a well-established literature in human–human (HH) interactions. This review examines how key HH findings, particularly the differential effectiveness of repair strategies following competence versus integrity violations, generalize to human–robot interaction (HRI). While some patterns hold, important divergences exist. The paper argues that better operationalizations of integrity violations and increased anthropomorphism can align HRI findings more closely with HH research. Authors: Cheng Z.; Tu S.; Chen Y.; Deng X.; Zhu C.
Title: How do UAVs govern data sovereignty in decentralized federated sensing networks? Tokenized access control via policy-driven smart contracts
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become pivotal in a wide range of applications due to their high mobility, broad coverage, and multi-sensor integration. Advances in wireless networks have further spurred interest in cross-domain collaboration among UAVs from diverse institutions, platforms, and control domains, giving rise to decentralized federated sensing as an emerging research direction. However, the absence of trusted intermediaries, dynamic network topologies, and heterogeneous data ownership make it challenging to achieve ownership-controllable and fine-grained data protection in such decentralized UAV networks. To tackle these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based decentralized access control framework integrating three novel mechanisms. First, a Hybrid Data Token Model (HDTM) unifies composable, fine-grained data permissions that distinguish fungible (replicable) from non-fungible (data-modifying) rights, and anchors them to data provenance via a cryptographic Data Ownership Signature. Second, an Unspent Fungible Token Outputs (UFTO) mechanism enforces attribute-level transfer constraints and discrepancy detection to govern permission lifecycle with full traceability. Third, a Smart contract-driven Attribute-Based Access Control (ScaBAC) algorithm distributes the ABAC decision pipeline across four modular, independently verifiable smart contracts, coupling access decisions to on-chain token state for auditable, verifiable authorization. An implementation implemented on Hyperledger Fabric achieves a throughput of 128–160 tx/s across the ScaBAC contract suite, a 32% reduction in average latency compared to the PpBAC baseline, and sub-10 ms read-query response. These results demonstrate that fine-grained, decentralized access control is feasible under the resource and topology constraints of UAV federated sensing networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Yin Y.; Zhou J.; Peng K.
Title: Online dating paradox: Why lonely hearts choose to ghost
Abstract: This study examines the differential associations of state and trait loneliness with ghosting behavior in online dating, considering self-presentation strategies and dating fatigue as potential explanatory pathways. Survey data from 881 Chinese mobile dating app users were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that state loneliness was negatively associated with ghosting, whereas trait loneliness was positively associated with ghosting. Dating fatigue was positively associated with ghosting and statistically mediated the associations between both forms of loneliness and ghosting in opposite directions. Acquisitive self-presentation was positively associated with state loneliness and negatively associated with trait loneliness; unexpectedly, it was negatively associated with dating fatigue. Authentic self-presentation was not significantly associated with loneliness or dating fatigue. These findings suggest that temporary and chronic loneliness may correspond to different patterns of engagement and disengagement in online dating. The study contributes to mobile dating research by distinguishing state and trait loneliness and by identifying dating fatigue as an important correlate of ghosting behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Sustainable production and export performance of globe artichoke in Egypt: evidence from 2000 to 2023
Abstract: The globe artichoke is one of the major vegetable crops cultivated in the Mediterranean Basin, with global production reaching nearly 1.6 million tons in 2023. Egypt is among the world’s leading producers, contributing almost one-fifth of global production; however, its export performance remains relatively limited compared with its production potential. This study examines the production dynamics, geographical distribution, and export competitiveness of globe artichoke in Egypt during 2000–2023 within the framework of sustainable agricultural development. Both quantitative and qualitative approaches were used to analyze trends in cultivated areas, productivity, and exports, in addition to major competitiveness indicators in international markets. The results indicate that production growth was driven mainly by horizontal expansion rather than improvements in yield. The cultivated area increased to 50.4 thousand fed in 2023, with an average annual growth rate of about 8%, whereas yield increased only marginally during the study period. Expansion was more pronounced in new lands than in old lands, reflecting the crop’s adaptability to new production areas but also indicating limited progress in productivity efficiency. Despite the increase in production, globe artichoke exports declined by approximately 1.4%, largely due to rising competition from Mediterranean countries, export market concentration, and price fluctuations. Italy, France, and Spain remained the main importers of Egyptian artichokes while simultaneously representing major competitors in international markets. The findings suggest that improving productivity efficiency, promoting value-added products, and diversifying export markets may contribute to strengthening export competitiveness and enhancing the long-term sustainability of globe artichoke production in Egypt. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Yu H.; Yang S.; Wang H.
Title: Quantifying compressibility-induced hydrodynamic deviations from isothermal assumptions in immersed top-blowing reactors
Abstract: Current designs of high-temperature top-blowing reactors predominantly rely on isothermal water models or incompressible simulations. These approaches inherently neglect gas thermal expansion, leading to a systematic underestimation of actual mixing capacity and equipment wear. To explicitly quantify these compressibility-driven effects, a compressible volume of fluid (VOF) model was established for an industrial-scale reactor. By contrasting a high-temperature condition (1473.15 K) against a cold baseline (293.15 K) representing conventional isothermal assumptions, this study isolates the hydrodynamic contribution of thermal expansion. The results are as follows: i) Thermal expansion-driven mechanism: The primary driver of liquid agitation is the rapid thermal expansion and pressure release of the injected gas. The resulting volumetric expansion strengthens gas–liquid momentum transfer, increases the required upstream supply pressure, extends gas residence time, and slows the periodic oscillation of the impinging cavity. ii) Enhanced liquid mixing capacity: Thermal expansion expands the impinging cavity volume to twice that of the cold state. Consequently, the total liquid kinetic energy increases by a factor of 2.31, the net gas–liquid interfacial area expands by 81%, and the dead zone volume fraction sharply decreases from 58.41% to 22.40%. iii) Intensified splashing and scouring: The thermodynamically enhanced mixing inherently triggers more violent interfacial dynamics, yielding a 2.47-fold increase in splash volume. This intensification corresponds to a fourfold escalation in reactor wall shear forces and a 62.2% rise in lance shear force. This study explicitly quantifies the physical deviations embedded in traditional isothermal models. These findings provide a quantitative reference for correcting isothermal modeling assumptions in the design and wear-risk assessment of high-temperature gas–liquid reactors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Does low-carbon policy improve the environmental performance in China?
Abstract: This study examines the impacts and driving mechanisms of low-carbon policy on environmental performance, with a focus on both direct policy effects and the underlying structural drivers. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions and years, the analysis employs a combination of econometric modeling and configurational approaches to capture heterogeneous and non-linear relationships. The results indicate that low-carbon policy significantly improves environmental performance, particularly in terms of emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and pollution control. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary across regions depending on differences in economic development, industrial structure, and governance capacity. Further analysis reveals that technological innovation, green investment, regulatory intensity, and public participation are key driving factors that jointly shape policy effectiveness. The study also identifies multiple pathways through which these factors interact to enhance environmental outcomes, highlighting the importance of synergistic policy design. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how low-carbon goals translate into measurable environmental improvements and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to optimize policy implementation in diverse socio-economic contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
Abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. The paper reflects on epistemic justice in energy- and ocean governance, and asks whether and how United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) facilitates that such justice is sought in the regulatory process of deep sea mining by focusing on procedural rules for the International Seabed Authority (ISA) and the representation of different knowers in the decision-making process, including its Council's structure, authority, and composition. It concludes that a very small number of individuals has the power to bring about a very large change in deep sea mining regulations, currently without legal requirements to include experiential, traditional or other forms of knowledges beyond the scientific method in the decision-making process. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Blockchain-powered traceability systems in high value agri-food supply chains: a systematic literature review featuring insights from the olive oil sector

Title: Estimating the direct impact of mega sport events on domestic tourism demand: A micro-level approach using Paris 2024
Abstract: Research on mega sport events and tourism demand has largely overlooked domestic tourism and relied on aggregated data that mask individual behavioural adjustments. Using Paris 2024 as a case study, we propose a methodology to estimate the direct impact of mega sport events on domestic tourism at the individual level. A retrospective paired-sample survey is used to construct a two-period panel dataset (2023–2024). Individuals are classified as positively affected, negatively affected, or unaffected using self-reported motivations validated by counterfactual behaviour absent the event to mitigate ex-post rationalisation bias. Tourism demand remains unchanged based on the full sample due to offsetting behavioural responses: travel versus stay-at-home attraction among positively affected, and substitution versus crowding-out among negatively affected. However, focusing on actual travellers, affected individuals exhibit a larger increase in overnight stays than unaffected residents, without increasing visit frequency. Micro-level approaches are critical to capture how mega events reshape tourism demand. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xu J.; Xu H.; Ma G.
Title: Political career incentives and the environmental costs: Evidence from China's promotion tournaments
Abstract: This paper shows that promotion incentives for county-level cadres in China are an important driver of air pollution deterioration. Building on the multi-winner tournament model proposed by Clark and Riis (1998), we predict an inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties within a prefecture and the promotion incentives for county-level cadres. Using the length of small rivers as an instrumental variable for the number of counties within a prefecture, our empirical analysis identifies a robust inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties and air pollution levels, suggesting that promotion incentives significantly exacerbate air pollution. Further analysis reveals that, in pursuit of economic growth, local cadres tend to relax environmental regulations and attract more pollution-intensive firms. In regions where cadres’ performance evaluation places less emphasis on economic growth, the inverted-U-shaped relationship does not exist. These findings suggest that local cadres’ career incentives stimulate economic growth at the expense of the environment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Evaluation of Prompt Engineering for LLM-Based Construction Contract Risk Analysis
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasing potential for complex analytical tasks; however, their reliability in high-stakes domains such as construction contract interpretation remains insufficiently understood. This study presents a controlled, human-in-the-loop evaluation of how prompt-engineering strategies influence the quality and perceived reliability of LLM-generated risk analyses for New Engineering Contract (NEC4)-style clauses. Generative pretrained transformer GPT-4.1 was applied in a deterministic configuration to identify contractor risks across six synthetic NEC4-style Z-clauses using five prompt strategies: baseline, direct, role based, chain of thought, and guided prompting. Thirty outputs were evaluated under a blinded protocol against expert-derived reference risk lists by a mixed-expertise cohort, supporting exploratory comparison. Assessment combined descriptive quantitative analysis of Likert-scale ratings of accuracy, completeness, clarity, legal salience, and hallucination risk with qualitative thematic analysis. Results indicate that guided, clause-anchored prompting produced more structured, legally grounded, and traceable outputs, whereas less constrained strategies exhibited narrative drift and weaker clause linkage. These findings suggest that structured prompting may support more consistent clause-level interpretation under controlled conditions, although conclusions remain bounded by the exploratory design, limited sample, and synthetic dataset. The study contributes to understanding how prompt design shapes interpretability and verifiability in contract analysis. The clause-guided human-in-the-loop (CG-HITL) framework is presented as a conceptual approach to support structured use of LLMs in preaward contract risk assessment.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
Abstract: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin. Applying two-way fixed effects, seemingly unrelated regression, and ordinary least squares models, the study finds that exposure to extreme heat is heterogeneously associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. Specifically, non-agricultural clients show suggestive evidence of the accumulation of precautionary savings after extreme heat days in the preceding quarter, while extreme heat days are negatively associated with agricultural clients’ savings. Microfinance clients increase their withdrawals when exposed to extreme heat within the preceding quarter, but the association is not robust for agricultural clients’ withdrawals in response to an increase in annual extreme heat days. Addressing the heterogeneous financial responses across different clients to extreme heat consequently requires explicit policy attention. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the associations between extreme heat and individual economic outcomes, how financial behavior relates to weather risk, and how microfinance clients respond to shocks. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: From tourism pressure to overtourism vulnerability regimes: A municipal impact assessment framework for sustainable destination governance
Abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. First, a regional tourism-pressure screening index is constructed for Euro-Mediterranean NUTS-2 regions to identify broader high-pressure contexts. Second, an Overtourism Vulnerability Index (OVI) is implemented for the main tourism hotspots in Apulia, Italy, using eight normalized indicators capturing direct tourism pressure, air accessibility, accommodation platformisation, economic dependence and heritage attractiveness. Rather than treating the OVI as a ranking device, the framework decomposes vulnerability into three diagnostic dimensions: direct pressure, structural fragility and gateway/heritage amplification. These dimensions identify four regimes: critical overload and fragility, gateway/heritage pressure, coastal fragility and platformisation, and monitor-and-prevent contexts. Robustness checks and an external waste-based plausibility check support the diagnostic interpretation. The resulting toolbox links each regime to assessment, monitoring and candidate intervention priorities, helping planners move from regional pressure screening to municipal scoping and targeted environmental and carrying-capacity assessment. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Han X.; Li S.; Liu H.; Zhang M.
Title: When GAI backfires: Understanding the process mechanism of consumers’ avoidance of generative AI conversational recommendation agents from a misaligned affordance perspective
Abstract: Generative AI-enhanced conversational recommendation agents (GCRAs) are being widely deployed on e-commerce platforms; however, consumers increasingly avoid these advanced recommendation tools. Prior research has not systematically identified which specific features of GCRAs drive such avoidance, nor has it clearly articulated the underlying process mechanisms through which avoidance emerges. To address these gaps, this study draws on affordance actualization theory and misaligned affordance theory to systematically investigate consumers’ perceived GCRA misaligned affordances and to model the complete pathways from these misaligned affordances to consumer avoidance behaviors. We employed a sequential mixed-methods approach. First, a qualitative interview research (N = 19) combined with a simple experiment identified three key GCRA misaligned affordances: limited choices, iterative dialogue, and hallucinated information. Second, a quantitative research (N = 538) validated that these misaligned affordances trigger cost-based comparative appraisals (opportunity and transaction costs), which in turn lead to negative experiences (both outcome-related and process-related), ultimately driving consumer avoidance. Finally, by integrating the findings across studies, we developed a comprehensive framework explaining consumers’ avoidance of GCRAs. Theoretically, this research advances the misaligned affordance actualization theory by highlighting the novel comparative appraisal stage, moving the theory from qualitative conceptualization to process-level mechanisms. Collectively, these findings provide new theoretical insights and practical guidance for improving the design and deployment of GCRAs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Divergent relationships between moral disengagement and cyberbullying bystander response behaviors: Examining the amplifying roles of humor and anonymity
Abstract: While bystander response behaviors are pivotal for cyberbullying (CB) intervention, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding their correlates, partly because it has often treated diverse bystander responses as a monolithic construct and failed to distinguish constructive defense from aggressive defense. Furthermore, few empirical studies have examined how digital affordances interact with individual factors in relation to diverse bystander responses within a Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) framework. To address these gaps, this study examined the main and interactive associations of individual moral disengagement (MD), perceived anonymity, and humor of CB with four distinct online bystander responses (constructive defense, aggressive defense, inaction, and reinforcement). A final analytic sample of 1201 Chinese secondary school students, selected via multi-stage random sampling, completed a survey assessing MD, CB contexts, and real online bystander responses. Multilevel analysis indicated that MD, perceived anonymity and humor were consistently and negatively associated with constructive defense but positively associated with inaction. Conversely, MD and anonymity were positively associated with aggressive defense, whereas humor showed no significant link. Regarding reinforcement behaviors, perceived anonymity and humor were positive predictors, whereas MD exerted a non-significant association. Moderation analyses revealed that anonymity strengthened MD's positive associations with inaction and reinforcement, whereas humor amplified MD's association solely with reinforcement. These findings underscore the necessity of distinguishing constructive from aggressive defense and integrating individual moral cognition with contextual cues for both exploring correlates of online bystander response and designing CB interventions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Effects of AI-based chatbot coaching on goal attainment, self-efficacy, and stress: A longitudinal randomized experiment
Abstract: Students in higher education face a range of academic challenges, which leads to high levels of stress among many students. While coaching has been shown to help students address these challenges, it is resource-intensive and therefore not broadly accessible. AI-based chatbots may help broaden access by providing interactive and personalized guidance at scale, yet empirical evidence on their effectiveness remains limited, particularly from longitudinal experimental studies. Addressing this gap, we conducted a longitudinal between-subjects experiment with four measurement points across an academic semester, randomly assigning 101 students to one of three conditions: AI-based chatbot coaching, literature-based self-study (active control), or a waitlist control condition. Students in the chatbot coaching and literature study conditions engaged in repeated interactions with the intervention, averaging approximately 100 min of cumulative interaction time accumulated across four sessions of 23–28 min each. We examined how students’ goal attainment, university-related self-efficacy, and stress developed over the course of the study. Results showed that students in the AI-based chatbot condition achieved significantly stronger increases in goal attainment over time compared to students in both control conditions. Self-efficacy also increased in the AI-based chatbot condition over time; however, between-condition differences were not consistent across time points, suggesting that the intervention had a more limited impact on self-efficacy relative to goal attainment. Furthermore, no significant effects were found for university-related stress. The findings suggest that AI-based chatbot coaching can effectively support students in achieving university-related goals and strengthening their self-efficacy, while its impact on stress reduction may be limited. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Enhancing situational awareness in health systems: A scoping review of technologies and cross-industry insights
Abstract: Background: Situational awareness technologies are increasingly utilised in healthcare systems to facilitate timely and coordinated decision-making. Reported implementation considerations include data quality, governance, and integration into everyday workflows. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map technologies, systems, and methods used to enhance situational awareness in health service delivery and to identify approaches used in other industries that could be adapted for healthcare, particularly in regional and remote settings. Methods: We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance for scoping reviews. Electronic databases (PubMed and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between January 2000 and October 2025. Reference lists and citation searches in Google Scholar were also examined. Records meeting the inclusion criteria were screened and reviewed, with key data extracted using a structured charting form and synthesised into seven application domains. Results: Searches identified 744 records, of which 23 studies were included. These covered diverse technologies such as dashboards, forecasting models, alert systems, and geospatial decision environments. Most studies were from high-income countries (n = 19). Studies reported potential benefits for visibility, coordination, and decision-making. However, most evidence was descriptive, with limited evidence of whether these systems improve service delivery. Recurrent implementation challenges included data fragmentation, limited interoperability, and misalignment between governance and workflow. Conclusions: This review highlights the need for more rigorous and context-sensitive evaluations of technologies used to enhance situational awareness in healthcare, especially in regional and resource-limited settings. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Title: Reliability evaluation of multi-state logistics networks with weibull-based capacities under time-dependent spoilage
Abstract: This paper investigates the reliability evaluation for a multi-state logistics network with time-dependent spoilage (MLN-TDS). In the MLN-TDS, arc capacities represent the number of available logistics vehicles, whose time-dependent availability is characterized by a Weibull distribution. Unlike conventional models that assume a constant spoilage rate, this paper evaluates the time-dependent spoilage (TDS) rate of each minimal path according to its delivery time. To account for the resulting discrepancy between dispatched and delivered quantities, intact flow vectors are constructed to determine the required dispatched quantities before deriving the corresponding capacity vectors. The MLN-TDS reliability is defined as the probability that demand can be fulfilled while simultaneously satisfying both loss cost and time constraints. Based on minimal paths and minimal capacity vectors, an algorithm is proposed to evaluate the MLN-TDS reliability, and the recursive sum of disjoint products method is used to compute its value. An illustrative example and a real-world fruit delivery case study are provided to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed evaluation procedure. The results identify critical demand thresholds and show how changes in TDS rates affect MLN-TDS reliability under high-demand conditions. These findings provide quantitative support for reliability-oriented logistics planning and operational decision making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Pyrolysis of biomass feedstocks for hydrogen-enriched syngas production: Cold gas efficiency modelling, latin hypercube uncertainty analysis, and parametric stress analysis
Abstract: Biomass-derived syngas offers a viable pathway for producing renewable, hydrogen-rich fuel gas. However, its conversion performance is influenced by feedstock type, temperature, feed rate, and moisture content. This study develops a Cold Gas Efficiency (CGE) model for four agricultural feedstocks: wheat, barley, oilseed rape, and beans. Results show that CGE is highly sensitive to temperature, with low-temperature stress (0–5th percentile) reducing mean CGE by up to 22%. High-moisture stress (95–100th percentile) produced an even larger decline, lowering mean CGE from ∼44% to ∼35% for wheat and compressing the distribution into a low-performance regime. Regression-based tornado charts indicate that temperature is the strongest linear driver (coefficient = +0.44), while Spearman rank correlations highlight feed rate as the most monotonic negative driver (−0.41). Feedstock probability density functions (PDFs) show that wheat as the most efficient and least variable performer, while Oilseed Rape (OSR) and beans exhibited broader distributions due to higher ash-related inhibition of char reactivity. The thermochemical and statistical results demonstrate that operational uncertainty, such as temperature and moisture, dominates CGE variability. Title: Grain refinement mechanism of ultrasonic application stage in wire arc additive manufacturing of alloy steel
Abstract: Ultrasound-assisted wire arc additive manufacturing (UA-WAAM) offers a promising route to refine the coarse columnar grains found in as-deposited components. However, the effects of ultrasound applied at different stages during the rapid solidification of the molten pool remain insufficiently understood, and the grain refinement mechanism requires clarification. A novel stage–specific ultrasonic application strategy was designed based on the phase transformation temperatures and thermal history of molten pool. Five discrete ultrasound intervention stages were investigated, before arc extinction, at arc extinction, during solidification, after solidification and continuous application. Microstructural evolution was characterized using optical microscopy and EBSD, while the cavitation dynamics and mechanical response of columnar grains were theoretically modeled to establish a quantitative fragmentation criterion. Results reveal that effective grain refinement occurs exclusively when ultrasound is applied during cooling and solidification stage, transforming coarse columnar grains into fine equiaxed and refined columnar grains. Ultrasound applied before arc extinction or after complete solidification produces negligible microstructural modification due to the absence of surviving nuclei or a liquid medium. Theoretical analysis reveals cavitation-induced grain fragmentation as a key mechanism, with predicted critical fragmentation lengths (15.3–25.8 μm) aligning quantitatively with the measured mean grain size (20.9 ± 3.7 μm). Acoustic streaming plays a supporting role by dispersing fragments as heterogeneous nucleation sites. The critical window for effective ultrasonic application is limited to the sub‑second interval from arc extinction to complete solidification. These findings establish a quantitative relationship between cavitation shock wave pressure and grain fragmentation behavior, providing a scientific foundation for optimizing energy-efficient ultrasonic strategies in WAAM. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Conflict expression: A decade of group conflict research

Title: Performative narratives and destination image in cross-cultural tourism livestreaming
Abstract: Tourism livestreaming allows global audiences to encounter destinations in real time, yet how livestreamers’ expressive behaviors shape audiences’ destination evaluations across cultures remains unclear. Drawing on a performative perspective, this research conceptualizes expressed destination image formation as a temporally situated process generated through live narrative enactment. Title: Encountering the “familiar stranger”: Activating latent cultural identification among Vietnamese tourists in China
Abstract: Tourism studies have largely examined cultural identification through encounters with difference, while paying less attention to culturally proximate travel contexts. Title: Modeling Japanese consumers' acceptance and rejection of tech-enhanced foods
Abstract: To maintain the well-being of the global population, strengthening the food supply system is necessary. Title: Activating competing goals: The dual effect of environmental fee

Title: Barriers and enablers to circular economy implementation in 3D concrete printing: A fuzzy decision-making approach
Abstract: The circular economy (CE) is increasingly emphasised in 3D concrete printing (3DCP), yet evidence remains limited on the key barriers to its implementation and the enablers needed to support practical uptake. Regulatory and standardisation issues emerged as the most critical barrier theme, followed by financial and market constraints, while the gap between low-TRL academic research and high-TRL industrial implementation was identified as the most prominent item-level barrier. Title: Emotional interaction and conversion value in live streaming E-commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Multi-agent emotional interaction constitutes a core characteristic of live streaming e-commerce. Title: Mobile internet connectivity and household wealth in the Philippines
Abstract: Mobile internet has become a fundamental modern infrastructure. We consider how access influences household wealth in the Philippines using a granular measure of local connectivity based on geocoded cell towers and identify causal impact through an instrument based on proximity to submarine cable landing points. We investigate potential mechanisms and find that improved connectivity stimulates activity in key economic sectors, improves educational outcomes, and increases female labor force participation, primarily in occasional work. Authors: Wang L.; Li S.
Title: The temporal shift in consumer hue preferences in hotel booking
Abstract: Despite the hospitality industry's ongoing pursuit of optimal color marketing strategies, it remains unclear whether consumers respond more favorably to cool or warm hues. This research investigates how consumers' hue preferences in digital marketing imagery shift as a function of time of day. Through a case coding analysis (n = 4510), an eye-tracking experiment (n = 105), three online experiments (n = 981), and a quasi-experimental field survey with real tourists (n = 316), this research reveals temporal shifts in hue preference in hotel booking contexts, such that consumers prefer hotel room photos with cool hues in the morning and warm hues in the evening. These preferences are mediated by the need for uniqueness and the need for belonging, respectively. Furthermore, the effect is moderated by visual temporal cues (window view) and individual circadian rhythms (chronotype). Authors: Wu Z.; Zhang D.; Li Y.
Title: Respect your privacy: An identifiable and authorized privacy-preserving data retrieval protocol through decentralized identifier
Abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires personal data processing to satisfy both the principles of lawfulness and data minimization. However, existing privacy-preserving data retrieval protocols rarely meet both principles, especially at the batch scale. To solve these problems, we present IAPDR, an Identifiable and Authorized Privacy-Preserving Data Retrieval protocol that builds on Decentralised Identifier (DID) that focuses on data-subject privacy under GDPR compliance. It uses non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKs) for anonymous authorization. The data controller can verify the lawfulness of each retrieval request without learning any personally identifiable data, thereby upholding data minimization. For scalable retrieval, IAPDR employs Private Set Intersection with Payload (PSI-Payload) to execute large-batch matching while keeping both identifiers and associated records confidential. We prove anonymity and unforgeability, and give a Universal Composability (UC) security analysis in the semi-honest model. Under the same dataset sizes and network settings on public benchmarks, IAPDR achieves an average 1.36 × improvement in computational efficiency and an average 3.62 × reduction in total communication compared with state-of-the-art schemes. Title: Automotive warranty intelligence through evidence-grounded graph retrieval and agentic reasoning
Abstract: Automotive warranty records contain detailed evidence on field failures, repeated repairs, and repair actions, but heterogeneous fields and fragmented vehicle–part–fault relations make reliability-oriented synthesis difficult. Title: Is state fragility a hindrance to trade openness in Africa?
Abstract: This paper analyses the effects of state fragility on trade openness in Africa, using panel data for 50 African countries over the period 1995–2018. Title: From perceived attractiveness to visitation: Multi-scale measurement and influencing factors across 143 Chinese historic cities
Abstract: Effective tourism management requires understanding how attraction attributes and supporting factors shape tourists’ perceived attractiveness, and how these in turn translate into visitation. Results show that (1) perceived attractiveness and visitation share a multi-core spatial structure, while visitation displays a polarized long-tail distribution; (2) attraction attributes, especially official designation, visual quality, and ticket pricing, dominate both metrics but shape them differently; (3) positively perceived social, economic, scientific, historic and aesthetical values increase visitation, whereas political value is negatively associated; and (4) accessibility and spatial agglomeration also contribute positively. Title: The generalization and diversity of global urban regularities
Abstract: The simple but appealing regularities have been observed in the complex urban systems, yet their applicability to contemporary global urbanization remains controversial. Here we conducted a global synthesis of urban regularities, including Zipf's law, Gibrat's law, and scaling law, through multiple urbanity dimensions across 9,014 consistently defined urban areas from 1985 to 2020. We found that general urban regularities governed global urban evolution, as evidenced by the enduring power distributions and common spatial scaling relationships, but with localized diversity reflecting urban development. Globally, Zipfian α moved toward 1, declining from 1.12 to 1.00 for urban area, increasing from 0.91 to 0.97 for population, and declining from 1.34 to 1.17 for GDP during the past decades. These changes were associated with the persistent deviations from Gibrat's law, linking size-dependent growth to the evolution of urban size distributions. Urban rank changes illustrated urban economic transformations and spatial realignments, particularly in Asia and Africa. Population scaled sublinearly with urban area, whereas GDP, nighttime light intensity, and CO2 emissions scaled superlinearly, revealing paradoxes in urban prosperity and environmental impact and prompting a reconsideration of sustainability paradigms, especially in less-developed regions. Title: When does AI design help or hurt? Brand positioning and the dual effects of homogeneity and trend relevance in fashion retailing

Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in fashion design to generate product aesthetics and forecast trends. Authors: Pang B.; Huang L.; Feng X.; Wei W.
Title: COLF: Disentangled forecasting for non-stationary time series via contrastive learning
Abstract: Non-stationary time series are widely prevalent in real world, characterized by changing temporal patterns, which greatly challenges the out-of-distribution generalization ability of forecasting approaches. Most existing approaches seek to achieve sequence stationarization through normalization methods, whose effectiveness is still limited since non-stationarity is not simply reflected in shift in mean and variance. Given this, we consider addressing non-stationarity from another perspective by pattern disentanglement, i.e., to distinguish between stable and unstable patterns according to temporal persistence and utilize them separately for forecasting. Considering the lack of supervised signals for disentanglement as temporal persistence is challenging to measure explicitly, we achieve this in a self-supervised manner and propose a model COLF. Specifically, COLF is designed with two contrastive learning mechanisms at different levels: the across-sample contrastive learning to disentangle stable and unstable patterns at sequence level, and the within-sample contrastive learning to further extract persistent components from unstable patterns under the local smoothness assumption at subsequence level. The final forecasted result is obtained by integrating the predictions derived from both stable patterns and the persistent components within unstable patterns. COLF is evaluated on six real-world datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that COLF achieves overall superior performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches across different forecasting horizons and evaluation metrics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Who eats matters: How eating-agent identity in short-form retail videos influences consumers’ purchase intentions

Abstract: Short-form retail videos frequently depict food consumption, yet little is known about whether the identity of the visible eater shapes how consumers evaluate the product. Study 2 demonstrates the sequential pathway through perceived naturalness and perceived healthiness. Title: BenchPDM: Benchmarking pattern detection methods in microservice-based systems using automatically generated pattern-assisted testbeds
Abstract: Microservices architecture (MSA) is an increasingly popular trend in software architecture design. While the use of microservices offers numerous benefits, such as enhanced flexibility and scalability, it also introduces specific challenges and complexities. To address these challenges, various design patterns have been applied in system implementations, each aimed at resolving specific issues within microservices-based systems (MBS). Understanding the design patterns employed in a large software system can significantly enhance comprehension of the system’s functionality. However, organizations often lack strong documentation regarding the types of patterns used, the number of patterns, and their locations within the system. To date, various pattern detection methods (PDMs) have been developed with the goal of identifying design patterns within software systems. The effectiveness of these PDMs may vary depending on factors such as the scale of the software system, the types of patterns used, and etc. Therefore, the selection of an appropriate PDM is highly dependent on the specific software system being targeted. Consequently, there is a critical need for a tool that can evaluate and compare PDMs from various perspectives. Although several benchmarks have been proposed for MBSs, none have focused on assessing PDM. In this article, we present a benchmark named BenchPDM aimed at benchmarking PDMs in MBS using automatically generated pattern-assisted test beds. To achieve this, BenchPDM includes two fundamental modules. In the PBMC module, pattern-assisted microservices-based systems (PAMBS) are generated with varying degrees of complexity to simulate real-world MBSs of small, medium, and large scales. The PDM-ES module then evaluates and compares the performance of PDMs using the generated PAMBS from different factors. To assess the performance of BenchPDM, we conducted experiments on five PDM methods, two of which are among the most popular and commonly adopted approaches, SVM-based and graph-based methods. The experimental results demonstrated that BenchPDM can effectively evaluate and compare PDMs across various factors. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: WISE: An interpretable word intensity framework for emotion-aware conversational systems
Abstract: Emotion-aware conversational systems are increasingly adopted in healthcare, yet most emotion detection approaches rely on sentiment polarity, which fails to capture emotional nuance and intensity in short, informal chat messages. To overcome these limitations, this study develops an interpretable emotion-aware framework called Word Intensity Scoring Engine (WISE) that explicitly models emotional intensity in short-form conversational text. Grounded in Plutchik's Wheel of Emotions, WISE integrates lexicon-based emotion labeling, synonym expansion, semantic similarity using word embeddings, and negation-aware feature extraction to calculate intensity-weighted emotion scores at the word level. The WISE framework is evaluated through experimental benchmarking and an expert review involving practicing healthcare professionals. Results show that WISE enhances the performance of ML and LLM-based classifiers. Further, expert evaluations indicate that WISE-derived responses are perceived as professional, contextually appropriate, and empathetic. This study contributes a transparent, theoretically grounded design artifact that advances affective computing research and informs the deployment of emotion-aware conversational agents in healthcare. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Knowledge graph–based data governance for small and medium-sized enterprises: A systematic literature review and socio-technical framework
Abstract: Established data governance frameworks provide valuable guidance for large enterprises, yet their assumptions about stable funding, dedicated governance teams, and mature infrastructure often do not reflect the realities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Recent research has explored the use of semantic technologies and knowledge graphs to automate governance tasks, improve traceability, and support policy enforcement. Yet, whether these approaches effectively address SME-specific needs remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic literature review of knowledge-graph-based data governance approaches, focusing on their relevance to SMEs. Following the PRISMA method, we analyzed evidence from 43 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 through multiple lenses, including core data governance activities (Define, Implement, Monitor), components of the Data Governance Institute framework, and stages of the data lifecycle. Using thematic network analysis we synthesize recurring limitations and structural patterns across the literature. Our findings show that while semantic technologies demonstrate strong potential for automating policy enforcement, metadata integration, and interoperability, most approaches are designed for mature enterprises. They commonly assume formal governance hierarchies, specialized expertise, and sustained operational capacity, conditions that are often absent in SMEs. As a result, governance designs are skewed toward technical controls and early lifecycle stages, with limited attention to monitoring, organizational roles, decision rights, and end-to-end governance. Building on these findings, this study advances a socio-technical perspective on data governance in SME contexts by reframing governance as a lifecycle-embedded and practice-oriented capability rather than a purely technical implementation. It further conceptualizes knowledge graphs as boundary objects that mediate between governance intent, technical enforcement, and organizational practice. Our key contributions include a structured synthesis of knowledge-graph-based data governance research, identifies eight recurring gaps that hinder SME applicability, and derives nine design principles alongside a conceptual research framework to guide future research and the development of SME-suitable governance solutions. © 2026

Title: Fuel vs. food? Climate shocks, biofuel expansion, and the future of global food security
Abstract: The expansion of biofuel production has generated debate over its potential trade-off with food security, particularly regarding land diversion, rising food prices, and climate-related agricultural stress. This study utilizes panel data from 5 emerging (BRICS) and 7 advanced economies (G7) employing Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for robustness to examine the association between biofuel production and agricultural total-factor productivity, crop value, and global food security during the period 2012-2022. Grounded in bioeconomy transition theory, induced innovation theory, the Porter hypothesis, and sustainable intensification, the empirical evidence indicates that biofuel expansion does not create a homogeneous food–fuel trade-off; instead, its associations vary across development and performance regimes. Biofuel production is positively associated with crop value in both groups but shows contrasting productivity associations, particularly across quantiles. Temperature anomalies exhibit heterogeneous associations with agricultural outcomes, while food prices are more strongly associated with food security. In line with induced innovation theory, innovation capacity is positively associated with several agricultural outcomes, while the climate–innovation interaction indicates heterogeneous adaptive associations across country groups. The differing associations of environmental policy stringency are broadly consistent with the conditional predictions of the Porter hypothesis, rather than indicating uniform regulatory benefits. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between biofuel expansion and food-system performance is conditional on development stage, climate exposure, innovation capacity, environmental policy stringency, and food-price conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Convergence of Implicit Gradient Descent for Training Two-Layer Physics-Informed Neural Networks
Source title: East Asian Journal on Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The optimization algorithms are crucial in training physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), as unsuitable methods may lead to poor solutions. Compared to the common gradient descent (GD) algorithm, implicit gradient descent (IGD) outperforms it in handling certain multi-scale problems. In this paper, we provide convergence analysis for the IGD in training over-parameterized two-layer PINNs. We first derive the training dynamics of IGD in training two-layer PINNs. Then, over-parameterization allows us to prove that the randomly initialized IGD converges to a globally optimal solution at a linear convergence rate. Moreover, due to the distinct training dynamics of IGD compared to GD, the learning rate can be selected independently of the sample size and the least eigenvalue of the Gram matrix. Additionally, the novel approach used in our convergence analysis imposes a milder requirement on the network width. Title: What do cross-lingual clone detectors really learn? A protocol and semantic counterfactual study
Abstract: Cross-lingual code clone detection aims to identify functionally equivalent code fragments written in different programming languages. Existing detectors often achieve high F1 scores on standard benchmarks, but these scores may be inflated by code or problem overlap and shallow lexical or structural cues. It is therefore unclear whether the detectors compare the semantics of two code fragments or exploit regularities in benchmark construction. To investigate this issue, we conduct a behavioral audit of six representative clone detectors on Java-to-X pairs from Project CodeNet. The audit combines protocols with increasingly strong isolation controls, shortcut controls, partner shuffling, and meaning-preserving and behavior-changing edits. Our results show that measured performance depends strongly on the evaluation protocol. GraphCodeBERT and UniXcoder fall from F1 scores of 0.9848 and 0.9916 under pair-random evaluation to 0.6588 and 0.6970 under problem-disjoint evaluation. Shallow Control achieves an F1 of 0.6889, showing that even problem-disjoint splits retain exploitable non-semantic cues. Partner shuffling further reveals that detectors differ in their reliance on the original cross-lingual pairing. Semantic counterfactuals show that GraphCodeBERT is stable under meaning-preserving edits but insensitive to behavioral changes, while DeepSeek-v4-flash exhibits the reverse pattern. No evaluated detector achieved both high preservation stability and high breaking rejection on this counterfactual set. Thus, neither high F1 nor clean splitting alone demonstrates cross-lingual semantic understanding. Evaluations should also test shortcut reliance, use of both code snippets, and responses to semantics-preserving and semantics-breaking edits. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group
Abstract: The energy transition triggers urgent questions about what values are important, who controls transitional processes, and who has the power to define the answers to the climate crisis. Energy companies claim their central role in the development of renewable energy as the ultimate solution. However, communities affected by large-scale renewable energy projects have extensively raised environmental and social justice concerns and denounced the industry's poor practices and abuses.In this article, we analyse 15 socio-environmental conflicts around renewable energy projects owned by the Enel Group, one of the world's largest energy utilities, through the values and valuation languages of the affected communities. We map them onto five dimensions: environmental, health-related, socio-economic, ontological, and political. We build on environmental justice and ecological economics literature on valuation languages and employ counter-accounting to gather bottom-up evidence of grievances.We argue that, while the company claims that RE is the ultimate solution and the ‘Creating Shared Value’ approach is beneficial to all parties, those impacted by Enel's projects question the corporate model of energy transition and defend a plurality of values embedded in relational worldviews that are systematically misrecognised. We eventually criticise the corporate self-attributed moral and value-centred mandate in the energy transition and call for inclusive research about desirable energy futures rooted in plural and relational value systems. Title: Examining the evolutionary patterns of open-source software projects
Abstract: Open-Source Software (OSS) is a cornerstone of modern software development, yet evaluating the trajectory of individual projects throughout their development lifecycle remains a challenge. This paper develops an exploratory classification framework for examining how OSS projects evolve along two interrelated dimensions: innovation intensity and contribution sustainability. Building on contemporary OSS research on governance and contributor dynamics, we analyze 1785 OSS projects initiated by Microsoft, Google, and Apache on GitHub. Our findings reveal that contribution sustainability is primarily driven by the resilience and engagement of the contributor base, rather than innovation alone. We further highlight the nuanced role of the first release in shaping early project dynamics, the evolutionary patterns observed in OSS projects, and the contrasting associations of for-profit and non-profit sponsorship with contribution sustainability and contributor retention. By synthesizing insights from OSS literature, this research seeks to offer theoretical contributions and practical strategies for project owners seeking to sustain innovation in OSS communities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: What counts as urban smartness? A longitudinal thematic analysis of smart city indexes
Abstract: Smart city indexes increasingly influence urban governance, policy benchmarking, and investment narratives, yet their conceptual evolution remains insufficiently examined. This article investigates how major smart city evaluation frameworks changed between 2017 and 2022 through a longitudinal thematic analysis of six prominent smart city indexes selected from an initial inventory of sixteen. Title: From precarious work to occupational health outcomes in hotel housekeepers: a narrative review with meta-synthesis
Abstract: Introduction: Hotel housekeepers sustain the core functioning of the hospitality industry yet perform demanding, repetitive, and undervalued work associated with substantial physical and psychosocial risks. Understanding how working conditions shape health, motivation, and lived experience is essential for informing prevention strategies and promoting decent work. Methods A sequential narrative review and qualitative meta -synthesis were conducted to integrate and reinterpret evidence across disciplines and study designs. Searches covered five academic databases and gray literature without year or language limits. Studies were screened using predefined criteria, appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and synthesized through narrative, tabular, and meta -analytical thematic analysis, with findings interpreted through the JD-R framework. Results Findings revealed employment precarity, work intensification, musculoskeletal pain, chemical and biological hazards, and elevated stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Time pressure fostered coping strategies such as skipping meals and delaying bathroom use. Gendered labor divisions, discrimination, and negative supervision contributed to invisibility and limited autonomy. Workers also expressed pride, intrinsic motivation, and collective action to make their contributions visible. Conclusions This review demonstrates that housekeeping is characterized by structural precarity and cumulative health burdens alongside resilience and emerging activism. Improving occupational health requires organizational and policy transformations: realistic workloads, safer equipment, secure contracts, participatory risk management, and leadership practices grounded in dignity and fairness; rather than reliance on individual coping. Structural change is essential to advance safer, more equitable, and sustainable workplaces in the hospitality sector. The JD-R framework highlights the need to reduce demand and strengthen resources. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Communication-efficient distributed quantile regression neural networks via convolution smoothing and poisson sampling
Abstract: Quantile regression neural networks (QRNNs) provide flexible nonlinear conditional quantile estimation, but training is hindered by the non-differentiability of the check-loss, and existing methods do not scale to large datasets stored non-randomly across distributed machines. We propose a convolution-smoothed QRNN (CS-QRNN) that replaces the check-loss with a twice-differentiable kernel-convolved surrogate, and a distributed extension (DCS-QRNN) that combines Poisson pilot sampling with a gradient-corrected surrogate loss. After a one-time pilot-sample collection and pilot-estimator broadcast, DCS-QRNN requires only a single round of gradient aggregation, with no further communication during optimization. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish consistency, asymptotic normality, and first-order equivalence to the centralized full-data estimator. In simulations across three nonlinear regression surfaces and three error distributions, DCS-QRNN achieves 80–100 ×  speedup at a 1% pilot ratio while preserving centralized accuracy: on a challenging multi-peak surface with t(3) errors, DCS-QRNN attains a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.3176 versus 0.3097 for the full-data estimator. Counting all three DCS-QRNN communication stages, the simulated wall-clock time at a network bandwidth of 100 Mbit/s and a latency of 100 ms per one-way stage is 38.0 seconds, versus 140.3 seconds for the fixed-budget FedAvg-QRNN protocol with (Formula presented). On the Household Electric Power Consumption and Beijing Multi-Site Air Quality datasets, DCS-QRNN preserves near-centralized accuracy while reducing running time by roughly an order of magnitude, confirming that its primary practical advantage is computational efficiency together with a substantially smaller number of synchronization stages. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Research on interruption risk propagation in aircraft supply chain network: A multi-layer network coupling model
Abstract: The aircraft supply chain (ASC) is a core component of national high-end equipment manufacturing systems, which have complex network characteristics of strong coupling. Once an interruption occurs at any node, it will propagate to relevant enterprises along the supply-demand relationship. However, the propagation process of interruption risks is not merely a matter of physical transmission, it is typically accompanied by the spread of risk information and the adoption of preventive measures. Therefore, investigating the dynamic coupling characteristics among risk information diffusion, adoption of preventive measures, and interruption risk propagation is of great significance for exploring the interruption risk propagation mechanisms in ASC. Considering the above facts, this paper proposes a three-layer coupled network model. This model divides enterprises into multiple different states and innovatively proposes different network layer propagation mechanisms and interlayer coupling methods. Subsequently, the microscopic Markov chain approach is employed to establish state transition Eqs., and the mathematical characteristics of interruption risk outbreak are derived through theoretical deduction. The proposed model is applied to the risk propagation analysis of real ASC networks, and the proposed method and key findings were visually demonstrated. The research results provide decision-making references for risk management in the aviation industry chain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Multi-output stability prediction of salt cavern energy storage using optimized machine learning model with interpretable features
Abstract: Salt cavern stability prediction is essential for the safe operation and risk prevention of underground energy-storage systems. In this study, a multi-output machine learning framework was developed to simultaneously predict maximum wall displacement (MD) and volume reduction rate (RV) of salt caverns. Fifteen machine learning algorithms were first compared using the Friedman test and Nemenyi post-hoc test, and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) was selected as the optimal base learner. Subsequently, four metaheuristic algorithms, including Jellyfish Search Optimizer (JSO), Tunicate Swarm Algorithm (TSA), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), were used to optimize the MLP hyperparameters. The results show that JSO-MLP provides the best overall performance. For MD prediction, the R2 values of the training and test sets are 0.9937 and 0.9854, respectively; for RV prediction, the corresponding R2 values are 0.9711 and 0.9606. Furthermore, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicates that MD is mainly influenced by cavern depth (CD), low operational pressure (LP), years of operation (t), and stress exponent (n), whereas RV is mainly affected by CD, LP, t , and high operational pressure (HP). These results demonstrate that the proposed JSO-MLP framework can provide an accurate and interpretable tool for salt cavern stability assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: D4RNet: A lightweight distracted driver detection network with knowledge distillation and gradient reversal layer
Abstract: Distracted Driver Detection (DDD) is critical for intelligent transportation systems, yet existing methods often incur high computational costs, leading to non-real-time detection on terminals and/or limited generalization across different camera views. In this work, we propose D4RNet, a lightweight Distracted Driver Detection network that integrates knowledge Distillation with a gradient Reversal layer (GRL) for the first time in this domain. Qualitative tests on real driving videos also demonstrate strong performance and robustness. Moreover, we introduce five new temporal–spatial combined splits for the 100-Driver dataset along with corresponding baselines, to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of model performance. We also indicate, based on numerous experiments, that future work should prioritize annotation quality and image diversity rather than architectural over-engineering. Title: Proactive vs reactive destination revitalisation

Title: Global research trends in nuclear forensic: A bibliometric review
Abstract: Nuclear forensic science is essential for global nuclear security, supporting the identification and attribution of nuclear materials outside regulatory control. Despite its strategic importance, a systematic understanding of the evolution, thematic structure, and key contributors shaping nuclear forensic research remains limited. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global nuclear forensic publication trends from 1973 to 2024 using peer-reviewed records from the Scopus database as of October 2025. Bibliometric indicators and network analyses were applied to examine temporal publication patterns, source journals, research themes, and authorship characteristics. Findings show that nuclear forensic research has transitioned from an emergent activity to a maturing and structured scientific discipline, mainly driven by international nuclear security priorities. Authorship and country-level analyses demonstrate a high concentration of research output within a limited number of nuclear-capable states and government-affiliated institutions. Title: Foodborne microplastics: Occurrence in food matrices, health implications, analytical challenges and multi-tiered control strategies
Abstract: This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on foodborne microplastics (MPs) to establish a scientific foundation for risk assessment and control. Despite their widespread presence in food systems, research is hindered by a lack of standardized detection methods and unresolved uncertainties regarding their health implications. Our synthesis shows that the toxicity of MPs arises from a combination of physical abrasion, chemical leaching, and a “Trojan horse” mechanism that carries co-pollutants, collectively triggering oxidative stress and inflammation. A primary challenge remains the absence of harmonized analytical protocols, especially for nanoplastics. Key conclusions emphasize the need for a multi-tiered control strategy, spanning from source reduction to the development of safer alternatives. While vigilance is warranted, the likely existence of a dose-response relationship argues against undue alarm. Future work should focus on standardizing methods and using human-relevant models to inform evidence-based food safety policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Trends in access to basic sanitation services across Brazilian municipalities under a new legal framework
Abstract: Federal Law No. 14,026/2020 updated Brazil's sanitation legal framework, reinforcing universalization targets for water supply and sewage services. It mandates that by the end of 2033, sanitation contracts must ensure 99% of the population has access to potable water and 90% to sewage collection and treatment. Given Brazil's vast territory and regional disparities, achieving these targets across all municipalities poses a significant challenge. This article examines whether water and sewage coverage rates converged between 2010 and 2022, analyzing municipalities segregated by state and region. The study provides an up-to-date assessment of these indicators and identifies challenges in meeting the established targets. Empirical estimation of convergence draws on economic methodologies for growth and income convergence, incorporating beta-convergence and sigma-convergence hypotheses. Title: Personality engineering with AI agents: A new methodology for negotiation research
Abstract: According to canonical negotiation theory, people's success in a negotiation depends on how well they balance competing demands—empathizing and asserting, demonstrating concern for other and concern for self, being soft on the people and hard on the problem. Yet people struggle to manage these tensions, so researchers have lacked the ability to rigorously test the field's prescriptions under controlled conditions. AI agents do not face the same limitations, and their precision, repertoire, consistency, and scalability enable a new class of experiments to contribute to negotiation theory. In this article, we introduce personality engineering—a methodology that precisely parameterizes the personas of AI agents based on established personality frameworks—and propose how this method can be used to study the traits and behaviors of negotiators. Given its relevance to negotiation theory, we propose the interpersonal circumplex—and its two core dimensions of warmth and dominance—as a foundational coordinate system for the field. This approach offers both a rigorous methodology for testing classic negotiation theories and a practical guide for designing the personas of AI negotiation agents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Management of Disputes in the Construction Industry during COVID-19: Contractors' Takeaways for Future Pandemics
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified construction disputes. While dispute management has been widely studied, limited research has examined pandemic-induced disputes globally, especially within the Sri Lankan construction context. Hence, this study aims to investigate how to manage the disputes due to COVID-19 in the Sri Lankan construction industry, considering the contractors' perspective. The study adopts an interpretivist philosophy and employs a qualitative Delphi technique involving two iterative rounds of semistructured interviews, thereby making a methodological contribution. The data were analyzed through manual content analysis. The findings reveal six positive impacts and 12 negative impacts of COVID-19 on the construction industry, along with suitable preventive measures to manage the 12 important causes of disputes arising from the pandemic. This is positioned as one of the limited studies identifying both positive and negative impacts and suitable preventive measures in managing the identified causes. The findings can be applied for developing contexts of a similar nature, particularly in managing disputes during future pandemics.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Toward sustainable oceans: Redirecting fisheries subsidies through cleaner production in Chile
Abstract: Fisheries subsidies are often linked to overcapacity, overfishing, and environmental harm. As a result, global efforts have increasingly focused on eliminating harmful subsidies, while paying less attention to how public support can be designed to promote positive environmental outcomes. This study analyzes an alternative paradigm from Chile’s industrial shrimp (Heterocarpus reedi) and prawn (Cervimunida johni and Pleuroncodes monodon) fisheries, where a government-supported Clean Production Agreement (CPA) incentivized the adoption of cleaner production methods. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative documentary analysis with quantitative evaluation of environmental and economic indicators, we assessed the design, implementation, and outcomes of the CPA. Our findings reveal that the scheme enhanced environmental performance by reducing fuel consumption, bycatch, freshwater use, waste, and air emissions, while simultaneously delivering tangible economic benefits for participating companies. The initiative’s success was driven by four key design features: conditional funding tied to environmental goals, mandatory private co-financing, independent auditing and certification, and collaborative governance involving both public and private sectors. Importantly, subsidies did not cover fuel, fleet expansion, or other activities that could increase fishing capacity, thereby mitigating the risks of overcapacity and greenwashing. The Chilean case demonstrates that well-designed environmental subsidies can effectively support sustainability transitions in fisheries and offers valuable policy lessons for differentiating beneficial subsidies from those that threaten marine sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Data-driven virtual engine framework for predicting performance and emissions of biomass waste-derived biofuel engine
Abstract: This research study aims to develop virtual engine models with biofuel blends to forecast their characteristics in terms of combustion, performance and emission by employing multimodal data driven modelling through artificial neural networks. A superior combustion efficiency, performance and exhaust emission was exhibited in a blend comprising 90% Gasoline and 10% pine oil than observed in other biofuel combinations. Title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
Abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Study 2 further differentiates in-group sources by their hierarchical level—supervisor, same-level colleague, and subordinate—and examines their specific impacts on emotional exhaustion, which, in turn, affects sabotage and turnover intentions. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Authors: Wang K.; Pan Z.; Lu Y.
Title: Incompetence or deception: Unraveling the asymmetric mechanisms of AI hallucinations on trust and distrust
Abstract: Reliance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) for knowledge work is increasing, yet confidently presented hallucinations can elicit strong negative user reactions. Existing literature frames hallucinations as technical failures that reduce trust, conflating the decline of trust with the emergence of distrust. However, trust and distrust are theoretically distinct constructs rather than opposite ends of a single continuum. Drawing on information manipulation theory (IMT), this study reconceptualizes AI hallucinations as violations of conversational norms. It proposes a model linking hallucination cues to perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially related to trust and distrust. It further examines whether perceived AI autonomy moderates the relationship between hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The model was tested using a sequential mixed-methods design that combined qualitative semi-structured interviews with a two-wave survey of 506 GenAI users. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). The findings revealed that hallucination cues were differentially associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, with the former more strongly associated with trust and the latter with distrust. Perceived AI autonomy moderated the associations between some hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The PLS-SEM–NCA analysis provided complementary evidence on net effects and necessary conditions that neither method could offer alone. Overall, this study extends research on AI hallucinations by conceptualizing them as distinct forms of conversational norm violations and explaining how different hallucination cues are associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially linked to trust and distrust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
